Atimastillas flavicollis: lowland to foothill open woodland, gallery forest, riparian scrub, plantations, and mangroves, from Senegambia eastward, avoiding rainforest, to southern Chad and northwestern Central African Republic, and southward to coastal southeastern Ivory Coast eastward to southwestern Nigeria
Atimastillas flavigula: lowland to foothill open woodland, swamp forest, and riparian thickets, from north-central Cameroon eastward to southern South Sudan and central Ethiopia, thence southward to northern Angola and western Tanzania
Atlapetes albiceps: arid scrub of southeastern Ecuador and northwestern Peru
Atlapetes albinucha: montane shrubby edge on Caribbean slope from San Luis Potosí to central Oaxaca (eastern Mexico), disjunctly Pacific slope from eastern Chiapas to central Panama, and all three ranges of Colombian Andes to far northern Ecuador
Atlapetes albofrenatus: montane forest edge from Mérida in north-central Venezuela and Norte de Santander in northeastern Colombia, to Huila in southern Colombia
Atlapetes canigenis: Andes of southeastern Peru (Cusco) and far western Bolivia (La Paz)
Atlapetes crassus: Andes of western Colombia and Ecuador (Pichincha and El Oro)
Atlapetes forbesi: Andes of south-central Peru (Apurímac, Cusco, and Puno)
Atlapetes fulviceps: Andes of central Bolivia from Cochabamba southward to northwestern Argentina
Atlapetes latinuchus: humid to semi-humid forest and scrub in the Andes from northern Colombia southward to north-central Peru (Ancash), in the eastern Andes mainly northeastern Colombia and more locally in northern Peru
Atlapetes leucopis: locally in Andes of southern Colombia and eastern Ecuador
Atlapetes leucopterus: montane edge and scrub west of the Andes from far northwestern Ecuador to Cajamarca in northwestern Peru and east of the Andes locally in central Ecuador to northern Peru
Atlapetes luteoviridis: humid montane forest of western Panama
Atlapetes melanocephalus: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
Atlapetes melanolaemus: subtropical Andes of southeastern Peru (Cusco and Puno)
Atlapetes melanopsis: Andes of southern Peru (Ayacucho and Huancavelica)
Atlapetes nationi: dry montane scrub from west-central to southwestern Peru
Atlapetes nigrifrons: Perijá Mountains (far northeastern Colombia and far western Venezuela)
Atlapetes pallidinucha: montane forest and edge of eastern and central Andes from Táchira in southwestern Venezuela southwestward through Cajamarca, in far northern Peru
Atlapetes personatus: tepuis of southern Venezuela, adjacent western Guyana, and Roraima, in far northern Brazil
Atlapetes pileatus: Pacific slope from southern Sonora and Caribbean slope from central Nuevo León to transvolcanic belt southward to southern Oaxaca
Atlapetes rufigenis: Andes of northwestern Peru (Cajamarca, La Libertad, Ancash, and Huánuco)
Atlapetes rufinucha: montane forest edge in Andes from western to east-central Bolivia
Atlapetes schistaceus: montane cloudforest in Andes of northwestern Venezuela, including Sierra de Perijá, southward across all Andes of Colombia, and along the eastern Andes to central Ecuador (northeastern Morona Santiago)
Atlapetes seebohmi: dry montane scrub of Loja in south-central Ecuador to Ancash in northwestern Peru
Atlapetes semirufus: cloudforest in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Sucre and Monagas westward to Lara), and in the Andes of western Venezuela westward along the northeastern Colombian Andes (to northern Meta)
Atlapetes taczanowskii: Andes of central Peru (Huánuco and Junín)
Atlapetes tibialis: humid montane forest of Costa Rica and western Panama
Atlapetes tricolor: east slope of Andes of central Peru (San Martín southward to western Cusco in the Apurímac Valley), also local on outlying ridges (Cordillera Azul, southwestern Loreto; Cerros del Sira, Huánuco)
Atrichornis clamosus: southwestern Australia (coastal heaths east of Albany)
Atronanus fuliginosus: lowland forest, forest edge, and villages, from southeastern Nigeria and western Cameroon southward to eastern Gabon
Attagis gayi: montane far southern Colombia to central Ecuador; disjunctly from central Peru to southeastern Chile and southern Santa Cruz Province (southwestern Argentina)
Attagis malouinus: breeds high-montane southern Chile and west-central Argentina southward to Cape Horn; winters to plains of southeastern Argentina
Atticora fasciata: eastern Colombia to the Guianas, southern Venezuela, northern Bolivia, and Amazonian Brazil
Atticora pileata: highlands of southern Mexico (Chiapas) to western Honduras
Atticora tibialis: disjunctly in clearings near humid lowland to foothill forest from eastern Panama eastward to the Guiana Shield of southeastern Venezuela, northern Brazil (Roraima), and French Guiana, west of the Andes southward to west-central Ecuador, in the Amazon basin from southern Venezuela southward to southeastern Peru, northwestern Bolivia and southwestern Brazil (Acre), locally in central and eastern Amazonian Brazil (eastern Amazonas eastward to Tocantins), and the Atlantic Forest of southeastern Brazil (Espírito Santo to São Paulo)
Attila bolivianus: varzea and gallery forest in the Amazon basin, mostly south of the Amazon River, from far southeastern Colombia and eastern Peru eastward along the Amazon River to northeastern Brazil ( Amapá), and central Brazil (southward to Goiás and Mato Grosso do Sul)
Attila cinnamomeus: southern Venezuela and the Guianas to northern Bolivia and Amazonian Brazil
Attila citriniventris: eastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, northeastern Peru (Loreto), and western Amazonian Brazil
Attila phoenicurus: Amazonian and southeastern Brazil to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
Attila rufus: humid forest and scrub in the Atlantic Forest region of Brazil from southern Bahia southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul
Attila spadiceus: humid to semi-deciduous and gallery forest and woodland from the Pacific (southern Sonora) and Gulf (southern Veracruz) slopes of Mexico southward (including the Yucatan Peninsula and Cozumel) to eastern Panama (including Coiba), western Venezuela and Colombia, including the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta and the Cauca and Magdalena valleys, west of the Andes from western Colombia to northwestern Ecuador, east of the Andes from northern Venezuela eastward to Trinidad, the Guianas, and northern Ceará (northeastern Brazil), southward throughout the Amazon basin to central Bolivia and southwestern Mato Grosso (central Brazil), and disjunctly in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil (Pernambuco southward to northern Espírito Santo)
Attila torridus: far southwestern Colombia to western Ecuador and northwestern Peru (Tumbes)
Augastes lumachella: locally in northeastern Brazilian plateaux (Bahia and Minas Gerais)
Augastes scutatus: campos rupestres, montane forest, and gallery forest and scrub in the highlands of the Cerrado in central Minas Gerais
Aulacorhynchus albivitta: montane cloudforest in Sierra de Perijá, Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, the Andes of western Venezuela southward along the central and eastern Andes of Colombia to far northern Peru north of the Río Marañón, and west of the Andes southward to southern Colombia, mostly north of the Río Patía in Cauca; in Peru south of the Río Marañón southward along the Andes to central Bolivia (westernmost Santa Cruz), including lowlands locally in Ucayali and Madre de Dios eastward to adjacent Brazil (Acre and adjacent Rondônia) and northernmost Bolivia (Pando)
Aulacorhynchus coeruleicinctis: Andes of eastern Peru (Huánuco) to southern Bolivia (Santa Cruz, Chuquisaca)
Aulacorhynchus derbianus: far southern Colombia along east slope of Andes to Bolivia
Aulacorhynchus haematopygus: humid and cloudforest in Sierra de Perijá and the far southwestern Andes of Venezuela southward along the western, central, and eastern Andes of Colombia; in the east southward to northeastern Ecuador, in the west southward along the western Andes of Ecuador, including the coastal Cordillera Mache Chindul and Chongon Colonche, to southernmost Ecuador, in Loja
Aulacorhynchus huallagae: locally in mountains of northern Peru (San Martín and La Libertad)
Aulacorhynchus prasinus: humid to semi-humid forest in the Gulf of Mexico and Pacific slopes of Mexico from Veracruz, San Luis Potosí and in the Sierra Madre del Sur of Guerrero eastward to eastern Oaxaca, including Sierra de los Tuxtlas, and in central-east Mexico from easternmost Oaxaca and Chiapas eastward across interior Quintana Roo and Belize to Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras and western Nicaragua; also in the mountains of northwestern Costa Rica eastward to easternmost Panama and adjacent Colombia in Cerro Tacarcuna
Aulacorhynchus sulcatus: cloudforest in the slopes of Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta and Sierra de Perijá of northern Colombia eastward to the Andes of Venezuela and locally in northeasternmost Andes of Colombia in Arauca, and in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela from easternmost Zulia eastward to the Paría Peninsula
Aulacorhynchus whitelianus: humid foothill forest in the tepuis of central and southern Venezuela, southern Guyana, far northern Brazil in Roraima, and western Suriname
Auriparus flaviceps: arid scrub and riparian areas of lowlands to hills, in southeastern California to southwestern Utah, eastward to northern Texas (USA), and southward through Baja California, Sinaloa, and Hidalgo (central Mexico)
Automolus cervinigularis: forest to plantations of lowlands and hills on Caribbean slope from central Veracruz and northern Oaxaca (southeastern Mexico) through Mexico, including the southern Yucatan Peninsula in east-central Campeche, Peten (northern Guatemala), and Belize, through northwestern Panama
Automolus exsertus: Pacific slope of southwestern Costa Rica to western Panama (Chiriquí)
Automolus infuscatus: tropical rainforest in the Río Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern and central Venezuela, the Guianas and northeasternmost Brazil (Amapá) southwestward to the western Amazon in Brazil, eastward to the Rio Negro region (Amazonas, northern Rondônia and Acre), Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, southward to northwestern Bolivia
Automolus leucophthalmus: humid forest in the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado regions of southeastern Brazil, from southern Bahia southward to northernmost Rio Grande do Sul and southwestward to Goiás and southern Mato Grosso, eastern Paraguay, and far northeastern Argentina (Misiones)
Automolus melanopezus: southeastern Colombia to southeastern Peru, far northwestern Bolivia, and western Amazonian Brazil
Automolus ochrolaemus: tropical rainforest from eastern Panama and northwestern Colombia southward along the Pacific lowlands to west-central Ecuador and southward along the Magdalena Valley (to Tolima); widespread east of the Andes in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from central and eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to Amazonia in eastern Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru, and central Bolivia (in western Santa Cruz), and in Brazil (eastward to Amapá and central-east Pará, southward to eastern Mato Grosso)
Automolus paraensis: Brazil south of the Amazon River (Rio Madeira to Rio Tocantins)
Automolus rufipileatus: riparian and varzea forest, Gynerium thickets and bamboo stands along the foothills of the Andes of western Venezuela southward to eastern Colombia, where also descends to the Amazon lowlands, and southward across Ecuador and Peru to northwestern Bolivia and southwestern Brazil, in Acre; also in southern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to northern Brazil and the eastern Amazon of Brazil, in Pará, eastern Amazonas, eastward to westernmost Maranhão and Tocantins, and southward to northern Mato Grosso and Rondônia
Automolus subulatus: tropical rainforest in the upper Orinoco and Amazon basins, from southern Venezuela southwestward to central and western Amazon of Brazil (from eastern Pará and southward to northern Mato Grosso and Rondônia), and from southeastern Colombia southward to northwestern Bolivia (southward to northern La Paz and adjacent Beni)
Automolus virgatus: humid forest of lowlands and foothills of southern Central America, southward from northeastern Honduras (where rare and local), on both slopes of Costa Rica, and Caribbean slope of Panama through much of central and western Colombia, thence west of the Andes to southwestern Ecuador
Aviceda cuculoides: lowland to montane woodland, rainforest, and riparian and coastal forest, from Senegambia eastward to southwestern Ethiopia, Kenya, and southern Somalia, and southward to Angola, northeastern Namibia and southern South Africa; some local populations short-distance migrants
Aviceda jerdoni: lowland to foothill rainforest, and coastal swamp forest, from southern India and Sri Lanka eastward through eastern India to southern China (including Hainan), and southward to Sumatra, Borneo, Sulawesi and associated islands, and Philippines
Aviceda leuphotes: lowland to foothill open tropical forest from central Nepal eastward through Himalayan foothills to south-central China (including Hainan), and southward to Andaman Islands and southeastern Asia; some northern populations migrate to southern India, Sumatra, and western Java
Aviceda subcristata: Wallacea (except Sulawesi), New Guinea region, northern and eastern Australia, Bismarck Archipelago, and Solomon Archipelago
Avocettula recurvirostris: southeastern Venezuela to the Guianas and north-central Brazil; eastern Ecuador
Aythya affinis: breeds North America from northern Alaska and western Canada southward through northern California, southern Colorado, and Minnesota (USA); winters to Hawaiian Islands, the Caribbean, and northern South America
Aythya americana: breeds Alaska to southern USA; winters to Guatemala and Greater Antilles
Aythya australis: Australia including Tasmania, Vanuatu (Banks Islands to Tanna), eastern Lesser Sundas, and southern New Guinea
Aythya baeri: breeds northeastern Asia; winters to southern Japan (southern Honshu to Kyushu), southern China and southeastern Asia (now rare everywhere)
Aythya collaris: breeds Alaska to southern USA; winters to Panama and southern Lesser Antilles, less often to central Japan
Aythya ferina: Palearctic, breeding British Isles and southern Scandinavia eastward through east-central Russia, in south from Iberian Peninsula and Türkiye eastward through northeastern China and northern Japan (northern Hokkaido, rare); winters to tropical Africa and India eastward to Japan (Honshu to Ryukyu Islands) and southward to the northern Philippines
Aythya fuligula: breeds northern Palearctic from Iceland eastward to Kamchatka, southward to central Europe, Mongolia, and northern Japan (northern Hokkaido, rare); winters to northern Africa and southern and southeastern Asia including Philippines
Aythya innotata: Lac Alaotra and Lac Matsaborimena (north-central and northwestern Madagascar, respectively); thought extinct until rediscovered at Lac Matsaborimena in 2006
Aythya marila: breeds subarctic from Iceland and Scandinavia to Kamchatka and the Commander Islands (southeastern Russia), and Alaska eastward to northern Quebec (eastern Canada); winters to coasts of northwestern and east-central Europe, Black and Caspian seas, eastern China, Korean Peninsula, Japan (Hokkaido to Ryukyu Islands), and Taiwan, and central California, Great Lakes, and North Carolina (southwestern to east-central USA)
Aythya nyroca: breeds discontinuously through southern Palearctic, from Spain through northeastern China; winters to India, southeastern Asia, eastern China, and southern Japan (central Honshu to Kyushu)
Aythya valisineria: breeds North America from northern Alaska and western Canada southward through northern California, southern Colorado, and Minnesota (USA); winters to central Mexico, less often to central Japan
Baeolophus atricristatus: deciduous to evergreen forest, woodland, orchards, and gardens in southwestern Oklahoma, far eastern New Mexico, and Texas (south-central USA) southward to central Veracruz (southeastern Mexico), with an isolated population in Sierra de los Tuxtlas (southern Veracruz; current status unclear)
Baeolophus bicolor: south-central Canada (Ontario) to eastern, central, and southeastern USA
Baeolophus inornatus: oak woodland from lowlands to mountains of southern Oregon through California to northern, and disjunctly, far southern Baja California (northwestern Mexico)
Baeolophus ridgwayi: arid juniper woodland in montane areas in southeastern Oregon eastward to southern Wyoming, southward to eastern California, far northeastern Sonora (northwestern Mexico), and far western Texas (south-central USA)
Baeolophus wollweberi: oak woodland and riparian areas mostly in mountains of southeastern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico in the west, and central Nuevo León in the east, to transvolcanic belt and through south-central Oaxaca (northeastern to south-central Mexico)
Baeopogon clamans: patchy in lowland to foothill primary forest and old secondary forest, especially along rivers and forest streams, from southeastern Nigeria eastward to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and southward to Gabon and western Republic of the Congo
Baeopogon indicator: lowland to foothill primary and secondary forest from Guinea-Bissau and western Guinea eastward to southern South Sudan and western Kenya, thence southward to northern Angola and northwestern Zambia
Balaeniceps rex: swamps of South Sudan and southwestern Ethiopia to southern Democratic Republic of the Congo and northern Zambia; irregular non-breeding visitor in Central African Republic
Balearica pavonina: patchy in lowland and foothill shallow wetland and grassland from Senegambia and southern Mauritania eastward in the Sahel to southern Sudan, Eritrea, and western Ethiopia, southward to South Sudan and far northern Kenya; some seasonal dispersal
Balearica regulorum: lowland and foothill shallow wetland, marsh, grassland, and savanna, from central Uganda and central Kenya southward through East Africa to southern Angola and northern Namibia to central Mozambique, and disjunctly in eastern and southern South Africa; some seasonal dispersal
Bambusicola fytchii: foothill to montane tall grassland, open scrub forest, thickets, and bamboo, from northeastern India and eastern Bangladesh eastward through south-central China (Sichuan and Yunnan), Myanmar, and southward to northwestern Thailand, northern Laos, and northern Vietnam
Bambusicola sonorivox: bamboo thickets and bushy areas in hills of Taiwan; introduced northern Kyushu (southern Japan)

Bangsia arcaei: foothill forest and edge of Caribbean slope from northwestern to central Costa Rica, and disjunctly western Panama and far northwestern Colombia (Cerro Tacarcuna area)
Bangsia aureocincta: Pacific slope of western Andes of Colombia
Bangsia edwardsi: Andean foothills of southwestern Colombia and northwestern Ecuador
Bangsia flavovirens: locally in humid western Andes of Colombia and northwestern Ecuador
Bangsia melanochlamys: central and western Andes of Colombia
Bangsia rothschildi: Andes of western Colombia to northwestern Ecuador (Esmeraldas)
Bartramia longicauda: breeds inland grassland from southeastern Alaska eastward to southeastern Canada and New England, in south to eastern Oregon and Pennsylvania (USA); winters inland grassland from southern Paraguay, southern Brazil, Uruguay, and west-central to east-central Argentina

Baryphthengus ruficapillus: lowlands of eastern Brazil to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
Basileuterus belli: pine-oak montane forest of Mexico (southern Sinaloa and southwestern Durango in the west and central Tamaulipas in the east) southward through Honduras
Basileuterus culicivorus: disjunctly in dry to humid forest in the lowlands and foothills of the Pacific slope from Nayarit (western Mexico) southward to El Salvador, and on the Gulf slope from southern Nuevo León southward in Mexico (including the Yucatan Peninsula) to western Panama, mountains of coastal Venezuela (to the Paría Peninsula), Trinidad, tepuis from central Venezuela southward to Roraima (northern Brazil) and southern Guyana, the Santa Marta foothills, the Andes of Venezuela through all Colombian Andes southward to northern Nariño, from central Bolivia eastward in southern Amazonian Brazil (from Ceará) in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil, southward to central Paraguay and Buenos Aires (northeastern Argentina), and the Yungas of Bolivia and northern Argentina; rare non-breeding visitor to far southern USA
Basileuterus delattrii: disjunctly in mountains of Chiapas (far southeastern Mexico) eastward to central Panama, and dry to semi-humid forests and scrub in the lowlands of northern Colombia and adjacent far western Venezuela, southward along the Cauca and Magdalena valleys of central Colombia
Basileuterus ignotus: humid montane forest of eastern Panama and far northwestern Colombia
Basileuterus melanogenys: montane forest from north-central Costa Rica to central Panama, with an undescribed population in Azuero Peninsula (south-central Panama)
Basileuterus melanotis: mountains of Costa Rica and western Panama
Basileuterus punctipectus: humid cloudforest in the eastern Andes of southeastern Peru (Puno) eastward along the Andes to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz)
Basileuterus rufifrons: scrub and edge mostly in foothills from northern Sonora (and southeastern Arizona; rare) in west and central Nuevo León in east (northeastern Mexico) southward and joining across the transvolcanic belt, southward (except Yucatan Peninsula) to southern Guatemala and Belize
Basileuterus tacarcunae: local in highlands of central Panama (Panamá and Guna Yala), eastern Panama (Cerra Tacarcuna, Darién), and adjacent northwestern Colombia (Chocó)
Basileuterus trifasciatus: humid forest in the western Andes of southwestern Ecuador (El Oro and Loja) and northwestern Peru (southward to La Libertad)
Basileuterus tristriatus: humid forest in coastal mountains of Venezuela (Falcón eastward to the Paría Peninsula), and in the Andes from western Venezuela and all Andes of Colombia, and the Sierra del Perijá and Serranía de San Lucas, southward in the Andes of Ecuador to southern Peru (Cusco)
Basilinna leucotis: montane forest and edge of southeastern Arizona (southwestern USA) on Pacific slope and central Nuevo León on Caribbean slope southward through northern Nicaragua
Basilinna xantusii: arid scrub of southern Baja California
Basilornis celebensis: Sulawesi region, including Lembeh (off northeast) and Muna and Buton islands (off southeast)
Basilornis galeatus: Peleng and Banggai, in Banggai Islands, and Taliabu and Mangole, in Sula Islands (off eastern Sulawesi)
Batara cinerea: dry to humid forest and woodland in the foothils of the Andes of southeastern Bolivia southward to northwestern Argentina, and in western Paraguay; in the Atlantic Forest region from central-eastern Brazil, in southern Bahia, southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul, northeasternmost Argentina, and adjacent Paraguay
Bathmocercus cerviniventris: patchy in lowland to submontane Upper Guinean rainforest understory, and secondary scrub along streams, from Sierra Leone and southeastern Guinea eastward to southwestern Ivory Coast (old records for Ghana)

Batis capensis: patchy in lowland to montane forest edge, dense bush, and miombo woodland, from central Zimbabwe and western Mozambique southward to Eswatini, Lesotho, and southern South Africa; local altitudinal migration
Batis crypta: patchy in foothill to submontane patches of evergreen forest in highlands of eastern and southern Tanzania, and adjacent northwestern Malawi; some downslope dispersal post-breeding
Batis dimorpha: foothill to montane rainforest of northern Malawi and adjacent eastern Zambia southward to southern Malawi and adjacent northern Mozambique
Batis diops: foothill to montane evergreen forest, particularly with bamboo, and cloudforest, in the Albertine Rift highlands of northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and eastward to southwestern Uganda, western Rwanda, and western Burundi
Batis erlangeri: lowland to montane secondary forest, open woodland, and wooded grassland, from southeastern Nigeria and central Cameroon eastward to southern Sudan, Eritrea, and Ethiopia, and southward to northern Angola, western Kenya, and northwestern Tanzania
Batis fratrum: southern Malawi to eastern Zimbabwe, Mozambique, and KwaZulu-Natal
Batis ituriensis: patchy in lowland and foothill secondary and (sometimes) primary forest, and degraded forest, from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and eastward to west-central Uganda
Batis margaritae: disjunctly in montane forest in western Angola, and open dry and riverine forest of southern Democratic Republic of the Congo and northwestern Zambia (possibly far eastern Angola)
Batis minima: patchy in lowland and foothill forest edge; old secondary growth, and old plantations, from southern Cameroon and southwestern Central Africa Republic, and southward through mainland Equatorial Guinea and Gabon to south-central Republic of the Congo
Batis minor: lowland and foothill acacia steppe, riparian and semi-deciduous woodland, from southern Somalia southward through southeastern Kenya, including Manda Island, to northeastern Tanzania
Batis minulla: patchy in lowland to foothill forest edge, thickets, and escarpment scrub, from northern Republic of the Congo and southeastern Gabon, southward to Cabinda (northwestern Angola), and eastward to western Democratic Republic of the Congo, and disjunctly in western Angola
Batis mixta: patchy in lowland to montane thickets, juniper forest, and coastal woodland, from southeastern Kenya and northeastern Tanzania southward to southeastern Tanzania (possibly northern Mozambique)
Batis molitor: lowland to montane wooded savanna, miombo and acacia woodland, open montane forest, and plantations, from southeastern Gabon eastward to southern South Sudan and western Kenya, and southward to northern Namibia and southeastern South Africa

Batis orientalis: lowland to montane dry wooded savanna, acacia woodland, and dense thorn-scrub, from northeastern Nigeria and southern Chad eastward to central and northeastern Sudan and Somalia, southward to Central African Republic and northern Kenya
Batis perkeo: lowland and foothill thornscrub, acacia woodland, dry scrub, and lightly wooded grassland, from northeastern Uganda and southeastern South Sudan eastward to eastern Ethiopia and adjacent Somali, and southward through central Kenya to northeastern Tanzania

Batis senegalensis: lowland to foothill thornscrub, wooded savanna, sparsely wooded grassland, and acacia woodland, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward, avoiding rainforest, to central Niger, Nigeria, and northern Cameroon

Batrachostomus affinis: northern Thailand, southern Myanmar, central Vietnam to Malayan Peninsula, northern Sumatra, Riau Islands (east of central Sumatra), and Borneo
Batrachostomus auritus: central and southern Thai-Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Natuna Islands, and Borneo
Batrachostomus cornutus: Sumatra, Bangka and Belitung (just off southern Sumatra), Borneo including Banggi (off northeastern Borneo), and Kangean Islands (northeast of Java)
Batrachostomus harterti: mountains of northern and central Borneo
Batrachostomus javensis: lowlands of western and central Java
Batrachostomus moniliger: humid forest of southwestern India and Sri Lanka
Batrachostomus stellatus: peninsular Thailand to Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, Borneo, and adjacent islands
Berenicornis comatus: far southern Myanmar, Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, and Borneo
Berlepschia rikeri: southeastern Colombia to eastern Peru, northwestern Bolivia, the Guianas, and Amazonian Brazil
Bias musicus: disjunctly in lowland to foothill forest and secondary woodland from Guinea-Bissau eastward to southern South Sudan, Uganda, and northwestern Tanzania, southward to northern Angola and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, of central Kenya and coastal eastern Tanzania, and from southern Malawi and Mozambique southward to eastern Zimbabwe
Biatas nigropectus: southeastern Brazil (southeastern Minas Gerais) to far northeastern Argentina (Misiones)
Bleda canicapillus: lowland to foothill evergreen and semi-deciduous forest, gallery forest, forest-savanna mosaic, woodland thickets, and old secondary forest, from Senegambia eastward to central Nigeria and far southwestern Cameroon
Bleda eximius: lowland to foothill understory of Upper Guinea rainforest, and old secondary forest, from Sierra Leone eastward to western Togo
Bleda notatus: lowland forest understory, swamp-forest, and old secondary forest, from southeastern Nigeria eastward through southern Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), to western Central African Republic, and southward to far western Democratic Republic of the Congo
Bleda syndactylus: lowland and foothill forest, gallery forest, and dense thickets, from Sierra Leone eastward to southern South Sudan, Uganda, and western Kenya, thence southward to northern Angola and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Bleda ugandae: lowland to foothill Congolian rainforest understory, swamp-forest, and old secondary forest, from southwestern Central African Republic eastward to southwestern South Sudan and Uganda, and southward to southeastern Republic of Congo, south-central Democratic Republic of the Congo, and far northern Tanzania
Blythipicus pyrrhotis: foothill to submontane forest, and bamboo, from Nepal eastward to southeastern China (including Hainan), and southward to Malayan Peninsula and southern Vietnam
Blythipicus rubiginosus: southern Myanmar, southwestern Thailand, Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, and Borneo

Boissonneaua flavescens: montane cloudforest in the Andes from western Venezuela southwestward in the western, central and eastern Andes of Colombia, to northern Ecuador (southward to Cotopaxi and Napo)

Boissonneaua matthewsii: Andes of far southeastern Colombia, Ecuador, and eastern Peru

Bolborhynchus ferrugineifrons: central Andes of western Colombia (Tolima and Cauca)
Bolborhynchus lineola: humid montane forest with abundant bamboo and mixed pine-evergreen forest in montane southern Mexico (Veracruz, adjacent Puebla, and northern Oaxaca) southward across Guatemala to northern Nicaragua, Costa Rica, and western Panama, coastal mountains of central Venezuela, Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Sierra de Perijá, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward to northernmost Peru, and locally in the eastern Andes of Peru southward to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz)
Bolborhynchus orbygnesius: Andes of Peru and western Bolivia

Bombycilla cedrorum: breeds North America; winters to northern South America and Greater Antilles
Bombycilla garrulus: breeds northern Europe and northern Asia, and northwestern North America; winters to western Europe, central and eastern Asia, and south of breeding range in North America
Bombycilla japonica: breeds southeastern Siberia and northeastern China; winters to southern China and Kyushu (southern Japan)

Bostrychia olivacea: disjunctly along lowland to montane streams and rivers in dense forest, and swamp forest, from Sierra Leone to Ghana, from southern Cameroon southward to Gabon and eastward to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and highlands of central Kenya and northeastern Tanzania; extinct on Príncipe (Gulf of Guinea)
Bostrychia rara: Liberia to Cameroon, Gabon, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and far northeastern Angola
Botaurus cinnamomeus: India to southeastern Asia east to southern Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Philippines, and Indonesia
Botaurus dubius: southwestern, northern, and eastern Australia (except Tasmania); winters to New Guinea
Botaurus eurhythmus: breeds southeastern Siberia, eastern China, Korean Peninsula, and (now rare) northern Japan (Hokkaido and northern Honshu); winters mainly from Malayan Peninsula to Greater Sundas, Sulawesi, and Philippines
Botaurus exilis: southern Canada to the West Indies, west-central Peru, the Guianas, southeastern Brazil, and Paraguay
Botaurus flavicollis: lowland and foothill forested streams and wetlands, swamps, and mangroves, from Pakistan and India eastward to southeastern China (including Hainan) and Taiwan, southward to southeastern Asia and Philippines, and from Sulawesi and Lesser Sundas eastward through New Guinea to Bismarck and Solomon archipelagoes, and southward to Australia; northern populations winter to Indonesia
Botaurus involucris: Colombia to the Guianas, southern Venezuela, central Argentina, and central Chile
Botaurus lentiginosus: breeds Alaska to Mexico; winters to Panama and West Indies
Botaurus minutus: central and southern Europe to Siberia, and Africa and Madagascar
Botaurus pinnatus: lowlands of eastern Mexico to Ecuador, the Guianas, northern Argentina, and Brazil
Botaurus poiciloptilus: far southwestern Western Australia, southeastern Queensland to southeastern South Australia (including Tasmania), Grande Terre and Ouvea (New Caledonia; rare); and North, South, and Stewart islands (New Zealand)

Botaurus stellaris: breeds from England, Sweden, and Spain through Europe, northern and southern Africa, Middle East, and central Asia eastward to Russian Far East, northeastern China, and central Japan (local, Honshu); winters in central and southern Europe, Mediterranean Basin and sub-Saharan Africa eastward to southern and southeastern Asia
Brachygalba albogularis: patchily distributed southeastern Peru to northern Bolivia and southwestern Amazonian Brazil
Brachygalba goeringi: tropical northeastern Colombia and northwestern Venezuela
Brachygalba lugubris: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin from eastern Colombia southward to northeastern Peru north of the Río Marañón, and eastward across southern and central Venezuela to the Guianas and northeastern Brazil; in the eastern Amazon of Brazil extends southward to interior Brazil (western São Paulo and Mato Grosso do Sul, and wesfward to Rondônia), and northeasternmost Bolivia (Santa Cruz)
Brachygalba salmoni: tropical eastern Panama and northwestern Colombia
Brachypteracias leptosomus: dense rainforest of central and northeastern Madagascar

Brachypteryx hyperythra: northeastern India (Sikkim to Arunachal Pradesh) to southwestern China (Yunnan)

Bradornis microrhynchus: dry bush in lowlands and hills from northwestern Ethiopia eastward through Somalia and southward through eastern Uganda to central Tanzania
Bradypterus baboecala: patchy in lowland to montane reedy marsh and papyrus swamp of western Chad (Lake Chad), Ethiopian highlands, western Angola, southeastern Kenya and eastern Tanzania, and from southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo southward to southern South Africa
Bradypterus bangwaensis: submontane to montane dense understory of forest edges and clearings, riparian tall grass and rank herbage, and bracken-bramble thicker, in highlands of southeastern Nigeria (Obudu Plateau, Mambilla Plateau, and Gotel Mountains) and southwestern Cameroon Highlands (Mt. Oku, Banso Mountains, Bamenda Highlands, Bamboutos Plateau, Mt. Manengouba, western Adamawa Highlands, and Poli)

Bradypterus lopezi: disjunctly in foothill and montane dense forest undergrowth of southeastern Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), western Angola, and from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to western Kenya highlands, and southward to northern Zambia, Malawi, and northern Mozambique
Bradypterus seebohmi: humid grassy swamps of eastern Madagascar
Bradypterus sylvaticus: patchy in lowland dense thickets in forest patches and edges, usually near water, in coastal South Africa (Western Cape eastward to KwaZulu-Natal)

Brotogeris pyrrhoptera: arid scrub of western Ecuador and far northwestern Peru

Brotogeris tirica: eastern Brazil (Bahia and southern Goiás to Rio Grande do Sul)
Brotogeris versicolurus: lowlands of southeastern Colombia to eastern Peru and Amazonian Brazil

Bubo scandiacus: Arctic circumpolar; irregular southern post-breeding irruptions

Buceros hydrocorax: Philippines (except West Visayas, Palawan group, and Sulu Archipelago)
Buceros rhinoceros: lowland forest of southern Malayan Peninsula, Java, and Borneo

Butastur liventer: savanna and woodland of southeastern Asia, Java, and Sulawesi
Butastur rufipennis: savanna and grassland of sub-Saharan Africa
Butastur teesa: woodland and plains of southeastern Iran to India, southern Tibet, and Myanmar

Buteo brachyurus: southern Florida; eastern Mexico to Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, and northern Argentina
Buteo buteo: breeds western and northern Palearctic including Atlantic islands, eastward to Caucasus and northern Iran; winters to sub-Saharan Africa and southern Asia
Buteo hemilasius: open steppes and montane slopes of eastern Asia

Buteo oreophilus: highlands of Ethiopia to Tanzania and Malawi

Buteo regalis: prairies and plains of southern Canada to northern Mexico
Buteo ridgwayi: lowlands of Hispaniola and satellite islands

Buteo trizonatus: South Africa (Western Cape and Eastern Cape north to Limpopo)
Buteo ventralis: Patagonian forest of southern Chile and Argentina
Buteogallus aequinoctialis: northeastern Venezuela (Río Orinoco delta) to eastern Brazil (Paraná)
Buteogallus anthracinus: southwestern USA to St. Vincent (southern Lesser Antilles), Trinidad, and Pacific coast of Colombia, Ecuador, and far northern Peru
Buteogallus coronatus: savanna of southern Brazil, Paraguay, and Bolivia to northern Argentina
Buteogallus gundlachii: Cuba including Isla de la Juventud
Buteogallus lacernulatus: lowland forest of coastal southeastern Brazil
Buteogallus meridionalis: savanna and marshes of western Panama to Brazil and northern Argentina
Buteogallus schistaceus: tropical southern Venezuela to eastern Bolivia and Amazonian Brazil
Buteogallus solitarius: cloudforest and pine-oak forest to deciduous forest in montane regions from Sierra Madre Occidental in northwestern Mexico and locally in Sierra Madre Oriental southeastward patchily through montane regions of Central America to western Panama; in Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Sierra de Perijá, the coastal mountains of north-central Venezuela, and the Andes of western Venezuela southward patchily in the Andes of Colombia, through eastern and southwestern Ecuador to northern Peru, and in the eastern Andes from northern Peru southeastward through Bolivia to northwestern Argentina (to Catamarca); also in the Guiana Shield in far southern Venezuela, northernmost Brazil, and adjacent Guyana

Cacicus cela: humid and deciduous forest from central Panama westward to the lowlands of Colombia and Venezuela, in the Pacific lowlands from far southwestern Colombia to far northwestern Peru, and east of the Andes from the lowlands of northern Venezuela, Trinidad, and the Guianas southward across the Amazon basin, and in the Atlantic Forest of east-central Brazil from Paraiba southward to São Paulo
Cacicus chrysonotus: montane cloudforest in the Andes from far western Venezuela southward across all Andes of Colombia, eastern Andes of Ecuador (including the Cajas plateau), and eastern Andes of Peru southward to central Bolivia
Cacicus chrysopterus: southeastern Bolivia (southern Santa Cruz to Tarija) to Paraguay, southern Brazil, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
Cacicus haemorrhous: disjunctly in humid and gallery forest in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern Venezuela, the Guianas, and northeastern Brazil southward across the Amazon to eastern Peru and northern Bolivia (to Santa Cruz) and Mato Grosso (central Brazil) and eastward to Maranhão, and in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil from Alagoas southward to eastern Parguay, northeastern Argentina (to Corrientes), and Uruguay
Cacicus latirostris: tropical southeastern Colombia to northeastern Peru and far western Brazil
Cacicus oseryi: tropical eastern Ecuador, eastern Peru, northwestern Bolivia (northern La Paz), and far southwestern Brazil (Amazonas)
Cacicus sclateri: tropical forest of eastern Ecuador and far northern Peru
Cacicus solitarius: southwestern Venezuela (Táchira, Apure) southward through eastern Colombia (Meta), eastern Ecuador, and eastern Peru, Brazil (south of Amazon eastward to Ceará, Pernambuco, and western Bahia; perhaps locally north of the Amazon River on Rio Branco, in Roraima) southward to northern and eastern Bolivia (Pando southeastward to Tarija), Chaco of Paraguay, northern and eastern Argentina (southward to Santiago del Estero, Santa Fe, and Buenos Aires) and western Uruguay (locally along Río Uruguay)
Cacicus uropygialis: humid forest from eastern Honduras southward to the lowlands of northwestern Colombia and southward along the Pacific lowlands to southern Ecuador (El Oro); also in humid cloudforest in the Andes from western Venezuela, including the Sierra de Perjia, southward along all Andes of Colombia and eastern Andes of Ecuador to southern Peru (Cusco and Ayacucho)
Cacomantis castaneiventris: New Guinea and northeastern Australia (Wet Tropics region, north-eastern Cape York Peninsula)
Cacomantis flabelliformis: montane New Guinea, southwestern and eastern Australia including Tasmania, New Caledonia, Solomon Archipelago, Vanuatu, and Fiji (southwestern Polynesia)
Cacomantis passerinus: India and Pakistan; winters to Sri Lanka
Cacomantis sepulcralis: tropical rainforest, mangroves, and adjacent clearings from southern Myanmar and southern Thailand southward to Singapore, Sumatra and satellite islands, Java and Bali, and Borneo, eastward through the Lesser Sundas to Alor, and the Philippines (including the Palawan group and Sulu Archipelago)
Cacomantis sonneratii: India and Sri Lanka to southern China, southeastern Asia, Greater Sundas, and Palawan (southwestern Philippines)
Cacomantis variolosus: lowland to foothill rainforest, scrub, and mangroves, from eastern Lesser Sundas (Timor to Wetar) and the Moluccas eastward through New Guinea, including many satellite islands, to Bismarck Archipelago, and southward to northern and eastern Australia; Australian populations migrate to tropics in winter
Cacomantis virescens: Sulawesi region including Banggai and Sula islands (off eastern Sulawesi) and Buton and Tukangbesi (to southeast)
Cairina moschata: lowland wetlands from northern Mexico southward, west of the Andes, to southwestern Ecuador and, east of the Andes, to northeastern Argentina and Brazil; domestic varieties introduced almost worldwide
Calamanthus montanellus: semiarid southwestern Australia (Geraldton to Point Culver)
Calamonastes fasciolatus: lowland and foothill semiarid savanna and rocky woodland from southwestern Angola and northern Namibia eastward to western Zimbabwe and northern South Africa
Calamonastes simplex: lowland to foothill acacia thornscrub, dry woodland, and arid savanna, from Djibouti, central Ethiopia, and Somalia southward to southeastern South Sudan, eastern Uganda, and northern Tanzania
Calamonastes stierlingi: lowland and foothill in miombo and acacia woodland, and thickets on termitaria, from northern Zambia eastward to southeastern Tanzania and northern Mozambique, and southward to northeastern Botswana, eastern South Africa, and Eswatini
Calamonastes undosus: lowland and foothill broadleaf and miombo woodland, and thickets on termitaria, from Cabinda (northwestern Angola), western Democratic Republic of the Congo, and adjacent Republic of the Congo, eastward (avoiding Congolian rainforest) to southwestern Kenya, and southward to western Angola, northern Zambia, and south-central Tanzania
Calamonastides gracilirostris: patchy in foothill papyrus swamp from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to western Kenya, southward to northern Burundi and far northwestern Tanzania, and in northern Zambia
Calamospiza melanocorys: breeds western Canada and western USA; winters to northern Mexico
Calandrella acutirostris: foothill to montane sandy or gravel plain with very sparse vegetation from southern Kazakhstan eastward to central China, and southward to southern Pakistan, northern Nepal, and northern Bhutan; migrates southward in winter as far as northern India
Calandrella blanfordi: montane grassland, bare stony areas, and short-grass plains of Eritrean and Ethiopian highlands
Calandrella brachydactyla: lowland to foothill dry country with sparse cover on sandy or stony soils, from Iberian Peninsula and southern Europe eastward to western Mongolia, and southward to northwestern Africa, Sinai Peninsula, and eastern Arabia; most populations migrate southward as far as the African Sahel, Arabian Peninsula, and western India
Calandrella cinerea: disjunctly in lowland to montane open grassland, including burned and heavily grazed grassland, and saltmarsh, of central Nigeria (Jos Plateau), and from northern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to southern Kenya and northern Tanzania, and from southern Democratic Republic of the Congo and southwestern Tanzania southward to southern South Africa; some populations migratory
Calandrella dukhunensis: breeds in central and eastern Mongolia, and possibly in adjacent China; reported in China eastward to Liaoning, but breeding in China is not confirmed, and most or all records may refer to migrants; migrant also in northern Myanmar; winters in central and southern India
Calandrella eremica: foothill and montane stony short grassland of the southwestern Arabian Peninsula and northern Somalia and adjacent northeastern Ethiopia
Calcarius lapponicus: breeds Greenland and Scandinavia to northeastern Siberia, including High Arctic islands, southward to Kamchatka, and Aleutians, Alaska, and northern Canadian Arctic eastward to Ellesmere Island; winters to central Eurasia and central USA
Calcarius ornatus: breeds prairies of central North America; winters southwestern USA to northern Mexico
Calcarius pictus: breeds Alaska and western Canada; winters in south-central USA
Calendulauda africanoides: disjunctly in foothill and montane semiarid savanna, clearings in thornscrub, and open woodland of Ethiopia and northern Somalia southward to eastern Uganda, Kenya, and northern Tanzania, and from southeastern Angola and Namibia to northeastern South Africa
Calendulauda albescens: lowland Karoo scrub, arid fynbos and coastal strandveld, in South Africa (from northwestern Northern Cape southward to Western Cape, and eastward to western Eastern Cape)
Calendulauda burra: lowland and foothill Karoo and vegetated dunes in west-central South Africa (northwestern Northern Cape)
Calendulauda erythrochlamys: lowland sandy plains, grassy dunes, and Namib Desert dunes, from coastal and western Namibia southward to northwestern South Africa
Calendulauda gilletti: lowland to montane semiarid savanna and rocky scrub of eastern Ethiopia, Somalia, and far northeastern Kenya
Calendulauda poecilosterna: lowland to foothill arid acacia scrub, and sandy savanna with ground cover, from southeastern South Sudan and southern Ethiopia eastward to southern Somalia, and southward through Kenya to northeastern Tanzania
Calendulauda rufa: patchy in lowland and foothill arid savanna and open rocky woodland of eastern Mali and western Niger eastward to southern Sudan
Calendulauda sabota: lowland and foothill acacia savanna, grassy Karoo, and mopane woodland, from northwestern Angola (Cabinda) and northern Namibia southward to eastern South Africa and Eswatini
Calherodius leuconotus: forested wetlands from Senegal eastward locally to central Ethiopia, and southward to northern Namibia and southern South Africa
Calidris acuminata: breeds low Arctic tundra from Lena to Kolyma rivers (northeastern Siberia); winters from Wallacea eastward through Australasia; prone to extreme vagrancy
Calidris alba: breeds high Arctic tundra wetlands of Holarctic from northwestern and southeastern Greenland, Svalbard (north of Norway), north Taymyr Peninsula and Severnaya Zemlya (to the north), Lena Delta, and New Siberian Islands (north-central Siberia), Alaskan North Slope (rare), Canadian Arctic islands from Banks to Ellesmere and south to Southampton; winters sandy coastal beaches worldwide from temperate to tropical zone, in Old World from the British Isles and Atlantic islands through Africa, Malagasy region, Middle East, southern Asia through Indonesian Archipelago to Australia, Melanesia, Philippines, and southern and central Japan (but rare New Guinea and New Zealand); in New World, southwestern and southeastern Canada and Caribbean southward to Tierra del Fuego, and including remote islands of eastern Polynesia
Calidris alpina: breeds low (locally high) Arctic to temperate wet tundra of Holarctic, from southwestern and northeastern Greenland, Iceland, Faroe Islands, northern British Isles, Scandinavia, Baltic region east through northern Russia including Novaya Zemlya (north of northwestern Siberia) and New Siberian Islands (north of east-central Russia), through Chukotskiy Peninsula, western Kamchatka, northern Kurile and northern Sakhalin islands (eastern Russia); Aleutians, western and northern Alaska and northwestern Canada, and north-central Canada north and west of Hudson Bay; winters coastal and inland wetlands from temperate to tropical zones mainly north of Equator, from British Isles, western Europe, Mediterranean, northern and north-central Africa, Middle East, and northern plains of India to northern Vietnam and eastern China, Taiwan, Korean Peninsula, and Japan (Honshu to Ryukyu Islands); southwestern Canada and New England to west-central Mexico and Yucatan Peninsula
Calidris bairdii: breeds high Arctic dry tundra from Wrangel Island to eastern Chukotskiy Peninsula (northeastern Siberia) through northern and central Alaska, northern Canada including Arctic islands from Banks to Ellesmere and Baffin islands, and northwestern Greenland; winters in mountains and coastally from southern Peru through Chile and southern Argentina
Calidris canutus: breeds patchily in high Arctic (mainly) tundra of Holarctic from northwestern and eastern Greenland, north-central Siberia, islands north of north-central and northeastern Siberia, and northern Chukotskiy Peninsula (northeastern Siberia); winters coasts worldwide from temperate zone to tropics; in Indian Ocean mainly western Australia, and in Pacific in New Zealand but rare on other remote islands
Calidris falcinellus: breeds patchily in low Arctic to subarctic tundra bogs of northern Palearctic from Scandinavia to Kanin Peninsula (northwestern Russia); Taimyr Peninsula (northwestern Siberia) and Lena to Kolyma rivers (northeastern Siberia); winters Paleotropical coasts from eastern Africa, Red Sea, and Persian Gulf through southeastern Asia, Indonesian Archipelago, southern New Guinea, and Australia (except south and Tasmania)
Calidris ferruginea: breeds drier tundra from Yamal Peninsula to northwestern Chukotskiy Peninsula (northwestern to northeastern Siberia), including New Siberian Islands; winters southern Europe and Africa eastward through southern Asia to Taiwan and Philippines and southward to Melanesia; prone to extreme vagrancy
Calidris fuscicollis: breeds wet tundra from North Slope of Alaska eastward in coastal northern Canada to northwestern Hudson Bay, and Banks to Devon and Baffin islands (northeastern Canada); winters to wetlands of southern Chile, southeastern Brazil, northwestern to southeastern Argentina, and Falkland Islands
Calidris himantopus: breeds tundra to taiga edge of North Slope of Alaska eastward to north-central Canada; winters Mexico and throughout the Caribbean; in Central America mainly along Pacific coast; coastal South America to Peru and northern Brazil, and in pampas of north-central Argentina
Calidris maritima: breeds montane tundra from Greenland and Iceland eastward through Arctic Europe and Russia to Taymyr Peninsula (north-central Siberia), also Banks to southern Ellesmere and Baffin islands (north-central Canada); winters rocky North Atlantic coasts from Iceland and Faroe Islands to western Europe, and Labrador and Gulf of St. Lawrence (southeastern Canada) southward to North Carolina
Calidris mauri: breeds Chukotskiy Peninsula and Anadyr (northeastern Siberia; few), St. Lawrence Island (Bering Sea), and western and northern Alaska mainland; winters coastal Washington to Peru and Galapagos, southeastern Canada to Caribbean, and inland central Mexico to northern Costa Rica
Calidris melanotos: breeds wet tundra from Yamal Peninsula eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula (northwestern to eastern Siberia), including New Siberian and Wrangel islands, also western and northern Alaska eastward through northeastern Canada, including Arctic islands; winters wet grassland and wetland edge mainly to Peru, Bolivia, and southern Brazil southward to Tierra del Fuego; prone to extreme vagrancy
Calidris minuta: breeds drier tundra from northern Scandinavia eastward through northern Russia to New Siberian Islands (east-central Siberia); winters mudflats and marshes from southern Europe and Africa eastward to southern Asia and southern Japan
Calidris minutilla: breeds tundra and taiga wetlands from eastern Aleutian Is through Alaska and Canada eastward to Labrador and Nova Scotia; winters mudflats and wetlands from southeastern USA, Caribbean, and Mexico southward to northern South America
Calidris ptilocnemis: breeds coastal low Arctic to subarctic tundra of far northern Pacific from eastern Chukotskiy Peninsula to (disjunctly) southern Kamchatka, Commander and (perhaps) northern Kuril islands (eastern Russia), Aleutian and Bering Sea islands, western Alaska from Seward Peninsula to Gulf of Alaska islands; winters rocky subarctic to temperate coasts to Hokkaido (northern Japan) and central California
Calidris pugnax: breeds tundra and steppe of northwestern Europe from Scandinavia southward to northern Ukraine and eastward to far eastern Siberia; winters from central Europe southward through Africa, eastward through southern Asia to central Japan southward to Philippines
Calidris pusilla: breeds tundra from eastern Chukotskiy Peninsula (northeastern Siberia) through northern Alaska and eastward in northern Canada to northern Labrador, including southern Canadian Arctic islands from Banks to Baffin; winters coasts from Isthmus of Tehuantepec and Yucatan Peninsula (southwestern Mexico) and Caribbean to far northern Chile and northeastern Brazil
Calidris pygmaea: breeds coastal tundra of eastern Chukotskiy Peninsula to northern Kamchatka (northeastern Russia); winters coastal mudflats from Taiwan and east-central China to Bangladesh; mainly Thailand, Myanmar, and Bangladesh; rare and local
Calidris ruficollis: breeds coastal tundra of Taymyr Peninsula eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula and northern Kamchatka Peninsula (north-central to north-eastern Siberia); winters coastal northeastern India and Sri Lanka eastward to southern Japan (Ryukyu Islands), Philippines, Australasia, and Melanesia
Calidris subminuta: breeds subarctic to temperate bogs of disjunctly in Chukotskiy Peninsula, northern Kuril and Commander islands (eastern Russia) and (perhaps) northern Mongolia; winters eastern India and Sri Lanka eastward through southern Asia to southern Japan (Ryukyu Islands) and southward to southeastern Australia
Calidris subruficollis: breeds high Arctic dry coastal tundra from Wrangel Island (northeastern Siberia) eastward through Alaskan North Slope to northeastern Canada, including Arctic islands from Banks to Devon; migrates to grassland of southeastern Brazil and Uruguay to central Argentina; prone to extreme vagrancy worldwide
Calidris temminckii: breeds tundra of Scandinavia eastward through northern Russia to Chukotskiy Peninsula (northeastern Russia), including New Siberian Islands; winters southeastern Europe southward to central Africa and eastward to central and southern Japan and Taiwan
Calidris tenuirostris: breeds montane tundra of northeastern Siberia from Yakutsk eastward to Anadyr Peninsula; winters coasts from northeastern Arabian Peninsula eastward to Taiwan, Philippines, and Australia
Calidris virgata: breeds montane tundra of Alaska mainland (except far northern) and Yukon (northwestern Canada); winters rocky coasts from southeastern Alaska to Tierra del Fuego
Caliechthrus leucolophus: New Guinea, including Salawati (Raja Ampat Islands, off western New Guinea)
Caligavis obscura: patchily in hills of New Guinea
Callacanthis burtoni: Himalayas from northwestern Pakistan eastward to Nepal and rarely Sikkim
Callaeas cinereus: formerly South Island, New Zealand; probably extinct, last confirmed sighting 1967
Callaeas wilsoni: North and Great Barrier islands (New Zealand)
Calliope calliope: Ural Mountains eastward to Kamchatka and Commander and Kuril islands, in south to northern Mongolia and northern Japan; also central China (northeastern Qinghai, southwestern Gansu, and northern Sichuan); winters in southeastern Asia, Taiwan, and Philippines
Calliope obscura: west-central China (southeastern Gansu, southwestern Shaanxi, northern Sichuan, and northern Yunnan)
Calliope pectardens: breeds mountains of southeastern Tibet to west-central China; winters to northeastern Myanmar
Calliope pectoralis: montane open scrub and scree above tree-line, dwarf rhododendron thickets, and meadows with willow or juniper scrub, from eastern Kazakhstan and northwestern China southward to northern Pakistan, thence eastward through Himalayas to Sikkim (India); migrates to Himalayan foothills of Pakistan, India, and Nepal
Calliope tschebaiewi: breeds eastern Ladakh to northwestern China (Gansu), southeastern Tibet, and far northern Myanmar; winters in foothills from eastern Nepal to northeastern India, northeastern Bangladesh, northern Myanmar, and southern Yunnan
Callipepla californica: Oregon to southern Baja California (western USA to northwestern Mexico); introduced to Corsica, King and Norfolk islands (Australia), New Zealand (North and South islands), Hawaiian Islands (Molokai, Maui, Hawaii), far southwestern Canada, northwestern USA, and central Chile and west-central Argentina
Callipepla douglasii: arid scrub of lowlands to foothills on Pacific slope from northern Sonora to northwestern Jalisco (northwestern to west-central Mexico); Tres Marias Islands (west of Nayarit)
Callipepla gambelii: desert typically with mesquite in lowlands and hills from southeastern California and western Colorado (southwestern USA) to central Sinaloa and far northern Chihuahua (northwestern Mexico); introduced Hawaiian Islands (Lanai, Kaho'olawe, and Hawaii)
Callipepla squamata: desert grassland and scrub of hills to mountains from southeastern Utah to southwestern Kansas (central USA) southward on central plateau of Mexico to Hidalgo
Calliphlox amethystina: widespread tropical South America to northeastern Argentina and southern Brazil
Callocephalon fimbriatum: coastal southeastern Australia (central New South Wales to southeastern South Australia)
Callonetta leucophrys: southern Brazil, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
Calochaetes coccineus: Andes of southeastern Colombia to Ecuador and eastern Peru (Cusco)
Caloenas maculata: known only from two specimens (one of which now is lost) and one illustration; probably was native to an island or island group in the South Pacific; extinct
Caloenas nicobarica: Andaman and Nicobar islands to Philippines, Indonesian Archipelago, New Guinea satellite islands, Bismarck Archipelago, Solomon Archipelago, and Palau (western Caroline Islands, western Micronesia)
Calonectris borealis: eastern Atlantic, breeding from Azores southward to Canary Islands and eastward to Galicia (northwestern Spain) and Berlengas Islands (off west-central Portugal); ranges widely in Atlantic, but mainly in upwelling systems of the Benguela and Agulhas currents
Calonectris diomedea: breeds Mediterranean islands and southwestern France; ranges mainly in upwelling systems of tropical eastern Atlantic
Calonectris edwardsii: breeds Cabo Verde; ranges mainly in upwelling systems of tropical and South Atlantic
Calonectris leucomelas: breeds coastal islands from Russian Far East, Korean Peninsula, and Japan to islands off western Taiwan; ranges western Pacific to Philippines, Indonesia, and northern Australia eastward through Melanesia to Micronesia
Caloperdix oculeus: forest of lowlands to hills from southeastern Myanmar and southwestern Thailand southward through Peninsular Malaysia (to Pahang), Sumatra, and north-central and northeastern Borneo
Calothorax lucifer: arid mountains of southwestern USA and northern Mexico; winters to southern Mexico
Calothorax pulcher: arid scrub of southern Mexico (Guerrero and southern Puebla to eastern Oaxaca)
Calypte anna: breeds southwestern Alaska to northwestern Baja California (northwestern Mexico); winters to northern Mexico
Calypte costae: breeds arid southwestern USA to southern Baja California and northwestern Mexico; withdraws from south-central USA in winter and reaches west-central Mexico
Calyptocichla serinus: patchy in lowland to foothill primary and secondary forest, forest edge, plantations, and abandoned cultivation, from Sierra Leone eastward through southern Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and southward to Cabinda (northwestern Angola) and far western Democratic Republic of the Congo
Calyptomena hosii: patchily distributed submontane forest of northern and central Borneo
Calyptomena viridis: tropical rainforest in the Malayan Peninsula from southern Myanmar (Tenasserim) and Peninsular Thailand southward to Singapore, Sumatra (including Nias and Batu and Mentawai islands), Riau Islands, and Borneo
Calyptomena whiteheadi: montane forest of northern and central Borneo
Calyptophilus frugivorus: Gonâve (just off western Haiti) and central and southwestern Dominican Republic (Hispaniola)
Calyptophilus tertius: mountains of southern Haiti and far southwestern Dominican Republic (western Sierra de Bahorucos)
Calyptura cristata: southeastern Brazil (Rio de Janeiro area); undocumented since 1860 and probably extinct
Camarhynchus heliobates: mangroves on northwest coast of Isabela (western Galapagos); restricted to very small area, formerly also on eastern coast of Isabela, and on Fernandina
Camarhynchus pallidus: mostly forested areas at higher elevations on main Galapagos Islands (except Marchena and Genovesa in far northeast and Espanola in far southeast)
Camarhynchus parvulus: mostly highland forest of main Galapagos Islands (except Pinta to Genovesa in north and Espanola in the far southeast)
Camarhynchus psittacula: highland forest of main Galapagos Islands (except Espanola, in the far southeast)
Camaroptera brachyura: lowland to montane forest understory, riparian thickets, savanna woodland, and gardens, widespread throughout sub-Saharan Africa, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to coastal Sudan and Somalia, and southward to northern Namibia and southern South Africa
Camaroptera chloronota: lowland to montane understory of primary and secondary forest from Sierra Leone and southern Guinea eastward through southern Nigeria and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to southern South Sudan and western Kenya, and southward to western and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and far northwestern Tanzania
Camaroptera harterti: lowland and foothill understory of primary and secondary forest, and thickets in old coffee plantations, in northwestern Angola
Camaroptera superciliaris: lowland to foothill forest edge, gallery forest, secondary growth, farmbush, and plantations, from southern Guinea and Sierra Leone eastward through southern Nigeria and southern Central African Republic to western Uganda, and southward to northwestern Angola and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Campephaga flava: lowland to foothill woodland, including acacia, miombo, mopane, and riparian woodland, gardens, and plantations, from South Sudan and southern Ethiopia southward, avoiding rainforest and desert, through southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Angola, Zimbabwe, and Mozambique, to eastern and coastal South Africa; nomadic seasonal dispersals
Campephaga petiti: disjunctly in lowland to submontane primary and secondary forest, logged forest with dense understory, and forest patches in savanna, from southeastern Nigeria and southwestern Cameroon, from southern Gabon to northwestern Angola, and from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, adjacent southwestern Uganda, and western Kenya
Campephaga phoenicea: lowland to foothill wooded grassland, forest patches and edge, gallery forest, juniper woodland, and thickets in savanna, from Senegambia eastward to Eritrea and Ethiopia, and southward, avoiding rainforest, to southern Cameroon, northern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and western Kenya; retracts from expanded breeding range to core resident areas post-breeding
Campephaga quiscalina: patchy in lowland to montane forest, wooded savanna, and plantations, from Sierra Leone and southern Guinea eastward to southern South Sudan, and western Kenya, and southward to northern Angola and eastern Tanzanian highlands
Campephilus gayaquilensis: arid Pacific lowlands of southwestern Colombia to northwestern Peru (Cajamarca)
Campephilus guatemalensis: mostly humid lowland forest and edge from southern Sonora, central Nuevo León, and central Tamaulipas (northern Mexico) southward on Pacific and Caribbean slopes through Mexico including Yucatan Peninsula (but not Cozumel) to western Panama
Campephilus haematogaster: humid forest east of the Andes in eastern Colombia to eastern Peru and far western Bolivia (western La Paz)
Campephilus imperialis: Sierra Madre Occidental of western Mexico; probably extinct
Campephilus leucopogon: dry woodland of north-central Bolivia to northern Argentina and southeastern Brazil
Campephilus magellanicus: Nothofagus forest of southwestern Argentina and southern Chile
Campephilus melanoleucos: humid forest from eastern Panama and northern Colombia southward along the Cauca and Magdalena valleys (to Cauca and Tolima), and west of the Andes southward to the Río Patía (Cauca), east of the Andes from northern Venezuela, Trinidad, and the Guianas southward across the Orinoco and Amazon basins to eastern Bolivia, eastern Paraguay, and far northern Argentina (Corrientes), and locally in eastern Brazil (Sergipe, Bahia, and São Paulo)
Campephilus pollens: montane cloudforest in the Andes from far western Venezuela, excluding the Sierra de Perijá, southwestward along the western, central and eastern Andes of Colombia to southwestern Ecuador, and along the eastern Andes of Ecuador southward to south-central Peru, in Junín
Campephilus principalis: at least formerly in mixed woodland and forest in the Mississippi River basin in southern Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Missouri, Oklahoma, Alabama, Tennessee, Louisiana, eastern Texas eastward to the Coastal Plains, and from North Carolina southward to southern Florida; also in the eastern part of Cuba; may be extinct
Campephilus robustus: lowlands of southeastern Brazil to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina (Misiones)
Campephilus rubricollis: tropical rainforest in the Guiana Shield and the Orinoco basin from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward across the Amazon basin to central Bolivia and central Brazil, in western Goiás and southern Mato Grosso
Campephilus splendens: humid forest of central Panama to western Ecuador
Campethera abingoni: patchy in lowland and foothill open woodland, brushy savanna, thickets, and coastal forest, from Senegambia and southern Mali eastward to southern South Sudan and southwestern Kenya, and southward to eastern Namibia and eastern South Africa
Campethera bennettii: lowland to foothill arid acacia brushy woodland, and miombo and gusu (Baikiaea) woodland, from central Angola through eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to eastern Tanzania, and southward to northeastern Namibia and northeastern South Africa
Campethera maculosa: lowland and foothill forest and forest edge, riparian and miombo woodland, and thornscrub savanna, from Senegal and Guinea-Bissau eastward to southwestern Ethiopia, and southward to northern Angola and Mozambique
Campethera mombassica: southern Somalia to coastal Kenya and northeastern Tanzania
Campethera notata: coastal southern South Africa (Western Cape eastward to far southern KwaZulu-Natal)
Campethera nubica: lowland to montane bushy grassland, acacia savanna, and riverine woodland, from southern Sudan, Ethiopia, and Somalia, southward to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and central Tanzania
Campethera punctuligera: lowland wooded savanna, and acacia grassland with scattered trees, from southwestern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward through southern Chad to southwestern Sudan, western South Sudan, and southward to Central African Republic and northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Campethera scriptoricauda: central and eastern Tanzania to southeastern Malawi and northern Mozambique
Campethera taeniolaema: foothill and montane forest from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to southwestern Kenya, and southward to Burundi and far western and northern Tanzania
Campethera tullbergi: mountains of southeastern Nigeria and western Cameroon; Bioko Island
Campicoloides bifasciatus: lowland to submontane boulder-strewn hills and escarpments with scattered bushes and trees, in eastern South Africa, Lesotho, and Eswatini
Campocolinus albogularis: scrub and disturbed savanna of lowlands from Senegal eastward to northern Cameroon; disjunctly, local in eastern Angola, northwestern Zambia, and southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Campocolinus coqui: grassland and woodland of lowlands and hills in Sahel, East Africa, and south-central to southern Africa, from southern Mauritania eastward to southern Nigeria and southward to Angola; central Ethiopia through eastern Africa southward to eastern and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, thence west to northern Namibia and southeastward to KwaZulu-Natal
Campocolinus schlegelii: Cameroon, southern Chad, northern Central African Republic, far southwestern Sudan and northwestern South Sudan
Camptorhynchus labradorius: formerly coastal northeastern North America; extinct, last reported 1875
Camptostoma caucae: Colombia (western Andes, and Cauca and Magdalena valleys)
Camptostoma flaviventre: Pacific coast of southwestern Costa Rica and Panama (including Coiba, Cébaco, and Pearl islands)
Camptostoma imberbe: southeastern Arizona to southern Texas, western Mexico, and northern Costa Rica; Cozumel
Camptostoma napaeum: Amazon basin, from southeastern Colombia eastward to the Guianas and Amapá, and southward to northeastern Peru, northern Bolivia, and western Brazil (western Amazonas)
Camptostoma obsoletum: far southeastern Peru and west-central Bolivia eastward to central and eastern Brazil, and southward to north-central Argentina and Uruguay
Camptostoma pusillum: Caribbean coast of northern Colombia, northern Venezuela, and Trinidad
Camptostoma sclateri: tropical western Ecuador and western Peru (southward to Lima), including (middle Marañón Valley)
Campylopterus calcirupicola: eastern Brazil (southeastern Goiás, southwestern Bahia, and northern Minas Gerais)
Campylopterus diamantinensis: southeastern Brazil (Serra Espinhaço in Minas Gerais)
Campylopterus duidae: tepuis of southern Venezuela and adjacent northern Brazil
Campylopterus ensipennis: mountains of northeastern Venezuela and Tobago
Campylopterus falcatus: mountains of Colombia, Venezuela, and eastern Ecuador
Campylopterus hemileucurus: montane forest and edge from central Veracruz on Caribbean slope and Guerrero on Pacific slope (central Mexico) southward through southern Mexico (except Yucatan Peninsula) through central Panama; some non-breeding movement to lower elevations
Campylopterus hyperythrus: tepuis of southeastern Venezuela and adjacent northwestern Brazil

Campylorhynchus gularis: oak-pine woodland of western and central Mexico

Campylorhynchus jocosus: arid oak-pine forest of southern Mexican plateau
Campylorhynchus megalopterus: pine-oak montane forest from eastern Jalisco through central Oaxaca
Campylorhynchus nuchalis: drier woodland and scrub of lowlands of northern Colombia and northern Venezuela eastward to Paría Peninsula
Campylorhynchus turdinus: disjunctly in tropical rainforest and borders in the Amazon basin of southeastern Colombia southward to Paraguay and northeastern Argentina (to Entre Rios), in Brazil widespread mostly south of the Amazon River eastward to wetern Maranhão, southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul, and the east-central Atlantic Forest of Brazil (southern Bahia southward to Espírito Santo)
Campylorhynchus yucatanicus: arid coastal lowlands of southeastern Mexico (northern Yucatan Peninsula)
Campylorhynchus zonatus: forest and edge from lowlands to mountains on Caribbean slope from southern Tamaulipas in east-central Mexico southward through Mexico (except Yucatan Peninsula) eastward through central Belize to southwestern Nicaragua, locally to Pacific slope; disjunctly on Caribbean slope from northwestern Costa Rica to western Panama, northern and central Colombia, and northwestern to west-central Ecuador
Canachites canadensis: coniferous forest from northern Alaska eastward across most Canada to Newfoundland and Labrador, and southward to northern US, in the west southward in the Rocky Mountains to northeastern Oregon and central Idaho, and in the east southward to northern Wisconsin, northern Michigan, and New York (formerly)
Canirallus oculeus: rainforest of Sierra Leone to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Uganda
Cantorchilus elutus: southwestern Costa Rica and Pacific slope of Panama (eastward to Panamá Province); also Caribbean slope of central Panama
Cantorchilus guarayanus: northern Bolivia, adjacent southwestern Brazil (southwestern Mato Grosso), and Paraguay
Cantorchilus leucopogon: forest edge in lowlands on both slopes of central Panama to north-central Colombia and, west of Andes, southward to west-central Ecuador
Cantorchilus leucotis: humid forest, thickets, gallery forest, and varzea from western Panama, including the Pearl Islands, eastward to northern Colombia and western Venezuela, southward in the Magdalena Valley, east of the Andes throughout the Orinoco and Amazon basins, Guiana Shield, and Cerrado from northern Venezuela southward to northern Bolivia, northeastern Paraguay, and Cerrado of Maranhão southward to Mato Grosso do Sul
Cantorchilus longirostris: forest edge, Caatinga, and mangroves of lowlands from Piauí eastward to northeastern Brazil and southward through Maranhão to Santa Catarina
Cantorchilus modestus: southern Mexico (Oaxaca) southward on the Pacific slope to northwestern Costa Rica; locally on the Caribbean slope from southern Mexico (Chiapas) to Honduras
Cantorchilus nigricapillus: humid forest edge near water in lowlands to hills on Caribbean slope from northern Honduras (rare), eastern Nicaragua to central Panama, thence both slopes eastward to north-central Colombia and southward west of Andes to southwestern Ecuador
Cantorchilus semibadius: Pacific lowlands of southwestern Costa Rica and far western Panama
Cantorchilus superciliaris: dry woodland and scrub of lowlands to hills from Manabí in west-central Ecuador through Ancash in northwestern Peru
Cantorchilus thoracicus: Caribbean lowlands of eastern Nicaragua to western Panama
Cantorchilus zeledoni: eastern Nicaragua to eastern Costa Rica and northwestern Panama (western Bocas del Toro)

Capito aurovirens: southeastern Colombia to eastern Peru and western Amazonian Brazil (east to Rio Negro)
Capito brunneipectus: Brazil south of the Amazon between lower Rio Madeira and Rio Tapajós

Capito niger: eastern Venezuela, the Guianas, and northeastern Brazil north of the Amazon
Capito quinticolor: western Colombia (Chocó) to far northwestern Ecuador (Esmeraldas)
Capito squamatus: far southwestern Colombia (southeastern Nariño) and western Ecuador (south to El Oro)
Capito wallacei: northern Peru: very local on ridge crests of Cordillera Azul (eastern San Martín and southwestern Loreto)

Caprimulgus concretus: lowlands of Sumatra, Belitung (off southeastern Sumatra), and Borneo

Caprimulgus longipennis: in breeding season from Senegambia to Liberia, eastward to southwestern South Sudan, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northwestern Uganda (present during the season in southern portion of this region, but breeding there not confirmed); winters north and east from southern Mauritania and northern Sengeal eastward to central Chad, southern Sudan, eastern South Sudan, central Uganda, Eritrea, western Ethiopia, and western Kenya
Caprimulgus macrurus: lowland to foothill open woodland, scrub, bamboo thickets, savanna, and villages, from northeastern Pakistan eastward through Himalayan foothills to southern China (including Hainan), and northern Vietnam, southward to eastern India, Greater Sundas, Palawan (southwestern Philippines), and eastward to New Guinea, Bismarck Archipelago, and northeastern Australia; some northern populations migratory
Caprimulgus mahrattensis: southeastern Iran to southern Afghanistan, Pakistan, and northwestern India
Caprimulgus natalensis: very patchy in lowland and foothill wet grassland adjacent to swamps, floodplain meadows, and bogs and dambos, from Gambia and Mali eastward to South Sudan and western Ethiopia, and southward through eastern Angola to southeastern South Africa

Caprimulgus prigoginei: known with certainty only from single specimen from eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (Itombwe Mountains)
Caprimulgus ritae: Timor, Rote, and Wetar (eastern Lesser Sundas)
Caprimulgus ruficollis: lowland to foothill open woodland, pine woodland, open scrub, thickets, and semi-desert, from Spain and Portugal southward to northern Morocco and eastward to northern Tunisia; winters in western Africa from Morocco southward to Senegambia, and eastward to Mali
Caprimulgus rufigena: lowland and foothill wooded savanna, miombo woodland, acacia thornscrub, and semi-desert, breeding from central Angola eastward to Zimbabwe, and southward through eastern Namibia and Botswana to southern South Africa; entire population migrates toward western equatorial Africa, wintering mostly in Cameroon and Nigeria

Caprimulgus stellatus: southern South Sudan, Ethiopia (and northern Somalia?), and northern Kenya
Caprimulgus tristigma: very patchy across sub-Saharan Africa in lowland to submontane rocky terrain, kopjes and inselbergs, and wooded escarpments in miombo and mopane woodland, from southern Senegal, Mali, and Guinea eastward to Ethiopia, and southward (avoiding rainforest) to southern South Africa

Cardellina versicolor: mountains of far southern Mexico (Chiapas) to Guatemala

Carpococcyx viridis: lowlands and foothills of southwestern Sumatra (Basiran Mountains)

Carpodacus rodochroa: Himalayan fir and birch forest from Kashmir to southern Tibet

Carpodacus thura: subalpine forest and alpine scrub of northeastern Afghanistan through Himalayas from northern Pakistan through western Arunachal Pradesh and adjacent southern and southeastern Tibet; some altitudinal movement in winter

Carpodectes hopkei: humid lowlands of eastern Panama to western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador
Carpodectes nitidus: Caribbean slope of northern Honduras to far western Panama

Carpospiza brachydactyla: arid Türkiye; winters to southwestern Arabia and northeastern Africa
Carterornis castus: Tanimbar Islands (Larat, Yamdena, and Selaru); Tayandu Islands (Kilsuin)
