Carterornis pileatus: Halmahera and Buru (northern and west-central Moluccas)
Caryothraustes canadensis: humid forest and borders in Cerro Pirre of easternmost Panama and in the Guiana Shield and Orinoco basin from eastern and southern Venezuela, easternmost Colombia, and the Guianas southward to the Amazon basin of northeastern Brazil, to eastern Amazonas and eastward to northeastern Brazil in Maranhão and western Piaui; also in the Atlantic Forest from northeastern Brazil (Pernambuco southward to Rio de Janeiro)
Caryothraustes poliogaster: forest and edge of lowlands and foothills of Caribbean slope from central Veracruz and northern Oaxaca (southeastern Mexico) southward (including eastern Yucatan Peninsula) through central Panama
Casiornis fuscus: Caatinga and scrub of northeastern Brazil
Casiornis rufus: southeastern Peru to eastern Bolivia, Paraguay, northern Argentina, and Amazonian and eastern Brazil
Cassiculus melanicterus: Pacific lowlands of western Mexico (southeastern Sonora) to southeastern Guatemala and northwestern El Salvador

Casuarius bennetti: New Guinea, including Yapen (Cenderawasih Bay, off northwestern New Guinea), and New Britain

Cathartes aura: breeds southern Canada through Greeater Antilles and South America to Tierra del Fuego and Falkland Islands
Cathartes burrovianus: southern Mexico southward to Argentina and Brazil (east of the Andes)
Cathartes melambrotus: the Guianas and southern Venezuela to northern Bolivia and northern Brazil

Catharus dryas: humid montane forest from southeastern Oaxaca (southeastern Mexico) to northwestern Nicaragua
Catharus frantzii: montane forest and edge from Jalisco and southern San Luis Potosí (north-central Mexico) to northern Nicaragua, then northern Costa Rica to far western Panama

Catharus gracilirostris: high montane forest and edge from north-central Costa Rica to western Panama
Catharus guttatus: breeds in varied coniferous, mixed and deciduous forests, and woodland from western Alaska eastward to southern Labrador (eastern Canada) and northeastern USA, southward in mountains of western USA to southern California, with an isolated population in northern Baja California (northwestern Mexico), and far southwestern Texas, and in the Appalachian Mountains southward to North Carolina (local); winters from coastal southwestern Canada southward to Baja California, across southern half of the USA southward to central Guatemala, southern Florida, and the Bahamas (scarce)
Catharus maculatus: humid forest in foothills and mountains from Lara in Andes of west-central Venezuela and Sierra de Perijá of western border with Colombia, westward and southward through eastern Andes to Ecuador on both slopes, and thence east slope only from Peru through Tucuman in northwestern Argentina
Catharus mexicanus: humid montane forest on Caribbean slope from central Nuevo León and central Tamaulipas (including Sierra de las Tuxtlas, eastern Veracruz) southward through northern Nicaragua, then northern Costa Rica on both slopes through central Panama
Catharus minimus: breeds in riparian woodland and thickets, and open woodland with shrubs in Chukotskiy Peninsula and Anadyrland (northeastern Siberia), northern Alaska eastward to Labrador (eastern Canada), and southward to central Canada; winters in humid forest of northern Andes and northwestern Amazonia, mainly from western Venezuela southward to northeastern Peru
Catharus occidentalis: montane forest from west-central Chihuahua and southwestern Nuevo León and transvolcanic belt southward to southern Oaxaca
Catharus ustulatus: breeds in coniferous forest, riparian and deciduous woodland, and thickets from central Alaska eastward to southern Labrador (eastern Canada), in western USA along the Pacific coast southward to southern California and in the Rocky Mountains to northern New Mexico, and in northeastern USA to southern New York and northern Pennsylvania; winters in varied lowland and montane forest and edge, mostly in Chiapas and Guatemala and the Andes southward to northwestern Argentina, with some on the Pacific and Gulf of Mexico slopes from northeastern and west-central Mexico through Central America
Catherpes mexicanus: steep cliffs, canyons, rocky outcrops, and villages (in Mexico) from south-central British Columbia (southwestern Canada) southward to southern Baja California, eastern Chiapas (southern Mexico), and eastward to southwestern South Dakota and central Texas (central USA)
Catreus wallichii: montane forest of eastern Afghanistan to central Nepal
Catriscus brevirostris: patchy in foothill and montane wet grassland, and sedge meadows, of Sierra Leone and adjacent Guinea, southeastern Nigeria and Cameroon, and highlands of South Sudan and western Ethiopia, and from southern Gabon eastward through northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to western and southern Kenya, and southward to western Angola and eastern South Africa, Eswatini, and Lesotho; southern highland populations migratory after breeding
Ceblepyris caesius: disjunctly in lowland to montane forest of southeastern Nigeria, southwestern Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), and of Ethiopia, southern South Sudan, and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo southward through eastern Tanzania to southern South Africa; post-breeding downslope altitudinal migrant
Ceblepyris graueri: patchy in foothill forest of western Albertine Rift Mountains of eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Ceblepyris pectoralis: lowland to foothill broadleaf forest, including miombo and mopane woodland, savanna woodland, and acacia groves, from Senegambia eastward to southern Sudan and eastern Ethiopia, and southward, avoiding rainforest, to northeastern Namibia, northern Botswana, Mozambique, and northeastern South Africa; some seasonal wandering
Cecropis abyssinica: lowland to foothill grassland, savanna, open woodland, cultivation and villages, from Senegambia eastward to Eritrea, Ethiopia, and western Somalia, thence southward to eastern and southern South Africa (avoiding Namib and Kalahari deserts); northwestern and southern populations migrate to tropics after breeding season
Cecropis cucullata: lowlands to submontane semiarid karoo, open grassland, cultivation, and human habitation, breeding from central Angola and southern Zimbabwe southward to South Africa, Lesotho, and Eswatini; migrates northward to south-central and southeastern Africa
Cecropis daurica: lowland to montane open habitats, including wetlands, cliffs, forest clearings, and villages, breeding from northeastern Kazakhstan eastward to Sakhalin and Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu), and southward to India, Philippines, and Indonesia; northern populations migrate to southern Asia, and as far as northern Australia
Cecropis melanocrissus: lowland to foothill open country, savanna, cultivation, and towns, from Senegambia eastward to Eritrea and Ethiopia, thence southward to Cameroon, northern Zambia, and Malawi; some local migration in non-breeding season
Cecropis rufula: Iberian Peninsula to northern Africa, Iran, Afghanistan, and northwestern India
Cecropis semirufa: lowland to foothill grassland, savanna, scrub, and villages, from Senegambia eastward to Chad, South Sudan, Uganda, and northern Tanzania, thence southward to northern Namibia and eastern South Africa; northern and southern populations migrate to tropics after breeding season
Cecropis senegalensis: lowland to montane grassland, savanna, mopane woodland, and villages, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to Ethiopia, thence southward to northern Namibia, southern Mozambique, and northeastern South Africa; partly migratory locally
Celebesica abbotti: high montane forest of northern, central, and southeastern Sulawesi
Celeus castaneus: Gulf-Caribbean slope of southern Mexico (southern Veracruz) to western Panama
Celeus elegans: tropical rainforest from northern Venezuela, including the Paría Peninsula, Trinidad and the Guianas southwestward across the Río Orinoco and Amazon basins to eastern Colombia, Ecuador and Peru to northern Bolivia; in Amazonian Brazil eastward to northern Maranhão and southward to central and eastern Mato Grosso
Celeus flavescens: gallery forest in the Cerrado of interior Brazil, and humid forest in the Atlantic Forest of coastal Brazil, from southern Piauí, northern Goiás, northern Mato Grosso, and central Bahia southward to southern Paraná, northern Rio Grande do Sul, eastern Paraguay, and northernmost Argentina
Celeus flavus: humid and gallery forest and mangrove in northeastern Venezuela and the Guianas southeastward to northeastern Brazil, and in the Amazon basin from southern Venezuela southward to central Bolivia and to the Brazilian Mato Grosso do Sul; also in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil in Alagoas southward to Espirito Santo
Celeus galeatus: humid forest of southeastern Brazil to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
Celeus loricatus: humid forest and edge of lowlands to foothills on Caribbean slope of eastern Nicaragua to western Panama, thence both slopes to Colombia, extending through much of northwestern Colombia, and southward west of Andes to southern Ecuador
Celeus lugubris: semi-deciduous forest and wooland in the Cerrado and Chaco from northern Bolivia and eastern Bolivia eastward to Mato Grosso, in Brazil, and southward across Mato Grosso do Sul and Paraguay to northern Argentina, southward to northern Santa Fe and western Corrientes
Celeus ochraceus: lower Amazonian Brazil (south of the Amazon River in Pará); northeastern Brazil, from Maranhão southward to northern Goiás and eastward to Ceará, Pernambuco, and western Bahia
Celeus spectabilis: Guadua bamboo and Gynerium cane along lowland rivers of western Amazonia from southwestern Caqueta (south-central Colombia) eastward to western Amazonas (western Brazil) and southward to Cochabamba (central Bolivia)
Celeus torquatus: varied forest types in lowlands and hills of Amazonia, the Guiana Shield, and the Atlantic Forest of Brazil, from eastern Ecuador east through northeastern Venezuela and eastward to Maranhão, in southern to north-central Bolivia and Mato Grosso (central Brazil); disjunctly from Bahia to Espírito Santo
Celeus undatus: tropical rainforest from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to the Amazon basin of eastern Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and northern Bolivia, and in Brazil eastward to northern Paraná and Maranhão and southward to Mato Grosso and Rondônia
Centrocercus minimus: Gunnison Basin of southwestern Colorado and adjacent southeastern Utah
Centrocercus urophasianus: prairies and sage grassland of western Canada to southwestern USA
Centronyx bairdii: breeds Great Plains of North America; winters to southwestern USA and northern Mexico
Centronyx henslowii: breeds tall grassland with forbs, including coastal marshes, in central and eastern USA from southeastern Minnesota eastward to New York State, and very locally in southern Ontario (southeastern Canada), southward to northeastern Oklahoma and Maryland; winters in southern USA, from eastern Texas eastward to southern North Carolina and Florida
Centropus andamanensis: Andaman Islands and adjacent Table, Great and Little Coco islands
Centropus anselli: lowland swamps from southern Cameroon to northwestern Angola and central Democratic Republic of the Congo
Centropus ateralbus: New Ireland and New Britain (eastern Bismarck Archipelago)
Centropus bengalensis: lowland to submontane tall grass and reedbed, marsh, bamboo thickets, open-country scrub, and cultivation, in southwestern India, and from northwestern India eastward to southern China (including Hainan) and Taiwan, and southward through Indonesian Archipelago, and Philippines
Centropus bernsteini: New Guinea including Batanta (Raja Ampat Islands) and Manam
Centropus burchellii: lowland and foothill riverine thickets, marsh, dense bush, and wooded edge to grassland, from southeastern Tanzania, including Mafia Island, southward through Mozambique and Zambezi River corridor to eastern Botswana and southern South Africa
Centropus chalybeus: Biak (Cenderawasih Bay, off northwestern New Guinea)
Centropus chlororhynchos: locally in wet zone of southwestern Sri Lanka
Centropus cupreicaudus: Angola to southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, and Malawi
Centropus grillii: intra-African migrant south of the Sahara
Centropus leucogaster: lowland undergrowth and secondary growth in forest, riparian thickets, dense grass, and swamp edge, disjunctly from southern Senegal and Guinea-Bissau eastward to western Cameroon and southward to western Gabon, and northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and far western Uganda
Centropus melanops: East Visayas and Mindanao group (east-central and southern Philippines)
Centropus menbeki: New Guinea and western satellite islands
Centropus monachus: lowland and foothill marsh, papyrus swamps, riverine thickets, and savanna near water, from Guinea eastward through northeastern Nigeria and adjacent Chad to southern Sudan, Eritrea, and Ethiopia, and southward to northern Angola, central Kenya, and northwestern Tanzania
Centropus phasianinus: lowland tall grassland, swamps, thickets, and mangroves, from Timor-Leste, Kai Islands (Indonesia), and New Guinea lowlands, southward to northern and eastern Australia
Centropus senegalensis: disjunctly in lowland and foothill coarse grass, woodland and riverine thickets, scrub, and parks and gardens, of the Nile River delta of Egypt, and from Senegambia eastward to western Ethiopia and western Somalia, southward to northern Angola and western Kenya, and from southern Democratic Republic of the Congo and central Tanzania southward to northeastern Namibia and far northeastern South Africa; some local movements in populations of arid areas
Centropus sinensis: lowland to foothill grassland, swamps, thickets, bamboo scrub, and mangroves, from eastern Pakistan and India eastward to southern China, and southward through Sri Lanka, southeastern Asia, Palawan (Philippines), Borneo, and Sumatra, to Java, Bali, and Kangean (western Indonesia)
Centropus superciliosus: lowland and foothill marsh, riverine thickets, and tall grass, of southwestern Arabian Peninsula and Socotra, and from Nile Valley of central Sudan, Eritrea, Ethiopia, and western Somalia southward through Tanzania and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo to western and southern Angola, northeastern Namibia and northwestern Mozambique
Centropus violaceus: New Ireland and New Britain (eastern Bismarck Archipelago)
Centropus viridis: Philippines (except Palawan group and southern Sulu Archipelago)
Cephalopterus glabricollis: humid highlands of Costa Rica and western Panama
Cephalopterus ornatus: southern Venezuela to Guyana, northern Bolivia, and Amazonian Brazil
Cephalopterus penduliger: western Andes of southwestern Colombia and western Ecuador (south to El Oro)
Cephalopyrus flammiceps: patchy in submontane to montane conifer and rhododendron forest, broadleaf woodland, and alpine scrub, from northern Pakistan eastward through Himalayas to southeastern China; populations move downslope in winter or migrate to low northern Indian foothills and northern Thailand and adjacent Myanmar
Cepphus carbo: breeds western North Pacific coast from Sea of Okhotsk, southern Kamchatka, Sakhalin, Kuril Islands (eastern Russia), Hokkaido (northern Japan), and perhaps northeastern Korean Peninsula; winters to central Japan and southern Korean Peninsula
Cepphus columba: arctic to temperate northwestern to east-central North Pacific coasts, from southern Chukotka to Kamchatka, Kuril and Commander islands (eastern Russia), Bering Sea Islands and Aleutians, and Gulf of Alaska to southern California; some withdrawal from north in winter
Cepphus grylle: breeds coasts of high Arctic to north temperate North Atlantic and Arctic Ocean from Greenland, Iceland, northern British Isles east through northeastern Russia; north slope of Alaska, eastern Canada including Hudson Bay; winters to ice-free waters near breeding range
Ceratogymna atrata: patchily distributed forest of western and central Africa; Bioko Island
Ceratogymna elata: patchily distributed forest of Senegambia to Cameroon
Ceratopipra chloromeros: lowlands and foothills of eastern Peru, adjacent western Brazil, and northern Bolivia
Ceratopipra cornuta: tepuis of southern Venezuela, western Guyana, and far northern Brazil
Ceratopipra erythrocephala: tropical rainforest and humid foothill forest from eastern Panama, northern Colombia, and western Venezuela southward in interior Colombia to the middle Cauca and Magdalena valleys, in western Colombia southward to the Serrania de Baudo (Choco), east of the Andes in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela, Trinidad, and the Guianas southward to the northern Amazon basin in Brazil (north of the Amazon River), and in the western Amazon southward to northeastern Peru
Ceratopipra mentalis: humid forest and edge of lowlands to hills on Caribbean slope of central Veracruz and northern Oaxaca (southeastern Mexico) through eastern Yucatan Peninsula (but not Cozumel) southward through Nicaragua, thence both slopes from Costa Rica through Panama, southward in Colombia west of the Andes to west-central Ecuador
Ceratopipra rubrocapilla: tropical eastern Peru to northern Bolivia, and southern Amazonian and eastern Brazil
Cercibis oxycerca: llanos of eastern Colombia to the Guianas and western Amazonian Brazil
Cercococcyx mechowi: Sierra Leone and northwestern Angola eastward to Uganda and northwestern Tanzania
Cercococcyx montanus: patchy in lowland to submontane forest, riparian woodland, and coastal thickets, from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to central Kenya, and southward to southern Mozambique, and in middle Zambezi River forest of southern Zambia and adjacent Zimbabwe; some highland breeders migrate westward
Cercococcyx olivinus: Liberia to Democratic Republic of the Congo, western Uganda, northwestern Zambia, and northern Angola
Cercomacra brasiliana: southeastern Brazil (southern Bahia and eastern Minas Gerais to Rio de Janeiro)
Cercomacra carbonaria: far northern Brazil (along Rio Branco) and adjacent Guyana
Cercomacra cinerascens: tropical rainforest in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to south-central Brazil and northern Bolivia
Cercomacra ferdinandi: central Brazil (Bananal Island and right bank of Rio Javaés, Tocantins)
Cercomacra manu: locally in southeastern Peru, northwestern Bolivia, and southern Amazonian Brazil
Cercomacra melanaria: eastern Bolivia to south-central Brazil (Mato Grosso) and northern Paraguay
Cercomacra nigricans: eastern Panama (including Pearl Islands) to western Ecuador and eastern Venezuela
Cercomacroides fuscicauda: southeastern Colombia to northeastern Bolivia and southwestern Amazonian Brazil
Cercomacroides laeta: shrubby edges of tropical humid forest in the southern Guiana Shield in southern Guyana and northern Brazil; in easternmost Amazon basin, east of the Rio Tocantins, in northeastern Brazil, and in coastal northeastern Brazil (Rio Grande do Norte southward to Alagoas)
Cercomacroides nigrescens: montane forest borders, also vine thickets, bamboo stands, and river islands in the slopes of the eastern Andes in Ecuador and adjacent southern Colombia southward to southeastern Peru; in the Guianas and far northern Colombia, and in the eastern and southern Amazon basin from northeastern Brazil, south of the Amazon River and west to the Rio Madeira, southward to south-central Brazil and northeastern Bolivia
Cercomacroides serva: southern Colombia east of Andes to northwestern Bolivia and southwestern Amazonian Brazil
Cercomacroides tyrannina: shrubby edges of humid forest from southeastern Mexico southward through Central America to northwestern Colombia, west of the Andes southward to southwestern Ecuador, and in interior Colombia southward to the middle Magdalena Valley; east of the Andes in the Sierra de Perijá, and the slopes of the Andes of western Venezuela southward to southeastern Colombia and eastward across the northern Amazon basin and Guiana Shield, north of the Amazon River, to the Guianas and northeastern Brazil
Cercotrichas galactotes: disjunctly in lowland to foothill dry open woodland, wooded grassland, brushy semi-desert, tamarisk and acacia stands, and orchards, from Iberian Peninsula eastward through Greece and Türkiye to southern Kazakhstan, southward to northwestern Africa, and eastward through Nile Valley (Egypt) and Arabia to western Pakistan, and from Mauritania eastward through the Sahel to Eritrea and Somalia; northern populations migrate to sub-Saharan Sahel and to eastern Africa
Cercotrichas hartlaubi: disjunctly in lowland to submontane tall-grass savanna, riparian thickets, secondary scrub, and plantations, in southeastern Nigeria eastward to western Central African Republic, and in northwestern Angola, and from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to western Kenya, and southward to Burundi and northwestern Tanzania
Cercotrichas leucophrys: lowland to montane thornscrub, open broad-leafed woodland, and dune scrub, from eastern Gabon and Republic of the Congo eastward to southern South Sudan, Ethiopia, and northern Somalia, thence southward to northern Namibia, northern Botswana, southern Mozambique, and eastern and southern South Africa
Cercotrichas paena: lowland to foothill open scrub, brushy edges to sand-pans, and lightly wooded savanna, from southwestern Angola and Namibia eastward to western Zimbabwe, and southward to northern South Africa
Cercotrichas podobe: lowland and foothill arid subdesert, shrubby savanna, and palm groves, from southern Mauritania and Senegal eastward through the Sahel to eastern Sudan, Eritrea, and Ethiopia, and on Arabian Peninsula; summer visitor to southern Israel (has bred), winter visitor to Somalia, some populations migratory
Cereopsis novaehollandiae: islands off southern Australia; winters to adjacent coast
Cerorhinca monocerata: breeds North Pacific islands from Sakhalin and Kuril Islands, Hokkaido and northern Honshu (northern Japan), Aleutians, southern Alaska to southern California; winters coastal waters to southern Japan and Korean Peninsula and northern Baja California
Certhia americana: breeds in coniferous, mixed, and deciduous forest from southern Alaska and British Colombia eastward to Newfoundland (western to eastern Canada), southward on Pacific coast and mountains of western USA to southern California, mountains of Mexico to northwestern Nicaragua, northeastern USA, and southward along the Appalachians (to eastern Tennessee and western North Carolina), with isolated populations along the US Atlantic coast (to southeastern Maryland); winters in wider range of habitats including edge, riparian areas, and orchards at lower elevations from southern Canada to northeastern Mexico and central Florida
Certhia brachydactyla: lowland to submontane broadleaf deciduous woodland, pine or juniper forest, riverine woodland, and parks, from continental Europe eastward to western Ukraine, and southward to northwestern Africa, Mediterranean Europe, including Crete and Cyprus, and Caucasus
Certhia discolor: Himalayas of Nepal to southern Tibet and northwestern India
Certhia familiaris: lowland to submontane deciduous and coniferous forest, riparian woodland, well-wooded farmland, and parks, from British Isles and Scandinavia eastward to Ussuriland and Sakhalin (Russia), and southward to Mediterranean Europe, Caucasus, northern China, and Japan (to Kyushu); some northern populations disperse southward post-breeding
Certhia himalayana: submontane to montane open coniferous forest, pine-rhododendron woodland, and juniper scrub at tree-line, from eastern Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan southward to northern India, thence eastward through Himalayas to Nepal, and disjunctly from central China southward to northern Myanmar; western populations disperse downslope in winter to central Pakistan
Certhia hodgsoni: submontane to montane coniferous forest, and mixed deciduous-rhododendron woodland, from northeastern Pakistan eastward through Himalayas to Tibet and south-central China; some downslope dispersal in winter
Certhia manipurensis: disjunctly in foothill to montane evergreen forest, and mixed pine and broadleaf evergreen forest, in northeastern India and western Myanmar, in eastern Myanmar and northern Thailand eastward to northwestern Vietnam, and in southern Vietnam
Certhia nipalensis: mountains of western Nepal to northeastern Myanmar, southeastern Tibet, and southwestern China
Certhiasomus stictolaemus: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin from eastern Colombia southward to eastern Peru in Ucayali and eastward to southern Venezuela and most of the Brazilian Amazon northeastward to Amapá and eastern French Guiana, eastward to northern Maranhão and southward to eastern Rondônia and northern Mato Grosso; also isolated in central Guyana and Suriname
Certhiaxis cinnamomeus: freshwater marshes in the lowlands of northern Colombia and western Venezuela, southward in the Magdalena Valley (to Huila); east of the Andes in the llanos of southwestern Venezuela and northeastern Colombia eastward across northern Venezuela to Trinidad, the savannas of Guyana and far northern Brazil (Roraima), the Guianas, and northeastern Brazil (Amapá); inland along the Amazon River to far southeastern Colombia and northeastern Peru (west to the middle Río Ucayali), and along the Rio Madeira and tributaries to northern Bolivia and far southeastern Peru, and eastern Brazil (northern Pará southward along the Atlantic Coast and interior Brazil) to eastern Bolivia, Paraguay, northern Argentina (southward to La Pampa and Buenos Aires), and Uruguay
Certhiaxis mustelinus: far southeastern Colombia to eastern Peru and Amazonian Brazil
Certhidea fusca: arid lowlands of smaller northern and eastern islands of the Galapagos, including Darwin and Wolf (far northwest), Pinta to Genovesa (northeast), Santa Fé, and Floreana to San Cristobal and Española
Certhidea olivacea: Galapagos (Santiago, Rábida, Pinzón, Isabela, Fernandina, and Santa Cruz)
Certhilauda chuana: disjunctly in foothill open savanna with sparse grass and scattered bushes, and fallow or grazed pasture, from southeastern Botswana southward to northern South Africa, and disjunctly in two areas in northeastern South Africa
Certhilauda curvirostris: lowland coastal scrub and sparsely vegetated dunes of coastal southwestern Namibia and western South Africa (to Western Cape)
Certhilauda semitorquata: lowland to foothill rocky grassland of eastern South Africa and Lesotho
Certhilauda subcoronata: lowland Karoo scrub and rocky hills and plains from southwestern Angola southward through western Namibia to western South Africa
Certhionyx variegatus: western and central Australia (central Western Australia to southwestern Queensland and northwestern New South Wales)
Ceryle rudis: disjunctly in lowland to montane wetlands, including lakes, rivers, shoreline, and mangroves, of sub-Saharan Africa, and of southern Türkiye and Nile Valley (Egypt) eastward to southern Iran, and from Indian subcontinent eastward to southern China (including Hainan), and southward to Thailand and Vietnam
Cettia brunnifrons: montane undergrowth and rhododendron scrub at forest edge, willow thickets, and bamboo, from northern Pakistan eastward through Himalayas to southeastern Tibet, and southward to northeastern Myanmar; altitudinal migrant downslope post-breeding
Cettia castaneocoronata: foothill to montane understory in forest, dense moist ravines with ferns, and bamboo scrub, from northern India eastward through Himalayas to southern China and northern Vietnam, and southward to northeastern Bangladesh, western Myanmar, and western Thailand; altitudinal dispersal downslope post-breeding
Cettia cetti: patchy in lowland and foothill reedy swamps, willow thicket and bramble, and riparian tangles, from southern Britain and Iberia eastward through southern Europe to Caucasus, Kazakhstan, and adjacent southern Russian and western China, and southward to northwestern Africa, Jordan, Iran, and Afghanistan; some eastern populations migrate to Middle East, southern Pakistan, and northwestern India
Cettia major: foothill to montane undergrowth in forest, and rhododendron scrub at or above tree-line, from northern India eastward through Himalaya to Tibet and central China, and southward to northeastern India and northern Myanmar; altitudinal migrant downslope post-breeding
Ceuthmochares aereus: lowland and foothill rainforest, secondary and riverine forest, thickets, and coastal scrub, from Senegambia eastward through southern Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to southern South Sudan and western Kenya, and southward to northern Angola and eastern Tanzania; some intra-African migration
Ceuthmochares australis: Ethiopia to Kenya, Tanzania, Mozambique, and eastern South Africa
Ceyx azureus: Moluccas, eastern Lesser Sundas, New Guinea and satellite islands, and northern and eastern Australia
Ceyx cyanopectus: Luzon group, Mindoro, and West Visayas (Philippines)
Ceyx erithaca: disjunctly in lowland and foothill evergreen forest, favoring shady streams and pools, of Western Ghats (India) and Sri Lanka, and from eastern India and Bangladesh eastward to southern China (including Hainan), and southward to Andaman and Nicobar islands, Myanmar, and Vietnam; northern populations migrate southward to Malayan Peninsula and Sumatra
Ceyx meeki: Buka, Bougainville, Choiseul, and Isabel (northern and central Solomon Archipelago)
Ceyx melanurus: Philippines (except West Visayas, Palawan group, and Sulu Archipelago)
Ceyx mulcatus: New Hanover, New Ireland, and Lihir Islands (eastern Bismarck Archipelago)
Ceyx pusillus: Moluccas, New Guinea and satellite islands, northern Australia, Bismarck Archipelago, and Solomon Archipelago
Ceyx rufidorsa: lowland and foothill forest, favoring streams and pools, swamp forest, and mangroves, from southern Myanmar and Malayan Peninsula eastward to Palawan and Lubang (Philippines), Greater and Lesser Sundas, and some adjacent islands
Ceyx sacerdotis: New Britain and Umboi (southeastern Bismarck Archipelago)
Ceyx sangirensis: Sangihe Islands (northeast of Sulawesi); probably extinct
Ceyx solitarius: New Guinea, including Raja Ampat Islands (off western New Guinea), Aru Islands (off southwestern New Guinea), and D'Entrecasteaux Archipelago (off southeastern New Guinea)
Ceyx wallacii: Sula Islands (Taliabu, Seho, Mangole, and Sanana)
Chaetocercus astreans: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
Chaetocercus berlepschi: lowlands of western Ecuador (Esmeraldas, Manabí, and Guayas)
Chaetocercus bombus: Andes of far southwestern Colombia (Nariño) to northern Peru
Chaetocercus heliodor: montane cloudforest in the Andes of western Venezuela southward in the central and eastern Andes of Colombia to the Andes of eastern Ecuador southward to Morona Santiago; in the western Andes of Colombia from Antioquia southward to Cauca, and possibly in the Andes of northwestern Ecuador
Chaetocercus jourdanii: montane cloudforest in the Andes of western Venezuela southward in the central and eastern Andes of Colombia to the Andes of eastern Ecuador southward to Morona Santiago; in the western Andes of Colombia from Antioquia southward to Cauca, and possibly in the Andes of northwestern Ecuador
Chaetocercus mulsant: Andes of Colombia to western Bolivia (Cochabamba)
Chaetops aurantius: foothill to montane steep-sloping alpine and subalpine grassland with rocky outcrops, from Lesotho highlands and adjacent South Africa, and south-westward to south-central South Africa (to eastern Western Cape); some downslope dispersal post-breeding
Chaetops frenatus: patchy in lowland to foothill open restio-dominated Fynbos, on upper slopes and ridges, particularly where recently burned, in southwestern South Africa
Chaetorhynchus papuensis: montane forest of New Guinea including Yule Island
Chaetura andrei: northern Venezuela, but distribution very poorly known: confirmed from the Orinoco Valley in Bolívar and from Sucre
Chaetura brachyura: varied forested to open lowland to hill habitats from southwestern Panama, southern Lesser Antilles, Trinidad and Tobago, trans-Andean southwestern Ecuador to northwestern Peru, and almost throughout cis-Andean northern South America eastward to Maranhão, southward to central Bolivia, and eastward to Mato Grosso
Chaetura chapmani: Panama to Colombia, Venezuela, Trinidad, the Guianas, and northeastern Brazil, and tropical eastern Peru to eastern Bolivia and western Amazonian Brazil
Chaetura cinereiventris: forest of lowlands and hills from northeastern Honduras to western Panama, northwestern Colombia to far northwestern Peru, northern Colombia, and Venezuela, Grenada (southern Lesser Antilles), Trinidad and Tobago, Amazonia, and Guianas including tepuis, and southward through eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
Chaetura egregia: eastern Ecuador to eastern Peru, northern Bolivia, and western Amazonian Brazil
Chaetura fumosa: southwestern Costa Rica and western Panama
Chaetura martinica: Guadeloupe to St. Vincent (central and southern Lesser Antilles)
Chaetura meridionalis: breeds from eastern Bolivia southward to northern Argentina and eastward to east-central Brazil; partially migratory, wintering north to Panama, northern Colombia, northern Venezuela, and Suriname
Chaetura pelagica: breeds eastern North America; winters in coastal Peru and northern Chile, in Amazonian Peru, and probably in western Brazil
Chaetura spinicaudus: forest and open habitats of lowlands to mid-mountains from central Panama to southwestern Ecuador; eastern Colombia eastward through northeastern Brazil and southward through Rondônia and Bahia (west-central and east-central Brazil)
Chaetura vauxi: breeds locally from southeastern Alaska to eastern Panama and northern Venezuela
Chalcites basalis: breeds Australia including Tasmania; winters to Java
Chalcites crassirostris: Moluccas (Tayandu and Kai islands) and Tanimbar Islands (Yamdena and Larat)
Chalcites lucidus: Australia, Solomon Archipelago, Vanuatu, New Caledonia, and New Zealand region including Chatham Islands (east of North Island); winters to Lesser Sundas, New Guinea region, Bismarck Archipelago, and Solomon Archipelago

Chlorostilbon russatus: northeastern Colombia (Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta) and the Serranía de Perijá (Colombia and Venezuela)
Chlorostilbon stenurus: humid shrubbery and forest in the foothills of the Andes in western Venezuela and northeastern Colombia in Norte de Santander; also in coastal mountains of northwestern Venezuela, in Carabobo
Chlorothraupis carmioli: forest and edge of foothills of Caribbean slope from northeastern Honduras to far northwestern Colombia
Chlorothraupis frenata: tropical southern Colombia to central Bolivia (La Paz eastward to western Santa Cruz)
Chlorothraupis olivacea: tropical eastern Panama (Darién) to western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador
Chlorothraupis stolzmanni: humid lowland and foothill forest in the base of the western Andes from northwestern Colombia southward to southwestern Ecuador
Chondestes grammacus: breeds shrub-steppe, prairie, and woodland-grassland ecotones from southern British Columbia eastward to southern Manitoba (interior southwestern to south-central Canada) southward across interior western and central USA to southern California, and Zacatecas and San Luis Potosí (north-central Mexico), and eastward to western Indiana and Arkansas, irregularly farther east; winters from southern USA southward to southern Baja California and to southeastern Oaxaca (southern Mexico)
Chondrohierax uncinatus: deciduous to humid forest, riparian woodland, swamps with trees, gallery forest, Cerrado woodland, and agricultural fields from northeastern Mexico and adjacent US, and from northwestern Mexico southeastward across Central America to eastern Panama; northern Colombia southward to the headwaters of the Río Cauca and Río Magdalena and southward in the Pacific to northwestern Peru; east of the Andes in Venezuela, Trinidad and Tobago, Grenada, and the Guianas southward across the Amazon basin and Cerrado of interior Brazil to eastern Bolivia, Paraguay, and northern Argentina; in eastern Brazil from Ceará and Piauí southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul, but absent in most Caatinga
Chondrohierax wilsonii: varied lowland forest and woodland types in far eastern Cuba; possibly extinct
Chordeiles acutipennis: breeds southwestern USA to western Peru and far northern Chile; northern populations winter to northern Colombia
Chordeiles gundlachii: breeds Florida Keys and throughout the West Indies; wintering range poorly known, with records mainly from northern Venezuela
Chordeiles minor: breeds central and southern Canada to Panama; winters to southern South America
Chordeiles nacunda: open areas and savanna from Trinidad and Tobago, northern Venezuela, and the Guianas southward across the Amazon basin to northern Bolivia and southward in the Chaco of eastern Bolivia, Paraguay, and northeastern Argentina, also southward seasonally to the foothills of the Andes in northwestern Argentina; in eastern and interior Brazil (Maranhão, Piauí, and Ceará southward to Rio Grande do Sul), Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina; also seasonal to northern Colombia and to the Cauca and Magdalena valleys

Chordeiles rupestris: riverbanks, river islands, flooded forest and oxbow lakes mostly along major rivers in the Amazon basin from southwestern Venezuela southward to southeastern Peru and northern Bolivia; in Brazil eastward to central-eastern Pará and western Tocantins
Chroicocephalus brunnicephalus: breeds inland Tibetan Plateau of Tajikistan, Xinjiang (western China), Ladakh (far northwestern India), and Tibet; winters inland and coastal Indian Subcontinent, southwestern China, and western southeastern Asia
Chroicocephalus bulleri: breeds mostly gravel riverbeds in South Island (New Zealand); winters to varied habitats of southern North Island
Chroicocephalus cirrocephalus: marshes, lakes, and coasts of Africa and South America, sub-Saharan Africa (except Congolian forest) and Madagascar; coastal Ecuador and Peru; coastal northeastern Brazil to northeastern Argentina and inland to Salta in the north and La Pampa in the south (north-central Argentina)
Chroicocephalus genei: breeds patchily on coasts and saline lakes from southern Iberian Peninsula to Central Asia, Pakistan, and coastal far northwestern India, also Mauritania and Senegambia; winters to coasts of Arabian Peninsula and western India
Chroicocephalus hartlaubii: coastal southwestern Namibia to southwestern South Africa
Chroicocephalus maculipennis: breeds inland and coastal southeastern Brazil, central Chile and Argentina southward through Tierra del Fuego, and Falkland Islands; some winter coastally farther north
Chroicocephalus novaehollandiae: inland southern Australia and coastal throughout Australia; coastal New Zealand and outlying islands and New Caledonia
Chroicocephalus philadelphia: breeds boreal forest zone from southwestern Alaska mainland across Canada to eastern Quebec (southeastern Canada); winters eastern North Pacific coast southward to west-central Mexico, inland southeastern USA, western North Atlantic coast and offshore Gulf Stream southward to the Bahamas and Cuba
Chroicocephalus ridibundus: breeds southern Greenland, Iceland, and western Europe eastward across Russia to Yakutsk region (eastern Russia), southward through Caspian Seato northeastern China, also west-central Newfoundland (southeastern Canada); winters to Africa, southern and eastern Asia, and (rare) eastern North America
Chroicocephalus serranus: breeds Andean lakes of far southwestern Colombia to south-central Chile and southwestern Argentina; some non-breeders move to adjacent Pacific coast
Chrysococcyx caprius: intra-African migrant in sub-Saharan Africa and southern Arabia
Chrysococcyx cupreus: Senegal and Gambia to South Sudan and Ethiopia, southward to Angola and eastern South Africa
Chrysococcyx flavigularis: Sierra Leone to southern Cameroon, southwestern South Sudan, western Uganda, and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Chrysococcyx maculatus: India to southern China, southeastern Asia, Sumatra, and Andaman and Nicobar islands
Chrysococcyx xanthorhynchus: northeastern India to southeastern Asia, Greater Sundas, and Philippines
Chrysocolaptes erythrocephalus: Philippines (Balabac, Palawan, Busuanga, and Calamian Islands)
Chrysocolaptes festivus: open deciduous woodland and scrub in terai zone of northern India from Uttarakhand eastward through southeastern Nepal, and disjunctly through most of Peninsular India from Gujarat and Rajasthan eastward southern West Bengal and to southward to Sri Lanka
Chrysocolaptes guttacristatus: Himalayan foothills in northwestern India and western Nepal eastward to Yunnan (southern China) and Vietnam, and southward to eastern Peninsular India and Malaysian Peninsula, Sumatra, Java, and Borneo
Chrysocolaptes haematribon: northern Philippines (Luzon, Polillo, Catanduanes, and Marinduque)
Chrysocolaptes lucidus: East Visayas and Mindanao group (east-central and southern Philippines)
Chrysocolaptes socialis: Western Ghats and coastal western India
Chrysocolaptes strictus: Java, Bali, and Kangean Islands (north of Bali)
Chrysocolaptes validus: tropical rainforest and adjacent plantations in the southern Malayan Peninsula, from southern Peninsular Thailand southward to Sumatra, Bangka, Java, Natuna Islands, and Borneo
Chrysocolaptes xanthocephalus: Philippines (Negros, Guimaras, Panay, Masbate, and Ticao)
Chrysocorythus estherae: montane forest, humid montane grasslands above treeline and heather-dominated meadows with scattered scrub in the mountains of northwestern Sumatra, locally in Java, and in central Sulawesi
Chrysocorythus mindanensis: southern Philippines (Mount Katanglad and Mount Apo on Mindanao)
Chrysolampis mosquitus: tropical eastern Panama to Colombia, Venezuela, eastern Bolivia, and Brazil
Chrysolophus amherstiae: mountains of southeastern Tibet and southwestern China to northern Myanmar
Chrysolophus pictus: mountain slopes of central and southern China
Chrysomma altirostre: very patchy in lowland tall grassland in riparian floodplains, and on riverine islands, in Pakistan (Indus River), northern India and adjacent Nepal (Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers), and in southern Myanmar (Ayeyarwady River)
Chrysomma sinense: lowland to foothill scrub, tall grass, reedbed, bamboo, and cane fields, from eastern Pakistan and India eastward to southeastern China, and southward to Sri Lanka, central Thailand, and southern Vietnam
Chrysomus icterocephalus: disjunctly in freshwater marshes in South America from the lowlands of eastern Panama eastward to Trinidad and the Guianas, to southeastern Venezuela, northernmost Brazil, and western Guyana, along the Amazon River in Brazil from its mouth westward to northern Peru (Loreto), in the lowlands of southern Venezuela and Colombia, and in highland marshes of the Bogotá plateau (northeastern Colombia)
Chrysomus ruficapillus: freshwater marshes in far eastern French Guiana and northeastern Brazil southward along the Atlantic coast and interior Brazil to Buenos Aires and La Pampa (central Argentina), and westward to central Bolivia
Chrysophlegma flavinucha: lowland to montane forest from northern and east-central India eastward to southeastern China (including Hainan), and southward to Malayan Peninsula highlands and Sumatra
Chrysophlegma mentale: humid forest in the Malay Peninsula from far southern Myanmar to southern Peninsular Malaysia, and in Sumatra, Bangka, Borneo and Java
Chrysophlegma miniaceum: tropical rainforest and adjacent open areas in the Malayan Peninsula from far southern Myanmar and southern Thailand southward to Singapore; also in Sumatra (including Nias), Bangka and Belitung, Java, and Borneo
Chrysothlypis chrysomelas: foothill forest and borders on Caribbean slope from northwestern Costa Rica through Panama to far western Colombia
Chrysothlypis salmoni: Pacific slope of Andes of Colombia and northwestern Ecuador
Chrysuronia boucardi: western coast of Costa Rica (Gulf of Nicoya to Golfo Dulce)
Chrysuronia brevirostris: humid to semi-deciduous forest and scrub, gallery forest, scrubby savanna, and borders in northern (west to Miranda) and eastern Venezuela, Trinidad and the Guianas, southward in central Venezuela in the Orinoco basin and the tepuis to western Guyana and far northern Brazil (Roraima)
Chrysuronia coeruleogularis: mangrove and dry woodland in the Pacific lowlands of western Panama and adjacent Costa Rica eastward across Panama to northwestern and northern Colombia, as far east as the Guajira Peninsula; west of the Andes as far south as northern Chocó
Chrysuronia goudoti: humid to dry woodland, scrub, and borders in the lowlands and foothills of northern Colombia and western Venezuela, southward in the Magdalena Valley to its headwaters (Huila)
Chrysuronia humboldtii: far southeastern Panama to Colombia and northwestern Ecuador
Chrysuronia leucogaster: mangrove and scrub from northeastern Venezuela eastward in coastal Guianas and northeastern Brazil to the central-east Brazil in Espirito Santo; locally in interior Guyana and Suriname

Chunga burmeisteri: Chaco of Paraguay and adjacent Bolivia to central Argentina
Cichladusa arquata: lowland to foothill borassus palm savanna, riparian thicket with ivory palm, and gardens with coconut palm, from eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward through Rwanda and Tanzania to southeastern Kenya, and southward through Zambia and Mozambique to northeastern South Africa
Cichladusa guttata: lowland to foothill riverine thickets, coastal scrub, and juniper scrub, from eastern South Sudan, central Ethiopia, and southern Somalia southward to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and central Tanzania
Cichladusa ruficauda: patchy in lowland to foothill ivory palm savanna, oil palm groves, thickets in gallery forest, and dry baobab-acacia woodland, from southern Central African Republic southward through southern Gabon and western Democratic Republic of the Congo to western Angola and far northwestern Namibia
Cichlocolaptes leucophrus: humid lowland and montane forest in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil, from central Bahia southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul
Cichlocolaptes mazarbarnetti: formerly northeastern Brazil; currently known from only two sites, in Alagoas and Pernambuco; extinct
Cichlopsis leucogenys: highly disjunct in tepuis of southeastern Venezuela, western Guyana, and locally in Suriname, foothill and montane cloudforest in the Andes of western Colombia (Chocó) southward to northwestern Ecuador, locally in the eastern Andes of central Peru (Huánuco, Ucayali, and Junin), and in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil, from southern Bahia southward to Espírito Santo

Ciconia episcopus: lowland and foothill grassland, peat-swamps, cultivation, and wetlands, from northern Pakistan, India, and Sri Lanka eastward to northern Malayan Peninsula, southern Vietnam, and Philippines, and from southern Sumatra eastward to Wallacea (Indonesia)
Ciconia maguari: plains and marshes of west-central South America east of the Andes
Ciconia nigra: central and southern Eurasia; southern Africa; winters to central Africa and India
Ciconia stormi: lowland wetlands of Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, Mentawai and Pagai islands (off Sumatra), and Borneo
Cinclidium frontale: disjunctly in foothill to montane dense bamboo in broadleaf evergreen forest, from northeastern India eastward to central China, and southward to northern Thailand, northern Laos, and northwestern Vietnam; some downslope dispersal in winter
Cinclocerthia gutturalis: forest of lowlands to mountains of Martinique and St. Lucia
Cinclocerthia ruficauda: humid forest of lowlands and hills from Montserrat to St. Vincent (Lesser Antilles, except Martinique, and records from St. Lucia unproven)
Cinclodes albidiventris: paramo grassland and arid montane scrub in the Andes from western Venezuela and Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta southward along the eastern and central Andes of Colombia through Ecuador to northern Peru, north and west of the Río Marañón; in the western Andes of Ecuador southward to northern Loja

Cinclodes antarcticus: coastal rocky and short-grass and tussock areas in Tierra del Fuego of far southern Chile and southern Argentina, including offshore islands in the Cape Horn Archipelago, and the Falkland Islands
Cinclodes aricomae: Andes of southern Peru and far western Bolivia (La Paz)
Cinclodes atacamensis: Andes of Peru to western Bolivia, northern Chile, and northern Argentina, and mountains of central Argentina (Sierra de Córdoba and northeastern San Luis)
Cinclodes comechingonus: Andes of north-central Argentina (western Córdoba to eastern Tucumán)
Cinclodes excelsior: dry to humid grassy and rocky paramo and adjacent montane scrub, bogs, meadows and Polylepis woodland in the northern part of the central Andes of Colombia, in Caldas, Risaralda, and Tolima, and from southern Colombia southward to southern Ecuador, in northern Loja
Cinclodes fuscus: southern Chile and southern Argentina; winters to southeastern Brazil, Uruguay, and Paraguay
Cinclodes nigrofumosus: rocky coasts of Chile (Arica southward to Valdivia)
Cinclodes olrogi: Andes of north-central Argentina (western Córdoba and northeastern San Luis)
Cinclodes oustaleti: open rocky and grassy areas from northern Chile and northwestern Argentina southward to Tierra del Fuego, including islands of the Cape Horn Archipelago; breeds in the Andes and migrates to the coast; also in Alejandro Selkirk Island off central Chile
Cinclodes pabsti: montane savanna with rocky outcrops and temperate grassland often near water in the highlands of southeastern Brazil, in Paraná and northern Rio Grande do Sul
Cinclodes palliatus: Andes of central Peru (Junín, Lima, and Huancavelica)
Cinclodes patagonicus: coastal rocky and short-grass areas, rocky streams, river and lake shores from central Chile and west-central Argentina (Mendoza) southward to Tierra del Fuego, including some islands
Cinclodes taczanowskii: rocky coasts of Peru (Ancash southward to Tacna)
Cincloramphus bivittatus: lowland scrub of Timor (eastern Lesser Sundas)
Cincloramphus cruralis: mainland Australia (except northern Kimberley, northern Northern Territory and northern Cape York Peninsula)
Cincloramphus grosvenori: known from 2 specimens from Whiteman Mountains of New Britain (southeastern Bismarck Archipelago)
Cincloramphus macrurus: New Guinea (except south-central) and eastern Bismarck Archipelago
Cincloramphus mariae: grassland and open heath of New Caledonia
Cincloramphus mathewsi: Australia (except the Nullarbor Plain and Tasmania)
Cincloramphus rubiginosus: scrub of New Britain (southeastern Bismarck Archipelago)
Cincloramphus rufus: montane northwestern and north-central Fiji (southwestern Polynesia)
Cincloramphus timoriensis: Philippines, Sulawesi, Ambon (central Moluccas), central and eastern Lesser Sundas, south-central New Guinea, and northern and eastern Australia
Cinclosoma ajax: patchily in western, southern, and southeastern New Guinea
Cinclosoma alisteri: south-central Australia (Nullarbor Plain, southeastern Western Australia, and southwestern South Australia)
Cinclosoma castaneothorax: east-central Australia (south-central Queensland and northwestern New South Wales)
Cinclosoma castanotum: southeastern Australia (Yorke Peninsula, southern Flinders Ranges, eastern Mount Lofty Range, northwestern Victoria, and southwestern New South Wales, central New South Wales)
Cinclosoma cinnamomeum: southeastern Queensland to northwestern New South Wales, central and northeastern South Australia, and southeastern Northern Territory
Cinclosoma marginatum: west-central Australia (Pilbara region southward to Southern Cross, eastward to southwestern Northern Territory)
Cinclosoma punctatum: east-central and southeastern Australia including Tasmania
Cinclus cinclus: Britain and Scandinavia southward to montane northern Africa, through mountains of central Asia to western Mongolia and Himalayas to central China
Cinclus leucocephalus: fast-flowing rivers in mountains from Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in northeastern Colombia, Sierra de Perijá on northern Colombia/Venezuela border, and Venezuelan Andes southward in Andes through central Bolivia
Cinclus mexicanus: fast-flowing streams from Alaska except north slope and including eastern Aleutians eastward through western Alberta, southward in east through Colorado and western South Dakota, southward in west to southern California, thence on Pacific slope through mountains from Nayarit, thence both slopes and transvolcanic belt southward to south-central Oaxaca, thence southern Chiapas through northern Nicaragua, disjunctly northwestern Costa Rica to western Panama; northern populations move to ice-free larger rivers
Cinclus pallasii: mountains of central Asia, Himalayas, and eastward through northeastern Asia to Kamchatka and southward to northern southeastern Asia
Cinclus schulzii: Andes of southern Bolivia (Chuquisaca and Tarija) and northwestern Argentina (southward to Catamarca and Tucumán)

Cinnycerthia olivascens: montane forest of Andes from northern Colombia through San Martin in northern Peru
Cinnycerthia peruana: eastern Andes of Peru (Amazonas to Ayacucho)
Cinnycerthia unirufa: humid montane forest from Sierra de Perijá on northern Colombia-Venezuela border and Andes of southwestern Venezuela southward through far northern Peru

Cinnyris aurora: varied lowland habitats in Palawan and satellite islands; also Cuyo Archipelago and Cagayan group in Sulu Sea (all in southwestern Philippines)

Cinnyris chalcomelas: lowland coastal thornscrub in southern Somalia and eastern Kenya

Cinnyris clementiae: varied lowland habitats of southern Moluccas from Buru eastward through Seram and the Kai Islands
Cinnyris coccinigastrus: lowland to foothill forest edge, secondary forest, dry thornscrub, savanna, riverine woodland, plantations, and gardens, from Senegambia eastward to southern South Sudan and Uganda, and southward to northwestern Angola, central Democratic Republic of the Congo, and far northern Tanzania
Cinnyris congensis: lowland riverine forest along the Congo, lower Ubangi, and Lefini Rivers (Republic of the Congo and Democratic Republic of the Congo)
Cinnyris cupreus: lowland to montane savanna, open woodland, swamps, mangroves, and gardens, from southwestern Mauritania and Senegal eastward to western Ethiopia, and southward through Gabon, western Kenya, and western Tanzania, to western Angola, northern Botswana, northern Zimbabwe, and central Mozambique; partially migratory in West Africa
Cinnyris erythrocercus: patchy in lowland to foothill riverine forest, savanna wetland, cultivation, and gardens, from South Sudan southward through northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and southwestern Kenya, to central Tanzania

Cinnyris fuelleborni: montane forest from northeastern Zambia and central Tanzania southward to southern Malawi and northern Mozambique
Cinnyris fuscus: lowland semiarid coastal plain, acacia scrub, and gardens, from southwestern Angola and Namibia southward to southwestern Botswana and western and central South Africa; some irruptive movements
Cinnyris gertrudis: foothill to submontane miombo woodland, riparian woodland, savanna, parks, and gardens, from western Angola eastward through southern Democratic Republic of the Congo to western Tanzania, and southward to Zambia and northern Malawi
Cinnyris habessinicus: lowland to montane arid thornscrub, rocky hillside, dry wadis, and gardens, from southeastern Egypt and northeastern Sudan southward to northeastern Uganda and central Kenya
Cinnyris hellmayri: scrub in wadis and hillsides in the western Arabian Peninsula from northern Saudi Arabia southward to Yemen and western Oman
Cinnyris idenburgi: northwestern New Guinea and Sepik Ramu
Cinnyris johannae: lowland rainforest, plantations and gardens, from Sierra Leone eastward to Ghana and adjacent Togo, and from southeastern Nigeria eastward to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, southward to Cabinda (northwestern Angola) and western Democratic Republic of the Congo
