Cinnyris mediocris: foothill to montane forest, bamboo, heathland, and gardens, from western and central Kenya southward to northern Tanzania
Cinnyris melanogastrus: foothill to submontane savanna, dry thornscrub, wooded grassland, and gardens, from south-central Kenya southward to central Tanzania
Cinnyris minullus: patchy in lowland to foothill primary and secondary forest, forest edge, wooded savanna, and plantations, from Sierra Leone eastward through southern Nigeria and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to western Uganda, and southward to far western and south-central Democratic Republic of the Congo
Cinnyris moreaui: foothill to montane forest, and forest edge, in highlands of east-central Tanzania
Cinnyris nectarinioides: lowland arid acacia savanna and riverine thornscrub from central Ethiopia and southern Somalia southward to northeastern Tanzania
Cinnyris neergaardi: lowland coastal scrub, dry sandy thornbush, and open woodland, in southeastern Mozambique and coastal KwaZulu-Natal (eastern South Africa)
Cinnyris ornatus: Myanmar to Thailand, Cambodia and northern Malayan Peninsula (southward to Penang), Andaman and Nicobar islands, and Greater and most Lesser sundas
Cinnyris osea: patch, in bushy riversides, valleys and savannas of eastern Cameroon, southwestern Chad (Lake Chad), Central African Republic, southwestern Sudan, far northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, southwestern South Sudan, and northwestern Uganda, and disjunctly Syria and Israel to Türkiye and Arabia (eastward to Oman)
Cinnyris oustaleti: disjunctly in lowland miombo woodland, scrub and secondary growth, in west-central Angola and in northeastern Zambia and southwestern Tanzania
Cinnyris pembae: lowland coastal forest, coastal rag scrub, plantations, and gardens, on Pemba Island (off northeastern Tanzania)
Cinnyris prigoginei: local in foothill to submontane forest, forest edge, and adjacent scrub, in Marungu Highlands (southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo)
Cinnyris pulchellus: lowland to foothill savanna, riverine woodland, dry thornscrub, mangrove scrub, and gardens, from southern Mauritania eastward through Sahel to Eritrea and Ethiopia, and southward to Sierra Leone, central Nigeria, Central African Republic, Uganda, and western Kenya; some post-breeding dispersal southward
Cinnyris regius: montane forest, bamboo and scrub, from western Uganda and northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo southward to western Tanzania
Cinnyris reichenowi: disjunct populations in lowland to montane forest edge, heath, gallery forest, and gardens, from southeastern Nigeria and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) eastward to northwestern Central African Republic, and from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and southern South Sudan southward to Burundi and central Kenya; undertakes altitudinal migration
Cinnyris rockefelleri: local in submontane to montane forest edge, tall bamboo, and heath, in North Itombwe Mountains and adjacent highlands (northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo)
Cinnyris rufipennis: local in foothill to submontane undisturbed primary forest in Udzungwa Mountains (south-central Tanzania)
Cinnyris shelleyi: lowland and foothill miombo woodland, acacia scrub, and gardens, from eastern Tanzania southward to northeastern Namibia, northwestern Zimbabwe, Malawi, and northern Mozambique
Cinnyris solaris: wooded habitats including gardens in lowlands and hills of main Lesser Sundas from Sumbawa eastward through Timor (except Sumba)
Cinnyris stuhlmanni: montane forest, scrub, bamboo, and heath, from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Uganda southward to western Burundi; disjunctly in east-central Tanzania (Rubeho and Udzungwa highlands) and northern Malawi (Nyika Plateau) and adjacent northeastern Zambia
Cinnyris superbus: patchy in lowland and foothill primary and secondary forest, wooded savanna, plantations, and mangroves, from Sierra Leone eastward through Central African Republic and northern Democratic Republic of the Congo to western Kenya and northwestern Tanzania, and southward to Angola
Cinnyris talatala: lowland to foothill dry savanna woodland, miombo or mopane woodland, riverine forest, and gardens, from western and southern Angola eastward through Zambia to southern Tanzania, and southward to northern Namibia, Botswana, and eastern South Africa; some seasonal dispersal with austral summer rains
Cinnyris teysmanni: Tanahjampea, Kalao, Bonerate, Kalaotoa, and Madu islands
Cinnyris tsavoensis: lowland to foothill arid acacia savanna, and riverine woodland, in eastern Kenya and northeastern Tanzania
Cinnyris ursulae: foothill to submontane primary and secondary forest, and forest edge, in highlands of southwestern Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea)
Cinnyris usambaricus: foothill to submontane forest, bamboo, and gardens, in Taita Hills (southeastern Kenya) and Usambara Mountains (northeastern Tanzania)
Cinnyris venustus: lowland to montane thornscrub, savanna, miombo woodland, mangroves, and gardens, from Senegambia eastward to Eritrea, Ethiopia, and western Somalia, and southward (except Congolian rainforest), to western Angola, eastern Zimbabwe, and Mozambique
Circaetus beaudouini: southwestern Mauritania southward to Guinea, eastward to southwestern Sudan and western South Sudan, possibly to northern Uganda
Circaetus cinerascens: savanna and thornscrub of sub-Saharan Africa
Circaetus cinereus: Senegambia to northern Ethiopia and southward to South Africa
Circaetus fasciolatus: mainly coastal districts of southern Somalia to eastern South Africa
Circaetus gallicus: breeds northwestern Africa and southern Europe, northward to Estonia, southward to the Levant, and eastward to Kazakhstan, also locally Arabian Peninsula, northern China, and Mongolia; also resident in South Asia (Pakistan, Nepal, and India), and in Lesser Sundas (Indonesia); western populations winter in the Sahel (Senegal and southwestern Mauritania to Ethiopia and western Kenya), eastern populations winter in South Asia and western Indonesia
Circaetus pectoralis: eastern Sudan and Ethiopia to South Africa
Circaetus spectabilis: lowland rainforest from Sierra Leone and southeastern Guinea eastward to southern South Sudan and western Uganda, and southward to northwestern Angola and east-central Democratic Republic of the Congo
Circus aeruginosus: lowland to foothill marsh, swamps, reedy lagoons, and paddyfields, from Europe eastward to upper River Yenisey (Russia) and Mongolia, and southward to northwestern Africa, eastern Türkiye, Iran, and Tajikistan; migrates southward in winter to sub-Saharan Africa, Middle East, and Indian subcontinent
Circus approximans: breeds Australia (except south-central), North, South, Stewart, and Chatham islands (New Zealand), Vanuatu, New Caledonia including Loyalty Islands, to Fiji and Tonga; non-breeders range to Trans-Fly (south-central New Guinea) and Kermadec Islands (northeast of New Zealand); introduced to Leeward and Windward Society Islands
Circus assimilis: Sulawesi, Sula Islands, eastern Lesser Sundas, and Australia (except Tasmania)
Circus buffoni: grassland of tropical South America, including Trinidad and Tobago
Circus cinereus: Andes of Colombia to Tierra del Fuego and Falkland Islands
Circus cyaneus: breeds Europe and northern Asia eastward to Russian Far East; breeds also in southern Georgia and possibly in nearby northeastern Türkiye, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and western Xinjiang (northwestern China); winters from Europe and northwestern Africa eastward through Türkiye and Middle East to southeastern China, Korean Peninsula, and Japan (Hokkaido to Ryukyu Islands)
Circus hudsonius: breeds North America; winters to northern South America
Circus macrosceles: Grande Comore, Mohéli, and Anjouan (northwestern and central Comoros), and western and central Madagascar
Circus macrourus: breeds central Eurasia; winters to southern Africa, India, and Myanmar
Circus maurus: arid grassland of southern Namibia, southwestern Botswana, and South Africa
Circus melanoleucos: breeds eastern Asia; winters to southern Asia, Philippines, and Greater Sundas
Circus pygargus: breeds northern Palearctic; winters to southern Africa, Iran, and India
Circus ranivorus: marshes and grassland of eastern and southern Africa
Circus spilonotus: breeds southeastern Siberia and Mongolia eastward to Ussuriland, Sakhalin, Japan (Hokkaido and Honshu), and northeastern China; winters from southeastern Asia, southern China, Korean Peninsula, and southern Japan to Indonesia (mainly Sumatra and northern Borneo) and Philippines
Ciridops anna: formerly Hawaii (Hawaiian Islands); extinct, last reported 1937
Cissa chinensis: eastern Himalayas to southeastern Tibet, Myanmar, southeastern Asia to northern Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, and northwestern Borneo
Cissa hypoleuca: lowland and foothill forest, and bamboo thickets, from south-central China (including Hainan), and northern Vietnam southward to southern Thailand and southern Vietnam
Cissa thalassina: lowland slopes of montane western Java
Cissomela pectoralis: northern Australia (Kimberley region, northern Western Australia, to Cape York Peninsula, northern Queensland)
Cissopis leverianus: eastern Colombia to southeastern Venezuela, the Guianas, northern Bolivia, Amazonian Brazil, and Paraguay to southeastern Brazil and adjacent northeastern Argentina (Misiones)
Cisticola aberdare: submontane to montane grassland, and moorland, in highlands of west-central Kenya
Cisticola aberrans: patchy in foothill and montane rocky slopes with grass, and grassy and miombo woodland, from southern Mauritania and Guinea eastward to southern South Sudan and southern Kenya, thence southward to western Angola and southern South Africa
Cisticola anderseni: lowland riverine edge with long grass and sedge in south-central Tanzania (Kilombero River floodplain)
Cisticola angusticauda: lowland and foothill grassland within miombo woodland, and grassy acacia savanna, from southwestern Uganda, eastern Rwanda, and southwestern Kenya southward through Tanzania to southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and northern Zambia
Cisticola anonymus: disjunctly in lowland to foothill tall grass with scattered bushes, swampy grassland, secondary growth, and plantations, from southern Nigeria eastward to southern Central African Republic and northern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and southward to northwestern Angola, and in southeastern Sierra Leone and Liberia
Cisticola aridulus: lowland and foothill desert grassland, and semiarid savanna, from southern Mauritania and Senegal eastward through the Sahel to Eritrea, Ethiopia, and Somalia, thence southward to Kenya and northern Tanzania, and from western Angola and northern Zambia through northern Namibia and Botswana, to central and eastern South Africa; Sahel populations nomadic with rains
Cisticola ayresii: patchy in foothill to montane grassland from western Gabon eastward through southern South Sudan and western Kenya, thence southward to western Angola, Zimbabwe, and eastern South Africa
Cisticola bailunduensis: foothill to submontane wooded rocky hills with rank grassy vegetation, and riparian thickets, in western Angola
Cisticola bakerorum: lowland flooded reedbed and tall sedge in south-central Tanzania (Kilombero River floodplain)
Cisticola bodessa: foothill and montane grassy savanna, and rocky hillsides with shrubs, from Eritrea and central Ethiopia southward to eastern South Sudan, northeastern Uganda, and northern Kenya
Cisticola brachypterus: lowland to montane heath, savanna woodland, and thickets on termitaria, from Senegambia eastward through southern Niger and southern Chad to Eritrea, Ethiopia, and southern Somalia, thence southward to Angola and southern Mozambique
Cisticola brunnescens: lowland to montane short-grass savanna, highland grassland, and heath, from central Cameroon eastward to Eritrea, Ethiopia, and northwestern Somalia, thence southward to southern Gabon and Republic of the Congo, and highlands of western Kenya and northern Tanzania
Cisticola bulliens: lowland dry savanna with thickets, forest edge, and coastal scrub, from Cabinda (northwestern Angola) and western Democratic Republic of the Congo southward to southwestern Angola (Namibe Plain)
Cisticola cantans: lowland to montane understory in open woodland, undergrowth, riparian corridors in savanna, and juniper forest, from Senegambia eastward to southern Sudan, Eritrea, and Ethiopia, thence southward (except in Congolian rainforest) to northern Mozambique and eastern Zimbabwe
Cisticola carruthersi: foothill to submontane tall papyrus swamp from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to Uganda and southwestern Kenya, and southward to Burundi and far northern Tanzania
Cisticola cherina: grassland of Madagascar and Aldabra (southwestern Seychelles)
Cisticola chiniana: lowland to foothill savanna, dry woodland, and semiarid scrub, from Eritrea and Ethiopia southward to northern Uganda and Kenya, and from southeastern Gabon eastward to Tanzania, thence southward to northern Namibia and eastern South Africa
Cisticola chubbi: disjunctly in foothill and montane tall grassland, forest edges, and bracken-brier, of southeastern Nigeria and southwestern Cameroon, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Uganda southward to Burundi and southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and eastern Uganda and western Kenya
Cisticola cinereolus: foothill to montane arid grassland, and dry acacia savanna, from central Ethiopia and northern Somalia southward to southeastern South Sudan, Kenya, and northeastern Tanzania
Cisticola cinnamomeus: patchy in lowland to montane wet grassland from southeastern Gabon eastward to southwestern Tanzania, thence southward to Angola and eastern South Africa
Cisticola dambo: patchy in foothill grassland, and seasonally flooded plain, of southeastern Gabon and from northeastern Angola eastward to southern Democratic Republic of the Congo and northwestern Zambia
Cisticola distinctus: patchy in foothill to montane grassland, forest edge, rocky slopes with grass or short scrub, disjunctly in eastern Uganda and northern Kenya, and from central Kenya southward to northern Tanzania
Cisticola erythrops: lowland to montane damp shrub and tall grass, riparian thickets, and forest clearings, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to southwestern Sudan and Ethiopia, thence southward to western Angola and eastern South Africa
Cisticola exilis: lowland to foothill tall grassland in open woodland, savanna, bracken scrub, and cultivation, from India eastward to southeastern China, Taiwan, and Philippines, and southward to Indonesia, New Guinea, Bismarck Archipelago, and eastern Australia; occasionally irruptive
Cisticola eximius: patchy in lowland to montane grassland, and wet highland grassland, from Senegal and southwestern Mali eastward to South Sudan, and southward to northern Republic of the Congo and southwestern Kenya; populations in Eritrea and Ethiopia are likely extirpated
Cisticola fulvicapilla: disjunctly in lowland to montane woodland understory, acacia savanna, and scrub on rocky slopes of southeastern Gabon, southern Republic of the Congo, and southwestern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and from Angola eastward to southern Tanzania, thence southward to northern Namibia and southern South Africa
Cisticola galactotes: lowland and foothill reedy wetland edges from southern Malawi southward through Mozambique and southeastern Zimbabwe to eastern South Africa
Cisticola guinea: patchy in lowland to foothill grassy understory of dry woodland and wooded savanna, grassy thickets, and fallow fields, from Senegambia eastward across Sahel to northern Cameroon and southern Chad
Cisticola haematocephalus: lowland marsh, arid scrub, and vegetated dunes, in coastal plain from southern Somalia southward to northeastern Tanzania
Cisticola hunteri: submontane and montane dense understory in forest edge and clearings, bamboo thickets, open moorland scrub, and marshy rank growth, in highlands of eastern Uganda (Mt. Elgon), west-central Kenya, and northern Tanzania
Cisticola juncidis: disjunctly in lowland to submontane grassland, seasonal wetland, saltmarsh, and cultivation, in western Palearctic from France and Iberia eastward to western Iran, and southward to northwestern Africa and Nile valley; in sub-Saharan Africa from Mauritania eastward to Somalia, and southwestern Arabian Peninsula, and southward to South Africa; and in eastern Palearctic from eastern Pakistan, India, and Sri Lanka, eastward to Japan (Honshu to southern Ryukyu Islands), and southward to Philippines, Indonesia, and northern Australia; some northern populations migratory
Cisticola lais: patchy in lowland to montane grassland, and rocky slopes with short scrub, of western Angola, and from southern Tanzania southward to southern South Africa
Cisticola lateralis: lowland to foothill grassy open woodland, thickets, and brushy termitaria, from Senegambia eastward to South Sudan and western Kenya, thence southward to southern and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, northern Angola, and far northwestern Zambia
Cisticola luapula: patchy in lowland reedbeds, emergent swampy vegetation, and grassy edges of seasonally inundated wetland, from northeastern Zambia and adjacent southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and southward through Zambia and eastern and southern Angola to northern Namibia, northern Botswana, and far western Zimbabwe
Cisticola lugubris: foothill to montane marsh edge rank vegetation, heath, and grassy savanna, in highlands of Eritrea and Ethiopia
Cisticola marginatus: lowland and foothill reedbed and marsh edges, and wet tall grass, from southern Mauritania and Senegal eastward to southern Sudan, western Ethiopia, and northern Kenya, thence southward to northwestern Angola and Malawi
Cisticola melanurus: lowland to foothill miombo woodland in southwestern and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo and northeastern Angola
Cisticola nana: lowland to foothill arid and semiarid acacia savanna, edges of saltpans, and grassy open woodland, from southeastern South Sudan and southern Ethiopia southward to northern and northeastern Tanzania
Cisticola natalensis: foothill and montane grassland, savanna, and open woodland, from Senegambia eastward to southern Sudan, Eritrea, Ethiopia, and southern Somalia, thence southward to Angola, Zimbabwe, southern Mozambique, and eastern South Africa
Cisticola nigriloris: foothill to montane tall grass, bracken-briar, forest edge, and secondary growth, in highlands of southern Tanzania, northeastern Zambia, and northern Malawi
Cisticola njombe: disjunctly in montane grassland, and bracken-brier scrub, of southern Tanzanian highlands, and of northeastern Zambia and Malawi
Cisticola pipiens: lowland papyrus swamps, reedbeds, and tall swamp grassland, from western Angola eastward to Burundi and southwestern Tanzania, thence southward to western Zambia and northeastern Namibia to northwestern Zimbabwe
Cisticola restrictus: lowland semiarid acacia thornscrub on flat sandy plains in eastern Kenya (lower Tana River valley)
Cisticola robustus: disjunctly in foothill and montane short grassland with bushes, and grassy rocky hills, of southeastern Nigeria and southwestern Cameroon highlands, Eritrean and Ethiopian highlands, and from eastern Republic of the Congo eastward to southwestern Kenya and northern Tanzania, thence southward to central Angola and eastern Zambia
Cisticola ruficeps: lowland to foothill grassland, and dry savanna, from northeastern Nigeria and northern Cameroon eastward to southern Sudan, Eritrea, and western Ethiopia, thence southward to northern Central Africa Republic and northern Uganda
Cisticola rufilatus: patchy in lowland and foothill semiarid savanna, and edges of broadleaf woodland, of southeastern Gabon and central Republic of the Congo, and from central Angola eastward to Malawi, thence southward through eastern Namibia, and eastward to northeastern South Africa
Cisticola rufus: patchy in lowland to foothill grassy savanna, and semiarid scrub. from Senegambia eastward to southern Chad, and southward to northern Sierra Leone, northern Ghana, and northwestern Central African Republic
Cisticola subruficapilla: lowland and foothill scrubby habitat, including arid Karoo and Fynbos, and coastal dunes, from southwestern Angola and Namibia southward to western South Africa (eastward to Free State and Eastern Cape)
Cisticola textrix: disjunctly in lowland and foothill grassland, grassy estuarine marsh, and heathland, of central and eastern Angola and western Zambia, and from southeastern Botswana through southern South Africa
Cisticola tinniens: disjunctly in lowland to montane moist grassland, sedges and reedbeds, and bamboo, of western Kenya highlands, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and from central Angola eastward to northeastern Zambia, thence southward through Zimbabwe to South Africa, Lesotho, and Eswatini
Cisticola troglodytes: foothill and montane grassy woodland, semiarid savanna, and riparian scrub, from southern Chad eastward to southern Sudan and western Ethiopia, southward to Central African Republic and far western Kenya
Cisticola woosnami: lowland and foothill grassland within open woodland, rocky hillsides, and riparian scrub, from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and southwestern Kenya, southward to southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, northern Zambia, and Malawi
Cistothorus apolinari: high-altitude wetlands and páramo of Boyacá to Bogotá in eastern ranges of Colombia
Cistothorus meridae: Andes of northwestern Venezuela (Trujillo and Mérida)
Cistothorus paludicola: breeds in marshes of southeastern Yukon and southern Northwest Territories southward through eastern British Colombia and eastern Alberta, central Nebraska, northern Baja California, and southern New Mexico, and disjunctly in central Mexico (Río Lerma marshes to Hidalgo and México to western Puebla); winters in interior of southwestern USA to central Mexico
Cistothorus palustris: breeds in marshes from eastern Alberta and throughout southern Canada, southward through eastern Nebraska and northeastern Kansas and Missouri to Pennsylvania, eastern US seaboard, and Gulf coast (except southern Texas and southern Florida); winters from east-central USA to Gulf Coast and northeastern Mexico
Cistothorus platensis: disjunctly in marshes, damp grasslands, shrubby vegetation, puna grasslands, and flooded savanna from mountains of central and southeastern Mexico southward to pine savanna in Belize, mountains of Guatemala to northern Nicaragua, central Costa Rica, Santa Marta and Perijá mountains, coastal mountains of Venezuela, tepuis of southern Venezuela, western Guyana, and far northern Brazil (Roraima), the Andes from western Venezuela southward to northwestern Argentina, reaching the lowlands in northern Bolivia, the Cerrado of Brazil (northern Goiás and central Minas Gerais) southward to eastern Paraguay and northern Uruguay, from central Chile and central Argentina southward to Tierra del Fuego, and the Falkland Islands
Cistothorus stellaris: breeds eastern Canada to eastern USA; winters Florida to northeastern Mexico
Cittura sanghirensis: rainforest of Sangihe and Siau islands (northeast of Sulawesi)
Cladorhynchus leucocephalus: breeds inland salt lakes of southwestern and south-central Australia; non-breeders reach southern Australia (including Tasmania)
Clamator coromandus: breeds northwestern India eastward to eastern China and southward to northern Peninsular India and southeastern Asia; winters to southern India, Sri Lanka, Greater Sundas, and Philippines
Clamator jacobinus: breeds disjunctly sub-Saharan Africa to South Africa, and northwestern India southward to southern India and Sri Lanka, and eastward to central Myanmar; winters in central and eastern Africa, and southern India and Sri Lanka
Clanga clanga: breeds central Eurasia and southern Asia; winters to Africa, China, and Indochina
Clanga pomarina: breeds locally in eastern Europe to Caspian lowlands; winters to southern Africa
Clangula hyemalis: breeds coastal Greenland (except northern), Iceland, northern Fennoscandia, northern Russia to Chukotka Peninsula, Alaska and northern Canada; winters mostly in coastal bays of northwestern Europe, northern Japan (Hokkaido and northern Honshu), and Korean Peninsula, and Aleutians to southwestern Canada
Claravis pretiosa: southeastern Mexico (San Luis Potosí) to northern Argentina and southern Brazil
Cleptornis marchei: central and southern Northern Mariana Islands (Saipan and Aguijan)
Clibanornis dendrocolaptoides: eastern Paraguay to southeastern Brazil and northeastern Argentina
Clibanornis erythrocephalus: deciduous to semi-deciduous forest in southwestern Ecuador (including the Chongon Colonche mountains in Manabí, Santa Elena, and Guayas), and northwestern Peru (southward to northern Lambayeque and western Cajamarca)
Clibanornis rectirostris: Campos of interior eastern and south-central Brazil to northeastern Paraguay
Clibanornis rubiginosus: humid montane and lowland forest on the Gulf of Mexico slope, from southern San Luis Potosí (Mexico), and the Pacific slope from Guerrero southeastward across Guatemala and adjacent El Salvador to northern Nicaragua, locally in eastern Costa Rica, western, central and eastern Panama and adjacent Colombia; in South America, west of the Andes from northwestern Colombia southward to southwestern Ecuador, and along the foothills of the central Andes and the western slope of the eastern Andes of Colombia (to Tolima and Cundinamarca); east of the Andes along the Andean foothills from southwestern Venezuela southward across Colombia and Ecuador to northwestern Bolivia (in Ecuador and Peru to the Amazon lowlands) and eastward to Acre and southern Amazonas (southwestern Brazil); also in southern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to northern Brazil (Roraima, Amapá, and eastern Amazonas)
Clibanornis rufipectus: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
Climacteris affinis: arid southern Western Australia eastward to ranges of central Australia, and eastern South Australia (western edge of Flinders Ranges), and southwestern Queenslandsouthward to southeastern South Australia
Climacteris erythrops: southeastern Australia (southeastern Queensland to Wombat Ranges, central Victoria)
Climacteris rufus: southwestern Australia (southwestern Western Australia eastward to Eyre Peninsula)
Clytoctantes alixii: northern Colombia and northwestern Venezuela (Sierra de Perijá)
Clytoctantes atrogularis: south-central Amazonian Brazil, in Rondônia, southern Amazonas, and northern Mato Grosso
Clytorhynchus sanctaecrucis: mountains of Santa Cruz Group (Temotu, southeastern Solomon Islands)
Clytorhynchus vitiensis: Fiji, Tonga, and Samoa (western to central Polynesia)
Clytospiza monteiri: patchy in lowland to foothill shrubby grassland, thickets, and fallow cultivation, from southeastern Nigeria and Cameroon eastward to southern South Sudan, Uganda, and far western Kenya, and southward to northern Angola and south-central Democratic Republic of the Congo
Cnemarchus erythropygius: treeline, shrubby paramo, and Polylepis woodland in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (rare), southward patchily along the eastern Andes of Colombia, from southern Colombia (Nariño) southward to northern Peru (Piura and Cajamarca), and in the eastern Andes from northern Peru southward to west-central Bolivia (to Cochabamba)
Cnemarchus rufipennis: dry montane scrub, cacti, grassland, rocky outcrops, and Polylepis woodland in the Andes from northern Peru (central Cajamarca and Amazonas) southward to far northern Chile and northwestern Argentina (to Tucumán)
Cnemathraupis aureodorsalis: Andes of central Peru (eastern La Libertad to San Martín and Huánuco)
Cnemathraupis eximia: humid montane forest and elfin forest in the Andes from far southwestern Venezuela southward along the Andes of Colombia to west-central Ecuador, and in the eastern Andes southward to northernmost Peru
Cnemophilus loriae: montane west-central to southeastern New Guinea
Cnemophilus macgregorii: montane west-central, east-central, and southeastern New Guinea
Cnemoscopus chrysogaster: humid montane forest in the Andes of Peru (Amazonas to Cordillera Vilcabamba in Cusco) and disjunctly in western Bolivia (near Tokoaque, in La Paz)
Cnemoscopus rubrirostris: humid montane forest in the Andes of Colombia to southwestern Venezuela (Táchira), eastern Ecuador, and northern Peru, north and west of the Marañón Valley
Cnemotriccus fuscatus: riparian thickets, scrub, river islands, and gallery forest in the lowlands of northern Colombia and western Venezuela southward to the headwaters of the Rio Magdalena, east of the Andes in the llanos of southwestern Venezuela eastward to Trinidad and Tobago, the Guianas, and Amapá (northeastern Brazil), and southward across Amazonia to southeastern Bolivia and northern Argentina (Tucuman to Corrientes); Argentine populations winter northward
Cnipodectes subbrunneus: lowlands of eastern Panama to western Colombia and western Ecuador, and southeastern Colombia to eastern Ecuador, eastern Peru, northwestern Bolivia, and western Amazonian Brazil
Cnipodectes superrufus: southwestern Amazonia in southeastern Peru, southwestern Brazil, and northwestern Bolivia
Coccopygia bocagei: foothill and submontane tall grassland, forest edge understory, and riverine woodland, in west-central Angola
Coccopygia melanotis: lowland to foothill open and brushy grassland, coastal scrub, and farmbush, from eastern and south-central Zimbabwe southward to eastern and southern South Africa, Lesotho, Eswatini, and adjacent southern Mozambique
Coccopygia quartinia: foothill and montane undergrowth, forest edge, rocky scrub or dense grass, from Eritrea and Ethiopia southward through east Africa to eastern Zimbabwe and adjacent Mozambique
Coccothraustes coccothraustes: lowland to submontane deciduous woodland, mixed broadleaf and coniferous forest, riverine forest, parks, and gardens, from Britain and southern Scandinavia eastward to Kamchatka and northern Japan, and southward to northwestern Africa, southern Europe, Caucasus, Tajikistan, central Afghanistan, and North Korea; some northern populations migrate to northern Africa, Middle East, northern Pakistan, southern China, and Japan
Coccycua cinerea: breeds Paraguay, northern Argentina, southern Brazil, and Uruguay; winters northward at least to Bolivia and western Brazil south of the Amazon River, rarely to eastern Peru and southeastern Colombia
Coccycua minuta: humid forest, borders, thickets and mangrove from eastern Panama eastward to northern Colombia and western Venezuela, in central Colombia southward to the headwaters of the Río Magdalena and Río Cauca; also in southwestern Colombia and western Ecuador; east of the Andes from northern Venezuela, Trinidad and the Guianas southward across the entire Amazon basin to central and eastern Bolivia, and in Brazil southward to southern Mato Grosso do Sul (and adjacent Paraguay) and west-central São Paulo, and eastward to eastern Maranhão, Tocantins, Goiás and adjacent Minas Gerais
Coccycua pumila: tropical northern and western Colombia and far northern Ecuador to northeastern Venezuela; rare eastern Panama
Coccyzus americanus: breeds Canada to Mexico and West Indies; winters to northern Argentina
Coccyzus erythropthalmus: breeds eastern North America; winters to Bolivia
Coccyzus euleri: locally from northern South America to southern Brazil and northeastern Argentina
Coccyzus lansbergi: breeds northern Colombia and northern Venezuela; migrates to western Peru
Coccyzus longirostris: varied woodland from lowlands to mountains of Hispaniola and satellite islands
Coccyzus melacoryphus: Venezuela to the Guianas, Brazil, northern Argentina, and Galapagos
Coccyzus merlini: wooded areas of lowlands and hills of central Bahamas, in Andros and Eleuthera, and at least formerly New Providence; Cuba and satellite islands
Coccyzus minor: locally from southern Florida to coastal northern Brazil
Cochlearius cochlearius: west-central and tropical eastern Mexico to the Guianas, Amazon basin, and northeastern Argentina
Cochoa azurea: mountains of western and central Java
Cochoa purpurea: montane forest of Himalayas from northern India (Uttarakhand) eastward to western Arunachal Pradesh and southern Assam hills, eastern Myanmar, south-central China (southern Sichuan and Yunnan), northwestern Thailand, northern Laos, and northern Vietnam (northern Tonkin)
Cochoa viridis: montane forest of eastern Himalayas from northeastern India (Sikkim and northern West Bengal to Arunachal Pradesh and southern Assam hills), western and eastern Myanmar, southern and eastern China (southern Yunnan and Fujian), western, northern, and southeastern Thailand, southwestern and eastern Cambodia, Laos, and Vietnam (Tonkin and Annam)
Coeligena bonapartei: eastern Andes of Colombia (Boyacá to Bogotá)
Coeligena coeligena: montane cloudforest in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Falcón eastward to Miranda), the Sierra de Perijá, and Andes of western Venezuela southward in the western, central, and eastern Andes of Colombia, to the eastern Andes of Ecuador, Peru, and central Bolivia (to western Santa Cruz)
Coeligena conradii: eastern Andes of Colombia to northwestern Venezuela (Trujillo and Mérida)
Coeligena eos: Andes of western Venezuela (Trujillo, Barinas, Mérida, and Táchira)
Coeligena helianthea: montane cloudforest and treeline in the Andes of northeastern Colombia and adjacent Venezuela
Coeligena inca: cloudforest of east slope of Andes from southeastern Peru through west-central Bolivia
Coeligena iris: Andes of south-central Ecuador (Cuenca) to northern Peru (west of Río Marañón in Cajamarca and La Libertad)
Coeligena lutetiae: montane cloudforest and treeline in the central Andes of Colombia, from Caldas, southward to northwestern Ecuador (southward to Bolívar) and south in the eastern Andes of Ecuador to far northern Peru, in Cajamarca and Piura
Coeligena phalerata: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
Coeligena prunellei: montane forest and edge of west slope of eastern Andes of Colombia and both slopes of Serranía de los Yariguíes (Santander, north-central Colombia)
Coeligena torquata: montane cloudforest in the Andes of far southwestern Venezuela southwestward across the western, central, and eastern Andes of Colombia to northern Peru north of the Río Marañón, and the eastern Andes of Peru south of the Marañón southward to southern Peru (Cusco)
Coeligena violifer: cloudforest and elfin forest of east slope of Andes from northern Peru through northwestern Bolivia
Coeligena wilsoni: Andes of southwestern Colombia and western Ecuador
Coenocorypha aucklandica: Antipodes Islands (southeast of Stewart Island) and Auckland and Campbell islands (south of South Island; New Zealand)
Coenocorypha barrierensis: formerly North Island (subfossils only); historically known only from Little Barrier Island (off northeastern North Island), New Zealand; extinct, last recorded 1870
Coenocorypha huegeli: Snares Islands (Northeast, Broughton, and Alert Stack), south of New Zealand; introduced to Codfish Island, off Stewart Island
Coenocorypha iredalei: formerly South and Stewart islands (subfossils only); historically known only from islands off Stewart Island (New Zealand); apparently extinct, last recorded 1964
Coenocorypha pusilla: Rangatira, Mangere, Little Mangere, and Rabbit islands, and Star Keys, Chatham Islands; originally found throughout Chatham Islands

Columba versicolor: formerly Ogasawara (Bonin) Islands; extinct, last reported 1889

Corvinella corvina: savanna to gardens of lowlands to highlands from southern Mauritania eastward to southern Sudan, and in south to Uganda and western Kenya
Corvus albicollis: lowland to montane grassland, gorges, and open hill woodland, from Uganda and Kenya southward through eastern Zambia, western Mozambique, and Zimbabwe to eastern and southern South Africa; post-breeding nomadic vagrants have reached southwestern Sudan and Namibia
Corvus albus: lowland to montane open country, including grasslands, open woodlands, savanna, rubbish dumps, villages, and towns, throughout sub-Saharan Africa, from Western Sahara and Sudan southward to South Africa, and on Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), Pemba and Unguja (in Zanzibar), Mafia (off Tanzania), Comoro Islands, Aldabra, Glorieuses Islands, and Madagascar; some seasonal dispersal
Corvus bennetti: semiarid Australia (mainland except tropical north, wetter east, southeast, and southwest)
Corvus brachyrhynchos: varied habitats from forest and woodland to open fields and cities from southern coastal Alaska, and southern Northwest Territories eastward to southern Labrador (northwestern to northeastern Canada) southward to far northern Baja California, southern Texas, and southern Florida; introduced Bermuda
Corvus capensis: open country over wide altitudinal range, disjunctly in northeastern Africa from Eritrea through northern Tanzania, and from Angola and Zimbabwe through South Africa
Corvus celebensis: Sulawesi region, including Talaud, Togian, and Tukangbesi islands; population in the Banggai Islands probably this subspecies (but possibly is Corvus enca mangoli)
Corvus corax: Holarctic, from Arctic Circle southward in mountains of Old World to northern Africa, Middle East, northern Indian Subcontinent, and the Kurile Islands; in the New World southward in mountains to northwestern Nicaragua and northern Georgia (southeastern USA)
Corvus corone: disjunctly in lowland to montane open habitats, from coastal cliff to grassland to farmland and forest edge, from Britain and Europe southward to Italy, Nile Valley in Egypt, and Iran and eastward to Kamchatka, and southward to eastern Iran, central China, Korean Peninsula, and Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu); northernmost populations migrate southward
Corvus coronoides: wooded habitats of southwestern, far southern coastal, and central to eastern Australia (except Cape York Peninsula and Tasmania)
Corvus crassirostris: foothill to montane open and wooded highlands, escarpments and sheer cliffs, cultivation, towns, and cities, in Eritrea and Ethiopia highlands; some post-breeding nomads have reached South Sudan and northwestern Somali
Corvus cryptoleucus: arid southwestern USA to central Mexico
Corvus edithae: lowland to submontane open country, including desert, brushy semi-desert, dry savanna, inshore islets, and villages, from eastern Eritrea, Djibouti, and northern Somalia southward to far southeastern South Sudan, northern Kenya, and southern Somalia
Corvus enca: lowland to foothill forest, secondary growth, plantations, and cultivation, from peninsula Malaysia, Sumatra and satellite islands, eastward to Borneo, Java, and Bali
Corvus florensis: lowlands and low hills of western Flores (western Lesser Sundas)
Corvus frugilegus: lowland to foothill flat open country, farmland, grassland, city parks, and villages, from British Isles and southern Scandinavia eastward to central Siberia, and southward to France, Türkiye, northern Afghanistan, and central China; northern and eastern populations migrate in winter to central Europe eastward to Korean Peninsula, Japan (Honshu to Kyushu), and southeastern China; introduced in New Zealand
Corvus fuscicapillus: western New Guinea including Waigeo and Gam (west Papuan islands) and Aru Islands (off southwestern New Guinea)
Corvus hawaiiensis: montane forest of Hawaii; extinct in the wild but reintroduced to Maui in 2024
Corvus imparatus: southern Texas (lower Río Grande Valley) to southeastern Mexico (northern Veracruz)
Corvus kubaryi: Rota (southern Northern Mariana Islands) and formerly Guam (where extirpated; southern Mariana Islands, western Micronesia)
Corvus leucognaphalus: Hispaniola; casual on Gonâve and Saona
Corvus macrorhynchos: lowland to montane woodland, coastal open scrub, alpine meadows above tree-line, agriculture, and urban landscape, from northeastern Afghanistan eastward through Himalayas to eastern China (including Hainan), Taiwan, and to Amurland (Russia), Sakhalin, and Japan, and southward to Peninsular India, Sri Lanka, Andaman Islands, Sumatra, southern Borneo, and Java eastward to Romang and Sermata (eastern Lesser Sundas)
Corvus meeki: Bougainville, Buka, and Shortland Islands (northwestern Solomon Islands)
Corvus mellori: southeastern Australia (northern New South Wales to Eyre Peninsula)
Corvus moneduloides: Grande Terre and (introduced) Loyalty Islands (New Caledonia)
Corvus nasicus: Cuba including Isla de la Juventud, and southern Bahamas (Caicos Islands)
Corvus orru: mostly open or edge habitats in lowlands and hills from northern Moluccas and Babar (eastern Lesser Sundas) eastward through New Guinea, including Trobriand Islands and Louisiade Archipelago (off southeastern New Guinea), southward through Australia (except far southwest, far southeast, and Tasmania)
Corvus ossifragus: eastern USA (New England to eastern Texas)
Corvus pusillus: southern Philippines (Balabac, Culion, Mindoro, and Palawan)
Corvus rhipidurus: patchy in lowland to submontane desert, arid cliffs and canyons, oases, and villages, from eastern Mali eastward through African Sahel to northern Somalia, and southward to northern Central African Republic, northern Uganda, and central Kenya, and in Middle East from Levant and Sinai (Egypt) southward to southwestern Arabia; some seasonal dispersal
Corvus ruficollis: lowland to submontane desert plains, semi-desert, dry savanna, rubbish dumps, and dry cultivation, throughout northern Africa southward to Mauritania, northern Nigeria, and Eritrea, and eastward through Arabia to southern Kazakhstan and western Pakistan, and on Cabo Verde and Socotra (off Somalia); some seasonal dispersal
Corvus sierramadrensis: northern Philippines (Sierra Madre mountains of Luzon)
Corvus sinaloae: coastal lowlands of western Mexico (southern Sonora to western Nayarit)
Corvus splendens: lowland to foothill open habitats, predominately around human habitation, from city parks to coastal villages, from southeastern Iran eastward through India and southern Tibet to western Myanmar, and southward to Sri Lanka, and Lakshadweep and Maldive islands; short-distance dispersal comm; introduced and feral populations widespread, including east Africa, Middle East, Indian Ocean islands, southeastern Asia, and Australia
Corvus tasmanicus: varied mostly wooded habitats of far east-central and far southeastern Australia including islands of Bass Strait and Tasmania
Corvus torquatus: central and eastern China to northern Vietnam; Hainan and Taiwan
Corvus tristis: New Guinea, including west Papuan Islands, Yapen (Cenderawasih Bay), and D'Entrecasteaux Archipelago (off southeastern New Guinea)
Corvus typicus: montane central and southern Sulawesi, including islands to southeast
Corvus unicolor: Peleng, in Banggai Islands (off eastern Sulawesi)
Corvus violaceus: Seram and Ambon, and possibly Buru (central Moluccas)
Corvus woodfordi: Choiseul, Isabel, and Guadalcanal (central Solomon Islands)
Corydon sumatranus: lowland to foothill primary forest, and dipterocarp and swamp forest, from southern Myanmar and Laos southward to Sumatra, North Natuna Islands, and Borneo
Corypha africana: savanna, open grassland with trees, grassy fynbos, and bare ground from northern Uganda, adjacent Democratic Republic of Congo, and western Kenya southward to Zambia, northwestern Mozambique, and adjacent Malawi, and from southern Democratic Republic of Congo and northern Angola southward to central Namibia and Botswana to southern South Africa and southern Mozambique
Corypha apiata: lowland and foothill Fynbos, shrubland, and Karoo scrub, from southwestern Namibia southward to coastal western and southwestern South Africa (and inland eastward to Northern Cape and western Eastern Cape)
Corypha athi: grassy fields in south-central Kenya and north-central Tanzania
Corypha fasciolata: lowland and foothill rocky tall grassland, and semiarid grasslands in Kalahari Desert, from western Zambia (and possibly southeastern Angola), southward to south-central South Africa
Corypha hypermetra: savanna and grassland with scattered trees from central Ethiopia southward through Kenya to northern Tanzania, and in southern Somalia
Corypha kabalii: grassy fields with sparse open areas from southeastern Gabon southward to eastern Angola and western Zambia
Corypha kidepoensis: savanna and grassland with scattered trees in southwestern Ethiopia and adjacent South Sudan, in northeastern Uganda, and far southeastern South Sudan
Corypha kurrae: grassy fields sparsely in western Africa, from southern Guinea, Sierra Leone, Liberia, and adjacent Ivory Coast, north-central Cameroon, Nigeria, southern Niger, southern Chad, and southwestern Sudan
Corypha nigrescens: grassy fields in the Kitulu and Nyika plateaus of southern Tanzania, northern Malawi, and adjacent Zambia
Corypha sharpii: patchy in lowland to foothill open grassy plains, and open dry woodland, in northwestern Somalia, with one record in adjacent northeastern Ethiopia
Corypha somalica: lowland open grassland, often on red sand, of Somalia and adjacent eastern Ethiopia
Coryphaspiza melanotis: tall grass in lowlands and plateaus of southern Amazonia from southeastern Peru and northern Bolivia northeastward through southern Amazonas and northeastern Pará (northeastern Brazil), and in the south through southeastern Paraguay, northeastern Argentina (no recent records?), and southeastern Brazil; generally rare
Coryphistera alaudina: arid lowland scrub, monte, and Chaco woodland from southeastern Bolivia and Paraguay southward across Argentina, western Uruguay, and southernmost Brazil (Rio Grande do Sul) to east-central Argentina, to southern Buenos Aires and adjacent La Pampa
Coryphospingus cucullatus: locally from southern Colombia eastward to the Guianas, and southward to central Argentina
Coryphospingus pileatus: Colombia in upper Magdalena Valley and arid northern Colombia and Venezuela, and east-central Brazil (Ceará and Piauí to Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro)
Corythaeola cristata: lowland rainforest of western and central Africa
Corythopis delalandi: southern Brazil to eastern Bolivia, eastern Paraguay, and northeastern Argentina
Corythopis torquatus: tropical rainforest in the Río Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southwest and southward across the entire Amazon basin to eastern Ecuador and Peru, central Bolivia, central Mato Grosso, western Tocantins, eastern Pará and adjacent Maranhão
Corythornis cristatus: lowland to montane marsh, lakes, large rivers, tidal estuaries, and mangroves, from Senegambia eastward through Nigeria, and São Tomé and Príncipe (Gulf of Guinea) to central Sudan, Eritrea, and (recently) Yemen, Arabian Peninsula, and southward to South Africa; some populations probably migratory to Somalia and southern Arabian Peninsula
Corythornis leucogaster: lowland and foothill forest, wooded and mangrove swamps, and tidal estuaries, from southwestern Mali and Guinea eastward through southern Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to southern Uganda and far northwestern Tanzania, and southward to northwestern Angola, southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northwestern Zambia
Corythornis vintsioides: central and southeastern Comoros and Madagascar
Coscoroba coscoroba: southern Brazil to Paraguay, Uruguay, Tierra del Fuego, and Falkland Islands
Cossypha albicapillus: lowland to montane riverine thickets, wooded dry savanna, and gallery forest, from Senegambia eastward to northern Cameroon, western Central African Republic, and southern Chad, and in southeastern South Sudan and western Ethiopia; some movement in the Sahel with rains
Cossypha cyanocampter: patchy in lowland to montane forest understory, wooded ravines, and coastal thickets, from eastern Guinea and Sierra Leone eastward to Central African Republic, and southward to Gabon and western Republic of the Congo, and from southern South Sudan southward to Uganda, western Kenya, and northwestern Tanzania
Cossypha dichroa: lowland to montane evergreen cloudforest, and coastal forest, in eastern and southern South Africa, and in Lesotho and Eswatini; partial altitudinal migrant
Cossypha heinrichi: disjunctly and local in dense forest understory, and gallery forest in savanna, in southwestern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and in northwestern Angola
Cossypha heuglini: lowland to montane forest edge, termitaria thickets in riverine forest, and acacia woodland, from northern Cameroon and southern Chad eastward to Ethiopia and Somalia, thence southward to western Angola and eastern South Africa
Cossypha natalensis: patchy in lowland and foothill forest, open woodland in thornbush, and dune forest, from central Nigeria eastward to Ethiopia and western Somalia, southward to northeastern Namibia, southern Mozambique, and eastern and southern South Africa; partial intra-African migrant
Cossypha niveicapilla: lowland to montane savanna thickets, riverine scrub, and coastal scrub, from southern Mauritania eastward to central Ethiopia, and southward to northwestern Angola, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, northwestern Tanzania, and the Lake Victoria basin
Cossypha semirufa: foothill to montane evergreen forest understory, riverine thickets, and shrubby gardens, from Eritrea, Ethiopia, and South Sudan southward to southern Kenya and northern Tanzania
Cossyphicula isabellae: mid-elevation and montane forest understory and wooded ravines from eastern Nigeria and western Cameroon southward to southwestern Cameroon
Cossyphicula roberti: disjunctly in foothill and montane forest understory in eastern Nigeria, western Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) and in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and Rwanda
Cotinga amabilis: Gulf lowlands of southern Mexico (Veracruz) to southeastern Costa Rica
Cotinga cayana: southern Venezuela and the Guianas to northern Bolivia and Amazonian Brazil
Cotinga cotinga: eastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, the Guianas, and northern and eastern Amazonian Brazil
Cotinga maculata: southeastern Brazil (southern Bahia and Minas Gerais to Rio de Janeiro)
Cotinga maynana: lowlands of southeastern Colombia to northern Bolivia and western Amazonian Brazil
Cotinga nattererii: central Panama to Colombia, northwestern Ecuador, and western Venezuela
Cotinga ridgwayi: Pacific slope of southwestern Costa Rica to western Panama (western Chiriquí)
Coturnicops exquisitus: breeds eastern Russia (southeastern Transbaikalia and southern Ussuriland), northeastern China (eastern Heilongjiang), and probably northern Japan (Hokkaido and northernmost Honshu); winters very locally from Korean Peninsula, Japan (including Ryukyu Islands), and southeastern China
Coturnicops noveboracensis: sedge meadows, brackish marshes and shrubby marshes in north-central and western Canada, from southern Northwest Territories and southern Alberta eastward to southeastern Canada and southward to north-central US in North Dakota, adjacent Montana, northern Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, northernmost New York and northern Maine; also locally in mountains of northern California and southern Oregon; formerly in central Mexico; winters in the southeastern Atlantic coast from North Carolina southward to southern Florida and the Gulf of Mexico coast, and in the central coast of California
Coturnix coromandelica: Pakistan to Myanmar and western Thailand
Coturnix coturnix: breeds Europe (including Atlantic islands) eastward to Mongolia and Bhutan, and southward to southern Africa, the Comoros, and Madagascar; northern populations migrate to Sahel zone; introduced Mauritius and Réunion (Mascarenes)
Coturnix delegorguei: patchy in grassland and lightly wooded savanna in sub-Saharan Africa from Chad, Cameroon and São Tomé (Gulf of Guinea) eastward to Ethiopia, thence southward to Angola and northern Namibia to eastern South Africa (avoiding rainforest and arid southwestern Africa), plus southwestern Arabian Peninsula and western Madagascar; movements associated with rain and nomadic, westward to Ivory Coast
Coturnix japonica: breeds in eastern Asia, from northern Mongolia northeastward through Baikal region to Vitim region of east-central Russia, eastward to Sakhalin, and southward to Japan (to central Honshu), Korean Peninsula, and northeastern China (eastern Shandong); also (presumably) in Bhutan and Myanmar; winters southward from central Japan and central China westward through northwestern Thailand and northern Myanmar to Bhutan and Assam, with small numbers as far northward as Buryatia and Ussuriland (Russia) in mild winters; introduced to Hawaiian Islands (Kauai and Hawaii, where now rare)
Coturnix novaezelandiae: formerly New Zealand; extinct, last reported 1875
Coturnix pectoralis: Australia including Tasmania, but not far north (Kimberley region of northern Northern Territory, and Cape York Peninsula)
Coua caerulea: rainforest of northwestern and eastern Madagascar
Coua coquereli: humid and dry deciduous forest of western Madagascar
Coua cursor: semiarid lowland forest of southwestern Madagascar
Coua gigas: thinly distributed in forest and savanna of western and southern Madagascar
Coua reynaudii: humid forest of northern and eastern Madagascar
Coua verreauxi: locally in subdesert of southwestern Madagascar
Cracticus louisiadensis: Tagula (Louisiade Archipelago, off southeastern New Guinea)
Cracticus mentalis: south-central and southeastern New Guinea and Cape York Peninsula (northeastern Australia)
Cranioleuca albicapilla: semi-humid shrubland and woodland in the Andes of central and southern Peru, from Junín southeastward to Apurimac, Ayacucho and Cusco
Cranioleuca albiceps: montane cloudforest, elfin forest and treeline in the Andes of far southeastern Peru (Pasco) and Bolivia, southeastward to westernmost Santa Cruz
Cranioleuca antisiensis: semi-humid to humid montane forest and woodland, Polylepis woodland, semi-humid scrub in the western Andes (locally in the eastern Andes) from southern Ecuador, from southern Chimborazo, southward to west-central Peru, in Lima; in the eastern Andes of Peru from Amazonas, south and east of the Río Marañón, to Huánuco and Pasco
Cranioleuca berlepschi: Andes of northern Peru (Amazonas to La Libertad)
Cranioleuca curtata: montane cloudforest and foothill forest in the Andes from northern Colombia, on the western slope of the eastern Andes from Santander southward to Huila, and the eastern slope of the eastern Andes from eastern Cundinamarca southward across the eastern Andes of Ecuador and Peru to central Bolivia (La Paz and Cochabamba)
Cranioleuca demissa: tepuis of southern Venezuela, adjacent Guyana, and northern Brazil (northern Roraima)
Cranioleuca erythrops: humid lower montane hill and montane forest of northwestern Costa Rica through western Panama, disjunctly in far eastern Panama and western Andes, and west slope of central Andes of Colombia southward through western Ecuador, including coastal Cordillera de Mache
Cranioleuca hellmayri: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
Cranioleuca henricae: Andes of northern Bolivia (Río La Paz drainage system)
Cranioleuca marcapatae: southern Peru in Vilcanota and Carabaya Ranges (Cusco)
Cranioleuca muelleri: lower Amazonian Brazil and Mexiana Island
Cranioleuca obsoleta: eastern Paraguay to southeastern Brazil (São Paulo) and northeastern Argentina
Cranioleuca pallida: mountains of southeastern Brazil (Brasília to Espírito Santo and southeastern São Paulo)
Cranioleuca pyrrhophia: deciduous forest, semi-deciduous, to arid scrub and woodland from the eastern foothills of the Andes of central Bolivia (La Paz and Cochabamba), southeastward to the Chaco of southestern Bolivia, western Paraguay, and northern Argentina (to northern Neuquén and Río Negro and southern Buenos Aires); eastward to southernmost Brazil (Rio Grande do Sul), and Uruguay
Cranioleuca semicinerea: deciduous to semi-deciduous forest from northeastern Brazil, in Ceará, southwestward across interior Brazil to northern Minas Gerais and central Goiás
Cranioleuca subcristata: humid montane forest and woodland in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela from Falcón and western Zulia eastward to the Paría Peninsula in Sucre, and in the Sierra de Perijá and Andes of western Venezuela southward to the foothills of the eastern Andes in northeastern Colombia (southward to northern Meta)
Cranioleuca vulpecula: river islands in Amazon system from eastern Brazil to eastern Peru
Cranioleuca vulpina: riparian woodland, scrub and thickets, gallery forest and river islands from the lower Río Orinoco in northeastern Venezuela southwestward to the llanos of western and southwestern Venezuela and northeastern Colombia (southward to Guaviare); along the Amazon River from far eastern Peru and southeastern Colombia eastward across Brazil to Pará, northward to northern Roraima and adjacent Guyana, and more widespread south of the Amazon River in central and eastern Brazil, eastward to Piauí, northern and western Bahia, and southeastward to São Paulo and northern Paraná; in central Brazil also southward to Acre, Rondônia and southern Mato Grosso, to southeastern Peru (Ucayali), northern Bolivia (southward to northwestern Santa Cruz and adjacent Cochabamba), and far northern Paraguay
Cranioleuca weskei: Andes of south-central Peru (Mantaro Valley in southeastern Junín, northern Ayacucho, and southward to Cordillera Vilcabamba in Cusco)
Crax blumenbachii: lowland forest of southeastern Brazil; on verge of extinction
Crax daubentoni: llanos of northeastern Colombia and adjacent northern Venezuela
Crax globulosa: humid southeastern Colombia to northern Bolivia and western Amazonian Brazil
Crax rubra: humid rainforest and drier woodland from lowlands to hills on Caribbean slope from central Tamaulipas (northeastern Mexico) southward through both slopes from Chiapas (southeastern Mexico) including Yucatan Peninsula and Cozumel through Panama, and west of the Andes to western Ecuador
Creagrus furcatus: breeds Galapagos and Malpelo Island (far west of Colombia); winters to Humboldt Current off Ecuador to northern Chile
Creatophora cinerea: lowland to foothill lightly wooded savanna, arid grassland, and cultivation, widespread in eastern and southern Africa, from Eritrea and Somalia southward through southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Angola, and Zambia, to South Africa; nomadic post-breeding, has reached Cameroon
Crecopsis egregia: sub-Saharan Africa from Senegal eastward to Kenya and southward to northern and eastern South Africa, except in driest areas
Creurgops dentatus: Andes of southeastern Peru to western Bolivia (La Paz and Cochabamba)
Creurgops verticalis: Andes of Colombia to southwestern Venezuela and eastern Peru (Ayacucho)
Crex crex: breeds British Isles eastward to northwestern China and central Siberia, and southward from central Europe, the Caucasus, Kyrgyzstan, northwestern Xinjiang (northwestern China), and northern Mongolia; winters mainly from eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and southern Tanzania southward to eastern South Africa
Crinifer concolor: lowland and foothill thornscrub, wooded savanna, and acacia and riparian woodland, from western Angola eastward to southern Tanzania, and southward to southern Namibia and eastern South Africa
Crinifer leucogaster: acacia savanna of Somalia and Ethiopia to northeastern Tanzania
Crinifer personatus: disjunctly in Ethiopian Rift Valley, from Dire Dawa and Ankober southward to Lake Abaya and Yabelo (Yavello); and southern Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, southwest Kenya, and Tanzania southward to northern Malawi, northeast Zambia, and southeast Democratic Republic of Congo
Crinifer piscator: acacia savanna of Senegambia to Central African Republic and western Democratic Republic of the Congo
Crinifer zonurus: acacia savanna of central and east Africa
Criniger barbatus: lowland, swamps, and gallery forest, from Sierra Leone and southeastern Guinea eastward to southern Nigeria
Criniger calurus: lowland to foothill forest, gallery forest and wooded savanna, from southwestern Senegal eastward through southern Nigeria and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to Uganda, thence southward through Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northern Angola
Criniger chloronotus: lowland to foothill primary forest, and swamp-forest, from southwestern Nigeria eastward to Central African Republic and western Uganda, and southward to far western, central, and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Criniger ndussumensis: lowland primary and old secondary evergreen and semi-deciduous forest, and swamp-forest, from southeastern Nigeria eastward to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and southward to far western and central Democratic Republic of the Congo
Criniger olivaceus: lowland to foothill Upper Guinea rainforest, old secondary rainforest, and gallery forest, from Sierra Leone and southeastern Guinea eastward to southern Ghana
Crithagra albogularis: lowland dry grassland, savanna, thornscrub, and coastal Fynbos from southern Angola southward through Namibia and southwestern Botswana to western and central South Africa and Lesotho; nomadic wandering seasonally
Crithagra ankoberensis: submontane to montane cliffs and escarpments with vertical bare rock faces, open highland grassland, and stunted tree-heath, in northern and central Ethiopia
Crithagra atrogularis: patchy in lowland savanna, acacia thornscrub, grassland near water, and miombo from southeastern Gabon eastward (avoiding Congolian rainforest) to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and southeastern Kenya, southward through Angola, Zambia, and Zimbabwe, to Namibia, Botswana, and western and central South Africa, eastward to northeastern South Africa and Lesotho
Crithagra buchanani: lowland to foothill dry thornscrub, acacia savanna, scrub, and grazed grassland, in southern Kenya and northeastern Tanzania
Crithagra burtoni: undergrowth of montane forest, alpine grassland, and lightly wooded heath in four disjunct areas: southeastern Nigeria, western Cameroon, and Bioko, Gulf of Guinea; northwestern Angola; from eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to western Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, and northwestern Tanzania; and from northeastern Uganda eastward to northern Kenya and southward to northern Tanzania
Crithagra canicapilla: patchily distributed in wooded savanna, farmbush, and montane dry forest from Guinea and Sierra Leone eastward to eastern Nigeria and Cameroon, and from southern Chad, Central African Republic, and southern South Sudan to northeastern Uganda and western Kenya; partly migratory in non-breeding season
Crithagra capistrata: lowland and foothill primary and secondary forest, marsh, and brushy grassland from Gabon and Republic of the Congo eastward (avoiding Congolian rainforest) to easternmost Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Burundi, southward to western Angola, southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northern Zambia
Crithagra citrinelloides: wet montane grassland and forest edges disjunctly from Eritrea and Ethiopia to western Kenya
Crithagra citrinipectus: patchy in lowland to foothill palm savanna, dry miombo and mopane woodland, scrub, and semiarid grassland, from southern Malawi, eastern Zimbabwe, and Mozambique southward to southeastern South Africa; nomadic post-breeding
Crithagra donaldsoni: lowland to foothill arid savanna, acacia thornscrub, and semi-desert scrub, from east-central Ethiopia and Somalia southward to central Kenya; nomadic post-breeding
Crithagra dorsostriata: lowland to montane grassland, lightly wooded savanna, and thornscrub from southeastern South Sudan, central Ethiopia, and Somalia, southward through Uganda and Kenya to central Tanzania; dry-season nomad
Crithagra flavigula: patchy in foothill and submontane semiarid desert, steep rocky scrub, acacia thornbush, and tussock grassland, in central Ethiopia
Crithagra flaviventris: lowland to montane scrub, open woodland, grassland, and dune Fynbos from southwestern Angola, Namibia, and Botswana southward to western, southern, and central South Africa, Eswatini, and Lesotho, nomadic in non-breeding season; introduced (nominate race) on Ascension and St. Helena islands (south Atlantic Ocean)
Crithagra frontalis: foothill to montane grassland, forest clearings, secondary forest, marsh, bracken-briar, cultivation, and gardens, from eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to Uganda and southwestern Kenya, and southward to western Tanzania and northeastern Zambia
Crithagra gularis: patchy in lowland to submontane scrub, savanna and miombo, and Fynbos from central Angola and northeastern Namibia eastward to northwestern Mozambique, then southward through Zimbabwe and northeast Botswana to eastern and southern South Africa, avoiding Namib and Kalahari deserts; partially migratory in non-breeding season
Crithagra hyposticta: foothill and montane forest, bracken-brier, and eucalypt plantations disjunctly from southern South Sudan and (reported) central Ethiopia, and from northwest Uganda and western Kenya southward through southern Kenya and eastern and southern Tanzania, Malawi, adjacent Zambia, and northern Mozambique
Crithagra koliensis: patchy in foothill papyrus swamp from Uganda and southwestern Kenya southward to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and northwestern Tanzania
Crithagra leucoptera: lowland to foothill fynbos, protea thickets, semiarid scrub, and open woodland, in southwestern South Africa
Crithagra leucopygia: lowland to foothill lightly wooded savanna and acacia thornscrub across the Sahel from southern Mauritania and Senegal eastward through southern Algeria to Sudan and Eritrea, thence southward to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and northwestern Uganda
Crithagra melanochroa: foothill to montane forest and brushy scrub in Iringa and Njombe highlands (southern Tanzania)
Crithagra menachensis: foothill to montane dry scrub, rocky hillsides, stony plateaus, and in villages and towns, in southwestern Saudi Arabia, western Yemen, and far western Oman
Crithagra mennelli: patchy in lowland to montane dry woodland, miombo woodland, coastal forest, and eucalypt plantations, from eastern Angola, southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Tanzania southward to Zimbabwe and Mozambique; nomadic post-breeding
Crithagra mozambica: sub-Saharan Africa from southern Mauritania and Senegal eastward to Eritrea and Ethiopia, southward (but avoiding rainforest) from Cameroon, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and western Kenya, to Angola, northeastern Namibia, northern Botswana, Zambia, and Mozambique (avoiding Namib and Kalahari deserts), and thence southward through Zimbabwe to eastern South Africa, widely nomadic in non-breeding season; introduced in São Tomé (Gulf of Guinea), Mafia Island (Tanzania), Mascarenes, Hawaiian Islands (mainly Oahu and Hawaii), and Puerto Rico
Crithagra reichardi: foothill to submontane miombo and teak woodland from central and western Tanzania and southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo southward to Zambia, Malawi, and disjunctly in northern Mozambique
Crithagra reichenowi: lowland to submontane arid bushy scrub, thornscrub, open woodland, and cultivation edges, from Ethiopia, southeastern South Sudan, and Somalia southward to eastern and southern Tanzania

Cyanoramphus novaezelandiae: North and Stewart islands and satellite islands, Chatham Islands (east of South Island) and Auckland Islands (south of South Island; New Zealand)
