Eremomela turneri: disjunctly in foothill and montane forest edge, and secondary growth of east-central Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Kenya; old record from southwestern Uganda
Eremomela usticollis: lowland and foothill acacia and miombo woodland, and riverine thornscrub, from southern Angola eastward to central northwestern Zambia, and southern Malawi, thence southward to northern Namibia and northeastern South Africa
Eremophila alpestris: Holarctic, in Old World from Arctic Circle southward to northern Africa, Iran, and the Himalayas, and eastward to eastern Russia and Inner Mongolia; in New World from Arctic southward to central Mexico, and disjunctly in central Colombia
Eremophila bilopha: desert of North Africa to northern Arabia and southwestern Iraq
Eremopterix australis: lowland to foothill shrubby grassland, and Karoo, from southern Namibia and southwestern Botswana southward to western and central South Africa; nomadic wandering in response to rainfall
Eremopterix griseus: grassland and stony plains of Indian subcontinent
Eremopterix leucopareia: lowland to foothill semiarid grassland and barren terrain, from northeastern Uganda and Kenya southward to northeastern Zambia, northern Malawi, and adjacent northwestern Mozambique; some post-breeding seasonal dispersal
Eremopterix leucotis: disjunctly in lowland to foothill semiarid savanna, short grassland, and burnt areas, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward across the Sahel to Sudan, Ethiopia, and western Somalia, thence southward to Kenya and Tanzania, and from southern Angola eastward to northern Mozambique, thence southward to eastern South Africa and Eswatini; nomadic with rains
Eremopterix nigriceps: arid and semiarid plains with scattered vegetation from Cabo Verde and Western Sahara eastward across the Saharan desert to eastern Africa from the Red Sea coast southward to Ethiopia and southern Somalia, and on the Arabian Peninsula (including Socotra), southern Israel, and southern Iraq eastward to southern Iran and western India
Eremopterix signatus: lowland to montane arid plains, grassy savanna, and open woodland, from southeastern South Sudan, southern and eastern Ethiopia, and Somalia southward to eastern Kenya
Eremopterix verticalis: lowland semiarid savanna, sparse shrubland, and open coastal plains, from coastal Angola (including Cabinda) and southwestern Zambia southward to western to northeastern South Africa; nomadic with rains and periodically irruptive
Eriocnemis aline: montane cloudforest in the eastern Andes and southern part of the central Andes of Colombia southward across Ecuador to south-central Peru, to Pasco
Eriocnemis cupreoventris: eastern Andes of Colombia and northwestern Venezuela (Mérida)
Eriocnemis derbyi: central Andes of Colombia and northwestern Ecuador
Eriocnemis glaucopoides: Andes of southern Bolivia and northwestern Argentina
Eriocnemis godini: Andes of northwestern Ecuador (northern Pichincha) and (?) southwestern Colombia; extremely rare, with no recent reports, and possibly not a valid species
Eriocnemis isabellae: Serranía del Pinche, southwestern Cauca, Colombia
Eriocnemis luciani: montane cloudforest and elfin forest in the Andes from southern Colombia southward to southern Ecuador, and in the eastern Andes of Peru south of the Río Marañón, southward to far northeastern Bolivia (La Paz)
Eriocnemis mirabilis: west slope of western Andes of Colombia (Cauca)
Eriocnemis mosquera: southwestern and central Andes of Colombia to northwestern Ecuador
Eriocnemis nigrivestis: Andes of northern Ecuador (Pichincha, Atacazo, and Imbabura)
Eriocnemis vestita: montane cloudforest in the Andes from western Venezuela southward in the western, central and eastern Andes of Colombia, and eastern Andes of Ecuador (to the western Andes only in Azuay), to northern Peru north of the Río Marañón, in Piura and Cajamarca
Erithacus rubecula: lowland to submontane understory of coniferous forest and deciduous woodland, riparian thickets, parks, and gardens, from British Isles and Scandinavia eastward to western Russia, and southward to Atlantic Islands (Azores, Madeira, and eastern Canary Islands), northwestern Africa, Mediterranean Europe, and Caucasus; northern populations migrate to northern Africa, Middle East, and southeastern Kazakhstan
Erithacus superbus: central Canary Islands (Tenerife and Gran Canaria)
Erpornis zantholeuca: lowland to montane evergreen forest, upland heath, and bamboo, from northwestern India (central Uttarakhand) eastward through Himalayas to southeastern China (including Hainan) and Taiwan, and southward through Indochina to Borneo and northern Sumatra
Erythrocercus holochlorus: lowland to foothill primary and secondary coastal forest, and riparian thickets, from southern Somalia southward to northeastern Tanzania
Erythrocercus livingstonei: lowland to foothill gallery forest, and miombo and mopane woodland, from southern Tanzania southward through southern Zambia and southern Mozambique
Erythrocercus mccallii: lowland and foothill primary forest from southwestern Mali and Guinea eastward to western Uganda, and southward through Gabon to western Republic of the Congo
Erythrogenys erythrogenys: foothill to submontane dense undergrowth at forest edge, bramble thickets, and scrub around villages, from northeastern Afghanistan eastward through Himalayas to Bhutan and northeastern India
Erythrogenys gravivox: foothill to montane forest edge, secondary growth, bamboo thickets, dry scrub, and lalang grassland, from eastern Tibet and north-central China southward to northeastern Myanmar, northern Laos, and northern Vietnam
Erythrogenys hypoleucos: patchy in lowland to submontane understory in broadleaf forest, bamboo, reeds, and tall grass, from northeastern India eastward to southeastern China (including Hainan), and southward to Indochina and Malayan Peninsula
Erythrogenys imberbis: foothill to submontane dense understory of oak and open evergreen forest, lalang grassland, and abandoned cultivation, in eastern Myanmar and northwestern Thailand
Erythrogenys mcclellandi: Assam south of the Brahmaputra to western Myanmar (Chin Hills)
Erythrogenys swinhoei: foothill to submontane dense understory in deciduous forest, brush-covered hillsides, and thickets adjacent to woodland, in southeastern China
Erythropitta arquata: primary submontane forest of northern half of Borneo
Erythropitta dohertyi: Peleng, in Banggai Islands and Taliabu, Seho, and Mangole, in Sula islands (off eastern Sulawesi)
Erythropitta erythrogaster: Philippines and Talaud Islands (northeast of Sulawesi)
Erythropitta granatina: tropical rainforest and flooded forest in southern Malayan Peninsula from far southern Thailand and Peninsular Malaysia, eastern Sumatra, and Borneo (except Sabah)
Erythropitta macklotii: tropical rainforest, bamboo and riparian thickets of New Guinea and many satellites, including D'Entrecasteaux Archipelago, and northeastern Cape York Peninsula (northern Queensland, northeastern Australia); Australian birds winter northward to New Guinea
Erythropitta meeki: Rossel (Louisiade Archipelago, off southeastern New Guinea)
Erythropitta novaehibernicae: New Ireland and New Britain groups (eastern Bismarck Archipelago)
Erythropitta rufiventris: northern Moluccas and Gebe (northwest of New Guinea)
Erythrotriorchis buergersi: montane forest of northern and eastern New Guinea
Erythrotriorchis radiatus: breeds northern Australia (Kimberley region, northern Western Australia, eastward to north Queensland, including Tiwi islands off Northern Territory); some non-breeders move southward to northwestern and central Australia; formerly southeastern Queensland and northeastern New South Wales
Erythrura hyperythra: disjunctly in foothill to montane bamboo thickets, evergreen forest edge, grassland, and rice fields, on Malayan Peninsula, northern Philippines (Luzon and Mindoro), highland Borneo, Sulawesi, and patchily from Java eastward through Lesser Sundas to Flores
Erythrura kleinschmidti: montane forest of Viti Levu (northwestern Fiji)
Erythrura papuana: mountains of New Guinea (Bird's Head Peninsula to southeastern ranges)
Erythrura pealii: Fiji (Viti Levu, Kadavu, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni)
Erythrura prasina: irruptive in bamboo, edge, and rice fields from northern Thailand southward through the Malayan Peninsula and southern Vietnam and Greater Sundas
Erythrura trichroa: Sulawesi, Moluccas, New Guinea and associated islands, northeastern Australia (Wet Tropics), Bismarck Archipelago, Vanuatu and Loyalty Islands (Lifou and Maré, New Caledonia), Solomon Islands, and Caroline Islands
Erythrura tricolor: Lesser Sundas (Timor, Wetar, Babar, Damar, Romang, and Tanimbar)
Esacus magnirostris: coasts and islets from Andaman Islands, Malayan Peninsula, southern Philippines, Indonesian Archipelago, New Guinea and satellites, northern and eastern Australia, Bismarck Archipelago (including Admiralty Islands), and Solomon Archipelago (except Rennell)
Esacus recurvirostris: estuaries of southern Iran; riverine systems of Indus Valley (central Pakistan), sub-Himalayan India southward to Sri Lanka and eastward to northern Thailand, northern Cambodia, and Vietnam
Estrilda astrild: widespread in sub-Saharan Africa (but avoiding rainforest and patchy in arid southwestern Africa), in lowland to montane grassland, acacia savanna, and grassy marsh, from Guinea, Sierra Leone, and southern Mali eastward to Eritrea, Ethiopia, and southern Somali, thence southward from Cameroon to Namibia, and from southern South Sudan to central Kenya and southward to South Africa and southern Mozambique; introduced widely, mostly on islands in tropical oceans, but also Iberian Peninsula and eastern Brazil
Estrilda atricapilla: patchy in central Africa, in lowland forest clearings with tall grass and sedges, and villages (but avoiding Congolian rainforest), from southern Cameroon to northern Angola and southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and adjacent Uganda
Estrilda kandti: patchy in submontane to montane forest edge and clearings, bamboo thickets, and bare rocky slopes, from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to central Kenya, and southward to Rwanda and Burundi
Estrilda melpoda: lowland to foothill grassland, forest edge, grassy woodland, plantations, and cultivation, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward through southern Chad and northern Democratic Republic of the Congo to western Uganda, Rwanda, and Burundi, and southward to northern Angola and northern Zambia; introduced to Spain, Singapore, Taiwan, Northern Mariana Islands (Saipan and Tinian), Hawaiian Islands (Oahu and Maui), and Caribbean (Puerto Rico, Guadeloupe, and Martinique)
Estrilda nigriloris: patchy in lowland to foothill tall grassland and bushy savanna in south-central Democratic Republic of the Congo
Estrilda nonnula: patchy in central Africa, in lowland to montane second-growth woodland, grassy forest edge, and gardens from southeastern Nigeria, Cameroon, and central Central African Republic, and southward to Gabon, and from southern South Sudan, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and western Kenya, southward to Burundi and northwestern Tanzania, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea)
Estrilda paludicola: patchy in lowland to montane grassy woodland, tall grass, and forest edge, from Central African Republic eastward to southern Sudan and western Ethiopia, and southward from Gabon southward to western Angola, and from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, southern South Sudan, and western Kenya southward to south-central Tanzania and northern Zambia
Estrilda poliopareia: disjunctly in lowland tall grass and sedge on sandy riverbanks, swamps, and estuaries, and in plantations, of coastal Benin and southern Nigeria
Estrilda rhodopyga: lowland to foothill acacia savanna, grassland, and overgrown cultivation from northeastern Sudan, Eritrea, Ethiopia, and Somalia southward to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Tanzania, and Malawi
Estrilda troglodytes: lowland to foothill grassy woodland, dense thickets, farmbush, swamp edge, and cultivation, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to southern Sudan, Eritrea, and western Ethiopia, and southward to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and southwestern Kenya; some seasonal dispersal, introduced in Spain, western Persian Gulf coast, Singapore, Hawaii (island of Hawaii), and Lesser Antilles (Guadeloupe and Martinique)
Eubucco bourcierii: humid forest in the mountains of western Costa Rica eastward to far eastern Panama and adjacent Colombia, and in South America, in the Andes slopes of western Venezuela southwestward to the central and eastern Andes of Colombia, not including Sierra de Perijá, and southward along the eastern Andes to far northern Peru; west of the Andes in the foothills and slopes of the western Andes of Colombia southward to west-central Ecuador, including Cordillera de Chongon Colonche in the southwest
Eubucco richardsoni: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin from east-central Colombia southward to northeastern Bolivia and western Amazonian Brazil (Amazonas, Acre, and Rondônia, mostly west of the Rio Negro and Rio Madeira)
Eubucco tucinkae: humid eastern Peru, northern Bolivia, and western Amazonian Brazil
Eubucco versicolor: montane cloudforest in the eastern Andes south of the Río Marañón from northern Peru (Amazonas), southeastward to central Bolivia (westernmost Santa Cruz)
Euchrepomis callinota: humid montane forest in the mountains of Costa Rica and western Panama, easternmost Panama and adjacent Colombia, locally in the Sierra de Perijá and the Andes of western Venezuela southward along the western and central Andes of Colombia to southern Ecuador, and along the eastern Andes from Colombia southward to south-central Peru, and in montane regions of the southern Guianas
Euchrepomis humeralis: eastern Ecuador to northwestern Bolivia and southwestern Amazonian Brazil
Euchrepomis sharpei: east slope of Andes of southeastern Peru (Cusco, Puno) and western Bolivia
Euchrepomis spodioptila: tropical rainforest in the Guiana Shield and Orinoco basin in eastern and southern Venezuela, the Guianas and easternmost Colombia southward in the eastern Amazon basin of Brazil to the lower Rio Madeira and Rio Tapajos, in western Pará and eastern Amazonas; also in the western Amazon basin from southeastern Colombia southward to northeastern Ecuador and northeastern Peru
Eucometis penicillata: tropical southeastern Mexico (Veracruz and Yucatán) to northern Colombia and far western Venezuela
Eudocimus albus: coastal and lowlands areas of western Mexico and the southeastern USA (expanding northward) southward to Costa Rica and the Greater Antilles, Panama, and Pacific coast from Colombia, southward to far northwestern Peru (Tumbes), coastal northern Colombia and northern Venezuela, and llanos of eastern Colombia and western Venezuela
Eudocimus ruber: coastal Colombia to Trinidad, the Guianas, and northeastern Brazil
Eudromia elegans: dry scrub of plains of northern Argentina from Salta in the northwest eastward through Buenos Aires province, southward through Patagonia (including southeastern Chile) to Strait of Magellan, southern Santa Cruz province (southern Argentina)
Eudromia formosa: dry Chaco scrub of southeastern Bolivia and western Paraguay to Santiago del Estero (northwestern Argentina)
Eudromias morinellus: breeds high Arctic coastal tundra and alpine zone, from northern British Isles and Scandinavia eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula and western Alaska; in south locally from Pyrenees through montane Mongolia; winters from Iberian Peninsula and northern Africa eastward to Arabian Peninsula and Iraq
Eudynamys melanorhynchus: Sulawesi and satellite islands, and Banggai and Sula islands (off eastern Sulawesi)
Eudynamys orientalis: central Moluccas to northern and eastern Australia
Eudynamys scolopaceus: Indian Subcontinent through eastern China, mainland southeastern Asia, the Phillippines, and Greater Sundas; Maldives, Lakshadweep, and Andaman and Nicobar islands
Eudyptes chrysocome: breeds far southern Chilean islands of Magallanes Province to Cape Horn Archipelago and Falkland Islands; winters northward along Patagonian coast
Eudyptes chrysolophus: subantarctic islands in South Atlantic Ocean and southern Indian Ocean
Eudyptes filholi: breeds coastally on Prince Edward, Crozet, Kerguelen, Heard (southern Indian Ocean), Macquarie (southeast of Australia), and Auckland, Campbell, and Antipodes islands (New Zealand)
Eudyptes moseleyi: breeds among coastal rocks and tussocks of Tristan da Cunha group and Gough (South Atlantic), and St. Paul and Amsterdam islands (South Indian Ocean)
Eudyptes pachyrhynchus: breeds inland in forests of southwestern South Island, western and southern Stewart Island, and satellites (New Zealand); winters to seas south of Australia
Eudyptes robustus: breeds coastal forest of Snares Islands; disperses westward to waters off southeastern Australia, and northward off New Zealand
Eudyptes schlegeli: breeds on coastal slopes of Macquarie and nearby Bishop and Clerk islands (southeast of Australia); winters mostly near colonies, with juveniles ranging farther
Eudyptes sclateri: breeds among rocks of Bounty and Antipodes islands (New Zealand); winters to waters of eastern South Island
Eudyptula minor: southern Australia and North, South, Stewart and Chatham islands (east of South Island; New Zealand)
Eugenes fulgens: mountains of southern Arizona, New Mexico, and Texas to northeastern Nicaragua
Eugenes spectabilis: montane forest of Costa Rica and western Panama
Eugralla paradoxa: south-central Chile (Santiago to Chiloé) and adjacent Argentina; Mocha Island
Eulacestoma nigropectus: montane west-central to southeastern New Guinea
Eulampis holosericeus: varied wooded habitats from lowland to mountains; coastal Puerto Rico (except western) and satellite islands, Virgin Islands, and Lesser Antilles southward to Grenada
Eulidia yarrellii: vegetated valleys in arid northern Chile, in Vitor and Camarones valleys (Arica); historical records from southern Peru (Tacna and possibly Moquegua), and Lluta and Azapa valleys in far northern Chile; critically endangered
Eulipoa wallacei: Moluccas and Misool (Raja Ampat Islands, off western New Guinea)
Eumomota superciliosa: deciduous woodland and edge in lowlands to hills from Yucatan Peninsula (excluding Cozumel), Pacific slope of southern Mexico from Chiapas to northern Guatemala, both slopes of eastern Guatemala to northern Honduras, and Pacific slope to northwestern Costa Rica
Eumyias albicaudatus: foothill forest of southwestern Peninsular India (southern Karnataka southward to Kerala)
Eumyias hoevelli: montane forest of central and southeastern Sulawesi
Eumyias panayensis: montane Philippines, Sulawesi, Obi, and Seram
Eumyias thalassinus: breeds northern Pakistan to southern China and Indochina; winters to Peninsular India, Thai-Malay Peninsula, and Sumatra
Euodice cantans: lowland and foothill savanna, acacia grassland, and thornscrub, from southern Mauritania eastward through the Sahel to northern Sudan (has occurred southeastern Egypt), Eritrea, Ethiopia, and Somalia, and southward to northern Tanzania, and southern Arabian Peninsula; population in southern Algeria is of origin uncertain, introduced to Hawaiian islands
Euodice malabarica: Arabian Peninsula to southeastern Iran, India, Sri Lanka, Nepal, and Sikkim
Eupetes macrocerus: tropical lowland rainforest, swamps, and heath forest in southern Malayan peninsula including southern Peninsular Thailand, Sumatra, Borneo, and Natuna Islands
Eupetomena cirrochloris: forest and scrub of eastern and central Brazil
Eupetomena macroura: open savanna, Caatinga, campos rupestres, humid to semi-humid and gallery forest in southern Suriname and northeastern Brazil, and from northeastern Brazil, in northern Maranhão southward across interior Brazil and the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil to southern Rio Grande do Sul, eastern Uruguay, northeasternmost Argentina (Misiones and adjacent Corrientes), northern and eastern Paraguay, and westward across southern Brazil (to western Mato Grosso, eastern Rondônia and southern Amazonas), also in northern Bolivia west to Pampas del Heath in far southeastern Peru, and to the upper Río Urubamba Valley in Cusco, Peru
Euphagus carolinus: breeds in wet areas of forest and woodland from northern Alaska eastward to Newfoundland and Labrador (eastern Canada) and southward to Ontario and Maine; winters in central and southeastern USA from eastern Nebraska eastward to Connecticut, and southward to eastern Texas and southern Florida; major rangewide population declines
Euphagus cyanocephalus: western Canada and western USA; winters to southern Mexico
Eupherusa cyanophrys: southern Mexico (Sierra de Miahuatlán of Oaxaca)
Eupherusa eximia: forest and edge in hills and mountains from central Veracruz to northern Nicaragua and disjunctly northwestern Costa Rica and central Panama; some non-breeding movement to lower elevations
Eupherusa nigriventris: montane forest of central Costa Rica and far western Panama
Eupherusa poliocerca: southern Mexico (Sierra Madre del Sur from Guerrero to western Oaxaca)
Eupherusa ridgwayi: Pacific slope of western Mexico (southern Nayarit, Jalisco, and Guerrero)
Euphonia affinis: open xeric woodland in lowlands, from Caribbean slope of Mexico from central Nuevo León and central Tamaulipas southward to southern Veracruz and thence on both slopes from Oaxaca and Yucatan Peninsula southward through northwestern Costa Rica
Euphonia anneae: forest and edge of Caribbean slope of hills and mountains from far northwestern Costa Rica through montane Panama to far northwestern Colombia
Euphonia cayennensis: tropical southeastern Venezuela, the Guianas, and eastern Amazonian Brazil
Euphonia chalybea: lowlands of eastern Paraguay to southeastern Brazil and northeastern Argentina
Euphonia chlorotica: disjunctly in varied dry to humid forest, woodland, and scrub habitats, including river islands, from llanos of eastern Colombia eastward in tepui region to Guyana and far northern Brazil, from eastern French Guiana and northeastern Brazil (Amapá) westward along the Amazon River to northeastern Peru, in eastern and interior Brazil southward to north-central Argentina (to San Luis and Entre Ríos), far southern Brazil (Rio Grande do Sul) and northern Uruguay, and in the Marañón Valley of far southeastern Ecuador and northern Peru
Euphonia chrysopasta: tropical rainforest in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from southern and eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to the entire Amazon basin, westward to eastern Ecuador, southward to central Bolivia (Santa Cruz), and eastward to northeastern Brazil (western Maranhão)
Euphonia finschi: southeastern Venezuela to the Guianas and northern Brazil (northern Roraima)
Euphonia fulvicrissa: humid lowland forest and edge from central Panama to northeastern Colombia and southward west of Andes to northwestern Ecuador
Euphonia godmani: arid tropical western Mexico (southeastern Sonora to Guerrero)
Euphonia gouldi: lowland forest and edge of Caribbean slope from southern Veracruz and northeastern Oaxaca of eastern Mexico to western Panama (Bocas del Toro)
Euphonia hirundinacea: forest edge from lowlands to hills of Caribbean slope from central Tamaulipas (northeastern Mexico, and including Yucatan Peninsula), and Pacific slope from southern Oaxaca southward to far western Panama
Euphonia imitans: forest edge in lowlands and foothills of Pacific slope from west-central Costa Rica to far western Panama
Euphonia laniirostris: disjunctly in humid to dry forest and woodland from the Pacific slope of Costa Rica southward to interior Colombia along the Cauca and Magdalena valleys, west of the Andes southward to northwestern Peru (to Cajamarca), and east of the Andes from western Venezuela southward to east-central Bolivia (Santa Cruz), in Brazil mostly south of the Amazon River (eastward to eastern Amazonas and Goiás)
Euphonia luteicapilla: tropical eastern Nicaragua to Costa Rica and Panama
Euphonia mesochrysa: foothill and montane cloudforest in the eastern Andes of Colombia and the headwaters of the Magdalena River (from Boyacá), southward to northern Peru north and west of the Marañón River, and in the eastern Andes from northern Peru east and south of the Marañón, southeastward to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz)
Euphonia minuta: disjunctly in humid and tropical rainforest from southeastern Chiapas (southern Mexico) and central Belize southward on the Caribbean slope of Central America to eastern Panama, and the Pacific slope of southeastern Costa Rica southward west of the Andes to northwestern Ecuador, in the Magdalena Valley of interior Colombia (to Cundinamarca), east of the Andes and in Andean foothills in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to eastern Peru, central Bolivia, and Amazonian Brazil (to northern Tocantins)
Euphonia pectoralis: eastern Brazil (eastern Alagoas) to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
Euphonia plumbea: southern Venezuela to Guyana, Suriname, and northern Amazonian Brazil
Euphonia rufiventris: southeastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, northern Bolivia (to western and northern Santa Cruz), and western Amazonian Brazil
Euphonia saturata: Colombia on both slopes of western Andes (southward from southern Chocó and Risaralda), western Ecuador, and far northwestern Peru (Tumbes)
Euphonia trinitatis: tropical northern Caribbean Colombia to northern Venezuela and Trinidad
Euphonia violacea: humid forest, woodland, and gallery forest from Trinidad and Tobago, eastern and southern Venezuela, and the Guianas southward across central and eastern Brazil (westward to eastern Amazonas, absent from drier Cerrado and Caatinga in interior Brazil) to eastern Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, and southeastern Brazil (northern Rio Grande do Sul)
Euphonia xanthogaster: disjunctly in humid forest from far eastern Panama southward to far northwestern Peru, in foothills and slopes in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Falcón eastward to Sucre), the Sierra de Perijá, the Andes of western Venezuela, and the upper Orinoco and Amazon basins, from southern Venezuela and eastern Colombia southward to central Bolivia (to western Santa Cruz) and eastward in Brazil (to northern Tocantins), the tepui region of southern Venezuela, western Guyana, and northernmost Brazil (Roraima), and the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil (central Bahia southward to Rio de Janeiro)
Euplectes afer: patchy in lowland to foothill grassland and seasonal swamps from southern Mauritania eastward to southern Sudan and central Ethiopia, southward to northern Namibia and Zimbabwe, thence southward to Lesotho and eastern South Africa, seasonally nomadic with rains; introduced on Iberian Peninsula, Jamaica, and some eastern Caribbean islands
Euplectes albonotatus: lowland and foothill bushed grassland from Central African Republic eastward through southern Sudan to Ethiopia, southward to Angola, northeastern Namibia, northern Botswana, and Zimbabwe, thence southward to southern Mozambique and eastern South Africa; introduced to São Tomé
Euplectes anomalus: patchy in lowland grassy clearings in forest near major rivers from southeastern Cameroon, southwestern Central African Republic, and northern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and southward to far western and central Democratic Republic of the Congo and northern Angola
Euplectes ardens: patchy in lowland to submontane open or sparsely-wooded grassland, cultivation, farmbush, and forest clearings, from Guinea (possibly Senegal) and southern Mali eastward to northern Uganda and southeastern Kenya, and southward to northern Angola, Zimbabwe, and eastern South Africa
Euplectes aureus: lowland grassland, open acacia savanna, and farmbush in coastal west-central Angola; presumably introduced to São Tomé (Gulf of Guinea)
Euplectes axillaris: patchy in sub-Saharan Africa (avoiding rainforest and southwest Africa), in grassland from southern Mali eastward to South Sudan, thence southward to northeastern Namibia and northwestern Botswana, and from western Ethiopia and southern Somalia southward through east Africa, including Pemba and Unguja (in Zanzibar, Tanzania), to southern Mozambique and eastern South Africa
Euplectes capensis: patchy in lowland to montane grassland and Fynbos from southeastern Nigeria to southern Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), and from Ethiopia and southern South Sudan southward to southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Angola, and Mozambique, and thence southward to Lesotho and southern and eastern South Africa
Euplectes diadematus: lowland to foothill grassland, bushy coastal dunes, cultivation, and seasonally flooded wetlands, from central Kenya eastward to southern Somalia, and southward to southeastern Kenya and adjacent far northeastern Tanzania; migratory or nomadic dispersal related to rains
Euplectes franciscanus: lowland to montane tall or brushy grassland, seasonally flooded wetland, and cultivation, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward through Sahel to Sudan, Eritrea, and Ethiopia, and southward to southern Nigeria, Uganda, and western Kenya; introduced in Puerto Rico
Euplectes gierowii: very patchily distributed in lowland to montane grassland, bush, and swamp from Cameroon and western Central African Republic eastward to western Ethiopia, and southward to northwestern Angola and central Tanzania
Euplectes hartlaubi: lowland and foothill swampy grassland from southeastern Nigeria and Cameroon eastward (except Congolian rainforest), to Uganda and western Kenya, and southward to western Angola, thence eastward to Zambia and southwestern Tanzania
Euplectes hordeaceus: lowland to submontane savanna, tall grassland, cultivation, farmbush, and seasonal wetland, from southern Mauritania and Mali eastward to southern Sudan and Ethiopia, and southward through Democratic Republic of the Congo and Tanzania, including Pemba and Unguja (Zanzibar), to Angola, northern and eastern Zimbabwe, and central Mozambique; introduced to São Tomé (Gulf of Guinea)
Euplectes jacksoni: foothill to montane open grassland in southwestern Kenya highlands and adjacent northeastern Tanzania
Euplectes laticauda: patchy in foothill and montane grassland, wooded savanna, and open bush in eastern South Sudan, Eritrea, and Ethiopia, and in western and central Kenya and northern Tanzania
Euplectes macroura: lowland to montane grasslands and wooded swamps from Senegal eastward to southern Sudan, Eritrea, and Ethiopia, southward to Angola, Zambia, Malawi, eastern Zimbabwe, and adjacent Mozambique
Euplectes nigroventris: lowland to foothill coastal grassland and cultivation from southeastern Kenya and eastern Tanzania, including Pemba and Unguja (Zanzibar), and southward to southwestern Tanzania and northern Mozambique; escapees reported Singapore
Euplectes orix: lowland to foothill grassland, farmbush, and cultivation, from northern Angola eastward to southern Uganda and southern Kenya, and southward to South Africa; introduced to United Arab Emirates
Euplectes progne: disjunctly in lowland to highland short-grass and coastal grassland, in central Kenya, and from Angola eastward to northeastern Zambia, and from southeastern Botswana to southern Mozambique, eastern South Africa, Lesotho, and Eswatini
Euplectes psammacromius: submontane to montane short grassland, often near streams, in southwestern Tanzania highlands, far northeastern Zambia, and northern Malawi

Frederickena viridis: southeastern Venezuela to the Guianas and northeastern Amazonian Brazil
Fregata andrewsi: breeds Christmas Island (east-central Indian Ocean); ranges Andaman Sea and Gulf of Thailand across Sunda Shelf to South China Sea and Sulu Sea (southwestern Philippines)
Fregata aquila: breeds Ascension Island (where recently re-established) and (mainly) nearby Boatswainbird Island (South Atlantic); ranges (rarely) to northeastern Brazil and western African coast
Fregata ariel: widespread, breeding tropical Indian and Pacific ocean islands, also northwestern South Atlantic; non-breeders range to waters off southeastern Africa, southwestern India and Sri Lanka, throughout Indonesian Archipelago and Philippines to Taiwan, New Guinea waters, northern Australia, and Melanesia
Fregata magnificens: breeds Cabo Verde (where almost extirpated), islands from southern Baja California (northwestern Mexico) to Ecuador including Galapagos, and eastern Mexico and far southern Florida through Caribbean to northeastern Brazil; ranges to coastal northern Baja California, Gulf of California, and southward to northern Peru, and to northern Florida and Gulf of Mexico
Fregata minor: widespread breeder, islands of tropical Indian and Pacific oceans, local east of eastern Brazil (tropical Atlantic Ocean); pelagic when non-breeding, ranging throughout tropical Indian and tropical and subtropical Pacific oceans
Fregetta grallaria: breeds tropical and subtropical southern ocean islands: south-central Indian Ocean islands, Lord Howe Island (far east of Australia), Kermadec Islands (northeast of North Island, New Zealand), Rapa (Austral Islands, eastern Polynesia), San Felix and San Ambrosio (Easter Island, southeastern Polynesia), and Juan Fernandez Islands (far west of central Chile); non-breeders range tropical and subtropical southern oceans between Equator and Subtropical Convergence
Fregetta lineata: breeds New Caledonia; ranges from the Coral Sea (just off eastern Australia) eastward to Samoa and the Marquesas Islands
Fregetta maoriana: breeds Little Barrier Island (northern North Island, New Zealand); ranges to seas off southeastern Australia and Fiji
Fregetta tropica: breeds circumpolar subantarctic islands of South Georgia, Antarctic Peninsula, Bouvetoya (southwest of Africa), Tristan da Cunha perhaps including Gough Island (south-central Atlantic Ocean); Prince Edward, Crozet, and Kerguelen (southwestern to southeastern Indian Ocean), Bounty, Antipodes, and Auckland islands (southeast and south of South Island, New Zealand); non-breeders range southern oceans mostly south of Equator to Antarctic Convergence
Fregilupus varius: formerly Réunion Island; extinct, last reported 1860
Fringilla canariensis: woodland habitats of La Palma and El Hierro eastward to Gran Canaria (western and central Canary Islands)
Fringilla coelebs: breeds British Isles, Scandinavia, and Iberian Peninsula eastward to south-central Siberia and northern Iran; northern populations winter to south
Fringilla montifringilla: breeds northern Europe eastward to eastern Russia (Chukotka), southward to northeastern Kazakhstan, Altai, Tuva, southern Lake Baikal, Russian Far East (southward to Amurland, Sakhalin, and Kamchatka); winters to southern Europe, northern Africa, Middle East, and southwestern, central, and eastern Asia
Fringilla spodiogenys: lowland to foothill woodland from western Morocco to northern Tunisia and northwest Libya, and in coastal northeastern Libya
Fringillaria affinis: mesic woodland of Sahel zone and northeastern Africa, from Senegal, far southern Mauritania to northern Guinea and eastward to western and southern Ethiopia, northern Uganda, and western Kenya
Fringillaria cabanisi: broadleaf woodland of tropical Africa: Guinea and far southern Mali eastward to far southern Sudan and northwestern Uganda; Angola, southern Zimbabwe, and central Mozambique
Fringillaria capensis: open rocky shrubland of southern Africa: southwestern Angola eastward to western Mozambique, southward through southern South Africa
Fringillaria flaviventris: open woodland of Sahel zone and disjunctly eastern and southern Africa: southern Mauritania to northern Eritrea and far northern Ethiopia; southern Democratic Republic of the Congo and far southern South Sudan through eastern Africa, southward through South Africa (except southwestern)
Fringillaria goslingi: foothill to submontane arid scrub, mesic woodland, lightly wooded savanna, bare or sandy ground, short grassland, and degraded pasture, from Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to eastern Sudan and northeastern South Sudan, and southward to Cameroon and Central African Republic; partial migrant with rains, and nomadic wandering
Fringillaria impetuani: southwestern African succulent and grassy Karoo: coastal central Angola to Namibia, Botswana, Zimbabwe, and western and central South Africa
Fringillaria poliopleura: foothill to submontane arid acacia scrub and thornscrub from southeastern South Sudan, Ethiopia, and Somalia southward to northeastern Tanzania
Fringillaria sahari: lowland to montane vegetated rocky hillsides, desert wadis, scrub, cultivation, and villages and towns, from Morocco eastward to northwestern Libya, and southward patchily to Mauritania, Mali, Niger, and Chad, has bred in southern Spain; post-breeding dispersal northward and southward
Fringillaria socotrana: densely vegetated rocky slopes of montane Socotra; winters to lower elevations
Fringillaria striolata: rocky scrublands of subtropical northeastern Africa to southwestern Asia: patchily in northeastern Chad and eastern Egypt to northeastern Somalia and southward to northwestern Kenya; Sinai Peninsula, Israel, and western Jordan, Arabian Peninsula, southern Iran, northeastern Afghanistan to far western India; winters to fields of west-central India
Fringillaria tahapisi: rocky hillsides of subtropical to tropical northeastern to southern Africa: Gabon eastward to northeastern Somalia and Socotra, and southern Arabian Peninsula southward through South Africa
Fulica alai: Hawaiian Islands (very local on Ni‘ihau, Kauai, Oahu, Molokai, Maui, and Hawaii)
Fulica americana: breeds southern Alaska across southern Canada, and southward through western and central USA to northwestern Costa Rica, the Caribbean (Greater and Lesser Antilles), and northern South America
Fulica ardesiaca: freshwater marshes and lakes in the Andes of southernmost Colombia southward to southern Ecuador, locally in western Ecuador lowlands, from northern Peru (southern Cajamarca) southward to northernmost Chile, across Bolivia, to northwestern Argentina (southward to Catamarca), and coastal Peru from Piura southward to northern Chile
Fulica armillata: Paraguay to Uruguay, southeastern Brazil, and Tierra del Fuego
Fulica atra: breeds Europe, northern Africa, Azores and Canaries eastward through central Asia to Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu) and southward to Indian Subcontinent, including Sri Lanka, Indonesia, New Guinea, Australia, and New Zealand; winters to Africa, Indonesia, and Philippines
Fulica cornuta: high Andean lakes of southwestern Bolivia to northern Chile and northwestern Argentina
Fulica cristata: southern Spain and Morocco; eastern and southern Africa and Madagascar
Fulica gigantea: Andes of southern Peru to northern Chile and northwestern Argentina
Fulica leucoptera: far southeastern Brazil to eastern Bolivia and southward to Tierra del Fuego
Fulica newtonii: formerly Réunion, and possibly Mauritius; extinct since late 1600s
Fulica rufifrons: Paraguay to Uruguay, southeastern Brazil, southern Peru, and Tierra del Fuego
Fulmarus glacialis: breeds islands and coasts of North Atlantic, bays between Arctic and North Atlantic, and North Pacific including Sea of Okhotsk to Hokkaido (northern Japan) and Bering Sea; non-breeders range to coasts of northwestern Pacific southward to central Japan, northeastern Pacific southward to Baja California (northwestern Mexico), western Atlantic southward to North Carolina, and eastern Atlantic southward to France
Fulmarus glacialoides: circumpolar in Antarctic, breeding islets and coast of Antarctica; ranges southern oceans from pack-ice to Humboldt Current off Chile and Peru
Fulvetta cinereiceps: foothill to montane understory in broadleaf and mixed forest, secondary growth, scrub, and bramble, in central and southwestern to southeastern China; some downslope in winter
Fulvetta danisi: patchy in foothill and submontane understory of broadleaf evergreen forest, secondary scrub, and bamboo, in Laos and central and southern Vietnam
Fulvetta ludlowi: Himalayas (southeastern Tibet to southwestern China, eastern Bhutan, and far northeastern India)
Fulvetta manipurensis: foothill to submontane broadleaf evergreen forest, scrub, and bamboo, from northeastern India and northern Myanmar eastward through southern China to northern Vietnam
Fulvetta ruficapilla: foothill to submontane broadleaf evergreen oak forest, dense secondary scrub, and brambles, in central and southern China
Fulvetta striaticollis: mountains of south-central China (southwestern Gansu to southeastern Qinghai, Sichuan, and northwestern Yunnan)
Fulvetta vinipectus: patchy in montane scrub, rhododendron thickets, bamboo, and understory in open pine or spruce forest, from northern India eastward through Himalayas to Bhutan, and in southern China, in western and northern Myanmar, and in northern Vietnam
Furnarius cinnamomeus: far southwestern Colombia (Nariño), western Ecuador, and northwestern Peru
Furnarius cristatus: Chaco of southeastern Bolivia to western Paraguay and northern Argentina
Furnarius figulus: riparian woodland, scrub and open-areas in the lower Amazon basin from eastern Amazonas eastward to central Pará and southward along the Rio Araguaia to northern Goiás and eastern Mato Grosso; also in eastern Brazil from northern Maranhão, Piauí, and Ceará southward to coastal Paraná and Santa Catarina, and inland to western São Paulo and adjacent Mato Grosso do Sul
Furnarius leucopus: open and semi-open areas, gallery forest and woodland, riparian scrub, and grassy fields from northern Brazil (Roraima) and adjacent Guyana southwestward across western Brazil (western Amazonas, Acre, and adjacent Rondônia) to far southeastern Colombia, eastern Peru and far southeastern Ecuador; to northern Bolivia, south-central Brazil (Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul), adjacent Paraguay, northeastward to eastern Brazil (to northern Maranhão, Piauí, and Ceará, and southward to Minas Gerais and Espírito Santo)
Furnarius longirostris: open areas and secondary scrub in the lowlands of northeastern Colombia and northwestern Venezuela (eastward to Yaracuy and Carabobo), west to the Gulf of Uraba region (Córdoba, northern Antioquia, and Chocó), and southward along the Magdalena Valley (to Tolima and northern Huila)
Furnarius minor: Amazonian Brazil, southern Colombia, eastern Ecuador, and northeastern Peru
Furnarius rufus: open areas and secondary scrub in northeastern Brazil (from southeastern Pará, southern Maranhão, and Pernambuco), southward across the Atlantic Forest and interior Brazil to south-central Argentina (northern Chubut and Río Negro), and westward in central Brazil (Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul) to central Bolivia (west to eastern La Paz)
Furnarius torridus: along the Amazon River (southern Colombia, northeastern Ecuador, northeastern Peru, and western Brazil)
Galbalcyrhynchus leucotis: Colombia east of the Andes to northeastern Peru and western Amazonian Brazil
Galbalcyrhynchus purusianus: tropical eastern Peru, northern Bolivia, and western Amazonian Brazil
Galbula albirostris: tropical rainforest north of the Amazon River from eastern Colombia eastward to northeastern Brazil in Amapá, including the Guiana Shield; in the western Amazon southward across Ecuador to central Peru, along the Río Ucayali to Pasco
Galbula chalcothorax: western Amazonia, from southeastern Colombia to eastern Peru (south to Ucayali) and eastward to western Brazil (east at least to the Juruá)
Galbula cyanescens: riverine forest of eastern Peru to northern Bolivia and western Amazonian Brazil
Galbula cyanicollis: humid lowlands of northeastern Peru and Brazil south of the Amazon
Galbula dea: humid to dry and gallery forest of lowlands and hills of Amazonia and the Guianas from eastern Ecuador and eastern Colombia east through western Maranhão and Mato Grosso, and southward to northern Bolivia
Galbula galbula: eastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, the Guianas, and northern and central Brazil
Galbula leucogastra: central Amazonia, from eastern Colombia and southern Venezuela eastward to the Guianas, southward to southeastern Peru (Madre de Dios), northern Bolivia, and south-central Amazonian Brazil (south to Mato Grosso)
Galbula pastazae: east slope of the Andes of southeastern Colombia, eastern Ecuador, and far northern Peru
Galbula ruficauda: humid to dry forest from eastern Mexico in Oaxaca, including interior Yucatan Peninsula, eastward across Central America to the lowlands of northern South America in Colombia and eastward across western and northern Venezuela to Trinidad and Tobago; in central Colombia extends southward along the Río Cauca and Río Magdalena to Huila, and west of the Andes southward to central-west Ecuador; also in the Guianan shield in Guyana and far northern Roraima, Brazil, and in Amazonian Brazil, south of the Amazon River, from Amazonas eastward to the Atlantic coast, and southward across interior Brazil to Mato Grosso to Sul and westward to northernmost Paraguay and to northern Bolivia; in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil southward to São Paulo
Galbula tombacea: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin from eastern Colombia southward to northeastern Ecuador and northeastern Peru, and eastward along the Amazon River to the western side of the Rio Negro, in Amazonas, in Brazil
Galerida cristata: patchy in lowland to submontane dry plains with sparse cover, dry cultivation, steppe, and sandy semi-desert, from western continental Europe eastward to northeastern China and Korean Peninsula, and southward to African Sahel, northern Kenya, Arabian Peninsula, and northern India
Galerida magnirostris: lowland to montane dry grassland, Karoo shrubland, and open coastal scrub of southwestern Namibia, western and central South Africa (eastward to Free State and western KwaZulu-Natal), and Lesotho
Galerida modesta: lowland and foothill short grassland, dry rocky hills, and arid savanna, from Senegambia eastward through the Sahel to southwestern Sudan, and southward to Sierra Leone, and northern Ghana to northwestern Uganda
Galerida theklae: disjunctly in lowland to montane arid steppe, open rocky hills with shrubs, and low acacia scrub of southern Iberian Peninsula including Balearic Islands, and far southern France, and from Western Sahara eastward to Tunisia and northern Libya, and from southern Eritrea, Ethiopia, and northern Somalia southward to northern Kenya
Gallicolumba crinigera: East Visayas, Mindanao group, and Jolo (northern Sulu Archipelago; east-central to southwestern Philippines)
Gallicolumba keayi: Negros and Panay (West Visayas; west-central Philippines)
Gallicolumba menagei: Tawitawi (Sulu Archipelago); known only from two specimens collected in 1891; probably extinct
Gallicolumba platenae: forest of Mindoro (central Philippines); status unknown
Gallicolumba rufigula: New Guinea and some satellite islands
Gallicrex cinerea: breeds from northern Pakistan eastward in sub-Himalayan region to northeastern China, southeastern Russia, and southern Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), southward to southeastern Pakistan, southern India, Sri Lanka, western Greater Sundas, and Philippines; northeastern populations winter to south, reaching Sulawesi and central Lesser Sundas
Gallinago andina: montane wet grassland of western South America from Peru to northern Chile and northwestern Argentina
Gallinago delicata: breeds central Aleutians to eastern Canada and northern tier of continental USA; winters south of breeding range to northern South America
Gallinago gallinago: breeds low Arctic to temperate wetlands of Palearctic from Iceland to British Isles, Scandinavia, France, and Azores eastward through northern Russia to central Chukchi Peninsula, Kamchatka, Sea of Okhotsk, and Commander Islands (southeastern Russia); in south to northern Kazakhstan, eastern Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Afghanistan, Kashmir (northwestern Himalayas), northern Mongolia, and northeastern China; winters temperate to tropical wetlands mainly north of Equator from British Isles to southern Europe, Atlantic islands, northern Africa, west-central to east-central Africa, Middle East, central to southern Asia, eastern China, Taiwan, Korean Peninsula, central and southern Japan, Philippines, and Greater Sundas
Gallinago hardwickii: breeds meadows and fields of eastern Amurland and southern Sakhalin (southeastern Russia) southward through Kyushu (Japan); winters freshwater wetlands of eastern Australia including Tasmania
Gallinago imperialis: elfin forest montane bogs from Ecuador to Peru (old records Colombia)
Gallinago jamesoni: montane bogs from west-central Venezuela to north-central Bolivia
Gallinago macrodactyla: marshes of eastern and central massif of Madagascar
Gallinago magellanica: breeds from central Chile and central Argentina southward to Tierra del Fuego and Falkland Islands; southernmost populations are migratory, nonbreeding distribution unclear but reaches Uruguay
Gallinago media: breeds meadows from northern Scandinavia and eastern Poland eastward to Yenisei River (western Siberia); winters wet grassland of tropical and subtropical sub-Saharan Africa
Gallinago megala: breeds wooded wetlands of south-central Siberia and northeastern Kazakhstan eastward to Amurland (southeastern Russia); winters wetland edge from east-central China, Taiwan, Philippines, and Malayan Peninsula eastward through New Guinea, Melanesia, and Micronesia
Gallinago nemoricola: breeds alpine meadows of western Himalayas from Himachal Pradesh to eastern India and south-central China; winters to lower-elevation wetlands and woodlands, rarely to Indian Peninsula and northern southeastern Asia
Gallinago nigripennis: subtropical to tropical wetlands of Africa from Eritrea southward through eastern Africa and Angola southward through South Africa
Gallinago nobilis: montane wet grassland far western Venezuela to far northern Peru
Gallinago paraguaiae: wetlands from central Colombia and Trinidad through the Guianas southward to northern Argentina and Uruguay
Gallinago solitaria: breeds montane wetlands of central and eastern Palearctic from Altai and Tian Shan mountains of south-central Russia, northeastern Kazakhstan, northwestern Xinjiang, and northern Mongolia eastward to Kamchatka and northeastern China; winters montane eastern Kazakhstan to eastern Afghanistan, Himalayas, northern southeastern Asia, west-central to southeastern China, Korean Peninsula, Sakhalin and Amurland (southeastern Russia), and Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu)
Gallinago stenura: breeds low Arctic tundra to temperate montane meadows from northwestern Siberia and northeastern Kazakhstan eastward to Sea of Okhotsk (eastern Siberia); winters inland wetlands from southern Arabian Peninsula eastward through southern Asia to Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan) and southward to Taiwan and Greater Sundas
Gallinago stricklandii: bogs of temperate central and southern Chile and southern Argentina to Cape Horn and Isla de los Estados (east of Tierra del Fuego)
Gallinago undulata: wet grassland of northern and southeastern South America from eastern Colombia through French Guiana, and disjunctly southeastern Peru and Bolivia (where very rare) through Bahia (northeastern Brazil) and southward through Paraguay and Rio Grande do Sul (southeastern Brazil)
Gallinula chloropus: breeds Europe, Africa, Malagasy region, and Atlantic islands eastward through Asia to Japan (Hokkaido to Ryukyu Islands), Philippines, and Mariana Islands, and southward to Sri Lanka and central Malayan Peninsula; winters to Arabian Peninsula and southern China
Gallinula comeri: Gough Island (South Atlantic Ocean); introduced to Tristan da Cunha in 1956
Gallinula galeata: breeds southwestern USA and southeastern Canada southward to the West Indies, Venezuela, Trinidad, and the Guianas, northern Argentina, Uruguay, and Brazil; northern populations move southward in winter
Gallinula nesiotis: formerly Tristan da Cunha; extinct, last reported 1900
Gallinula pacifica: formerly Sava'i Island (western Samoa); probably extinct, last reported 1873
Gallinula silvestris: Makira (southeastern Solomon Islands); the only specimen was collected in 1929
Gallinula tenebrosa: Wallacea, New Guinea, eastern Australia including Tasmania, New Britain (southeastern Bismarck Archipelago), and New Caledonia
Gallirallus australis: North, South, and Stewart islands and satellite islands (New Zealand)
Gallirallus castaneoventris: Aru Islands (off southwestern New Guinea) and coastal northern Australia
Gallirallus dieffenbachii: formerly Chatham Islands; extinct, last reported 1900
Gallirallus insignis: forest of New Britain (southeastern Bismarck Archipelago)
Gallirallus lafresnayanus: forest of New Caledonia (probably extinct; no definite records since 1890)
Gallirallus modestus: formerly Chatham Islands; extinct, last reported 1900
Gallirallus okinawae: forest and edge from lowlands to hills of northern Okinawa (Ryukyu Islands, southern Japan)
Gallirallus owstoni: forest of Guam (southern Mariana Islands); extinct in the wild until successfully reintroduced to Rota (southernmost Northern Mariana Islands) and Cocos Island (just south of Guam)
Gallirallus pacificus: formerly Tahiti; extinct, last reported 1800; reports from Mehetia probably erroneous
Gallirallus philippensis: Philippines southward through Wallacea to New Guinea and Australia and eastward to Palau, Bismarck Archipelago, Solomon Archipelago, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Fiji, Tongam Samoa, and Niue; formerly Macquarie Island
Gallirallus poecilopterus: formerly Viti Levu and Ovalau, Fiji (western Polynesia); extinct, last reported 1973
Gallirallus torquatus: Philippines, islets off Sabah (Malaysian Borneo), Sulawesi and satellite islands, and western New Guinea
Gallirallus wakensis: formerly Wake Island; extinct, last reported 1944
Gallirex johnstoni: patchy in high-montane forest and bamboo of northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, southwestern Uganda, Rwanda, and Burundi
Gallirex porphyreolophus: lowland and foothill woodland, riparian and miombo woodland, and coastal forest, from southwestern Uganda and southeastern Kenya southward through eastern Zambia, Zimbabwe, and Mozambique to Eswatini and eastern South Africa
Galloperdix bicalcarata: humid forest of southern Sri Lanka
Galloperdix spadicea: lowland to submontane hilly deciduous scrub, Lantana thickets, and scrubby bamboo in India, from southern Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh southward to Kerala and Tamil Nadu
Gallus gallus: native range fragmented in lowland to lower montane open woodland, moist forest, and mangroves, from northeastern India eastward across Himalayan foothills to southern China (including Hainan), and southward through eastern India and southeastern Asia to Vietnam, the Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, Java, and Bali. Feral junglefowl widespread throughout native range, and likely introduced to Philippines, Sulawesi, and parts of the Lesser Sundas (Indonesia). Feral populations widely introduced away from native range, including Micronesia, Melanesia, and Polynesia; domesticated stock released in open warm habitats globally, including North America, South Africa, New Zealand, and many tropical islands.
Gallus varius: Java eastward to Alor (central Lesser Sundas); introduced Cocos (Keeling) Islands (northeastern Indian Ocean)
Gampsonyx swainsonii: dry savanna, shrubby habitats, and grasslands with trees from southern Honduras, El Salvador, and adjacent Guatemala southward to eastern Panama; from northern Colombia southward in the Cauca and Magdalena valleys, and west of the Andes from northwestern Ecuador and adjacent Colombia southward to northwestern Peru; from northern Venezuela southward to northeastern Peru, and from eastern Venezuela, Trinidad, and the Guianas southward across the central and eastern Amazon basin, and the Cerrado and Atlantic Forest of Brazil to eastern Peru, northern and eastern Bolivia, Paraguay, northern Argentina, and southeastern Brazil (São Paulo and Paraná)
Gampsorhynchus rufulus: Nepal to Sikkim, Bhutan, Assam, southwestern Myanmar, and western Yunnan
Gampsorhynchus torquatus: patchy in lowland to foothill understory in broadleaf evergreen forest, bamboo, long grass, and secondary growth, from eastern Myanmar, south-central China, and northern Vietnam southward to Malayan Peninsula and southern Vietnam
Garritornis isidorei: lowlands of New Guinea, including Misool (west Papuan islands)
Garrodia nereis: breeds circumpolar subantarctic islands in Falkland Islands, South Georgia, Gough (Atlantic), Crozet and Kerguelen (Indian Ocean), Macquarie (few; Australia), Chatham, Antipodes, and Auckland (New Zealand) islands; ranges mainly between Antarctic and Subantarctic convergences, northward to southern Tasman Sea and about 35°S
Garrulax canorus: lowland to foothill open woodland, bamboo thickets, scrub, reeds, and gardens, from southeastern China (including Hainan), southward to central Vietnam and adjacent Laos; introduced in Japan (central Honshu and Kyushu), Taiwan, and Hawaii (all main islands)
Garrulax castanotis: disjunctly in foothill to submontane broadleaf evergreen forest in northern and central Vietnam, and adjacent Laos, and on Hainan (southeastern China)
Garrulax leucolophus: lowland to submontane broadleaf evergreen and mixed deciduous forest, secondary growth, bamboo thickets, and scrub, from northern India eastward through Himalayas to southern China and northern Vietnam, and southward to Indochina
Garrulax maesi: southeastern China from south-central Sichuan, far eastern Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, and northern Guangdong) and northern Vietnam
Garrulax merulinus: foothill to submontane understory of broadleaf evergreen forest, bamboo, and dense secondary growth, from northeastern India eastward to southern China and northern Vietnam, and southward to western Myanmar and northern Thailand
Garrulax milleti: patchy in foothill broadleaf evergreen forest in central Vietnam and adjacent Laos, and in southern Vietnam
Garrulax monileger: lowland to foothill broadleaf evergreen and deciduous forest, secondary growth, and scrub, from Nepal eastward through Himalayan foothills to southeastern China (including Hainan), and southward to southeastern Thailand and southern Vietnam
Garrulax strepitans: Myanmar to southwestern China (southwestern Yunnan), western Thailand, and northwestern Laos
Garrulus glandarius: widespread in temperate Palearctic in lowland to montane forest, woodland, parks, and orchards, from British Isles and Scandinavia eastward to southern Siberia and Japan, southward to northwestern Africa, Mediterranean Europe, and Middle East, and from northern Pakistan eastward through Himalayas to Indochina, eastern China, and Taiwan; seasonal downslope dispersal in mountains, and occasional irregular irruptions
Garrulus lanceolatus: Himalayas (Afghanistan to northern India and central Nepal)
Garrulus lidthi: northern Ryukyu Islands (Amami Ōshima and nearby islets, southern Japan)
Gavia adamsii: breeds Arctic northwestern Russia from Novaya Zemlya eastward to Chukotka Peninsula, through northern Alaska and northern Canada to Nunavut (east-central Canada); winters to northern Norway, Japan (northern Honshu), Korean Peninsula, and coastal British Columbia (southwestern Canada); prone to extreme vagrancy
Gavia arctica: breeds Arctic to temperate northern and central Eurasia and far western Alaska; non-breeders to coastal southern European and western Asian seas, to Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu) and Korean Peninsula
Gavia immer: breeds in southern Greenland, Iceland, and northern North America southward to northern tier of US states; winters from Iceland and Scandinavia southward to the Iberian Peninsula and from southern Alaska and the Maritime Provinces (Canada) southward to northern Mexico
Gavia pacifica: breeds coastal eastern Siberia and northern North America eastward through northern Canada to Baffin Island and James Bay (eastern Canada); winters to Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu) and southern Baja California
Gavia stellata: breeds across the northern Holarctic region; winters coastally in the north Pacific Ocean from the Kamchatka Peninsula and Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu) to the Yellow Sea, and from southern Alaska to northwestern Mexico; and in the northern Atlantic Ocean from the Maritime Provinces (Canada) to the southeastern USA, from Scandinavia south to the Mediterranean, and the Black and Caspian seas
Gavicalis fasciogularis: coastal eastern Australia (Townsville, Queensland southward to Clarence River, New South Wales)
Gavicalis versicolor: coastal New Guinea and satellite islands, and northeastern Australia
Gecinulus grantia: patchy in lowland and foothill forest, secondary growth, and bamboo scrub, from eastern Nepal eastward to southeastern China, and southward to northern Thailand and southern Vietnam
Gecinulus rafflesii: tropical rainforest and swamp forest in the Malayan Peninsula from southern Myanmar (southern Tenasserim) and Peninsular Thailand southward to southern Malaysian Peninsula, Sumatra, Bangka, and Borneo
Gecinulus viridis: lowlands of eastern Myanmar, adjacent Thailand, northern Laos, and Malayan Peninsula
Gelochelidon macrotarsa: breeds Australia (except arid areas); ranges to coastal southern New Guinea and Timor (eastern Lesser Sundas)
Gelochelidon nilotica: local yet widespread inland, rivers and lakes from southwestern Europe to northeastern China; coastal China; coastal western North Atlantic, and Caribbean; coastal southern California and Mexico; coastal South America and inland north-central Argentina; winters to subtropical and tropical coasts (including northern Australia), worldwide (except remote islands)
Geobiastes squamiger: dense rainforest of central and northeastern Madagascar
Geocerthia serrana: tall puna grassland, arid montane scrub and Polylepis woodland in the Andes from northern Peru (Cajamarca) southward to southern Peru (northeastern Ayacucho)
Geococcyx californianus: arid southwestern USA to southern Mexico
Geococcyx velox: arid western Mexico (east-central Sonora) southward in Pacific coast of Mexico, in east-central Veracruz, northwestern and north-central Yucatan Peninsula, and to northwestern Nicaragua
Geoffroyus geoffroyi: Moluccas and Lesser Sundas to northeastern Australia
Geokichla camaronensis: disjunctly in lowland and foothill primary forest understory from southern Cameroon (sight record for Bioko, Gulf of Guinea) southward to western Republic of the Congo and far western Democratic Republic of the Congo, and in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Uganda
Geokichla citrina:
foothill to montane understory of deciduous and evergreen forest, mixed secondary woodland, and bamboo thickets, from northern Pakistan eastward through Himalayas to southeastern China (including Hainan), and southward to Peninsular India, Andaman and Nicobar islands, central Indochina, and disjunctly to northern Borneo, Java, and Bali; Himalayan populations migrate south as far as
 Sri Lanka and Malayan Peninsula
Geokichla crossleyi: disjunctly in foothill and montane primary forest understory, from southeastern Nigeria and Cameroon southward to southern Republic of Congo, and in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Geokichla dohertyi: Lesser Sundas (Lombok, Sumbawa, Sumba, and Flores) and western Timor
Geokichla erythronota: Sulawesi and islands to the southeast
Geokichla gurneyi: patchy in foothill and montane primary forest understory from western Angola, southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and southern Kenya southward through Tanzania, Malawi, Mozambique, and eastern Zimbabwe, to eastern South Africa
Geokichla guttata: disjunctly in lowland and foothill evergreen forest, coastal dune forest, and coral-rag forest, from southern South Sudan, southeastern Tanzania, southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, southern Malawi, and northeastern and southern Mozambique southward to coastal southeastern South Africa; some populations migrate to coastal northeastern Tanzania and southeastern Kenya
Geokichla interpres: Thai-Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Java, Borneo, southern Philippines (Sulu Archipelago), and Lesser Sundas (Lombok, Sumbawa, and Flores)

Helopsaltes fasciolatus: breeds northeastern Asia; winters to Philippines, Indonesia, and western New Guinea

Hemicircus concretus: humid and swamp forest and adjacent clearings in the Malayan Peninsula from southernmost Myanmar (Tenasserim) and southern Peninsular Thailand southward to southern Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatra (including the Mentawai Islands), Bangka, Java, and Borneo
Hemignathus affinis: formerly wet ohia forest of Maui (Hawaiian Islands); extinct
Hemignathus hanapepe: formerly wet ohia forest of Kauai (Hawaiian Islands); extinct
Hemignathus lucidus: formerly wet ohia forest of Oahu (Hawaiian Islands); extinct, last reported in the 1860s
Hemignathus wilsoni: montane koa forest of Hawaii (Hawaiian Islands); rare
Hemimacronyx chloris: patchy and local in submontane to montane open short grassland, often with tussocks, in highlands of western and central Kenya
Hemiphaga chathamensis: Chatham Islands; now mainly southeastern Chatham Island
Hemiphaga novaeseelandiae: North, South, and Stewart islands (New Zealand) and formerly Norfolk Island (far east of Australia)
Hemiprocne comata: Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, Borneo, and Philippines (except Palawan)
Hemiprocne coronata: India to southwestern China, Myanmar, and Indochina

Hemiprocne mystacea: northern and central Moluccas, New Guinea, Bismarck Archipelago, and Solomon Archipelago
Hemipus hirundinaceus: Thai-Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, and associated islands (Simeulue, Nias, Riau and Lingga archipelagos, Bangka and Belitung islands), Borneo (including Banggi, off northern Borneo), Java, and Bali
Hemipus picatus: lowland to submontane open forest, secondary forest, bamboo, scrub, and plantations, from western Himachal Pradesh (northern India) eastward through Himalayan foothills to south-central China, and southward to southwestern India, Sri Lanka, Sumatra, and Borneo
Hemitesia neumanni: foothill to montane forest understory, riparian thickets, and swamp-forest, in Albertine Rift highlands of eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to southwestern Uganda, western Rwanda, and western Burundi

Hemithraupis ruficapilla: humid to semi-humid forest and woodland in the Atlantic Forest region from eastern Brazil (Bahia), southward to southeastern Brazil (northern Rio Grande do Sul)
Hemitriccus cinnamomeipectus: southern Ecuador (Cordillera del Cóndor) to northern Peru (San Martín)

Hemitriccus diops: southeastern Brazil (southeastern Bahia) to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
Hemitriccus flammulatus: mostly bamboo thickets inside tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin of southeastern Peru (Ucayali, Cusco, Madre de Dios, and northern Puno), and disjunctly in northern San Martin southward to northern and central Bolivia (to western Santa Cruz), and southwestern Brazil (Acre eastward to western Mato Grosso)

Hemitriccus granadensis: montane cloudforest in the coastal mountains of central-north Venezuela, and in the Sierra de Perijá, Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta and the Andes from far western Venezuela southward along the western and central Andes of Colombia to far northwestern Ecuador, and along the eastern Andes of Colombia and Ecuador to the eastern Andes of Peru and southeastward to northwestern Bolivia, to Cochabamba
Hemitriccus griseipectus: tropical rainforest, varzea forest, and woodland from far eastern Peru southward to northern Bolivia, foothills of the Andes to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz), and eastward across Amazonian Brazil, south of the Amazon River (to east-central Pará and adjacent Tocantins), and the Atlantic Forest region of northeastern Brazil (Rio Grande do Norte southward to Alagoas)
Hemitriccus inornatus: northwestern Brazil (locally on Rio Negro and tributaries)
Hemitriccus iohannis: southeastern Colombia to eastern Peru, northern Bolivia, and western Amazonian Brazil
Hemitriccus josephinae: southern Guyana to Suriname, French Guiana, and northern Brazil (Amapá)
Hemitriccus margaritaceiventer: arid to semiarid scrub, riparian thickets, scrub, and savanna in the lowlands of northern Colombia and northern Venezuela Iincluding Isla Margarita), southward in interior Colombia along the Magdalena Valley, the tepuis of southern and eastern Venezuela, adjacent Guyana, and northernmost Brazil, Sierra de Chiribiquete in eastern Colombia, and locally in dry valleys of eastern Peru and northwestern Bolivia; also in the Cerrado and Caatinga from northeastern Brazil southwestward to eastern Bolivia, Paraguay, and northernmost Uruguay, to northern Argentina, southward to northern Buenos Aires, San Luis, and Córdoba, and locally in southern Amazonia west to eastern Amazonas and Rondônia

Hemitriccus mirandae: lowlands of eastern Brazil (Ceará, Pernambuco, and Alagoas)
Hemitriccus nidipendulus: humid forest and restinga in the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado regions of eastern Brazil from Sergipe and northern and interior Bahia southward to southern Paraná and adjacent Santa Catarina

Hemitriccus orbitatus: lowlands of southeastern Brazil (southern Minas Gerais to northeastern Rio Grande do Sul)
Hemitriccus rufigularis: foothills on east slope of Andes in Ecuador, Peru, and western Bolivia
Hemitriccus spodiops: Yungas of southeastern Peru (Puno) and Bolivia (southward to western Santa Cruz)
Hemitriccus striaticollis: humid to semi-humid woodland and scrub, thickets and bamboo stands in the Amazon basin in eastern Colombia, locally in dry valleys in eastern Peru and in the Cerrado and Caatinga from northeastern Brazil, in northern Maranhão and adjacent Pará southwestward to northern Mato Grosso do Sul and northern Bolivia; also in southern Amazonia in Brazil, south of the Amazon River, west to eastern Amazonas and north to central Pará, and in the Atlantic Forest from Rio Grande do Norte southward to central Bahia
Hemitriccus zosterops: tropical rainforest and woodland in the Amazon basin from southeastern Colombia southward to northeastern Peru, to Ucayali and adjacent Huánuco and Pasco, and eastward north of the Amazon River in Brazil, southern Venezuela and southern Guyana to northeastern Brazil, Suriname and French Guiana
Hemixos castanonotus: lowland to foothill broadleaf evergreen forest, secondary growth, and brushy ravines, in southeastern China (including Hainan), and northern Vietnam; may be irruptive in winter
Hemixos cinereus: montane Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, and Borneo
Hemixos flavala: patchy in foothill pine and broadleaf forest, bamboo, and wooded ravines, from northern India eastward through Himalaya foothills to northern Vietnam and adjacent China, and southward to southern Myanmar and western Cambodia; some downslope movement in winter
Henicopernis longicauda: New Guinea, including Raja Ampat Islands (off western New Guinea), Aru Islands (off southwestern New Guinea), and Yapen (Cenderawasih Bay, off northwestern New Guinea)
Henicophaps albifrons: New Guinea and some western satellite islands
Henicophaps foersteri: Umboi, New Britain, and Lolobau (southeastern Bismarck Archipelago)
Henicorhina anachoreta: temperate and upper subtropical Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
Henicorhina leucophrys: disjunctly in humid montane forest from Jalisco and San Luis Potosí (west- and east-central Mexico) southward to northern Nicaragua, and from northwestern Costa Rica to far northwestern Colombia, in coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Falcón eastward to Miranda), Santa Marta and Perijá mountains, Andes of western Venezuela southward to northern Peru north and west of the Río Marañón, and eastern Andes from northern Peru to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz)
Henicorhina leucoptera: Andes of northern Peru and adjacent Ecuador
Henicorhina leucosticta: disjunctly in humid forest in the Gulf slope, including the Yucatan Peninsula, from southern San Luis Potosí (east-central Mexico) to eastern Panama, the Pacific slope of Chiapas and Guatemala, and the Pacific lowlands of Costa Rica to northern Colombia southward along major river systems and west of the Andes southward to northwestern Ecuador, and east of the Andes in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from southern Venezuela, the Guianas, and northern Brazil, north of the Amazon River, westward to eastern Colombia and central Peru (to Pasco)
Herpetotheres cachinnans: northern Mexico (from southern Sonora and San Luis Potosí) southward through Central America to northeastern Panama and northern Colombia and, west of the Andes, southward to northwestern Peru (to Lambayeque), and east of the Andes, southward to Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, and southern and eastern Brazil
Herpsilochmus atricapillus: northeastern Brazil to eastern Bolivia, northwestern Paraguay, and far northwestern Argentina
Herpsilochmus axillaris: montane cloudforest in the western and central Andes of Colombia, and along the eastern Andes from southeastern Colombia southward to southeastern Peru and adjacent western Bolivia
Herpsilochmus dorsimaculatus: far eastern Colombia, southern Venezuela, and northwestern Amazonian Brazil
Herpsilochmus dugandi: locally in far southeastern Colombia, eastern Ecuador, and northeastern Peru
Herpsilochmus frater: humid to semi-humid forest in the lowlands of northwestern Colombia and eastern Panama, and isolated in western Ecuador; in the Sierra de Perijá and the slopes of the Andes of western Venezuela eastward along the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela, and from northern Venezuela southward along the eastern Andes to central Bolivia; also in the Guiana Shield of central and eastern Venezuela, adjacent Guyana, locally in Suriname and northern Brazil, in the eastern and southern Amazon basin from northeastern Brazil, south of the Amazon River, southward to south-central Brazil, in southern Mato Grosso and northeastern Bolivia; and isolated in Atlantic Forest of northeastern Brazil, in Rio Grande do Norte southward to Alagoas
Herpsilochmus gentryi: sandy soil forest in far southeastern Ecuador and northern Peru
Herpsilochmus longirostris: Brazilian plateau (Piauí to Mato Grosso do Sul) and northeastern Bolivia
Herpsilochmus motacilloides: east slope of Andes of Peru (Huánuco to Cusco)
Herpsilochmus parkeri: east slope of Andes of north-central Peru (San Martín)
Herpsilochmus pectoralis: locally in northeastern Brazil (Maranhão, Rio Grande do Norte, and Bahia)
Herpsilochmus pileatus: coastal eastern Brazil (Bahia south of Salvador)
Herpsilochmus praedictus: southwestern Amazonian Brazil (south of the Amazon River and west of the Rio Madeira)
Herpsilochmus roraimae: montane forest and sandy-soil forest in the tepuis of southeastern Venezuela, western Guyana, and northernmost Brazil (Roraima)
Herpsilochmus rufimarginatus: northeastern Brazil (Bahia) southward to eastern Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, and southeastern Brazil
Herpsilochmus stictocephalus: far eastern Venezuela to the Guianas and far northern Brazil
Herpsilochmus sticturus: eastern Venezuela to the Guianas and northeastern Amazonian Brazil
Herpsilochmus stotzi: Amazonian Brazil (south of the Amazon River, on the east bank of the Rio Madeira)
