Hesperiphona vespertina: breeds in conifer forest and pine-oak woodland from southern Yukon eastward to Newfoundland (northwestern to eastern Canada) southward to northern USA, in western USA southward in mountains to eastern California and New Mexico, and in Mexicon mountains to Durango, and (rare) in the volcanic belt of central Mexico to northern Oaxaca; winters irruptively from south-central Canada southward to south-central USA
Hesperoburhinus bistriatus: dry savanna, open scrub, pastures, and coastal grassy plains on the Gulf of Mexico slope (southern Veracruz to Tabasco and northern Chiapas) and adjacent Guatemala, and on the Pacific slope from southeastern Oaxaca southward to northwestern Costa Rica, in southern Bahamas (Great Inagua), and Hispaniola, and in northern Colombia and northwestern Venezuela (eastward to the Paría Peninsula and Isla Margarita), in interior Colombia southward along the Cauca and Magdalena valleys. east of the Andes in the llanos of southwestern Venezuela and northeastern Colombia, in the Guianan plateau of western Guyana, southeastern Venezuela, and northernmost Brazil (Roraima), and isolated in northeastern Brazil, north of the Amazon River (Amapá)
Hesperoburhinus superciliaris: arid littoral of southwestern Ecuador to northern Chile
Heteralocha acutirostris: formerly New Zealand; extinct, last reported 1907
Heterocercus aurantiivertex: locally in eastern Ecuador and adjacent northeastern Peru (southwestern Loreto)
Heterocercus flavivertex: eastern Colombia to southwestern Venezuela and northern Amazonian Brazil
Heterocercus linteatus: Amazonian Brazil (south of the Amazon River), far southeastern Peru, and northern and northeastern Bolivia
Heteromirafra archeri: disjunctly in foothill open grassland, rocky grassland with sparse scrub, and grassland among acacia savanna, at two sites in northeastern and southern Ethiopia; prior populations in northwestern Somali may be extirpated
Heteromirafra ruddi: disjunctly in foothill to submontane moist grassland, preferably native grassland that is moderately to heavily grazed, in northeastern and eastern South Africa
Heteromunia pectoralis: northern Australia (mainly Kimberley region, northern Western Australia, eastward to northwestern Queensland, but ranges to Pilbara Region and southwestern Cape York Peninsula)
Heteromyias albispecularis: northwestern New Guinea (Tamrau and Arfak mountains)
Heteromyias armiti: montane west-central, east-central, and southeastern New Guinea
Heteromyias cinereifrons: northeastern Australia (upland Wet Tropics region, northern Queensland)
Heteronetta atricapilla: lowlands of central Chile to Paraguay and southward to central Argentina
Heterophasia capistrata: foothill to montane broadleaf evergreen forest, oak-fir forest, secondary growth, and gardens, from northeastern Pakistan eastward through Himalayas to northeastern India and adjacent southern Tibet
Heterophasia desgodinsi: montane forest and edge from northeastern Myanmar eastward to western Hubei (central China) and south disjunctly through Laos and Vietnam
Heterophasia gracilis: montane forest of northeastern India, Myanmar, and southern China (western Yunnan)
Heterophasia melanoleuca: patchy in foothill to submontane broadleaf evergreen forest from eastern Myanmar eastward to western Laos, and southward to western Thailand
Heterophasia picaoides: foothill to montane broadleaf evergreen and oak-pine forest, secondary growth, and forest clearings, from northeastern India and Bhutan eastward through Himalayas to south-central China, and southward to central Vietnam, peninsular Malaysia, and Sumatra
Heterophasia pulchella: northeastern India (Arunachal Pradesh) and adjacent southern China (southeastern Tibet) and eastern Arunachal Pradesh southward to Nagaland), northern Myanmar, and southern China (western and northwestern Yunnan)
Heteroscenes pallidus: Australia including Tasmania; winters northward to eastern Lesser Sundas
Heterospingus rubrifrons: humid lowlands of eastern Costa Rica and Panama
Heterospingus xanthopygius: tropical rainforest from eastern Panama and northwestern Colombia eastward to the middle Magdalena Valley and southward along the Pacific lowlands to northwestern Ecuador
Heterotetrax humilis: acacia and thornbush of eastern Ethiopia and northern Somalia
Heterotetrax rueppelii: lowland and foothill subdesert, dark basaltic gravel plain, and barren flats with sparse grass or stunted scrub, of southwestern coastal Angola and coastal western and central Namibia

Heteroxolmis dominicana: southeastern Brazil (Paraná) to Paraguay, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
Hieraaetus ayresii: woodland and savanna of sub-Saharan Africa
Hieraaetus morphnoides: open woodland and savanna of Australia (except Tasmania)
Hieraaetus pennatus: breeds southern Palearctic and sub-Saharan Africa; winters to India and Sri Lanka, and southeastern Asia
Hierococcyx bocki: mountains of Malayan Peninsula and Sumatra
Hierococcyx fugax: southern Thailand, Malayan Peninsula, and Greater Sundas
Hierococcyx hyperythrus: breeds southeastern Siberia, northeastern China, Korean Peninsula, and Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu); winters to southeastern Asia, northern Borneo, and northern Sulawesi
Hierococcyx nisicolor: breeds Himalayas from eastern Nepal and hills south of the Brahmaputra River eastward to eastern China, from southern Sichuan northeast to Jiangsu and southeast to Hainan, and northern southeastern Asia; winters to Greater Sundas

Hierococcyx vagans: southern Myanmar including Mergui Archipelago, Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, and Borneo
Hierococcyx varius: lowland and foothill forest, plantation, and gardens, from northeastern Pakistan eastward through Himalayan foothills to western Myanmar, and southward through India to Sri Lanka; partially migratory at higher elevations

Himantopus leucocephalus: Philippines, Indonesian Archipelago, New Guinea region, Australia (including Tasmania), North, South, Stewart, and Chatham islands (New Zealand), and New Britain

Himantopus novaezelandiae: MacKenzie Basin (central South Island, New Zealand); winters to North Island
Himantornis haematopus: humid forest of Sierra Leone to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Gabon
Himatione sanguinea: Kauai, Oahu, Molokai, Maui, and Hawaii (Hawaiian Islands)
Hippolais icterina: breeds central Europe to western Siberia and northern Iran; winters to southern Africa
Hippolais languida: breeds south-central Asia; winters in northeastern Africa and southern Arabia
Hippolais olivetorum: breeds Balkan Peninsula and Türkiye; winters in eastern and southeastern Africa
Hippolais polyglotta: breeds southwestern Palearctic; winters in savanna of western Africa
Hirundapus caudacutus: disjunctly in foothill to montane forest, woodland, and sparsely vegetated slopes, from central Siberia eastward to Sakhalin and Kuril islands, and southward to Mongolia, northeastern China, Korean Peninsula, and Japan (Hokkaido to central Honshu), and from northeastern Pakistan eastward through the Himalayas to south-central China; northern population winters to New Guinea and eastern Australia
Hirundapus cochinchinensis: very local breeder, foothill to montane forest from Uttarakhand (western Himalayas) through northeastern India, also southern and eastern China (including Hainan) and Taiwan; winters southward through Malayan Peninsula and Java; generally scarce and little-known
Hirundapus giganteus: humid to deciduous forest and open areas in Western Ghats of Peninsular India from southern Maharashtra southward, and central and southern Sri Lanka, disjunctly in Assam and northeastern Indian hills south of Brahmaputra River, Bangladesh, and Andaman Islands, southward through northern Myanmar and southernmost China (southern Yunnan; rare) to southern Cambodia and Vietnam, the entire Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, Java, Bali, and Borneo, and Palawan (southwestern Philippines)
Hirundinea ferruginea: rocky outcrops, cliffs, canyons, landslides, and banks near humid montane and lowland forest in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Sierra de Perijá, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward along the central and eastern Andes of Colombia and eastern Andes of Ecuador to northwestern Argentina, including the sierras of Córdoba and San Luis; in the Guiana Shield of southern Venezuela, the Guianas, easternmost Colombia and northern Brazil; and widespread in eastern and interior Brazil (Maranhão, Piauí, and Ceará southward), to eastern Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, and Uruguay; also locally in southern Amazon of Brazil and in eastern Bolivia

Hirundo albigularis: lowland to foothill grassland, open woodland, floodplain, and towns, often near water, from southern Malawi and southern Zambia southward to South Africa; southern populations migrate north to Angola and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Hirundo angolensis: patchy in lowlands to montane open country, grassland, cultivation, swamp and forest edge, and villages, from Gabon eastward, avoiding rainforest, to Uganda and western Kenya, and southward to Angola, northern Zambia, and northern Malawi; some post-breeding dispersal
Hirundo atrocaerulea: patchy in foothill and submontane open grassland, swamps, and woodland edge, from southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, southern Tanzania, and Malawi, southward to eastern South Africa and Eswatini; migrates northward to eastern Africa (Lake Victoria basin)
Hirundo dimidiata: lowland grassland, scrub, open woodland, farms, and towns, from Angola eastward through southern Democratic Republic of the Congo to Malawi, thence southward to southern South Africa; southernmost populations migratory
Hirundo javanica: southeastern Asia from Andamans to Ryukyu Islands southward through Indonesia and Philippines to New Guinea, Bismarck Archipelago, Solomon Islands, New Caledonia, Vanuatu, Fiji, and Tonga (western Polynesia)
Hirundo leucosoma: lowland to foothill wooded savanna, rivers and lakes, forest clearings, and towns, from Senegambia eastward, avoiding rainforest, to western Niger and central Nigeria
Hirundo lucida: patchy in lowland to montane grassland, savanna, marsh, and towns, from western Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to Benin, and riverine habitats in Gabon and along the Congo River in Republic of the Congo and western Democratic Republic of the Congo, and highlands in Ethiopia; some local migration in western African populations
Hirundo megaensis: foothill to submontane open acacia woodland, semiarid grassland, and villages, in highlands of southern Ethiopia
Hirundo neoxena: western, southern, and eastern Australia; some winter north to central Australia and Cape York Peninsula, Torres Strait, Lord Howe and Norfolk islands (east of Australia); colonized Norfolk Island and New Zealand including the Chatham Islands in the mid-20th century; also recently recorded southern New Guinea and New Caledonia
Hirundo nigrita: lowland to foothill rivers and streams in rainforest, lagoons, and mangroves, from southern Guinea and Sierra Leone eastward to western Uganda, and southward to northern Angola and south-central Democratic Republic of the Congo
Hirundo nigrorufa: lowland to foothill grassland, savanna, seasonally flooded plains, and burnt or cleared woodland, from central Angola eastward to southern Democratic Republic of the Congo and northern Zambia; some post-breeding dispersal
Hirundo rustica: open areas of Eurasia from northern Scandinavia and most of Europe southward to northern Africa and eastward through Central Asia, China, and Siberia to Kamchatka, and southern Alaska and northwestern Canada southward to southern US and northern Mexico; winters in Africa south of the Sahara, the Indian subcontinent, southeastern Asia including the Philippines, most of Indonesia, New Guinea and northern Australia, and most Central America and South America; also breeds in east-central Argentina
Hirundo smithii: disjunctly, in sub-Saharan Africa from Senegal, southern Mali and central Ivory Coast eastward to central Sudan and Somalia, and southward (outside central rainforest zone) to northern Namibia and northeastern South Africa, and breeding visitor to southern Uzbekistan, southern Tajikistan, Afghanistan, northern Pakistan, and northwestern India; resident in southeastern Pakistan, most of India, southwestern Nepal, through southeastern Asia (except Malayan Peninsula)
Hirundo tahitica: mainly in forested river valleys of Moorea (rare) and Tahiti (Windward Society Islands)
Histrionicus histrionicus: breeds eastern Siberia and northern Japan (Hokkaido to central Honshu), Alaska southward to Oregon and Wyoming, eastern Canada (southeastern Baffin Island southward to the Gulf of St. Lawrence), Greenland, and Iceland; winters coastally from Siberia to Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu) and Korean Peninsula, from Alaska to central California, to the northeastern USA, southern Greenland, and Iceland
Histurgops ruficauda: foothill thornscrub and grassland in north-central Tanzania and, recently, adjacent Masai Mara (south-central Kenya)
Hoploxypterus cayanus: riverbanks and mudflats of lowlands to hills in tropical South America east of the Andes south to Paraguay, south-eastern Brazil, and (rarely) north-eastern Argentina; west of the Andes only in western Ecuador
Horizocerus albocristatus: lowland and foothill Upper Guinea rainforest, and swamp forest, from Sierra Leone and southeastern Guinea to southern Benin
Horizocerus cassini: Benin through Congo basin to western Uganda and northern Angola
Horizocerus granti: Congo Basin of Central African Republic to Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda
Horizocerus hartlaubi: Sierra Leone to northern Democratic Republic of the Congo (west of the Congo River)
Horornis acanthizoides: patchy in foothill to montane tall grassland, bamboo thickets, understory of forest, and stunted juniper above tree-line, in central and southeastern China and Taiwan; some may move downslope in winter
Horornis annae: Palau (Babelthuap, Koror, Garakayo, Peleliu, and Ngabad)
Horornis brunnescens: Himalayas of northern India, Nepal, Bhutan, and southeastern Tibet
Horornis canturians: breeds central and eastern China, southeastern Siberia, and Korean Peninsula; winters to southern China, southeastern Asia, and northern Philippines
Horornis diphone: montane forest borders, bush, gardens, and bamboo thickets from southern Sakhalin and Kuril Islands (southeastern Russia) southward through Japan to Ryukyu, Ogasawara (Bonin), and Iwo (Volcano) islands, and in South Korea; introduced to Hawaiian Islands (all main islands)
Horornis flavolivaceus: Himalayas to northern Vietnam and central China and montane Greater and Lesser Sundas and Palawan (southwestern Philippines)
Horornis fortipes: foothill to montane dense understory of forest, bamboo thickets, and grassy edges to clearings, from northern Pakistan eastward through Himalayas to central and southeastern China and Taiwan, and southward to western Myanmar and northern southeastern Asia; downslope altitudinal migrant in winter
Horornis seebohmi: montane forest of northern Luzon (northern Philippines)
Houbaropsis bengalensis: disjunctly in lowland open grassland with scattered bush, and recently burnt or grazed grassland, from southern Nepal eastward to northeastern India, and in Cambodia; dispersive post-breeding; extirpated Bangladesh and southern Vietnam
Hydrobates castro: breeds on northeastern Atlantic islands, islets near St. Helena and Ascension islands, in Pacific off central Japan (northeastern Honshu), Hawaiian Islands (Kauai), and the Galapagos; ranges in Atlantic to Gulf Stream, Gulf of Mexico, western Africa including Gulf of Guinea, in North Pacific, seas off Japan, the Marquesas Islands, near the main Hawaiian Islands, and coasts of southern Central America to northwestern South America
Hydrobates cheimomnestes: winter breeder on islets off Guadalupe Island (western Mexico); nonbreeding range poorly known, but apparently disperses southward in eastern Pacific, at least as far as the Galapagos
Hydrobates furcatus: breeds islands off northern Kuril and Commander islands (southeastern Russia), Aleutians, and Gulf of Alaska to northern California; non-breeders range to northeastern coast of Japan, southern Sea of Okhotsk, northern Bering Sea, and central Californian coast
Hydrobates homochroa: breeds islands off California and northern Baja California, from Mendocino County (northwestern California) patchily southward to Isla Todos Santos (northwestern Baja California); ranges coastal California Current to northern California (including Monterey Bay) and north-central Baja California
Hydrobates hornbyi: breeds Atacama Desert, mostly in mountains well inland (northern Chile); ranges Humboldt Current of southern Ecuador to north-central Chile
Hydrobates jabejabe: breeds in winter on Cabo Verde; present all year around Cabo Verde, and extent of at-sea range unknown, possibly to eastern North America

Hydrobates matsudairae: breeds Iwo (Volcano) Islands, possibly also Ogasawara (Bonin) Islands (far southern Japan); disperses westward to Arabian Sea, Seychelles, and off eastern African coast, eastward to western Micronesia, seas of eastern Indonesia, and off northwestern Australia

Hydrobates monteiroi: breeds in summer on Azores; present Azores mainly April-August, and extent of at-sea range unknown, possibly to eastern North America
Hydrobates pelagicus: islets of northeastern North Atlantic from southern Iceland and central Norway to northern Spain, Canary Islands, western Africa, and western and north-central Mediterranean Sea
Hydrobates socorroensis: summer breeder on islets off Guadalupe Island (western Mexico); ranges in eastern Pacific north to southern California and southward to ca. 10°N

Hydrobates tristrami: breeds Izu, Ogasawara (Bonin), and at least formerly Iwo (Volcano) Islands (southern Japan), and Northwestern Hawaiian Islands; ranges eastern coastal waters of Japan and eastward to Hawaiian Islands (Kauai)
Hydrochous gigas: southern Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, Java, and Borneo
Hydrocoloeus minutus: breeds Baltic region eastward to Sea of Okhotsk and southward to northern Kazakhstan and northeastern China, also rarely Great Lakes, Hudson and James bays (east-central Canada); winters North Atlantic coasts and North, Mediterranean, Baltic, Black, and Caspian seas
Hydrophasianus chirurgus: breeds northern Pakistan eastward in sub-Himalayan region to southeastern China and Taiwan, and southward to southern India, Sri Lanka, southeastern Asia, and Philippines; winters sparsely southward to Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, Java, and Bali

Hydropsalis cayennensis: dry savanna, low arid and open scrub, and thickets in the Pacific lowlands of Costa Rica and Panama, and in northern Colombia eastward to northern Venezuela, the Netherlands Antilles, Trinidad and Tobago, the Guianas, and far northern Brazil, in Amapá and Roraima; in Venezuela southward to northern Amazonas and southwestward to the llanos of northeastern Colombia, and in central Colombia southward to the headwaters of the Río Magdalena and Río Cauca; also locally in Andean valleys of northern Ecuador, and on Martinique (Lesser Antilles)
Hydropsalis climacocerca: riverine habitats of Amazonia and the Guianas from eastern Colombia eastward to north-central Brazil and southward through central Bolivia and Mato Grosso (central Brazil)
Hydropsalis forcipata: southeastern Brazil and adjacent northeastern Argentina (Misiones)
Hydropsalis torquata: arid scrub, grasslands, dry scrub, and open fields in the Sipaliwini savanna of southern Suriname, and from northeastern Brazil, in southern Amapá and northern Pará, southward and southwestward across the southern Amazon, interior and eastern Brazil to northern and eastern Bolivia and southeastern Peru, and southward across Paraguay and Uruguay to central Argentina, seasonally to western Buenos Aires, southern La Pampa, eastern Neuquén, and northern Río Negro; also locally in dry Andean valleys in eastern Peru

Hydrornis cyaneus: patchy in lowland to foothill forest and bamboo, often with steep ravines, and in limestone forest, from northeastern India and eastern Bangladesh, and eastward to central Vietnam, thence southward to peninsular Thailand and Cambodia
Hydrornis elliotii: far southeastern Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, and Cambodia
Hydrornis gurneyi: far southern Myanmar (southern Tenasserim); formerly also peninsular Thailand, where now may be extinct
Hydrornis irena: southern peninsular Thailand, Malayan Peninsula, and Sumatra
Hydrornis nipalensis: patchy in lowland to foothill tropical secondary forest, bamboo, and swamp-forest, from eastern Nepal eastward through Himalayan foothills to northern Vietnam and adjacent southern China, and southward to northern Thailand and central Laos
Hydrornis oatesi: patchy in foothill to montane dense primary and secondary forest, from northern Myanmar eastward to northern Vietnam and southern China, and southward to southern Vietnam and peninsula Malaysia
Hydrornis phayrei: Bangladesh to Myanmar, Thailand, southern China, southern Cambodia, and central Annam

Hyliota flavigaster: moist savanna and open woodland from Senegal eastward to central Ethiopia and western Kenya, and in the south to central Angola and central Mozambique
Hyliota usambara: lowland to foothill forest canopy, forest edge, and coffee plantations, on eastern Usambara Mountains in northeastern Tanzania
Hyliota violacea: forest, woodland, and edge of lowlands to hills from Sierra Leone eastward to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Hylocharis chrysura: Bolivia to Paraguay, Uruguay, southeastern Brazil, and northern Argentina
Hylocharis sapphirina: eastern Colombia to the Guianas, southern Venezuela, southeastern Brazil, and northeastern Argentina
Hylocichla mustelina: breeds eastern North America; winters southern Texas to Panama
Hylomanes momotula: humid forest in lowlands to hills of Caribbean slope from eastern Veracruz and northern Oaxaca (southeastern Mexico) southward through southern Yucatan Peninsula to north-central Nicaragua; Pacific slope in Chiapas to El Salvador, and northwestern Costa Rica; and patchily in Panama and adjacent northwestern Colombia
Hylopezus auricularis: northern Bolivia (southeastern Pando and northern Beni)
Hylopezus macularius: tropical rainforest and gallery forest in the Guiana Shield and the Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern and southern Venezuela, the Guianas, and eastern Colombia southward to northern Brazil, southeastern Colombia, and northeastern Peru north of the Amazon River
Hylopezus ochroleucus: interior northeastern Brazil (Piauí and Ceará to far northern Minas Gerais)

Hylopezus perspicillatus: humid forest of lowland and hills on Caribbean slope of northeastern Honduras to western Panama and Pacific slope from north-central Costa Rica through Panama to north-central Colombia and, west of the Andes, to northwestern Ecuador

Hylophilus moxensis: marsh scrub in Beni, north-central Bolivia
Hylophilus olivaceus: subtropical Andes of eastern Ecuador to central Peru (Junín)

Hylophilus poicilotis: northern Bolivia to eastern Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, and southern Brazil

Hylophylax punctulatus: southeastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, northern Bolivia, and Amazonian Brazil

Hylorchilus sumichrasti: lowlands of southern Mexico (Veracruz, Puebla, and adjacent northern Oaxaca)
Hymenolaimus malacorhynchos: central and southern North Island and western South Island (New Zealand)

Hypargos niveoguttatus: patchy in lowland to foothill thickets, long grass, and riparian forest, from Rwanda and Burundi to central Kenya and southern Somalia southward to northeastern Angola, southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northern Mozambique, thence southward to northeastern Botswana, eastern Zimbabwe, and southern Mozambique

Hypocnemis flavescens: east-central Colombia to southern Venezuela and far northwestern Amazonian Brazil

Hypocnemis ochrogyna: eastern Bolivia (eastern Beni and Santa Cruz) and south-central Amazonian Brazil

Hypocnemis rondoni: south-central Brazil, between the Rio Madeira/Rio Ji-Paraná and the Rio Aripuanã
Hypocnemis striata: tropical rainforest in the eastern Amazon basin, south of the Amazon River, from northern Para southward to northern Mato Grosso, west to the Rio Madeira and east to the Rio Tapajos
Hypocnemis subflava: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin from north-central Peru, in southern San Martin, southward to southwestern Brazil and central Bolivia
Hypocnemoides maculicauda: eastern Peru to northern Bolivia and southern Amazonian Brazil
Hypocnemoides melanopogon: flooded rainforest, white-sand, and gallery forest in the Guiana Shield, the Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward northeastern Ecuador, northeastern Peru, and in Brazil southward along the Rio Madeira basin to southeastern Amazonas and northern Rondônia

Hypoedaleus guttatus: southeastern Brazil to eastern Paraguay and far northeastern Argentina (Misiones)
Hypositta corallirostris: forest and plateaus of humid eastern Madagascar
Hypothymis azurea: lowland to foothill broadleaf forest, secondary growth, bamboo, and plantations, from Haryana and Gujarat (western India) eastward to southeastern China (including Hainan) and Taiwan, and southward to Sri Lanka, Andaman and Nicobar islands, Philippines, Greater Sundas, and Lesser Sundas (eastward to Alor)
Hypothymis helenae: Philippines (except Palawan group, Mindoro, West Visayas, and Sulu Archipelago)
Hypsipetes borbonicus: evergreen forest of Réunion (western Mascarene Islands)
Hypsipetes chloris: northern Moluccas (Morotai, Halmahera, Bacan, and Kasiruta)
Hypsipetes everetti: East Visayas, Mindanao group and Sulu Archipelago (east-central and southern Philippines)
Hypsipetes ganeesa: open forest and woodland in the Western Ghats of India from northern Maharashtra southward to southernmost Kerala and southwestern Tamil Nadu, and Shevaroy Hills in southern Eastern Ghats, and in the wet zone of central and southern Sri Lanka
Hypsipetes guimarasensis: central Philippines (Guimaras, Masbate, Panay, Negros, Ticao, and Verde)
Hypsipetes harterti: Peleng, Banggai, and Labobo, in Banggai Islands (off eastern Sulawesi)
Hypsipetes leucocephalus: foothill to montane broadleaf forest, and oak, pine and rhododendron forest, from northeastern Afghanistan and northern Pakistan eastward to southeastern China (including Hainan), and Taiwan, and southward to southern Myanmar and Indochina; most mainland China populations migrate southward in winter, downslope dispersal post-breeding in Himalayas
Hypsipetes madagascariensis: Comoros, Aldabra (southwestern Seychelles), Madagascar, and some satellite islands
Hypsipetes olivaceus: upland mostly native forest of Mauritius (western Mascarene Islands)
Hypsipetes philippinus: northern, central, eastern, and southern Philippines
Hypsipetes rufigularis: southern Philippines (Basilan and Zamboanga Peninsula of western Mindanao)
Hypsipetes siquijorensis: Tablas, Romblon, Cebu, and Siquijor (north-central and central Philippines)
Hypsipetes thompsoni: montane forest of southern Myanmar to northwestern Thailand
Ianthocincla bieti: mountains of southern China (southwestern Sichuan and northwestern Yunnan)
Ianthocincla cineracea: northeastern India (from hills south of the Brahmaputra), northern Myanmar, and southwestern China eastward to Fujian, Guangdong, and far northern Vietnam; introduced southern Japan (Shikoku)
Ianthocincla lunulata: south-central China (southern Gansu, southern Shaanxi and western Sichuan)
Ianthocincla maxima: mountains of southeastern Tibet to southern China (southern Gansu, western Sichuan, and northwestern Yunnan)

Ichthyaetus relictus: breeds lakes of northeastern Kazakhstan eastward to Transbaikalia (southeastern Russia) and Inner Mongolia (northeastern China); winters coasts of Korean Peninsula, Bohai Bay, Yellow Sea, and East China Sea

Icterus abeillei: riparian woodland of central plateau and eastern Mexico
Icterus auricapillus: lowlands of eastern Panama to northern Colombia and northern Venezuela

Icterus melanopsis: Cuba including Isla de la Juventud
