Lamprotornis hildebrandti: foothill to submontane thornscrub, open woodland, and villages, from north-central Kenya southward to central Tanzania
Lamprotornis iris: lowland to foothill wooded savanna from southern Guinea and northern Sierra Leone eastward to central Ivory Coast; seasonal dispersal
Lamprotornis mevesii: open woodland of lowland and hills from west-central Angola and northern Namibia eastward to northeastern Zambia, Malawi, and southwestern Mozambique
Lamprotornis nitens: lowland to submontane wooded savanna woodland, riverine woodland, forest edge, plantations, parks and gardens, from far western Democratic Republic of the Congo and western and southern Angola, and eastward to southern Zambia, and southward to South Africa (except southwest) and southern Mozambique
Lamprotornis pulcher: lowland to foothill dry savanna, thornscrub, brushy steppe, cultivation, and villages, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward across the Sahel to central Sudan and Eritrea; nomadic dispersal post-breeding
Lamprotornis purpureus: savanna and scrub including around villages from lowlands to hills from far southern Mauritania and western Senegal, and in southern Ghana, eastward to southern South Sudan and western Kenya
Lamprotornis purpuroptera: open woodland to urban areas from lowlands to hills in southeastern Sudan and Eritrea eastward to central Somalia and southward through far northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, Burundi, and western and northern Tanzania
Lamprotornis regius: lowland to foothill savanna, thornscrub, and dry brushy grassland, from eastern and southern Ethiopia and Somalia southward to northeastern Tanzania
Lamprotornis shelleyi: lowland to foothill open woodland, brushy steppe, thornscrub, and semi-desert, from northern Somalia southward through eastern and southern Ethiopia to southeastern South Sudan, northern Uganda, and northern Kenya; some migrate southward post-breeding to central and southern Kenya and northeastern Tanzania
Lamprotornis splendidus: forest and edge to cultivation of lowlands to hills from Senegal eastward to southwestern Ethiopia and southward to Angola and Zambia; also Bioko and irregularly Príncipe (Gulf of Guinea)
Lamprotornis superbus: lowland to montane open woodland, arid brushy savanna; lakeshore woodland, cultivation, parks and gardens, from South Sudan eastward to Somalia, and southward through eastern Uganda and Kenya to south-central Tanzania
Lamprotornis unicolor: foothill dry open woodland, savanna, and wooded grassland, from north-central to south-central Tanzania; some nomadic dispersal in dry season
Laniarius aethiopicus: lowland to montane forest edge, bamboo thickets, juniper woodland, miombo woodland, acacia scrub, and tall grass savanna, from Eritrea eastward to northern Somalia, and southward through Ethiopia to eastern South Sudan and far northern Kenya
Laniarius amboimensis: patchy and local in lowland to foothill understory of evergreen escarpment forest, degraded farmbush and plantations, of northwestern and western Angola
Laniarius atrococcineus: lowland to foothill thornscrub, and dense acacia woodland, from southern Angola, southwestern Zambia, and western Zimbabwe southward to northern South Africa
Laniarius atroflavus: foothill to montane dense understory in forest, and in patches of remnant forest, and bamboo thickets, in southeastern Nigeria and western Cameroon
Laniarius barbarus: lowland dense undergrowth in dry wooded savanna, riverine bush, and mangroves, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to central Mali and southern Chad, and southward to coastal Sierra Leone and northern Cameroon
Laniarius bicolor: lowland papyrus swamp and reedbeds, riverine thickets, and mangroves, from coastal Cameroon and Gabon southward to western Angola, thence eastward to northern Namibia, western Zambia, and northern Botswana
Laniarius brauni: patchy and local in lowland understory of degraded secondary forest, gallery forest, and escarpment forest in northwestern Angola
Laniarius erythrogaster: lowland to foothill thornscrub, bushy grassland, riparian thickets, acacia woodland, and papyrus swamps, from northeastern Nigeria, northern Cameroon, and southern Chad eastward to southeastern Sudan and Eritrea, and southward to southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and northern Tanzania
Laniarius ferrugineus: lowland semiarid dense woodland, riverine thickets, and coastal scrub, from far southeastern Zimbabwe and southern Mozambique southward to southeastern Botswana, Eswatini, and southern South Africa (west to Western Cape)
Laniarius fuelleborni: foothill to montane forest understory, and dense highland bush, from northeastern Tanzania southward through Eastern Arc Mountains (Tanzania) to northern Malawi and far eastern Zambia (Nyika Plateau)
Laniarius funebris: central Ethiopia and Somalia southward to Uganda and central Tanzania
Laniarius holomelas: montane dense understory and edges of cloudforest, gallery forest, and bamboo thickets, in Albertine Rift highlands of northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and eastward to western Uganda, Rwanda, and Burundi
Laniarius leucorhynchus: disjunctly in lowland to foothill dense understory in rainforest and in remnant forest in savanna, swamp-forest, and thickets in papyrus marsh, from Sierra Leone and southeastern Guinea eastward to southern Togo, and from southeastern Nigeria eastward to southwestern South Sudan and Uganda, and southward to far northwestern and northeastern Angola and central Democratic Republic of the Congo
Laniarius luehderi: disjunctly in lowland to montane open secondary forest, and overgrown plantations, from southeastern Nigeria and southern Cameroon southward to Cabinda (northwestern Angola) and western Democratic Republic of the Congo, and from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to southern South Sudan and western Kenya, and southward to Rwanda, Burundi, and western Tanzania
Laniarius major: lowland to montane riverine lowland forest edges, and miombo woodland, from Guinea eastward to southern South Sudan and western Kenya, and southward to northeastern Namibia and northeastern South Africa
Laniarius mufumbiri: lowland to submontane papyrus swamps and reedbeds, usually beside meandering rivers and along lakeshores, from Uganda and southwestern Kenya southward to far eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi, and northwestern Tanzania
Laniarius nigerrimus: patchy in lowland riparian scrub, tall scrubby woodland, acacia thickets, and thornscrub, from southeastern Somalia southward to coastal northeastern Kenya
Laniarius poensis: foothill to montane forest understory and edges, of far southeastern Nigeria, western Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea)
Laniarius ruficeps: lowland and foothill thornscrub from Eritrea, eastern Ethiopia and northern Somalia southward to southeastern Kenya
Laniarius sublacteus: lowland to submontane understory of highland forest, coastal forest, riparian thickets, and woody tangles in cultivation, from coastal southern Somalia southward through coastal Kenya to northeastern Tanzania, including Unguja (in Zanzibar)
Laniarius turatii: lowland savanna woodland, mostly in dense canopy, from southern Senegal and Guinea-Bissau southward to Sierra Leone
Laniarius willardi: patchy in submontane to montane forest on eastern slope of Albertine Rift highlands in southwestern Uganda, and southward to northwestern Burundi and adjacent eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Laniellus albonotatus: montane forest of western and central Java
Laniisoma buckleyi: humid foothill and montane forest in the eastern Andes from far southwestern Venezuela southward patchily from Colombia to western Bolivia
Laniisoma elegans: tropical southeastern Brazil (Espírito Santo to eastern Paraná)
Lanio aurantius: Gulf-Caribbean lowlands of southeastern Mexico to northwestern Honduras
Lanio fulvus: tropical rainforest in the foothills of the Andes in northeastern Colombia and adjacent western Venezuela, in the Orinoco basin of eastern Venezuela, the Guianas, and northern Amazon basin, north of the Amazon River, from southeastern Colombia to northeastern Peru and eastward to northern Brazil
Lanio leucothorax: lowland forest of Caribbean slope from northeastern Honduras through central Panama, and Pacific slope of southwestern Costa Rica and far western Panama
Lanio versicolor: tropical rainforest in the southern Amazon basin from northeastern Peru (Loreto), southward along the base of the Andes to central Bolivia, and eastward across Brazil, south of the Amazon River (to eastern Pará, west of the Rio Tocantins)
Laniocera hypopyrra: eastern Colombia to Venezuela, eastern Brazil, northern Bolivia, and Amazonian Brazil
Laniocera rufescens: humid forest from southeastern Mexico southward along the Caribbean slope of Central America to eastern Panama; in northern Colombia in the lower Cauca and middle Magdalena Valleys, and west of the Andes southward to northwestern Ecuador
Lanioturdus torquatus: lowland acacia thornscrub, miombo and mopane woodland, teak woodland, and wooded scrub on rocky hillsides, from southwestern Angola southward to west-central Namibia; some seasonal dispersal
Lanius borealis: breeds central to eastern Siberia, southward to northwestern China and northwestern Mongolia to Sakhalin and Kuril Islands, and breeds Alaska and northern Canada, southward to far northern British Columbia and Alberta, northern Ontario and Quebec; winters Mongolia to central Japan, and southern Canada and northern USA
Lanius bucephalus: patchy in lowland to submontane forest edge, farmland, and open habitats, from north-central China eastward to Ussuriland and Sakhalin (Russia), and southward to Korea and Japan; northern populations migrate to southeastern China
Lanius cabanisi: lowland to foothill savanna, shrubby open woodland, and cultivation, from southern Somalia southward through southern Kenya to eastern Tanzania
Lanius collaris: open areas of lowlands to mountains from northern Angola eastward to northeastern and south-central Tanzania, in south to southern Cape of South Africa
Lanius collurio: breeds Palearctic region; winters to South Africa
Lanius collurioides: foothill to montane forest edge, scrubby woodland, cultivation, and gardens, from Myanmar eastward to southeastern China, and southward to northern Thailand, eastern Cambodia, and southern Vietnam; some populations migrate to southeastern India and southern Thailand
Lanius cristatus: lowland to foothill taiga, tundra forest, steppe, and lightly wooded grassland, from central Siberia eastward to Sakhalin and Kamchatka (Russia), and southward to eastern China, Korean Peninsula, and Japan; most populations migrate southward to India, Sri Lanka, Philippines, and Indonesia
Lanius dorsalis: lowland to foothill dry open woodland, acacia woodland, and scrubby savanna, from southeastern South Sudan and northeastern Uganda eastward through southern Ethiopia to southern Somalia, and southward to northeastern Tanzania; some post-breeding dispersal
Lanius excubitor: lowland to montane open areas, from tundra and taiga to steppe, semi-desert, and rocky desert, from Scandinavia and France eastward to western Siberia, Caucasus, and Mongolia, and southward to Canary Islands, northern Africa, Arabian Peninsula, Socotra, and India; many populations move downslope in winter or migrate to lowland Europe, Middle East, or southern India
Lanius excubitoroides: savanna to gardens in lowlands to hills of southeastern Mauritania eastward to southern Sudan and central Ethiopia, and southward to south-central Tanzania
Lanius giganteus: breeds mountains of eastern Tibet; winters to southeastern China
Lanius gubernator: patchy and discontinuous in lowland to foothill brushy savanna, grassland in open woodland, and abandoned cultivation, from northern Ivory Coast eastward through northern Nigeria to southern South Sudan, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northern Uganda; may be a post-breeding visitor to Mali
Lanius humeralis: open areas of lowlands to mountains from Guinea eastward to Eritrea and southward through Angola eastward to Malawi
Lanius isabellinus: lowland to submontane dry steppe, tamarisk thickets, and scrub, from northwestern China eastward through Mongolia to northeastern China, and southward to west-central and north-central China; migrates to open habitats of central and eastern Africa, Arabian Peninsula, and western India
Lanius ludovicianus: breeds in varied open habitats with bushy vegetation from eastern Washington and Alberta eastward to southwestern Manitoba (south-central Canada), southward to southern Baja California and Oaxaca (western Mexico), including islands off southern California, and locally in southeastern USA to the Gulf coast and southern Florida; populations from southern USA southward are resident, and reaches southeastern Mexico in winter; formerly much more widespread in eastern North America
Lanius mackinnoni: disjunctly in lowland to submontane savanna, forest edge, and locally also secondary growth and plantations, from southeastern Nigeria southward through Gabon to northwestern Angola, and from northern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to southwestern Kenya, and southward to Burundi and northern Tanzania
Lanius minor: breeds Iberian Peninsula to Siberia and central Asia; winters to southern Africa
Lanius newtoni: São Tomé (Gulf of Guinea); rediscovered 1990 after 50-year absence
Lanius nubicus: breeds Greece to southwestern Iran; winters to central Africa and southwestern Arabia
Lanius phoenicuroides: Iran to Pakistan, southern Kazakhstan, and far western China (western Xinjiang)
Lanius schach: lowland to montane steppe, semi-desert, brushy grassland, scrub, and light woodland, from Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, and southern Kazakhstan eastward through Himalayas to eastern China (including Hainan) and Taiwan, and southward to Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Indonesia, Philippines, and eastern New Guinea; northern populations move downslope or migrate southward in winter
Lanius senator: patchy in lowland to foothill open woodland, old orchards, steppe, and desert edge, from southern Europe and northwestern Africa eastward to Jordan and Iran; migrates post-breeding to the African Sahel and open habitats in western and eastern Africa
Lanius somalicus: lowland and foothill short-grass savanna, arid open bush, semi-desert, and stony desert, from northeastern Ethiopia and northern Somalia southward to southeastern South Sudan and northwestern Kenya; some post-breeding dispersal
Lanius souzae: open woodland in hills of southeastern Gabon patchily eastward to northwestern Tanzania, and in south to northern Namibia and central Mozambique
Lanius sphenocercus: mountains of eastern Russia (Amur region) to northeastern and central China
Lanius tephronotus: montane forest edge, grassland, and meadows, from northern India eastward through Himalayas to central China and Tibetan plateau, migrates post-breeding downslope or southward to Bangladesh, Myanmar, and northern Vietnam
Lanius tigrinus: breeds southeastern Siberia, eastern and northeastern China, Korean Peninsula, and Japan (northern and central Honshu); winters to southeastern Asia, Greater Sundas, and Philippines
Lanius vittatus: lowland to foothill semi-desert, dry open woodland, scrub, and acacia-wooded plain, from southeastern Turkmenistan, eastern Iran, and northern Oman, eastward to Kashmir and the Indian subcontinent to central Bangladesh; northern populations migrate to Arabian Peninsula and India
Larosterna inca: breeds islands off northern Peru to central Chile; ranges rarely northward to Ecuador
Larus argentatus: various coastal and inland open habitats near and away from water in Iceland, Faroe Islands, Scandinavia, the British Isles, northwestern Russia, and northern Europe southward to southern Poland, central Germany, and the western coast of France; winters as far south as the northern coast of Spain and northern Portugal, and apparently spreading to the Mediterranean coast in southern Europe
Larus armenicus: breeds lakes of Caucasus to eastern Türkiye and northwestern Iran; winters to eastern Mediterranean, southern Black and Caspian seas, and Persian Gulf
Larus atlanticus: breeds coastal southern Buenos Aires and Chubut (east-central Argentina); some winter to coasts of southeastern Brazil
Larus belcheri: western coast and islets of Humboldt Current of northern Peru to northern Chile; disperses to northern Ecuador and central Chile
Larus brachyrhynchus: breeds Alaska mainland eastward to northwestern Alberta and southward to southwestern British Columbia (southwestern Canada); winters Pacific coast to central Japan (Honshu) and from southern British Columbia southward to northwestern Baja California (northwestern Mexico)
Larus cachinnans: breeds inland southern Poland and Hungary eastward through Black, Caspian, and Aral seas to eastern Kazakhstan; winters southeastern Europe, Black Sea, eastern Mediterranean, Persian Gulf, and northern Arabian Sea
Larus californicus: breeds on islands in lakes and rivers of central Northwest Territories to central Manitoba (central Canada) to northeastern South Dakota; eastern Washington to Montana and southward to Colorado and central California; winters on coast from southern British Columbia (southwestern Canada) to west-central Mexico
Larus canus: breeds mostly wetlands, subarctic and low Arctic of Palearctic from Iceland and northwestern and central Europe to Kamchatka (eastern Siberia), and in the south disjunctly in western and central Asia; winters Europe to northern Africa, Mediterranean, Black and Caspian seas, and Persian Gulf; disjunctly Sea of Okhotsk (southeastern Russia), Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu), and Korean Peninsula to southeastern China
Larus crassirostris: breeds coasts and islets of eastern Siberia to Kuril Islands (southeastern Russia), Hokkaido to Kyushu and Izu Islands (northern and central Japan), Korean Peninsula, eastern China, and Matsu Island (off Taiwan); winters to southward, some reaching southern Vietnam and Philippines
Larus delawarensis: breeds inland British Columbia eastward to Labrador and Newfoundland (eastern Canada), Pacific Northwest states, and Great Lakes (northern USA); winters to coastal and inland southern USA, southern Mexico, Bahamas, and Greater Antilles
Larus dominicanus: breeds coasts and islets of southern continents and islands, mostly in temperate to Antarctic waters, in Africa from Namibia around Cape through northeastern South Africa, and southern Madagascar; in Australia including Tasmania, and New Zealand and associated islands; in South America from northern Peru and southern Brazil south to Tierra del Fuego; and in subantarctic and Antarctic islands; some winter farther north
Larus fuscus: breeds from Greenland, Iceland, and western Europe to central Asia and north-central Siberia; winters mostly coastally to southwestern Europe, Africa (except southwestern and southern), India, and Sri Lanka, and eastern North America
Larus glaucescens: breeds coastal North Pacific from eastern Siberia, Kamchatka, Kuril and Commander islands (eastern Russia) eastward through Aleutian and Pribilof islands, and southwestern Alaska to northern Washington; winters to Japan (southward to Honshu) and northwestern Mexico
Larus glaucoides: breeds on rocky cliffs of Arctic northeastern Canada to Greenland; winters coastal Iceland to northwestern Europe; Labrador to west-central North Atlantic coast; and east-central North Pacific coast
Larus heermanni: coastal western Mexico; winters British Columbia to Guatemala
Larus hyperboreus: circumpolar breeder on (mostly) high Arctic coasts; winters coasts of Hudson Bay to northeastern Canada, Greenland, Iceland, northwestern Europe (northern North Atlantic); Sea of Okhotsk, Japan (southward to Honshu), southwestern Alaska, and southwestern Canada; widely vagrant farther south and inland
Larus livens: breeds islets in Gulf of California, from Roca Consag to La Paz Bay; winters to Salton Sea (southern California) and throughout Gulf of California (northwestern Mexico)
Larus marinus: breeds North Atlantic coasts, from southern Greenland and Iceland to Svalbard and Baltic states, and coastal and inland northeastern Canada to Great Lakes and Atlantic coast southward to New Jersey; winters to coastal southwestern Europe and coastal Florida
Larus michahellis: Atlantic coasts of Portugal, Spain, and Morocco; coastal and inland Mediterranean region from Belgium to Poland and Türkiye; winters to eastern British Isles and southern Scandinavia
Larus mongolicus: breeds Altai Republic to Lake Baikal (south-central Russia) and Mongolia, Lake Khanka (Heilongjiang, northeastern China), and Yellow Sea islands (western Korean Peninsula); winters mostly to coastal wetlands of Japan (Honshu to Ryukyu Islands), Korean Peninsula, eastern China, and Taiwan
Larus occidentalis: breeds on islands of western North Pacific coast from northwestern Washington to Isla Guadalupe and central Baja California (northwestern Mexico); some winter to southern British Columbia and southern Baja California
Larus pacificus: sandy coasts of southwestern to southeastern Australia including Tasmania
Larus schistisagus: breeds coasts and lakes of northeastern Siberia including Kamchatka southward to Kuril Islands (eastern Russia), and eastward to Hokkaido and northern Honshu (northern Japan); winters to coasts of Japan southward to Kyushu and Izu Islands, Korean Peninsula, Bohai Sea (northeastern China), and Taiwan; prone to extreme vagrancy
Larus smithsonianus: breeds northern and western Alaska eastward across subarctic Canada to Baffin Island and Newfoundland, southward on Pacific coast to southern British Columbia, eastward to inland northeastern USA and Atlantic coast southward to North Carolina; winters from Japan (southward to Honshu) and Aleutians southward on Pacific coast to Nayarit (western Mexico), Gulf coast, and inland to Honduras and northern Caribbean
Larus vegae: breeds Arctic central and eastern Siberia from Taymyr eastward to Chukotka, New Siberian Islands, and St. Lawrence Island (Bering Sea); winters mostly to rocky coasts of Japan (Honshu to Ryukyu Islands), Korean Peninsula, and eastern China
Larvivora akahige: breeds on southern Sakhalin Island, the southern Kuril Islands, and Japan; winters in southeastern China (northwestern Fujian southward to Guangdong and Guangxi)
Larvivora brunnea: montane dense understory in cloudforest, rhododendron and bamboo thickets, and riparian scrub and ravines, from northeastern Afghanistan eastward through Himalayas to central China, and southward to northeastern India and western Myanmar; Himalayan and northern populations migrate to southern India and Sri Lanka
Larvivora cyane: foothill to submontane dense scrub in taiga forest, understory of deciduous and coniferous forest, and riparian thickets, from northeastern Kazakhstan, south-central Siberia, and northern Mongolia eastward to eastern Siberia, and southward to northeastern China, Korean Peninsula, and Japan (to Honshu); migrates to Indochina, Sumatra, and Borneo
Larvivora komadori: breeds Danjo Islands (off southwestern Kyushu) and northern Ryukyu Islands (Tanegashima southward to Tokunoshima); winters southward to the southern Ryukyu Islands (mainly Miyako, Ishigaki, Iriomote, and Yonakuni, southern Japan)
Larvivora ruficeps: breeds north-central China (Tsingling Mountains of Shaanxi and Sichuan); breeding range poorly known but recorded from southern Cambodia and northern Malaysia
Larvivora sibilans: breeds southern Siberia to Sea of Okhotsk; winters southern China to southeastern Asia
Larvivora tanensis: Izu, Tanegashima, and Yakushima islands (southern Japan)
Laterallus albigularis: freshwater marshes, damp grasslands, and fields from eastern Honduras southward along the Caribbean slope to eastern Panama, and the Pacific slope from Costa Rica to western Panama, northern Colombia and adjacent western Venezuela (except Guajira Peninsula), southward to the headwaters of the Cauca and Magdalena valleys, and west of the Andes southward to southwestern Ecuador and adjacent Peru
Laterallus exilis: Guatemala and Belize to northern Bolivia, and Amazonian and eastern Brazil
Laterallus flaviventer: freshwater marshes, grassy edges of lakes and ponds, and damp fields on the Gulf of Mexico coast of southeastern Mexico and the Pacific coast from western Mexico southward to central Panama. the Greater Antilles except Bahamas, northern Colombia and western Venezuela southward to the middle Cauca and Magdalena valleys, the llanos of southwestern Venezuela southward to northeastern Colombia and locally in northeastern Ecuador, Trinidad and Tobago, northern Venezuela and the Guianas eastward to northeastern Brazil and southward across the Cerrado, and Atlantic Forest regions of Brazil to northeastern Bolivia and Uruguay, and patchily in the Amazon basin of southern Brazil, northern Bolivia, and southeastern Peru
Laterallus jamaicensis: coastal central California, breeds eastern seaboard of USA and very locally Kansas, Cuba, and Belize, arid littoral of Peru, and Andes of central Peru (Lake Junín), and central Chile (Atacama to Malleco) and far western Argentina
Laterallus levraudi: locally in wetlands of northern Venezuela north of the Río Orinoco
Laterallus melanophaius: tropical southeastern Colombia and southern Venezuela to the Guianas, Brazil, Bolivia, and northern Argentina
Laterallus notatus: locally in lowlands of South America east of the Andes
Laterallus ruber: lowlands of southern Mexico to northwestern Costa Rica (northern Guanacaste)
Laterallus spiloptera: southern Brazil and Uruguay to north-central Argentina
Lathamus discolor: breeds Tasmania; winters southeastern South Australia to southeastern Queensland
Lathrotriccus euleri: far eastern Colombia to northern Venezuela, Trinidad, and Suriname, eastern Ecuador to northern Bolivia, southern Venezuela, and Amazonian Brazil, and eastern Bolivia to Paraguay and northern Argentina; southern populations winter to north
Lathrotriccus griseipectus: arid tropical southwestern Ecuador and northwestern Peru
Laticilla burnesii: Indus River Valley of Pakistan, and northwestern India (Punjab) to eastern Nepal
Laticilla cinerascens: wet grassland of northeastern India (Assam) and northern Bangladesh
Legatus leucophaius: breeds in semi-humid to humid forest and woodland on Gulf slope of Mexico from southern San Luis Potosí and northern Veracruz, and Pacific slope from Chiapas (including the Yucatan Peninsula), southward to central Panama; resident in eastern Panama and west of the Andes in western Colombia to southwestern Ecuador, in major Colombian intermontane valleys, and east of the Andes throughout Amazonia to Catamarca (northwestern Argentina), eastern Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, and southeastern Brazil (Rio Grande do Sul); populations from Mexico to central Panama winter southward, and those from Argentina and southern Brazil winter northward
Leiopicus mahrattensis: disjunctly in lowland to foothill dry open woodland, desert scrub, and riverine forest, in eastern Pakistan, subcontinental India, and Sri Lanka, and in western Myanmar and central Thailand, and in southern Laos, eastern Cambodia, and adjacent Vietnam
Leioptila annectens: patchy in foothill to submontane broadleaf evergreen or semi-deciduous forest, from eastern Nepal eastward through Himalayas to southern China and northwestern Vietnam, and southward to western Thailand and southern Vietnam
Leiothlypis celata: breeds in shrub and woodland from Alaska eastward to Newfoundland (eastern Canada) and southward through most of the western USA to northern Baja California and New Mexico; winters on Pacific coast of USA and southern USA throughout Mexico (rarer in the Yucatan Peninsula) except the far south
Leiothlypis crissalis: breeds Chisos Mountains of southwestern Texas patchily through Sierra Madre Oriental in central Coahuila to southwestern Tamaulipas, northeastern Zacatecas, and northern San Luis Potosí; winters southeastern Sinaloa southward to central Guerrero and eastward to Morelos
Leiothlypis luciae: breeds arid southwestern USA to northeastern Baja California and northeastern Sonora; winters to southwestern Mexico
Leiothlypis peregrina: breeds southeastern Alaska and southern Yukon to northern USA; winters southern Mexico to northwestern South America
Leiothlypis ruficapilla: breeds disjunctly in deciduous and secondary forest in southern British Columbia (southwestern Canada) and northwestern USA southward to central California, and from Saskatchewan eastward to Nova Scotia (central to eastern Canada), and in the northeastern USA from northern Minnesota eastward to the Atlantic coast, thence southward to Maryland, and in the Appalachians southward to West Virginia; winters southern California and southernmost Texas through northern and central Mexico, and more rarely to Honduras
Leiothlypis virginiae: breeds mountains in Great Basin of southwestern USA (Idaho eastward to Colorado, and southeastern California eastward to western Texas); winters to southwestern Mexico
Leiothrix argentauris: foothill to submontane understory of broadleaf evergreen forest, open pine forest, secondary growth, bamboo, and plantations, from northern India eastward through Himalayas to southern China, and southward to southern Vietnam, Malayan Peninsula, and Sumatra; introduced in Hong Kong
Leiothrix lutea: foothill to montane forest understory, forest edge, secondary growth, scrub, and bamboo, from northeastern Pakistan eastward through Himalayas to southeastern China, and southward to northeastern India and northern Vietnam; introduced in Hawaiian Islands (Oahu eastward to Hawaii) and Japan (central Honshu to Kyushu)
Leipoa ocellata: semiarid southern Australia (southwestern Australia to south-central New South Wales)
Leistes bellicosus: grassland and fields from lowlands to mountains on Pacific slope of southwestern Colombia to Region I of far northern Chile
Leistes defilippii: tall-grass pampas mainly of southern Buenos Aires Province (east-central Argentina) and Uruguay; formerly Rio Grande do Sul (southeastern Brazil)
Leistes loyca: grassland, scrub, and fields from lowlands to mountains from northern Jujuy (far northwestern Argentina) and Region III of northern Chile eastward in Buenos Aires province and southward to Tierra del Fuego, including mountains of Cordoba and San Luis (north-central Argentina), and Falkland Islands
Leistes militaris: southwestern Costa Rica to Trinidad and the Guianas, Amazonian Brazil, and northwestern Bolivia
Leistes superciliaris: far southeastern Peru to Paraguay, Uruguay, northern Argentina, and Brazil
Lepidocolaptes affinis: drier to humid montane forest of Caribbean slope from central Nuevo León and Pacific slope from Guerrero (northeastern and west-central Mexico) southward (not including Yucatan Peninsula) through northern Nicaragua and, disjunctly, northwestern Costa Rica through western Panama
Lepidocolaptes albolineatus: eastern Venezuela (Monagas and Bolívar) to the Guianas and northern Brazil (east of the Rio Branco and Rio Negro)
Lepidocolaptes angustirostris: deciduous forest and scrub, gallery and savanna forest, and palm swamps in northeastern Brazil, in Isla Marajó and river islands and riparian areas in the eastern Amazon River eastward to the Rio Tapajós in eastern Pará, and in savanna of southernmost Suriname; also in the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado regions of eastern Brazil (Maranhão, Piauí, and Ceará southward to Paraná and Mato Grosso do Sul, and west to southern Mato Grosso and adjacent Rondônia), Paraguay, central and eastern Bolivia, Uruguay, and western Rio Grande do Sul, southward to south-central Argentina (southward to La Pampa, northern Río Negro, and southern Buenos Aires; absent from the pampas)
Lepidocolaptes duidae: northwestern Amazonia, from Venezuela and Brazil (west of the Rio Branco and Rio Negro) westward to Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru north of the Amazon
Lepidocolaptes falcinellus: southeastern Brazil to northeastern Argentina, northeastern Uruguay, and southeastern Paraguay
Lepidocolaptes fatimalimae: western Amazonia, south of the Amazon: eastern Peru southward to Bolivia and eastward to Brazil west of the Rio Madeira
Lepidocolaptes fuscicapillus: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin, south of the Amazon River, from northeastern Brazil (northeastern Pará) southwestward to Rondônia, southern Mato Grosso and northeastern Bolivia
Lepidocolaptes lacrymiger: montane cloudforest in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (from Carabobo eastward to Sucre), Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Sierra de Perijá, the Andes from western Venezuela southward along the western, central, and eastern Andes of Colombia, through Ecuador to northwestern Peru (to Cajamarca, west of the Río Marañón), and from northern Peru east and south of the Marañón, southeastward in the eastern Andes to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz)
Lepidocolaptes leucogaster: montane semiarid to humid forest of northeastern Sonora (northwestern Mexico) south on Pacific slope to Nayarit, thence across transvolcanic belt of Mexico and southward to south-central Oaxaca
Lepidocolaptes souleyetii: deciduous to semi-humid forest and woodland on the Gulf of Mexico slope of southeastern Mexico (northern Oaxaca and adjacent Veracruz), and the Pacific slope (Guerrero and Oaxaca) southward across Central America to eastern Panama, northern Colombia, northern Venezuela, and Trinidad, the tepuis of southeasternmost Venezuela, adjacent Guyana, and far northern Brazil (Roraima), east of the Andes in the foothills of southwestern Venezuela and northeastern Colombia (southward to northern Meta), in central Colombia southward along the Cauca and Magdalena valleys, and west of the Andes in southwestern Colombia, western Ecuador, and northwestern Peru
Lepidocolaptes squamatus: deciduous and semi-deciduous woodland, gallery forest and humid forest in the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado regions of eastern Brazil from southern Piauí southward to northern São Paulo
Lepidothrix coeruleocapilla: east slope of Andes of southern Peru (southern Huánuco to Puno)
Lepidothrix coronata: tropical rainforest to foothil forest in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from southern Venezuela southward across western Brazil to northern Bolivia
Lepidothrix iris: tropical rainforest in the eastern Amazon basin in Pará, northeastern Mato Grosso, adjacent Maranhão, and Tocantins, westward to the Rio Tapajos
Lepidothrix isidorei: humid foothills forest in the eastern base of the Andes from northeastern Colombia, in southwestern Casanare, southward to northeastern Peru, in Huanuco
Lepidothrix nattereri: tropical rainforest in the southern Amazon basin mostly in the Rio Madeira-Rio Tapajos interfluvium, from northern Brazil, in western Pará southward to southern Mato Grosso, Rondônia, and northeastern Bolivia
Lepidothrix serena: southeastern Guyana, Suriname, French Guiana, and northern Amazonian Brazil
Lepidothrix suavissima: tepuis of southern Venezuela to northern Guyana and far northern Brazil
Lepidothrix velutina: humid forest of lowlands and hills from west-central and far southeastern Costa Rica through Panama to western and west-central Colombia, thence west of the Andes to west-central Ecuador
Lepidothrix vilasboasi: eastern Amazonian Brazil (near headwaters of Rio Tapajós in southwestern Pará)
Leptasthenura aegithaloides: arid scrub, espinal, rocky slopes, forest borders, and puna grassland with bushes in the coast of southern Peru, in Arequipa, southward to southern Chile; also in the Andes from far southeast Peru southward across the Andes of Bolivia and northeastern Chile to southern Argentina, to Tierra del Fuego; southern populations migrate northward during the austral winter to north-central Argentina
Leptasthenura andicola: shrubby paramo, humid to arid montane scrub, Polylepis woodland, and treeline in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Andes of western Venezuela and the eastern Andes of Colombia (Boyacá to Cundinamarca), the central Andes of Colombia (from northern Tolima and Caldas) southward to southern Ecuador (northern Loja), and disjunctly in Zamora Chinchipe, Andean puna from northern Peru (Ancash) southeastward to southeastern Peru and adjacent western Bolivia (La Paz)
Leptasthenura fuliginiceps: arid to humid montane scrub and Polylepis woodland in the Andes from western Bolivia southward to west-central Argentina (Mendoza and the sierras of Córdoba and San Luis)
Leptasthenura pileata: Polylepis and Gynoxys woodland and adjacent scrub in the Andes from northern Peru, in southern Cajamarca, southward to southern Peru, in Arequipa
Leptasthenura platensis: southern Paraguay; far southwestern Brazil, Uruguay, and Argentina
Leptasthenura setaria: southeastern Brazil (Rio de Janeiro to Rio Grande do Sul) to northeastern Argentina
Leptasthenura striata: arid montane scrub in the western Andes of northern Peru, from La Libertad southward to northernmost Chile, in northern region of Antofagasta; also in inter-Andean valleys of southern Peru, in Huancavelica, Ayacucho, and Apurimac
Leptasthenura striolata: southeastern Brazil (Paraná southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul)
Leptasthenura xenothorax: Andes of southern Peru (Apurímac and Cusco)
Leptocoma aspasia: forest and scrub habitats, including mangroves, in Sulawesi region (including Sangihe and Talaud islands), eastward through Moluccas to New Guinea and associated islands, and Bismarck Archipelago
Leptocoma brasiliana: lowland to foothill forest edge, secondary growth, coastal scrub, mangroves, plantations, coconut groves, and gardens, from northeastern Bangladesh and adjacent Assam, northeastern India, and western Myanmar eastward to southern Vietnam, and southward to Sumatra and Borneo and satellite islands, and western Java
Leptocoma calcostetha: mangroves and coastal scrub of southeastern Asia, Palawan, and Greater Sundas
Leptocoma minima: India (Western Ghats to hills of southern Kerala)
Leptocoma sperata: Philippines, from Calayan southward to Palawan and Sulu Archipelago
Leptocoma zeylonica: jungle and shrubby habitats of the Indian Subcontinent from Gujarat and Rajasthan eastward to far southeastern Nepal, Assam, Bangladesh, and westernmost Myanmar southward through southernmost Peninsular India and Sri Lanka
Leptodon cayanensis: humid to semi-humid forest from southeastern Mexico (including the Yucatan Peninsula) southward across Central America to eastern Panama and northern Colombia, southward to the middle Magdalena Valley, and along Pacific Colombia to southwestern Ecuador; east of the Andes across Venezuela, the Guianas, and Trinidad southward across the Amazon basin to central and eastern Bolivia, eastern Paraguay, and northeastern Argentina; in interior and eastern Brazil (Piauí, Ceará, and Sergipe southward to southern Mato Grosso do Sul, Paraná, and northern Rio Grande do Sul)
Leptodon forbesi: Atlantic lowland rainforest of northeastern Brazil (Pernambuco and Alagoas)
Leptopoecile elegans: coniferous forest of north-central China to Tibet and Sichuan
Leptopoecile sophiae: montane scrub and thicket in spruce and juniper forest from southeastern Kazakhstan and northwestern China southward to northern India, and patchy eastward through Himalayas to Tibetan Plateau and central China; irruptive southward and downslope in hard winters
Leptopogon amaurocephalus: semi-deciduous, gallery and humid forest from the Gulf of Mexico slope in southeastern Mexico southeastward to northern Costa Rica, and in the Pacific lowlands of western Panama and adjacent Costa Rica; in northern Colombia and western Venezuela southward to the middle Cauca and Magdalena valleys, and east of the Andes in the Amazon basin from western Venezuela southward to central Bolivia, westward across southern Brazil and southward along the Yungas to northwestern Argentina; in the Guiana Shield and Orinoco basin in eastern Venezuela, the Guianas and northern Brazil (Roraima and Amapá), and in interior and eastern Brazil from northern Maranhão, Piauí and Rio Grande do Norte southward to eastern Bolivia, eastern Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, and northernmost Uruguay
Leptopogon rufipectus: Andes of Colombia to eastern Ecuador, western Venezuela, and northern Peru
Leptopogon superciliaris: semi-deciduous to humid foothill and montane forest from western Costa Rica eastward to eastern Panama,coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Falcón eastward to the Paría Peninsula), Trinidad, the Sierra de Perijá, the Andes from western Venezuela southward along the western, central, and eastern Andes of Colombia to northern Peru north of the Río Marañón (in western Ecuador down to the coastal lowlands), and in the eastern Andes from northern Peru southeastward to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz and northern Chuquisaca)
Leptopogon taczanowskii: east slope of Andes of Peru (Amazonas to Cusco)
Leptoptilos dubius: eastern Nepal, north-central to northeastern India (modern-day records only from Assam Valley, West Bengal, Bihar, and eastern Uttar Pradesh), and northern Bangladesh, and Indochina (principally in Cambodia); breeding now probably restricted to Assam, Bihar and Cambodia
Leptoptilos javanicus: India and Sri Lanka to southern China, Indochina, and Indonesia
Leptosittaca branickii: humid Andes of southern Colombia to Ecuador and central Peru
Leptosomus discolor: rainforest to deciduous, littoral and gallery forest, spiny bush-forest, and degraded woodland in the Comoros (including Mayotte) and throughout Madagacar
Leptotila cassinii: second-growth forest of lowlands and hills on Caribbean slope from eastern Chiapas (southeastern Mexico) and Belize southward through northern Costa Rica, thence both slopes through Panama and to north-central Colombia
Leptotila conoveri: forest and edge of mid-elevations on east slope of central Andes (Caldas southward to Huila) and west slope of eastern Andes (Cundinamarca) of Colombia
Leptotila jamaicensis: semidarid forest and scrub of lowlands to hills on northern Yucatan Peninsula, including islas Holbox, Mujeres, and Cozumel, islands north of Honduras, Cayman Islands, Jamaica, and Isla San Andrés (to far northwest of Colombia, off eastern Nicaragua); introduced New Providence Island (northern Bahamas)
Leptotila megalura: Andes of Bolivia and northwestern Argentina
Leptotila ochraceiventris: southwestern Ecuador (Manabí) to far northwestern Peru (Tumbes and Piura)
Leptotila pallida: tropical lowlands of western Colombia and western Ecuador
Leptotila plumbeiceps: northeastern Mexico (southern Tamaulipas) to northwestern Costa Rica and Caribbean slope of western Panama; also slopes surrounding the Cauca Valley (west-central Colombia)
Leptotila rufaxilla: humid forest from the Catatumbo depression of northeastern Colombia and western Venezuela, the foothills of the Andes in western Venezuela and the Orinoco basin of eastern and southern Venezuela and the Guianas southward across the Amazon basin of Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and northern Bolivia; in the Cerrado and Atlantic Forest regions from northeastern Brazil (Maranhão, Ceará, and Piauí) southward to northern Uruguay, northeastern Argentina, and eastern Paraguay
Leptotila verreauxi: southern Texas and coastal Mexico southward to southern Bolivia, Paraguay, southern Brazil, Uruguay, and north-central Argentina
Leptotila wellsi: arid scrub of southern Grenada (southern Lesser Antilles)
Leptotrygon veraguensis: Caribbean lowlands of Costa Rica to northwestern Ecuador
Lerwa lerwa: Himalayas from eastern Afghanistan to southern Tibet and southwestern China
Lesbia nuna: humid forest and scrub in the eastern (from Norte de Santander) and central (from Caldas) Andes of Colombia southward across Ecuador and the Andes of western and eastern Peru to central Bolivia, eastward to westernmost Santa Cruz
Lesbia victoriae: semi-humid to dry scrub and treeline in the Andes of northeastern Colombia and from southern Colombia southward across Ecuador to southeastern Peru, in Cusco
Lessonia oreas: Andes of Peru (Huánuco) to northern Chile and northwestern Argentina
Lessonia rufa: central Chile and Argentina to Tierra del Fuego; winters to southeastern Brazil
Leucippus fallax: coastal northeastern Colombia, and coastal Venezuela including islas La Tortuga and Margarita
Leucocarbo atriceps: rocky shores, islets, sea cliffs, stacks, and inshore coastal waters of Prince Edward, Marion, Crozet, Kerguelen, Heard, and Macquarie islands, and islands and coasts of south-central Chile and Argentina southward to Cape Horn, Falkland Islands, South Georgia, South Sandwich, South Orkney, and South Shetland islands, and Antarctic Peninsula
Leucocarbo bougainvilliorum: breeds coasts and islands off Peru southward to central Chile
Leucocarbo carunculatus: islands in Marlborough Sounds, Cook Strait (New Zealand)
Leucocarbo chalconotus: southeastern coast of South Island, Foveaux Strait, and Stewart Island (New Zealand)
Leucocarbo magellanicus: breeds coasts of south-central Chile and Argentina, and Falkland Islands; winters northward to coastal southern Brazil
Leucochloris albicollis: eastern Bolivia to eastern Paraguay, northern Argentina, and southeastern Brazil
Leucogeranus leucogeranus: breeds Arctic east-central Siberia (Yakutia) and western Siberia (at least formerly basin of Kunovat River; also basins of Konda and Alymka rivers); winters very locally on southern shore of Caspian Sea in north-central Iran, with most wintering on middle Yangtze River (mainly Poyang Lake) in east-central China; formerly also Keoladeo (Bharatpur) in northwestern India, but not recorded since 2002
Leuconotopicus albolarvatus: montane coniferous forest, especially ponderosa pine, of south-central British Columbia (southwestern Canada) and north-central Washington and western Idaho southward through far south San Diego County (southern California)
Leuconotopicus arizonae: montane oak and pine forest from southeastern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico on Pacific slope of western Mexico to Michoacán
Leuconotopicus borealis: patchily distributed in pine forest of southeastern USA
Leuconotopicus fumigatus: humid forest in the Gulf of Mexico slope from Tamaulipas, Mexico, southeastward across Central America, including the Yucatan Peninsula and Belize to western Panama, and in the Pacific slope from Nayarit, Mexico, southeastward to eastern El Salvador and again in Costa Rica to western Panama; in South America in montane cloudforest in Cerro Tacarcuna, Cerro Pirre, Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Sierra de Perijá and the Andean slopes from western Venezuela southward across Colombia and Ecuador to central Peru in Lima and Huancavelica; also in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela eastward to Monagas; and in Andean slopes from far southeastern Peru southeastward to the Yungas of southern Bolivia and northern Argentina southward to Salta
Leuconotopicus stricklandi: coniferous forest of eastern Mexico (Michoacán to west-central Veracruz)
Leuconotopicus villosus: mostly forest from central Alaska southward across North America to southern California and northern Baja California del Norte, in Mexico, to southern Arizona and New Mexico, and southward along the Sierra Madre Oriental and Occidental of Mexico southeastward across montane regions of Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua and Costa Rica to westernmost Panama; in North America eastward to Newfoundland and southward along the Atlantic Coast to southern Florida and the Bahamas
Leucopeza semperi: montane forest of St. Lucia (Lesser Antilles); likely extinct
Leucophaeus atricilla: breeds on flat islands off western North Atlantic coast of Maine to Florida and the Gulf of Mexico to southern Texas; Gulf of California to Colima (western Mexico); Caribbean, islands off Yucatan Peninsula, and islands north of Venezuela, Trinidad and Tobago, and to French Guiana; winters coastally to northern Peru and northeastern Brazil
Leucophaeus modestus: breeds inland nitrate desert of Chile and at least formerly Peru; ranges to coastal Ecuador
Leucophaeus pipixcan: breeds prairie marshes of western and northern Alberta eastward to southwestern Manitoba, and southward from east-central Oregon to northwestern Minnesota; winters coasts from Ecuador (including Galapagos) to central Chile
Leucophaeus scoresbii: breeds coasts of southern Chile, Argentina, and Falkland Islands; some move north on coasts
Leucopsar rothschildi: coastal northwestern Bali (Bali Barat National Park); extinct in the wild with reintroductions in Nusa Penida Island and (usually unsuccessful) in western Bali
Leucopternis kuhli: rainforest of eastern Peru, northern Bolivia, and southern Amazonian Brazil
Leucopternis melanops: southeastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, northeastern Ecuador, and northern Amazonian Brazil
Leucopternis semiplumbeus: humid forest of Honduras to western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador
Leucoptilon concretum: patchy in lowland to montane dense forest, wooded and scrubby ravines, secondary forest, and bamboo, in northeastern India from easternmost Assam eastward to southern China and northern Vietnam, and southward to Mizoram, Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, and Borneo
Leucosarcia melanoleuca: eastern Australia (central eastern Queensland southward to eastern Victoria)
Leucosticte arctoa: subarctic to temperate central and northeastern Palearctic in Altai to eastern Russia in barren alpine rocky areas and snowfields: northeastern Kazakhstan, Altay, and Tuva regions (south-central Siberia) and western and northern Mongolia; disjunctly Baikal area to Sea of Okhotsk, Kamchatka, and northern Kuril Islands (eastern Russia), northwestern Inner Mongolia (far northern China), and (perhaps) central Hokkaido (northern Japan); winters to lowland Sakhalin, northeastern coastal China, Korean Peninsula, and Hokkaido to central Honshu (northern and central Japan)
Leucosticte atrata: breeds mountains of Idaho and Montana to Nevada and Utah; winters to Arizona
Leucosticte australis: mountains of southeastern Wyoming, Colorado, and north-central New Mexico
Leucosticte brandti: barren high-alpine zone from eastern Kazakhstan northeastward to Altay and Tuva regions (south-central Russia), western and northwestern Xinjiang (northwestern China), and northern and western Mongolia; in south through northeastern Afghanistan, east in Karakorum, Tibet, and Inner Himalayas to far northern Myanmar, northeastward to northern Qinghai and northwestern Gansu (north-central China); some winter to lower elevations
Leucosticte nemoricola: alpine meadows and subalpine scrub from eastern Kazakhstan northeastward to Altay and Tuva regions (south-central Russia), western and northwestern Xinjiang (northwestern China), and western Mongolia; in south through northeastern Afghanistan, eastward in Karakorum, Tibet, and Inner Himalayas to far northern Myanmar and northwestern Yunnan, northern Qinghai, Gansu, and southern Shaanxi (north-central China); winters to lower elevations
Leucosticte tephrocotis: breeds patchily in alpine areas near glaciers, cliffs, and outcrops above treeline from northern Alaska, including the Aleutians and Pribilof Islands, and northern Yukon (northwestern Canada), southward in western USA mountains eastward to northwestern Montana and southward to east-central California; winters at somewhat lower elevations from southwestern Canada southward to northern New Mexico
Lewinia mirifica: montane north-central Luzon (northern Philippines); few recent records
Lewinia muelleri: predator-free islands of Auckland Islands (Adams and Disappointment)
Lewinia pectoralis: central Lesser Sundas, New Guinea, and eastern Australia
Lewinia striata: lowland to foothill wetland, marshy meadows, reedbeds, and mangroves, from Indian subcontinent, including Sri Lanka, eastward to southern China (including Hainan) and Taiwan, and southward through southeastern Asia to the Greater Sundas and Philippines; some populations winter to Indonesia, eastward to Sulawesi
Lichmera argentauris: Moluccas and Raja Ampat Islands (off western New Guinea)
Lichmera incana: central and southern Vanuatu and New Caledonia including Loyalty Islands
Lichmera indistincta: Bali, Lesser Sundas, south-central New Guinea, including Aru Islands (off southwestern New Guinea), and western, northern, central, and eastern Australia
Lichmera lombokia: western Lesser Sundas (Lombok, Sumbawa, and Flores)
Lichmera squamata: Lesser Sundas (Wetar to Tanimbar and Kai islands)
Limnoctites rectirostris: far southern Brazil to southern Uruguay and eastern Argentina
Limnoctites sulphuriferus: southern Brazil (Rio Grande do Sul) to Uruguay and eastern Argentina
Limnodromus griseus: breeds north temperate bogs in tundra and muskeg from Gulf of Alaska and inland south-central Alaska, southwestern Yukon, and montane northwestern British Columbia (northwestern Canada); north-central Alberta to western Manitoba (central Canada); southwestern Hudson and James bays to western Labrador (east-central Canada); winters coastal mudflats and mangroves from northern California to northern Peru and Galapagos, and North Carolina to northeastern Brazil
Limnodromus scolopaceus: breeds wet meadows from Lena River through northeastern Siberia, St. Lawrence Island (Bering Sea; rare), western Alaska and northern Northwest Territories (north-central Canada); winters inland from Japan (Honshu to Ryukyu Islands) and the southern US through Mexico, along the Pacific coast from the Pacific Northwest southward to northwestern Costa Rica, and along the Atlantic and Gulf coasts from the mid-Atlantic southward to the Yucatan Peninsula
Limnodromus semipalmatus: breeds inland wetlands from southwestern Siberia and eastern Kazakhstan, (probably) northern Mongolia to southeastern Siberia, and northeastern China; winters coastal Thai-Malay Peninsula, Indonesian Archipelago, and northern Australia
Limnornis curvirostris: far southern Brazil to southern Uruguay and eastern Argentina
Limnothlypis swainsonii: breeds locally in varied (often mesic) forests southeastern USA (Missouri eastward to southern Virginia, and eastern Texas eastward to northern Florida); winters southeastern Mexico and Belize to Guatemala and West Indies
Limosa fedoa: breeds subarctic to temperate grassland disjunctly in central Alaska Peninsula; south-central Canada to north-central USA; and west James Bay area (northern Ontario, east-central Canada); winters coastal USA from Washington to central Panama and New Jersey to Yucatan Peninsula
Limosa haemastica: breeds patchily in low Arctic bogs near treeline, in western and south-central Alaska, northern and south-central Northwest Territories, and southwestern Hudson Bay (northwestern to east-central Canada); winters mainly to temperate coastal wetlands, where highly localized, in northern Peru to southern Chile and southern Brazil to southern Argentina
Limosa lapponica: breeds patchily in low Arctic tundra of northern Palearctic from far northern Scandinavia to Chukotskiy and Anadyr peninsulas (northeastern Russia) and northern and western Alaska; winters mainly temperate to tropical coasts from British Isles, southern Europe, western Mediterranean, Africa, and Malagasy region through Middle East, Indian subcontinent, southeastern Asia, Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), southeastern China, Taiwan, Philippines, Indonesian Archipelago, Australasia from New Guinea region to Melanesia and New Zealand, and Fiji (southwestern Polynesia)
Limosa limosa: breeds in subarctic and temperate wet grassland from Iceland, Faroe Islands, British Isles, and Scandinavia southward to southwestern France, east through northwestern Russia, northern Kazakhstan, and northern Mongolia eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula, Kamchatka, Sakhalin, and Amurland (eastern Russia) and Inner Mongolia (northeastern China); winters coastal and inland temperate to tropical wetlands from southern British Isles, southern Europe, Africa (except southern), Middle East, southern Asia, Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), Taiwan, southeastern China, Philippines, Indonesian Archipelago, southern New Guinea, and Australia
Linaria cannabina: open lowland woodland and fields (alpine meadows in south) of British Isles, southern Scandinavia eastward to Altai region (south-central Russia), northern Xinjiang (northwestern China), and far western Mongolia, in south to Madeira and Canary Islands, Morocco to northern Libya, throughout Mediterranean to Türkiye, Cyprus, and the Levant, through Caucasus, Iran, and northern Afghanistan to eastern Kazakhstan; makes short-distance movements in winter
Linaria flavirostris: low Arctic to temperate northwestern and montane central Palearctic in open areas: northern and central British Isles, western and northern Scandinavia; disjunctly Caucasus and south-central and northeastern Türkiye eastward through south-central Russia, northern Kazakhstan, northern and western Xinjiang (northwestern China), and Mongolia, in south to northwestern Iran, central Afghanistan through Altai region, northwestern Himalayas eastward to Nepal, Tibet, Qinghai, and Gansu (north-central China); winters to lower elevations and southward
Linaria johannis: foothill to montane arid plateaus, juniper woodland, thickets, scrub, and olive groves, in northern Somalia
Linaria yemenensis: foothill to montane rocky scree, wadis with thornscrub, acacia scrub, juniper woodland, and plantations, in southwestern Saudi Arabia and western Yemen
Linurgus olivaceus: disjunctly in montane cloudforest, from southeastern Nigeria, western Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) in west Africa, and from southern South Sudan, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to Burundi, eastward to eastern Uganda and central Kenya, and southward through eastern Tanzania to Malawi in east Africa; some downslope movement in non-breeding season
Liocichla omeiensis: mountains of southwestern China (central Sichuan on Mount Omei Shan)
Liocichla phoenicea: patchy in foothill to submontane understory of broadleaf evergreen forest, dense thicket bordering cultivation, and scrub, from northeastern India (possibly eastern Nepal) eastward through Himalayas to southern China, and southward to western Myanmar
Liocichla ripponi: patchy in foothill to submontane scrubby ravines, open swampy forest, and bamboo jungle, from eastern Myanmar eastward to southeastern China, and southward to northern Thailand, northeastern Laos, and adjacent Vietnam
Lioparus chrysotis: montane dense understory of mixed forest, and bamboo thickets, from central Nepal eastward through Himalayas to central and southeastern China, and southward to northeastern India, northern Myanmar, and central Vietnam
Liosceles thoracicus: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin from southern Colombia southward to northwestern Bolivia and eastward in Brazil, south of the Amazon River, to the Rio Tapajos in western Pará
Lipaugus ater: southeastern Brazil (Rio de Janeiro and southern Minas Gerais to far eastern São Paulo)
Lipaugus conditus: cloudforest of southeastern Brazil in Rio de Janeiro (Serra dos Órgãos)
Lipaugus fuscocinereus: Andes of Colombia to Ecuador and far northern Peru (Piura)
Lipaugus lanioides: southeastern Brazil (Espírito Santo and Minas Gerais to northeastern Santa Catarina)
Lipaugus streptophorus: tepuis of southern Venezuela, adjacent western Guyana, and far northern Brazil
Lipaugus unirufus: humid forest in lowlands and hills on Caribbean slope from central Veracruz and northern Oaxaca (southeastern Mexico) through central and southern Belize and Nicaragua, thence both slopes of Costa Rica and Panama through western and north-central Colombia, southward west of Andes to northwestern Ecuador
Lipaugus uropygialis: southern Peru (Cordillera Apolobamba of Puno) and western Bolivia
Lipaugus vociferans: eastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, the Guianas, northern Bolivia, and Amazonian and eastern Brazil
Lipaugus weberi: northern slope of central Cordillera of Andes of Colombia
Lissotis hartlaubii: eastern Sudan to Ethiopia, Somalia, northeastern Uganda, and northern Tanzania
Lissotis melanogaster: lowland and foothill dry grassland, Karoo, Kalahari sandveld, open savanna, and grassy dunes, from northern Namibia and northern Botswana southward to northern and central South Africa (south to Northern Cape and Eastern Cape) and western Lesotho
Loboparadisea sericea: montane western to southeastern New Guinea
Lobotos lobatus: lowland Upper Guinea rainforest, open swamp-forest, and managed forest, from eastern Sierra Leone and southeastern Guinea eastward to southwestern Ghana
Lobotos oriolinus: disjunctly in lowland primary and secondary forest, often near rivers, from southeastern Nigeria eastward to southwestern Central African Republic, and southward to Gabon, and in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Lochmias nematura: rivers and streams in montane forest in the mountains of far eastern Panama and adjacent Colombia, and in the western (southward to Valle del Cauca), central (except northern), and eastern Andes of Colombia, from Cundinamarca southward across eastern Andes of Ecuador and Peru to southern Bolivia and adjacent northwestern Argentina; in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela in Yaracuy eastward to Aragua), and in the tepuis of southern Venezuela and adjacent Guyana; also in interior and eastern Brazil from Tocantins and central Bahia southward to Paraná and Rio Grande do Sul, Uruguay, eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina (Misiones), and westward in Brazil to southern Mato Grosso and northern Mato Grosso do Sul
Locustella accentor: montane forest of northern Borneo (mounts Kinabalu and Trus Madi)
Locustella alfredi: patchy in foothill and montane tall grassland, bamboo in forest, and riverine marsh, from southeastern South Sudan and western Ethiopia southward through Uganda and northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to western Tanzania and northern Zambia
Locustella caudata: montane Luzon and Mindanao (northern and southern Philippines)
Locustella chengi: breeds in southern China (Shaanxi, Sichuan, Guizhou, Hubei, northwestern Hunan, and northwestern Jiangxi); nonbreeding range unknown
Locustella davidi: disjunctly in foothill streamside thickets, and clearings of taiga forest, from northern Altai Mountains (Siberia) eastward to northeastern China and North Korea, and in central China; migrates to northeastern India, northern Myanmar, and northern Thailand
Locustella fluviatilis: breeds central and eastern Europe to western Siberia; winters in eastern Africa
Locustella idonea: highlands of central and southern Vietnam (Kon Tum and Da Lat plateaus)
Locustella lanceolata: breeds northern Europe eastward to Sakhalin Island, southern Kuril Islands, and northern Hokkaido (northern Japan); winters to southern Asia, Greater Sundas, and Philippines
Locustella luscinioides: patchy in lowland to foothill marsh, reedbeds, tall grass, and riverine brush, from continental Europe eastward to eastern Kazakhstan and northwestern China, and southward to northwestern Africa, Jordan (and perhaps Oman?), and northern Iran; migrates as far as Senegal, Chad, and Ethiopia
Locustella luteoventris: Himalayas of eastern Nepal to northeastern India (Assam), southeastern Tibet, southwestern China, southern Myanmar, and northern Thailand
Locustella major: patchy in montane brushy grassland, upland terraced cultivation, and alpine meadows, in northern China, northern Pakistan, and northern India; probably moves downslope in winter
Locustella mandelli: eastern Himalayas to central and southeastern China
Locustella montis: montane Java, Bali, and Timor (eastern Lesser Sundas)
Locustella naevia: lowland to foothill edges of open woodland, tall grass, scrubby sedge or reed marsh, and upland moorland, from British Isles and southern Scandinavia eastward to south-central Siberia and western Mongolia, and southward to northern Spain, Caucasus, and western China; migrates to western sub-Saharan Africa, Ethiopia, and western India
Locustella tacsanowskia: breeds eastern Siberia to southeastern Tibet and southern China; winters to northern Indochina
Locustella thoracica: montane alpine scrub, and juniper and rhododendron thicket in forest clearings, from Nepal eastward through Himalayas to Tibet and central China; moves downslope in winter to southern Nepal and northeastern India
Loddigesia mirabilis: Andes of northern Peru (along east bank of Río Utcubamba)
Lonchura atricapilla: lowland to foothill grassland, marsh, mangroves, rice paddies, and gardens, from northern India eastward to southeastern China (including Hainan), and Taiwan, southward to Philippines, Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, Borneo, Sulawesi, and satellite islands; introduced to Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), Hong Kong, Moluccas, Palau, Vanuatu, Hawaiian Islands (all main islands), Jamaica, Martinique, and central Colombia
Lonchura caniceps: grassy areas and gardens from lowlands to mountains in southeastern peninsula of New Guinea
