Mimus polyglottos: open shrubby habitats and woodland including urban areas from southernmost Canada (rare) southward across most USA (but rare in north-central USA) to southern Florida, southern Baja California and most Mexico (including western islands) southward to northern Oaxaca, and the Greater Antilles eastward to the Virgin Islands; introduced to Hawaii; range expanding northward
Mimus saturninus: open areas including pasture and urban parks of lowlands to mountains from southern Suriname and Amapá to southeastern Pará in northern Brazil, disjunctly from eastern Pará eastward through northeastern Brazil and southwestward to western Bolivia, southward to coastal Chubut in southern Argentina
Mimus triurus: central Argentina and Bolivia (Beni); winters to southwestern Brazil
Minla ignotincta: foothill to montane broadleaf evergreen or conifer forest, especially oak and rhododendron forest, from Nepal eastward through Himalayas to central and southeastern China, and southward patchily to central Myanmar, southern Laos, and adjacent Vietnam
Mino anais: New Guinea, including Salawati (Raja Ampat Islands, off western New Guinea)
Mino dumontii: New Guinea, including Raja Ampat Islands (off western New Guinea) and Aru Islands (off southwestern New Guinea)
Mino kreffti: Bismarck Archipelago, and northern and central Solomon Islands
Mionectes macconnelli: tropical rainforest in the Guiana Shield and the eastern Amazon basin from eastern Venezuela southeastward across the Guianas to northeastern Brazil, to southern Pará and eastern Amazonas, east of the Rio Negro; also in southeastern Peru, adjacent Brazil and northwestern Bolivia southward to western Santa Cruz
Mionectes oleagineus: humid forest from the Gulf of Mexico slope of southeastern Mexico, including the Yucatan Peninsula, and the Pacific slope in Chiapas, southeastward across Central America to northern Colombia and western Venezuela; in interior Colombia southward along the Cauca and Magdalena valleys, west of the Andes southward to northern Cauca, and from southwestern Colombia southward to far northwestern Peru; east of the Andes in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela eastward to Trinidad and Tobago and the Guianas southward across the Orinoco and Amazon basins to central Bolivia; also the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil from Paraíba southward to Rio de Janeiro
Mionectes olivaceus: foothills and highlands of Costa Rica and western Panama (to Chiriquí and Ngäbe-Buglé), humid lowland and foothill forest from central Panama eastward to northwestern Colombia, southward to the headwaters of the Río Cauca and Río Magdalena, southward along the Pacific lowlands to northwestern Ecuador and along the foothills of the Andes to southwestern Ecuador; east of the Andes in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela eastward to the Paría Peninsula and Trinidad, and in the Andes from western Venezuela southward to western Bolivia
Mionectes roraimae: tepuis of southern and southeastern Venezuela, adjacent northern Brazil, and western Guyana
Mionectes rufiventris: southeastern Brazil (Espírito Santo) to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
Mionectes striaticollis: montane cloudforest in the Andes from northern Colombia southward to northern Peru, and in the eastern Andes from northern Peru southeastward to southern Bolivia (Chuquisaca)
Mirafra albicauda: disjunctly in lowland to foothill dense short grassland, mostly on black-cotton soils, often at lake margins, locally in western Chad, eastern Sudan, northern South Sudan, south-central Ethiopia, and from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward through northern Uganda to western Kenya, and southward to northern and southwestern Tanzania
Mirafra cheniana: disjunctly in lowland to foothill grassy slopes, and open grassland with bare patches, in southwestern Kenya, northern Tanzania, central Zimbabwe, and eastern and central South Africa
Mirafra cordofanica: patchy in lowland and foothill sparse grassland on red sands from Mauritania and northern Senegal eastward across Sahel to southern Sudan and northern South Sudan; likely nomadic
Mirafra javanica: Sahel zone and eastern Africa, southern Arabian peninsula, western Indian Subcontinent, southeastern Asia, Philippines, Timor and Atauro (eastern Indonesia), New Guinea, and Australia
Mirafra passerina: lowland to foothill arid savanna, grassland, and acacia and mopane woodland, from southern Angola eastward to southwestern Zambia and southern Zimbabwe, and southward to central Namibia, Botswana, and north-central and northeastern South Africa; irruptive to semi-desert after heavy rains
Mirafra pulpa: disjunctly in foothill dense grassland with lightly scattered bushes and with some bare ground, in central Kenya and in southeastern Kenya and northeastern Tanzania, some seasonal dispersal with rains
Mirafra williamsi: disjunctly in foothill rocky desert grassland on red lava soils, and low shrubby rocky desert, in northern Kenya (near Marsabit) and in central Kenya (Isiolo to Garba Tula)
Mitrephanes aurantiiventris: highlands of Costa Rica and Panama southward to northwestern Ecuador
Mitrephanes olivaceus: east slope of Andes of northeastern Peru (Piura) to northwestern Bolivia
Mitrephanes phaeocercus: montane forest from northern Sonora (has bred southeastern Arizona, USA) and southern Tamaulipas (northern Mexico) through central plateau of Mexico to Oaxaca, and disjunctly through highlands from Chiapas through northern Nicaragua
Mitrospingus cassinii: dense forest edge in lowlands and foothills of Caribbean slope from far northern Costa Rica and adjacent Nicaragua (sight reports) through central Panama, thence both slopes southward through north-central Andes of Colombia and Chocó west of Andes southward to west-central Ecuador
Mitrospingus oleagineus: humid foothill forest on sandy-soil at the base of the tepuis of southeastern Venezuela, westernmost Guyana, and adjacent Brazil
Mitu mitu: coastal eastern Brazil (Alagoas); extinct in wild
Mitu salvini: humid lowlands of southern Colombia to eastern Ecuador and northeastern Peru
Mitu tomentosum: Guyana to southern Venezuela, eastern Colombia, and adjacent northwestern Brazil
Mitu tuberosum: tropical southeastern Colombia to northern Bolivia and Amazonian Brazil
Mixornis bornensis: Java, Borneo, and some satellite islands
Mixornis gularis: sub-Himalayan lowlands from western Nepal and east-central Peninsular India, eastward through southern China and southeastern Asia, through Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, and many associated islands including Anambas and North Natunas (off northwestern Borneo)
Mixornis kelleyi: forest of southern Laos, central and southern Vietnam, and Cochinchina
Mniotilta varia: breeds deciduous and mixed forests in northwestern Canada (Northwest Territories to Maritime Provinces) and in south from east Texas eastward to North Carolina; winters Mexico to Peru and West Indies
Modulatrix stictigula: northeastern (Usambara and Nguru mountains) and eastern Tanzania (Ukaguru Mountains) to northern Malawi (Masuku Mountains)
Moho bishopi: formerly Molokai and Maui; extinct, last reported 1981
Mohoua albicilla: North Island, and Little and Great Barrier, Arid, and Kapiti islands (New Zealand)
Mohoua novaeseelandiae: forest of South and Stewart islands (New Zealand)
Mohoua ochrocephala: forest of South and Stewart islands (New Zealand)
Molothrus aeneus: breeds southeastern California to Gulf coast of Mississippi southward to central Panama; some withdrawal from north in winter
Molothrus ater: grassland with scattered trees, thickets, and fields from far southeastern Alaska and northwestern Canada eastward to Labrador (eastern Canada), and southward across the USA to northern Baja California, central Mexico (Michoacan), the Gulf of Mexico coast in the US and central Florida; winters to southern Baja California and Oaxaca (southwestern Mexico), southern Florida, and the Bahamas
Molothrus bonariensis: varied humid to dry, mostly open habitats from southern Florida and throughout the Caribbean (where self-introduced), from Costa Rica to South America, including Aruba, Curaçao, and Trinidad and Tobago, southward to southern Argentina (to northern Santa Cruz), west of the Andes southward across western Colombia and Ecuador, and introduced and established throughout Chile
Molothrus oryzivorus: varied open habitats and forest borders mostly in lowlands and foothills on the Gulf slope in Veracruz and on the Pacific slope from Oaxaca (southern Mexico) locally through Panama, and South America from Colombia eastward to Trinidad and Tobago and the Guianas and northeastern Brazil, west of the Andes southward to northwestern Peru, and east of the Andes southward to northern Argentina and far southeastern Brazil
Molothrus rufoaxillaris: eastern Bolivia to Paraguay, southern Brazil, Uruguay, and northern Argentina
Momotus aequatorialis: montane cloudforest in the western, central, and eastern Andes of Colombia southward along the eastern Andes of Ecuador and Peru to western Bolivia (La Paz)
Momotus coeruliceps: northeastern Mexico (Nuevo León and Tamaulipas to northern Veracruz)
Momotus lessonii: humid forest to edge of lowlands and hills on Caribbean slope from central Veracruz and northern Oaxaca then on both slopes of Mexico including Yucatan Peninsula (but not Cozumel) through Nicaragua, thence on Pacific slope and central valley of Costa Rica to central Panama
Momotus mexicanus: northwestern Mexico (southern Sonora to adjacent Chihuahua and Sinaloa) southward in western Mexico through Oaxaca, Chiapas, and far northwestern Guatemala
Momotus momota: forest and edge of lowlands to hills of Amazonia and the Guianas from eastern Colombia to French Guiana and Amapá, southward to northwestern Argentina, eastern Paraguay, and São Paulo; also far northeastern Brazil
Momotus subrufescens: deciduous and semi-deciduous to humid forest in the lowlands of northern Colombia and western Venezuela (eastward to Aragua), southward in interior Colombia along the Cauca and Magdalena valleys (to Cauca and Huila); west of the Andes in central Panama and northwestern Colombia southward to central Chocó in the Tribuga Gulf area west of the Río Atrato; and in the Pacific lowlands of western Ecuador and northwestern Peru (to Lambayeque)
Monachella muelleriana: New Guinea and New Britain (southeastern Bismarck Archipelago)
Monarcha castaneiventris: Choiseul to Makira (central and southern Solomon Islands except New Georgia group)
Monarcha cinerascens: mainly islets from Sulawesi region and Lesser Sundas to Bismarck Archipelago and northern Solomon Islands
Monarcha frater: New Guinea and far northeastern Australia
Monarcha melanopsis: breeds eastern Australia (Wet Tropics region to central Victoria); some winter southern New Guinea
Monarcha richardsii: forest of New Georgia group (west-central Solomon Islands)
Monasa atra: far eastern Colombia to Venezuela, the Guianas, and northern Brazil
Monasa flavirostris: Amazon basin (southeastern Colombia to northern Bolivia and western Amazonian Brazil)
Monasa morphoeus: humid forest from eastern Honduras southeastward across the Caribbean slope of Nicaragua and Costa Rica to the lowlands of northern Colombia, west of the Andes southward to west-central Colombia in Valle del Cauca and in central Colombia southward along the Magdalena Valley (to Tolima); east of the Andes in the Amazon basin from southernmost Venezuela and eastern Colombia southward to northern Bolivia and eastward across Amazonia, west of the Rio Negro in northwestern Brazil and south of the Amazon River from eastern Amazonas to northeastern Pará and Maranhão; also in the Atlantic Forest of central-east Brazil (Bahia and Espírito Santo)
Monasa nigrifrons: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin from eastern Colombia southward to central Bolivia and eastward across most Amazonian lowlands of Brazil to Maranhão and Piauí, and southward to western Minas Gerais and São Paulo, in interior Brazil; also locally in northeastern Atlantic Forest in Pernambuco and Alagoas
Montecincla cachinnans: southwestern Peninsular India (Nilgiri Hills in western Tamil Nadu)
Montecincla fairbanki: southern India (Palni and Anaimalai hills and northern Kerala)
Montecincla jerdoni: hill forest of southwestern India (Western Ghats in Coorg region)
Montecincla meridionalis: hill forest of southwestern India (southern Kerala)
Monticola angolensis: foothill to montane miombo woodland from western Angola eastward to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and western and southern Tanzania, thence southward to northeastern Botswana, Zimbabwe, and western Mozambique
Monticola brevipes: foothill to montane arid scrub, grassland with rock outcrops, and escarpments, from western Angola southward to Namibia, southeastern Botswana, and South Africa; local downslope dispersal post-breeding
Monticola cinclorhyncha: breeds mountains of eastern Afghanistan, northern Pakistan and India; winters to Myanmar
Monticola erythronotus: highland forest of northernmost Madagascar (Montagne d'Ambre)
Monticola explorator: breeds montane grassland and rocky outcrops in southern and eastern South Africa, Lesotho, and western Eswatini; downslope migration, occurs in austral winter to southern Mozambique
Monticola gularis: breeds southeastern Siberia to northeastern China and Korean Peninsula; winters to southeastern Asia
Monticola rufiventris: Pakistan to southeastern Tibet, southwestern China, Myanmar, northern Laos, and northern Vietnam
Monticola rufocinereus: foothill to montane rocky scrub, lightly wooded open slopes, and ravines, in southwestern Arabian Peninsula, and from Eritrea, Ethiopia, and northern Somalia southward to northern Tanzania
Monticola rupestris: lowland to montane rocky mountain slopes, cliffs and gorges with scattered bushes, and old buildings, in southern and eastern South Africa, Lesotho, and Eswatini; some downslope dispersal in winter
Monticola saxatilis: breeds rocky regions of southern Palearctic region; winters to eastern Africa
Monticola semirufus: foothill to montane scrubby gorges, wooded rocky ravines, and open Podocarpus forest with rocky outcrops, in south-central Eritrea and Ethiopia
Monticola solitarius: lowland to montane steep rocky valleys, crags and gorges, sea cliffs, and ruins, from Iberia eastward through Türkiye and Caucasus to southern Kazakhstan, and in northeastern China and Korean Peninsula eastward to Sakhalin and Japan including southward to Ogasawara (Bonin) and Iwo (Volcano) islands, and southward to northwestern Africa, Levant, Middle East, Himalayas, southeastern China, and Taiwan, thence southward to Philippines, Malayan Peninsula, and Sumatra; altitudinal migrant and long-distance migrant in winter, reaching western and northeastern Africa, India, and Indonesia
Montifringilla adamsi: rocky steppe near streams and snowline in Ladakh (far northwestern India) and adjacent Tibet eastward to northeastern Qinghai and western Gansu, and southward to northern Nepal and northern Sikkim and adjacent Tibet; nomadic in winter but remains at high elevations
Montifringilla henrici: eastern Tibetan Plateau (northeastern Tibet and Qinghai)
Montifringilla nivalis: southwestern and central Palearctic in rocky alpine barrens, meadows and buildings, from northern Spain eastward through Austria to southwestern and far south-central Russia, Xinjiang (northwestern China), and Mongolia, southward to Corsica and eastward through northern Afghanistan to southeastern Kazakhstan; mostly resident but some move to lower elevations and straggle elsewhere
Morococcyx erythropygus: arid and thorny scrub, semiarid woodland, and savanna in the Pacific slope from northwestern Mexico (southern Sinaloa), southward to northwestern Costa Rica; in Honduras and Nicaragua northward along some valleys of the Caribbean basin
Morphnarchus princeps: montane forest of Costa Rica to Colombia and northern Ecuador
Morphnus guianensis: forest of eastern Guatemala to northeastern Argentina and southern Brazil
Morus bassanus: breeds North Atlantic coasts from Iceland through Norway and France, and Newfoundland (southeastern Canada); ranges southward on coasts to western Mediterranean and northwestern Africa, and to Florida and northern Gulf of Mexico
Morus capensis: breeds islands off southern Africa; disperses to coastal Mozambique
Morus serrator: breeds islands off southeastern Australia including Tasmania, and coasts and islands off New Zealand
Motacilla aguimp: widespread sub-Saharan Africa in lowland to montane wetlands, rivers, parks, and towns (but mostly absent from Congolian rainforest except along large rivers, eastern Somalia, and the Namib and Kalahari deserts), from Senegambia eastward to Sudan (and northward along the Nile to southern Egypt), southward to southern Africa
Motacilla alba: widespread in lowland to montane open habitats, including seashore, river edge, farmland, short grassland, and towns, from Iceland, British Isles, and Scandinavia eastward to Siberia and western Alaska, and southward to northwestern Africa, Europe, Levant, northern Iran, northern India, southern China, and Japan; northern populations migrate to African Sahel, eastern Africa, southern and southeastern Asia, and northern Philippines
Motacilla bocagii: locally in forest of southern São Tomé
Motacilla capensis: lowland to montane grassland, wetlands, and towns from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Uganda eastward to central Kenya, thence southward to Burundi and northwestern Tanzania, and western Angola eastward to Zambia, and southward through Namibia and Zimbabwe to South Africa and southern Mozambique
Motacilla cinerea: lowland to montane fast-flowing streams in forest, foothill rivers, and flatland canals with artificial waterfalls, from British Isles and Scandinavia eastward to Siberia and Kamchatka, and southward to Azores, Madeira, and Canary Islands, southern Europe, Caucasus, northeastern China and Japan, and from Afghanistan eastward through Himalayas to northeastern India; migrates southward to northern and eastern Africa, southern and southeastern Asia, Philippines, Greater Sundas, and Indonesia
Motacilla citreola: breeds north-central Europe to north-central Siberia and northeastern China, and southward in Himalayas; winters to central Asia, Indian subcontinent, southeastern Asia, and southeastern China
Motacilla clara: patchy in sub-Saharan Africa, along lowland to montane rocky rivers and streams in forest, from Guinea to southeastern Nigeria southward to Angola, plus Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), and Eritrea and Ethiopia southward to southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and southwestern Tanzania, and through Zimbabwe and southern and eastern South Africa
Motacilla flava: lowland to montane marsh, wet meadows, grassy tundra, bogs, damp steppe, and waterside pastures, from British Isles and Scandinavia eastward to northwestern Siberia, and southward to northwestern Africa, Mediterranean Europe, Nile Valley (Egypt), Arabian Peninsula, northern Afghanistan, and western China; migrates southward to sub-Saharan Africa and Indian subcontinent
Motacilla flaviventris: open country and streams throughout Madagascar
Motacilla grandis: breeds Japan from Hokkaido southward to Kyushu; winters to China, Korean Peninsula, and Taiwan
Motacilla maderaspatensis: Himalayas (northern Pakistan to Bangladesh) and Peninsular India
Motacilla samveasnae: lower Mekong delta of Cambodia and Laos
Motacilla tschutschensis: lowland to foothill grassy swamps, wet meadows, grassy tundra, and grassy clearings in forest, from northern Siberia eastward to northern and western Alaska, and southward to northern Mongolia, northeastern China, and Commander and Kurile Islands; migrates southward to southeastern Asia, Philippines, Greater Sundas, Indonesia, and northern Australia
Moupinia poecilotis: mountains of southwestern China (southeastern Qinghai to northwestern Sichuan and northwestern Yunnan)
Mulleripicus fuliginosus: east-central and southern Philippines (Samar, Leyte, and Mindanao)
Mulleripicus pulverulentus: terai zone of northern India and Nepal eastward through northeastern India to northern Myanmar, southwestern China, and Indochina, and Malayan Peninsula to Sumatra, Java, Borneo, and Palawan group
Mundia elpenor: formerly Ascension Island; extinct, may have survived until 1815
Muscicapa adusta: lowland to montane forest edges and clearings, miombo woodland, Fynbos, and plantations, from southeastern Nigeria, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), eastward to southern Eritrea, western Ethiopia, and northern Kenya, and southward to western Angola and eastern and southern South Africa; partial migrant in southern populations
Muscicapa aquatica: lowland and foothill vegetated edges to lakes, pools, rivers, and papyrus swamps, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to South Sudan, thence southward through eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and western Kenya, to northeastern Tanzania and central Zambia
Muscicapa cassini: lowland to foothill forest adjacent to rivers and streams, and seasonally flooded forest, from central Guinea and adjacent Sierra Leone eastward to eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Uganda, and southward to northwestern Angola and northern Zambia

Muscicapa ferruginea: breeds Nepal to northern India, southern China, and Taiwan; winters to Indochina
Muscicapa gambagae: very patchy in foothill to submontane arid woodland, acacia and brushy savanna, and dry highland forest, from central Guinea and central Mali eastward to central Ethiopia, northern Somalia, and southwestern Arabian Peninsula, and southward to central Cameroon, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and central Tanzania; some post-breeding dispersal
Muscicapa griseisticta: breeds southeastern Siberia to northeastern China; winters to New Guinea and Philippines
Muscicapa muttui: breeds northeastern India to southern China and northern Vietnam; winters to Sri Lanka
Muscicapa sethsmithi: disjunctly in lowland to submontane open understory and clearings in primary and old secondary forest, from southeastern Nigeria and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) eastward to western Central African Republic, and southward to western Republic of the Congo, and in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Uganda
Muscicapa sibirica: disjunctly in submontane to montane taiga spruce forest, evergreen forest, and rhododendron scrub in secondary woodland, from eastern Kazakhstan eastward to Kamchatka, and southward to northeastern China and Japan, and from northeastern Afghanistan eastward through Himalayas to central China, and southward to western Myanmar; migrates to southeastern China and Indochina to Sumatra and Borneo

Muscicapa tyrrhenica: breeds Balearic Islands, Corsica, Sardinia, Tuscan archipelago, and narrow band of Tyrrhenian coast of Peninsular Italy; winters to western and southwestern Africa
Muscicapa williamsoni: disjunctly in lowland to foothill broadleaf evergreen and semi-evergreen forest, from southeastern Myanmar and southern Thailand southward to northwestern peninsular Malaysia, and in northeastern Borneo; some populations migrate southward to Sumatra and Borneo
Muscigralla brevicauda: arid southwestern Ecuador to far northern Chile; Gorgona Island (Colombia)
Muscipipra vetula: southeastern Brazil (Minas Gerais) to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
Muscisaxicola albifrons: Andes of southern Peru (Ancash) to western Bolivia and far northern Chile
Muscisaxicola albilora: breeds Andes of central and southern Chile and adjacent Argentina; winters to southern Ecuador
Muscisaxicola alpinus: arid montane scrub, dry, grassy, and Espeletia paramo in the Andes of northeastern Colombia (Santander to Distrito Capital), in the central Andes of Colombia (Caldas to Cauca), and from southernmost Andean Colombia (Nariño) to southern Ecuador (Loja)
Muscisaxicola capistratus: breeds southern Chile and southern Argentina; winters northward in Andes to southern Peru
Muscisaxicola cinereus: breeds in dry to semi-humid grassy puna, lakesides, and montane scrub in Andes of northeastern Chile and northwestern Argentina southward to southwestern Argentina (Chubut); winters in Andes from northwestern Argentina to central Peru (Huánuco and Ancash)
Muscisaxicola flavinucha: breeds on rocky and sparsely vegetated slopes, bogs, and puna grasslands in the Andes from northern Chile and northwestern Argentina to Tierra del Fuego; winters in the Andes of Bolivia and northwestern Argentina northward to northern Peru (Ancash)
Muscisaxicola frontalis: breeds Andes of Chile and Argentina; winters northward to southern Peru (Arequipa)
Muscisaxicola griseus: páramo of Peru and western Bolivia (La Paz to Cochabamba)
Muscisaxicola juninensis: Andes of Peru (Junín and Lima) to northern Chile and northwestern Argentina
Muscisaxicola maclovianus: breeds in open meadows and bogs and short grassland in southern Chile and southwestern Argentina (from Neuquén) southward to Tierra del Fuego and the Falkland Islands (where resident); winters mainly coastally northward to western Peru (from Lambayeque) and Uruguay

Muscisaxicola rufivertex: Andes of Peru from central Cajamarca southward to central Chile and northwestern Argentina (northern Neuquén), and in the sierras of Cordoba and San Luis
Mustelirallus albicollis: northern Colombia to Venezuela, Trinidad, the Guianas, and eastern Brazil to Paraguay, eastern Bolivia, and far northern Argentina
Mustelirallus colombianus: marshes, grassy and shrubby fields and damp grassland from central Panama and northern Colombia southward along the Pacific lowlands of Colombia to west-central Ecuador
Mustelirallus erythrops: damp grassland and thickets, freshwater marshes, ditches, and semi-dry grassy fields from northwestern Costa Rica eastward to eastern Panana, northern Venezuela, Trinidad, and Guianas to the llanos of northeastern Colombia, locally southward to northeastern Ecuador, Cauca and Magdalena valleys of central Colombia, and west of the Andes in northwestern Colombia, western Ecuador southward locally to west-central Peru, the Galapagos Islands, the Amazon basin southward across interior and eastern Brazil (to southern São Paulo and Santa Catarina), northern Paraguay, adjacent northeastern Argentina, and northern Bolivia, southward seasonally to northwestern Argentina, and locally in eastern Peru
Myadestes coloratus: highlands of far eastern Panama (Darién) and adjacent northwestern Colombia
Myadestes elisabeth: hill and montane forest of far western and disjunctly far eastern Cuba
Myadestes genibarbis: montane forest and edge of Jamaica and Hispaniola, and from Dominica to St. Vincent (central to southern Lesser Antilles)
Myadestes lanaiensis: montane forest of Molokai and formerly Lanai; perhaps extinct
Myadestes melanops: mountains of Costa Rica and western Panama (east to Veraguas)
Myadestes occidentalis: forest in hills and mountains from east-central Sonora and central Nuevo León to central Honduras; also Tres Marias Islands (west of Nayarit)
Myadestes ralloides: montane forest and edge of Sierra de Perijá on northern Colombia-Venezuela border, coastal ranges, and Andes of Venezuela southward through central Bolivia
Myadestes townsendi: breeds in varied montane humid coniferous forest types from central Alaska eastward to western Northwest Territories (northwestern Canada) southward to southern California, New Mexico, and Zacatecas and Jalisco (central Mexico), and eastward to western South Dakota; winters to lowlands from southwestern Canada southward to northern Baja California, northern Durango, and southern Coahuila (northern Mexico)
Myadestes unicolor: humid montane forest from southeastern San Luis Potosí and Hidalgo (southern Mexico) southward to north-central Nicaragua
Mycerobas affinis: mountains of northern Pakistan to southeastern Tibet, northeastern Myanmar, and central China
Mycerobas carnipes: mountains of central Asia, southern China (Xinjiang to Shaanxi), and Himalayas from northern Pakistan eastward to northeastern India (Arunachal Pradesh) and northern Myanmar
Mycerobas icterioides: montane forest of northeastern Afghanistan to central Nepal
Mycerobas melanozanthos: mountains of northern Pakistan to southern Tibet, southwestern China, Myanmar, and Thailand
Mycteria americana: southern USA to northern Argentina, Brazil, Cuba, and Hispaniola
Mycteria cinerea: lowlands of Malayan Peninsula, Indochina, Greater Sundas, and Sulawesi
Mycteria leucocephala: lowlands of Indian subcontinent to southern China and southeastern Asia

Myiagra atra: Numfor and Biak (Cenderawasih Bay, off northwestern New Guinea)
Myiagra caledonica: Rennell (southeastern Solomon Islands), Vanuatu, and New Caledonia including Loyalty Islands
Myiagra cyanoleuca: breeds eastern and southeastern Australia (Wet Tropics region, northern Queensland, to Millicent, southeastern South Australia, Tasmania, and Flinders and King Islands, Bass Strait); winters to New Guinea
Myiagra eichhorni: New Hanover, New Ireland, Dyaul, and New Britain (eastern Bismarck Archipelago)
Myiagra erythrops: mangroves and lowlands of Palau (western Caroline Islands)
Myiagra ferrocyanea: Solomon Islands (except Makira, Rennell, and Temotu, southeastern Solomon Islands)
Myiagra freycineti: formerly Guam (southern Mariana Islands); extinct, last reported 1983
Myiagra inquieta: eastern and southern Australia (northeastern Queensland to Eyre Peninsula, and Jonndalup to Esperance, southwestern Australia)
Myiagra nana: southern New Guinea and northern Australia (Kimberley region, northern Western Australia, to southwestern Cape York Peninsula, northern Queensland; northwestern Torres Strait islands)
Myiagra rubecula: southern and southeastern New Guinea and northern and eastern Australia
Myiagra ruficollis: Lesser Sundas, Tanimbar Islands (southern Moluccas), southern New Guinea, and northeastern Western Australia to northeastern Queensland (northern Australia)
Myiagra vanikorensis: Vanikoro (southeastern Temotu, southeastern Solomon Islands) and Fiji (southwestern Polynesia)
Myiarchus antillarum: Puerto Rico including Isla de Culebra and Isla de Vieques (both just east of Puerto Rico), and Virgin Islands
Myiarchus apicalis: arid scrub of Colombia (west of the eastern Andes)
Myiarchus barbirostris: open woodland and montane forest of Jamaica
Myiarchus cephalotes: foothill and montane cloudforest in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Carabobo eastward to the Paría Peninsula), the Andes of western Venezuela southward to central Bolivia (Cochabamba and western Santa Cruz)
Myiarchus cinerascens: breeds in varied drier woodland types of lowlands to mountains of western USA from south-central Washington southeastward to east-central Texas, in the west, southward to southern Baja California and Guanajuato (northwestern and central Mexico); non-breeders shift as far southward as northwestern Nicaragua
Myiarchus crinitus: breeds southeastern Canada to Gulf States; winters to northwestern South America
Myiarchus ferox: llanos of eastern Colombia to Venezuela and Guyana, and tropical southeastern Colombia to northern Bolivia, the Guianas, and northern Brazil to southern Brazil to eastern Bolivia, eastern Paraguay, and northeastern Argentina
Myiarchus flavidior: Pacific lowlands of southern Mexico (Chiapas) to western Nicaragua, and arid interior valleys of Honduras
Myiarchus nugator: southern Lesser Antilles (St. Vincent and the Grenadines, and Grenada)
Myiarchus nuttingi: semiarid western Mexico (northern Sonora and southwestern Chihuahua southward to Chiapas) and central Mexico, and arid interior montane valleys of Chiapas to northwestern Costa Rica
Myiarchus oberi: forest to thornscrub of lowlands and hills, Lesser Antilles from Sint Eustatius and Barbuda southward to St. Lucia (excluding Montserrat and perhaps Antigua)
Myiarchus panamensis: mangroves and other woodland types of lowlands to hills on Pacific slope from northwestern to southwestern Costa Rica, both slopes of Panama northward to northwestern Venezuela and southward west of Andes to far northwestern Ecuador, and in inter-Andean valleys of northern Colombia
Myiarchus phaeocephalus: dry forest, woodland, and scrub in western Ecuador (from southern Esmeraldas) southward to northwestern Peru, and far southeastern Ecuador and northern Peru eastward across the Marañón Valley (to Amazonas)
Myiarchus sagrae: varied forest, woodland, and edge types from lowlands to hills, Bahamas from Grand Bahama and Andros southward in larger islands to Great Inagua; Cuba and satellite islands, and Grand Cayman; repeated vagrancy to southeastern Florida
Myiarchus semirufus: arid coastal northwestern Peru (Tumbes to northern Lima)
Myiarchus stolidus: varied forest, woodland, and edge types from lowlands to hills of Jamaica and Hispaniola and satellite islands
Myiarchus swainsoni: southern Venezuela and the Guianas to eastern Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, Uruguay, and southern Brazil (northward to São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro); winters in northern South America, from eastern Colombia, Venezuela, and Trinidad eastward and southward to Paraíba, Brazil
Myiarchus tuberculifer: breeds southwestern USA and northwestern Mexico, eastern Mexico (Nuevo León) to west-central Peru and northeastern Colombia, and widespread east of Andes to Guianas and northwestern Argentina, and southeastern Brazil
Myiarchus tyrannulus: southwestern USA through western Mexico to Oaxaca, and Tres Marías Islands, southern Texas through eastern Mexico including Yucatan Peninsula, Pacific coast of El Salvador to northwestern Costa Rica, eastern Colombia to Trinidad and the Guianas, and northern Brazil (lower Amazon River westward to Manaus) to north-central Argentina; southern populations from south of Tucuman and Corrientes winter to southwestern Amazonia
Myiarchus validus: wooded hills and mountains of Jamaica
Myiarchus venezuelensis: Caribbean lowlands of northern Colombia and northern Venezuela; Tobago
Myiarchus yucatanensis: dry forest and humid forest edge of lowland Yucatan Peninsula including Cozumel, southward to Peten (northern Guatemala) and northern Belize
Myiobius atricaudus: humid to semi-humid and deciduous forest and woodland in southeastern Costa Rica and Panama, northern Colombia southward along the Cauca and Magdalena valleys, the Pacific lowlands southward to southwestern Ecuador and adjacent Peru, east of the Andes in the middle to low Orinoco Valley of Venezuela, and in the Amazon basin from southeastern Colombia southward to east-central Peru, eastward locally in the southern Amazonian Brazil, and the Cerrado, Caatinga, and Atlantic Forest regions (northeastern Brazil southward to São Paulo and adjacent Santa Catarina)
Myiobius barbatus: humid forest in the middle Magdalena Valley in northern Colombia, and east of the Andes in the Orinoco basin of eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward across the Amazon basin to southeastern Peru, southwestern Brazil and northernmost Bolivia; also in the Atlantic Forest region from northeastern Brazil southward to southeastern Brazil in northern Santa Catarina and locally in interior Brazil, in eastern Goiás and western Minas Gerais
Myiobius sulphureipygius: humid to semi-humid forest and woodland from the Gulf of Mexico slope in southeastern Mexico and Yucatan Peninsula, southward along the Caribbean slope to eastern Panama and in the Pacific slope of Costa Rica and Panama, and from northwestern Colombia southward along the Pacific lowlands southward to southwestern Ecuador and adjacent Peru
Myiobius villosus: humid foothill and montane forest in the Cerro Tacarcuna in easternmost Panama, in the Sierra de Perijá and the Andes of western Venezuela southward along the eastern Andes to western Bolivia, and in the western Andes from northern Colombia, including the northern end of the central Andes, southward to southwestern Ecuador
Myioborus albifacies: tepuis of southern Venezuela (Cerros Guany, Yaví, and Paraque)
Myioborus albifrons: Andes of western Venezuela (Trujillo, Táchira, and Mérida)
Myioborus brunniceps: Andes of Bolivia (La Paz eastward to south-central Santa Cruz) and southward to northwestern Argentina
Myioborus cardonai: tepuis of southern Venezuela (Cerro Guaiquinima in west-central Bolívar)
Myioborus flavivertex: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
Myioborus melanocephalus: montane Andean cloudforest from far southern Colombia southward through Ecuador to northern Peru, and eastern Andean slope of Peru southeastward to far Bolivia (western Santa Cruz)
Myioborus miniatus: montane forest from northern Mexico southward to Darién (eastern Panama), and in South America in montane cloudforest in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, northeastern Colombia, southward across the Andes of western Venezuela, all Andes of Colombia and Ecuador to northern Peru, and along the eastern Andes of Peru to Chuquisaca in southern Bolivia, also coastal mountains of Venezuela, tepuis of southern Venezuela and adjacent Guyana and Brazil, and coastal mountains of southwest Ecuador
Myioborus ornatus: montane Andean cloudforest from southwestern Venezuela southwestward in the eastern Andes of Colombia, and in the western and central Andes of Colombia
Myioborus pariae: northeastern Venezuela (humid cloudforest of Paría Peninsula)
Myioborus pictus: montane forest of Arizona, western New Mexico, and southwestern Texas in west, and Nuevo León in east, southward through northern Nicaragua; some withdrawal of non-breeders from north in winter; repeated vagrancy to California and elsewhere
Myioborus torquatus: humid montane forest of Costa Rica and western Panama
Myiodynastes bairdii: arid southwestern Ecuador to northwestern Peru (Lima)
Myiodynastes chrysocephalus: east slope of Andes of Peru to Bolivia and northwestern Argentina
Myiodynastes hemichrysus: montane cloudforest in Costa Rica and western Panama, eastern Panama (Darién), the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Falcón to Monagas), the Santa Marta and Perijá mountains, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward to northern Peru (north of the Río Marañón)
Myiodynastes luteiventris: breeds southeastern Arizona to Costa Rica; winters eastern Ecuador to northern Bolivia
Myiodynastes maculatus: breeds Gulf slope of Mexico to northwestern Peru (Piura), Caribbean coast of Colombia and Venezuela, the Guianas, and through eastern Peru and central Argentina; northern and southern populations migratory
Myiomela leucura: patchy in foothill to montane understory of dense broadleaf evergreen forest, often in bamboo, and river-valley riparian thickets, from central Nepal eastward to central China (including Hainan) and Taiwan, and southward to western Cambodia and adjacent Thailand, and peninsular Malaysia
Myiomela sumatrana: mountains of northern and west-central Sumatra
Myiopagis caniceps: southeastern Peru, northern Bolivia, and adjacent Brazil (undescribed subspecies, not true caniceps?); eastern and southern Bolivia southward to northwestern Argentina and eastward to Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, and south-central and eastern Brazil
Myiopagis cinerea: eastern Colombia to eastern Ecuador, northeastern Peru, southern Venezuela, and northwestern Brazil
Myiopagis flavivertex: southern Venezuela to the Guianas, northeastern Peru, and western Amazonian Brazil
Myiopagis gaimardii: tropical rainforest, gallery forest, and semi-humid forest from central Panama eastward to the lowlands of northern Colombia and western Venezuela, in central Colombia southward to the middle Cauca and Magdalena valleys, east of the Andes from northern Venezuela, Trinidad, and the Guianas, southward across the Amazon basin to eastern Peru, Bolivia, and Brazil (Maranhão to southern Mato Grosso do Sul), and disjunctly in the Atlantic Forest of northeastern Brazil (Pernambuco and Alagoas)
Myiopagis olallai: humid montane and foothills forest disjunctly in the Sierra de Perijá, the northern end of the central Andes of Colombia, including Sierra de San Lucas, the eastern slope of the Andes of southern Colombia and Ecuador, and locally in the eastern Andes of south-central and southeastern Peru
Myiopagis parambae: forest and edge of lowlands to hills from central Panama (disjunct) and eastern Panama south west of Andes to west-central Ecuador
Myiopagis subplacens: western Ecuador (western Esmeraldas and Manabí) to northwestern Peru
Myiopagis viridicata: disjunctly, Pacific slope of Mexico from Sinaloa and Tres Marías Islands, and tropical southeastern Mexico (Tamaulipas), including Cozumel, to northern South America, Guyana, and southeastern Peru to eastern Bolivia, eastern Paraguay, northern Argentina, and central, eastern and southeastern Brazil
Myiophobus crypterythrus: west of the Andes in southwestern Colombia, western Ecuador, and northwestern Peru (southward to southwestern Cajamarca)
Myiophobus cryptoxanthus: tropical eastern Ecuador and northeastern Peru (San Martín)
Myiophobus fasciatus: dry forest, scrub, riparian thickets, brushy savanna, river islands, and bamboo stands from the Pacific slope of Costa Rica eastward to eastern Panama (including the Pearl Islands), in the foothills of the Santa Marta and Perijá mountains, east of the Andes in northern Venezuela eastward to Trinidad and northern Guianas, the tepuis of eastern Venezuela, northernmost Brazil (Roraima), and adjacent Guyana, along the western Andes of Colombia (southward to Nariño), the foothills of the eastern Andes, and locally in the lowlands of eastern Ecuador to central Argentina (Mendoza to Buenos Aires), but local in the Amazon basin; populations of central Argentina winter northward
Myiophobus flavicans: foothill and montane cloudforest in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Yaracuy eastward to Sucre), the Sierra de Perijá, the Andes from western Venezuela southward across the Andes of Colombia to northern Peru north of the Río Marañón (Piura and Cajamarca), and the eastern Andes of Peru east and south of the Río Marañón (Amazonas to northwestern Cusco)
Myiophobus inornatus: east slope of Andes of southern Peru (Cusco) to western Bolivia
Myiophobus phoenicomitra: wet foothill forest in the western slope of the western Andes of Colombia southward to southwestern Ecuador, the northern end of the Central Andes of Colombia, and the eastern slope of the eastern Andes from southern Colombia southward to southern Ecuador, and locally in northeastern Peru (San Martín and adjacent eastern Amazonas)
Myiophobus roraimae: montane cloudforest and sandy-soil forest in the tepuis of southern and southeastern Venezuela, far northern Brazil (northern Roraima), and adjacent Guyana, disjunctly in outlying ridges in southeastern Ecuador (cordillera de Cutucu, cordillera del Condor, and locally in the southeastern Andes), southward locally along the eastern Andes of Peru to (very locally) northwestern Bolivia (La Paz)
Myiophobus rufescens: west of the Andes from northern Peru (southern Lambayeque) southward to far northern Chile (Arica)
Myiopsitta luchsi: xeric intermontane valleys of central Bolivia
Myiopsitta monachus: semiarid savanna with scattered trees and various grassland habitats in the Cerrado from south-central Brazil (in southern Mato Grosso southward to southern Mato Grosso do Sul, Paraná, and southern Rio Grande do Sul), and southward across Uruguay to central-eastern Argentina (to Río Negro and Chubut); also west to Paraguay, and eastern Bolivia
Myiornis albiventris: east slope of Andes of Peru (Huánuco) to western Bolivia (Santa Cruz)
Myiornis atricapillus: humid lowlands of Costa Rica to western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador
Myiornis auricularis: humid forest in the Atlantic Forest, Caatinga and Cerrado regions of eastern Brazil from Pernambuco southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul, eastward southern Goiás and southern Mato Grosso do Sul, eastern Paraguay, and northeastern Argentina
Myiornis ecaudatus: tropical rainforest in the Río Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas, also in Trinidad, the foothills of the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela, and the foothills of the Andes in western Venezuela and northeastern Colombia, southward across most Amazonia to north-central Bolivia and southern Mato Grosso, and in Brazil eastward to western Tocantins and western Maranhão
Myiotheretes fumigatus: humid montane forest in the Sierra de Perijá and the Andes of western Venezuela southward along the Andes of Colombia and Ecuador to the Andes of northern Peru (Cajamarca), and in the eastern Andes from northern Peru (Amazonas) southward to southeastern Peru (Cusco)
Myiotheretes fuscorufus: east slope of Andes of southern Peru (Pasco) to western Bolivia
Myiotheretes pernix: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
Myiotheretes striaticollis: humid to semi-humid forest borders, woodland, and treeline in the Santa Marta and Perijá mountains, and the Andes of western Venezuela southward to far northern Chile and northwestern Argentina (to northern La Rioja)
Myiothlypis bivittata: humid forest in the tepuis of central and southern Venezuela, adjacent Guyana, and far northern Brazil, and cloudforest and semi-humid forest in the eastern Andes of southeastern Peru (Madre de Dios and Puno), Bolivia, and southward to Tucumán (northwestern Argentina)
Myiothlypis chlorophrys: tropical southwestern Colombia (Cauca and Nariño) to northwestern Ecuador
Myiothlypis chrysogaster: east slope of Andes of central and southern Peru (Huánuco and far southwestern Loreto southward to Puno) and western Bolivia (La Paz)
Myiothlypis cinereicollis: montane Andean cloudforest from eastern Andes of northeastern Colombia including Sierra de Perijá to western Venezuela
Myiothlypis conspicillata: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
Myiothlypis coronata: montane Andean cloudforest from western Venezuela and all Andes of Colombia southward to northern Peru, and along the eastern Andes of Peru to central Bolivia (far western Santa Cruz)
Myiothlypis flaveola: disjunctly in humid and deciduous forest in the coastal mountains and Andes of northern Venezuela to northeasternmost Andean foothillls of Colombia, tepuis of far southern Venezuela, adjacent Brazil, and western Guyana, southern Amazonia in central Brazil (Pará and Maranhão), southward to the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil, west to the Cerrado and Caatinga of central Brazil, and southward through eastern Bolivia and central Paraguay to far northeastern Argentina
Myiothlypis fraseri: dry and semi-humid forest in the lowlands and Andean foothills of western Ecuador, from far southern Esmeraldas southward to Piura and Lambayeque (northwestern Peru)
Myiothlypis fulvicauda: riverbanks in humid forest from northern Honduras southward to eastern Panama, and in South America from the lowlands in northern Colombia southward along the Cauca and Magdalena valleys in central Colombia and southward west of the Andes to southwestern Ecuador; in the Amazon from north-central Colombia (Casanare) southward to northwestern Bolivia and Brazil (west of the Rio Negro and to the Rio Madeira and Rio Teles Pires)
Myiothlypis griseiceps: cloudforest of coastal mountains of northeastern Venezuela
Myiothlypis leucoblephara: eastern Paraguay to southeastern Brazil, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
Myiothlypis luteoviridis: montane Andean cloudforest from western Venezuela and all Andes of Colombia, southward in eastern Andes of Ecuador (including Cordillera de Cutucu) to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz)
Myiothlypis nigrocristata: Andes of Colombia to northern Venezuela, Ecuador, and northern Peru
Myiothlypis rivularis: disjunctly on riverbanks in humid forest from northern Venezuela eastward to French Guiana, southward across central and eastern Amazonian Brazil (east of the Rio Negro and to Pará), also along the eastern base of the Andes in central Bolivia, and also humid forest in the Atlantic Forest of southeastern Brazil (Bahia southward to Santa Catarina), to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
Myiothlypis signata: montane cloudforest in the eastern Andes from Huánuco (central Peru) southward to Salta (northwestern Argentina)
Myiotriccus ornatus: humid montane and foothill forest in the Andes from northern Colombia southward to southern Ecuador, and along the eastern Andes southeastward to southeastern Peru; in western Ecuador also in isolated coastal ridges
Myiozetetes cayanensis: shrubby clearings and open areas near semi-humid to humid forest, Cerrado, and Caatinga from southwestern Costa Rica southward in Pacific slope of Colombia to southwestern Ecuador, and throughout South American east of the Andes southward to eastern Paraguay, far northeastern Argentina (one recent record), and southeastern Brazil (northern Paraná)
Myiozetetes granadensis: open areas near humid forest and woodlands from eastern Honduras southward to eastern Panama, the Pacific lowlands of southern Costa Rica and western Panama, northern Colombia southward to the middle Magdalena Valley, west of the Andes southward to northwestern Ecuador, and in the Amazon basin from southern Venezuela eastward to far northern Brazil (Roraim) and southward through northern and western Brazil (western Amazonas and Acre) to northwestern Bolivia (to Cochabamba)
Myiozetetes luteiventris: tropical rainforest edge in the Orinoco and Amazon basins, from southern Venezuela eastward to French Guiana and northeastern Brazil (Amapá) and westward to southeastern Colombia, eastern Ecuador, eastern Peru, northwestern Bolivia, and western Mato Grosso (central Brazil)
Myiozetetes similis: semi-deciduous to humid forest borders and adjacent cleared areas on the Pacific and Gulf of Mexico slopes from northern Mexico (southern Sonora, northern Nuevo León, and northern Tamaulipas) southward throughout Central America in northern Colombia and western Venezuela to the headwaters of the Río Magdalena, west of the Andes in western Ecuador and far northwestern Peru, and widespread east of the Andes to central Bolivia, southward to eastern Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, and far southern Brazil (northern Rio Grande do Sul)
Myophonus borneensis: foothill and montane forest of Borneo
Myophonus caeruleus: central and eastern China (from southeastern Gansu and eastern Sichuan eastward to northern Hebei and Zhejiang, and southward to Guangdong, Hong Kong, and Guangxi); non-breeding also southward to eastern Myanmar, northern Thailand, Laos, and northern Vietnam
Myophonus flavirostris: breeds central Asia through Himalayas eastward to south-central China (Yunnan) and southward to Sumatra and Java
Myophonus glaucinus: montane forest of Java and Bali
Myophonus horsfieldii: swift flowing rocky streams of Peninsular India
Myophonus robinsoni: moist montane forest of central Malaya
Myopornis boehmi: lowland to foothill miombo woodland from central Angola eastward to west-central Tanzania, and southward to Zambia and Malawi
Myornis senilis: Andes of Colombia, Ecuador, and northern Peru (south to Pasco)
Myrmeciza longipes: dry to semi-humid and humid forest in central and eastern Panama; northern Colombia and western Venezuela, southward to the headwaters of the Río Magdalena, and southward along the eastern base of the Andes to northeastern Colombia; in northern and eastern Venezuela, easternmost Colombia, Trinidad, western Guyana and southern Suriname southward to northern Brazil (Roraima), and in northeastern Brazil in the mouth of the Amazon River (northern Pará and Amapá)
Myrmecocichla aethiops: disjunctly in foothill to montane grassland with termitaria, and open acacia woodland, from southern Mauritania eastward through the Sahel to south-central Sudan, and from central Kenya southward to northern Tanzania
Myrmecocichla arnotti: lowland to highland miombo woodland, and mopane and acacia woodland, from western Angola eastward to southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and central Tanzania, thence southward to northeastern Namibia and northeastern South Africa
Myrmecocichla formicivora: lowland to foothill open grassland, semi-desert scrub, sparsely-bushed steppe with termitaria; and on grassy pans, from Namibia eastward to far western Zimbabwe, and southward to South Africa, Lesotho lowlands, and western Eswatini
Myrmecocichla melaena: foothill to submontane bare rocky cliffs, ravines, gorges, or waterfalls, and adjacent brush, in southern Eritrea and Ethiopia highlands
Myrmecocichla monticola: lowland to montane open rocky grassland, escarpment, and Karoo semi-desert, from western Angola southward through Namibia to South Africa (eastward to Mpumalanga and KwaZulu-Natal), and Lesotho and Eswatini
Myrmecocichla nigra: patchy in lowland to submontane grassland with termitaria, open savanna, farmed land, and recently-burnt ground, from southeastern Nigeria and southern Chad eastward to southern South Sudan and southwestern Kenya, and southward Angola, Zambia, and southern Tanzania; previously Senegambia and Liberia but may be extirpated there
Myrmecocichla tholloni: disjunctly in foothill open grasslands on sandy or marshy ground, often with sparse bush or termitaria, from southeastern Gabon southward to western Democratic Republic of the Congo, and in northeastern Angola and adjacent Democratic Republic of the Congo, and in central Angola
Myrmelastes brunneiceps: southern Peru (Cusco, Madre de Dios, and Puno) and far west-central Bolivia
Myrmelastes caurensis: humid to semi-deciduous forest in the Orinoco basin and tepuis of southern Venezuela, in western Bolívar, southward to northern Brazil, in northernmost Amazonas
Myrmelastes humaythae: western Amazonian Brazil (east to the Rio Madeira), southeastern Peru (eastern Madre de Dios), and northern Bolivia (Pando)
Myrmelastes hyperythrus: southern Colombia to eastern Peru, northwestern Bolivia, and southwestern Amazonian Brazil
Myrmelastes leucostigma: tropical rainforest and borders in the eastern foothills of the Andes from northeastern Colombia and adjacent Venezuela southward to southeastern Colombia and across the western Amazon basin southward to southeastern Peru, southwestern Brazil, and adjacent Bolivia; also in southeastern and southern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to the Amazon basin of Brazil, mainly north of the Amazon River
Myrmelastes rufifacies: Brazil south of the Amazon River (Rio Madeira to Rio Tocantins, and northern Rondônia)
Myrmelastes saturatus: tepui region of far southeastern Venezuela, adjacent Guyana (Mount Roraima environs), and adjacent Brazil
Myrmelastes schistaceus: southeastern Colombia to northeastern Ecuador, eastern Peru, and west-central Amazonian Brazil
Myrmia micrura: arid scrub of southwestern Ecuador and northwestern Peru
Myrmoborus leucophrys: humid forest in the foothills of the Andes of western Venezuela and northeastern Colombia, and in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to south-central Brazil, in southern Mato Grosso, and northern Bolivia, but absent from most of northern Amazonia, north of the Amazon River
Myrmoborus lophotes: far southwestern Amazonian Brazil to southeastern Peru and northwestern Bolivia
Myrmoborus lugubris: dense scrub and woodland in river islands of the Amazon basin from northeastern Peru and adjacent eastern Ecuador eastward along the Amazon River and main tributaries to central Brazil, in eastern Amazonas, west of the Rio Tapajos
Myrmoborus melanurus: tropical northeastern Peru and adjacent Brazil (far western Amazonas)
Myrmoborus myotherinus: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin from southern Venezuela and eastern Colombia southward to south-central Brazil (southern Mato Grosso) and central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz)
Myrmochanes hemileucus: islands in the Amazon River (northeastern Ecuador to northern Bolivia and western Brazil)
Myrmoderus eowilsoni: northern Peru: local on ridge crests of Cordillera Azul (eastern San Martín)
Myrmoderus ferrugineus: humid forest and woodland savanna in the lower Orinoco basin in northeastern Venezuela and in the Guianas southward in eastern Brazil to south-central Amazon basin, between the Rio Madeira and Rio Tapajos, in northwestern Mato Grosso and eastern Rondônia
Myrmoderus loricatus: eastern Brazil (Bahia, Minas Gerais, Espírito Santo, and Rio de Janeiro)
Myrmoderus ruficauda: humid to semi-humid forest in the Atlantic Forest region of eastern Brazil from eastern Paraiba southward to Espírito Santo and adjacent Minas Gerais
Myrmoderus squamosus: southeastern Brazil (Rio de Janeiro to northeastern Rio Grande do Sul)
Myrmophylax atrothorax: riparian thickets, varzea forest, stunted savanna woodland, swampy thickets, and forest borders in the Orinoco and Amazon basins, and the Guiana Shield from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to central Bolivia and south-central Brazil in southern Mato Grosso and adjacent Goiás
Myrmorchilus strigilatus: deciduous to semi-humid woodland and scrub in the Caatinga and Cerrado regions of northeastern Brazil southward to northern Minas Gerais, and in the Chaco region of eastern Bolivia, western Paraguay, and adjacent Brazil southward to northern Argentina
Myrmornis torquata: tropical rainforest from southeastern Honduras, northern and southern Nicaragua, and eastern Panama and adjacent Colombia; the northern base of the western and central Andes of Colombia southward to Boyaca in the Magdalena Valley; east of the Andes in southeastern Colombia, eastern Ecuador, and northeastern Peru, and in the Orinoco basin in eastern Venezuela, the Guianas, and southward in the eastern Amazon basin of Brazil to western Maranhão, and between the Rio Madeira and Rio Tapajos to southwestern Brazil, in northern Rondônia
Myrmothera berlepschi: dense thickets, riparian forest, overgrown clearings, gallery forest, and bamboo stands in the Amazon basin south of the Amazon River, from northern Brazil (Pará and eastern Amazonas) southward to south-central Brazil, northern Bolivia southward to western Santa Cruz, and southeastern Peru
Myrmothera campanisona: tropical rainforest in the Guiana Shield and Orinoco and Amazon basins, from eastern and southern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to south-central Brazil (northern Mato Grosso and Rondônia), eastern Peru, and northwestern Bolivia
Myrmothera dives: humid thickets and forest edge of lowlands and hills on Caribbean slope of northeastern Honduras to central Panama, disjunctly from east Panama and south, west of Andes, to far southwestern Colombia
Myrmothera fulviventris: dense thickets, riparian forest, and overgrown clearings in the western Amazon basin from southeastern Colombia southward across eastern Ecuador to northeastern Peru
Myrmothera simplex: dense humid forest, cloudforest, and stunted woodland in the tepuis of southern and southeastern Venezuela, adjacent western Guyana, and northernmost Brazil, in Roraima
Myrmothera subcanescens: Amazonian Brazil, south of the Amazon River, from the right (east) bank of the Rio Madeira to the upper Rio Xingu
Myrmotherula ambigua: far eastern Colombia, southwestern Venezuela, and northwestern Amazonian Brazil
Myrmotherula assimilis: river islands, wooded oxbow lakes, and forest streams in the Amazon River and large tributaries from the Río Napo in northeastern Peru eastward to the eastern Amazon River at the mouth of the Rio Trombetas and Rio Tapajos, and southward to southwestern Brazil and northern Bolivia, along the Rio Madeira and tributaries
Myrmotherula axillaris: humid forest from northeastern Honduras southward to northern Colombia and western Venezuela, southward in interior Colombia to the middle Magdalena Valley and southward on Pacific lowlands to southwestern Ecuador; east of the Andes from Trinidad, eastern Venezuela, and the Guianas southward across the Amazon basin to south-central Brazil, in southern Mato Grosso, and to northern and central Bolivia; also in the Atlantic Forest from northeastern Brazil southward to southern Rio de Janeiro
Myrmotherula behni: humid foothill and montane forest in the tepuis of southern Venezuela, western Guyana, and adjacent Brazil, and locally in the foothills of the eastern Andes and outlying ridges in eastern Colombia and eastern Ecuador
Myrmotherula brachyura: eastern Colombia to the Guianas, Amazonian Brazil, and northern Bolivia
Myrmotherula cherriei: southeastern Colombia, southwestern Venezuela, northeastern Peru, and northwestern Brazil
Myrmotherula fluminensis: southeastern Brazil (known from a 1988 specimen from Serra dos Órgãos)
Myrmotherula grisea: Andean foothills of western Bolivia (La Paz, Cochabamba, and Santa Cruz)
Myrmotherula ignota: tropical rainforest from central Panama and northwestern Colombia southward along the Pacific lowlands to northwestern Ecuador and southward in interior Colombia to the middle Magdalena Valley; also in the western Amazon basin from southeastern Colombia and northwestern Brazil southward to northeastern Peru, southward to Ucayali
Myrmotherula iheringi: bamboo stands in tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin, south of the Amazon River and west of the Rio Tapajos, from western Pará southwestward to southeastern Peru and northwestern Bolivia
Myrmotherula longicauda: humid foothill forest and edges at the base of the eastern Andes from southeastern Colombia southward to western Bolivia, and isolated in the Río Samiria basin of northeastern Peru
Myrmotherula longipennis: tropical rainforest in the Orinoco basin and the Guiana Shield from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward across the entire Amazon basin to south-central Brazil, in central Mato Grosso and to southwestern Brazil and northwestern Bolivia
Myrmotherula menetriesii: tropical rainforest in the Orinoco basin and the Guiana Shield from southern and eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward across the entire Amazon basin to south-central Brazil and northern Bolivia
Myrmotherula minor: coastal southeastern Brazil (southeastern Bahia to far northeastern Santa Catarina)
Myrmotherula multostriata: eastern Colombia to northern Bolivia and Brazil south of the Amazon River
Myrmotherula pacifica: Panama (Veraguas) to coastal Pacific Colombia and western Ecuador

Notiomystis cincta: North Island and satellite islands (New Zealand)
Notopholia corusca: coastal forest and edge from lowlands to hills from southern Somalia southward to southern Cape of South Africa; also Pemba, Zanzibar, and Mafia islands (off Tanzania)
Nucifraga caryocatactes: lowland to montane coniferous forest, taiga, and alpine meadow to tree-line, from southern Scandinavia eastward to eastern Siberia, and southward to European Alps, Caucasus, Korean Peninsula, and Japan; irruptive dispersal during irregular cone-crop failures
Nucifraga columbiana: Rocky Mountains (southwestern Canada to northern Baja California); casual to northwestern Mexico
Nucifraga hemispila: disjunctly in montane rhododendron and coniferous forest, and alpine meadow to tree-line, from Himachal Pradesh (northwestern India) eastward to northeastern China, and southward to northern Myanmar and south-central China, and on Taiwan; irregular irruptive dispersal
Nucifraga multipunctata: eastern Afghanistan (northeastern Paktia and Nuristan), northern and western Pakistan (Fort Sandeman northward along Suleiman Range, Chitral, Gilgit, and Baltistan), Kashmir (Sind Valley, Kishtwar, and Badrawar), northwestern India (eastward to Lahul, in Himachal Pradesh), and possibly adjacent far southwestern Tibet (western China)
Numenius americanus: breeds inland grassland from southern British Columbia eastward to southwestern Saskatchewan (southwestern Canada) southward to northeastern California and northeastern New Mexico (southwestern USA); winters to coastal and inland California, and Gulf Coast to central Panama and western Yucatan Peninsula
Numenius arquata: breeds subarctic and temperate Palearctic wetlands and meadows from Faroe Islands, British Isles, and Scandinavia southward to southern France, eastward through northern Kazakhstan and (locally) northern Mongolia to Transbaikalia (northeastern Russia), Inner Mongolia, and Heilongjiang (northeastern China); winters mainly subtropical to tropical coasts and larger rivers from Iceland, southern British Isles, southern Europe, Mediterranean, Africa, and Malagasy region through Middle East, Indian subcontinent, southeastern Asia, central and southern Japan, Korean Peninsula, southeastern China, Taiwan, Philippines, and Indonesian Archipelago
Numenius borealis: formerly bred low Arctic tundra of northwestern North America, from northern Northwest Territories (northwestern Canada; possibly also northern Alaska); wintered in grassland from southeastern Brazil, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina; probably extinct, last confirmed record 1963
Numenius hudsonicus: Alaska to northern Canada; winters to southern South America
Numenius madagascariensis: breeds inland wetlands from east-central Siberia to Kamchatka and Ussuriland (southeastern Russia) and Heilongjiang (northeastern China); winters to Philippines, Indonesia, Australia, and New Zealand (scarce)
Numenius minutus: breeds patchily in subarctic taiga of west-central to east-central Siberia; winters coastal and inland south-central New Guinea, Port Moresby area (southeastern New Guinea), and northern Australia to west-central and east-central coasts
Numenius phaeopus: breeds patchily northern Palearctic and steppes of southwestern Russia; winters widely on coasts of Old World
Numenius tahitiensis: breeds upland low Arctic tundra of western Alaska, in north-central Seward Peninsula and northern Yukon Delta; winters from Micronesia and Fiji eastward through Northwestern Hawaiian Islands and Kauai (rarer on other main Hawaiian Islands), and throughout Polynesia
Numenius tenuirostris: formerly bred southwestern Siberia; wintered to coastal Tunisia and Morocco; extinct, last verified report 1995
Numida meleagris: open country, wooded savanna, and thornscrub throughout sub-Saharan Africa eastward to eastern Somalia and southward to central Namibia and eastern South Africa and Eswatini (except rainforest); western and central South Africa (the latter now inhabited by non-native domestics); population in northwestern Morocco likely extinct; introduced in Canary Islands and Cabo Verde, Madagascar, Comoro Islands, Arabian Peninsula, Caribbean, Australia, and New Zealand
Nyctanassa violacea: central and eastern USA to eastern Brazil; Galapagos
Nyctibius aethereus: forest interior in lowlands and hills from Chocó of western Colombia, Amazonia and the Guianas from eastern Colombia through northeastern Brazil and southward through central Bolivia and Mato Grosso (central Brazil); disjunctly from southern Bahía to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
Nyctibius grandis: far southern Mexico to northern Bolivia, Paraguay, and southeastern Brazil
Nyctibius griseus: eastern Nicaragua and southwestern Costa Rica southward west of the Andes to northwestern Peru, east of the Andes to northwestern Venezuela, the Guianas, Trinidad and Tobago, and southward to northern Argentina
Nyctibius jamaicensis: forest to open areas in lowlands to hills of Sinaloa on Pacific slope, and Tamaulipas on Caribbean slope, southward through Mexico including Yucatan Peninsula including Cozumel and southward through northwestern Costa Rica; also Cuba, Jamaica, and Hispaniola
Nyctibius leucopterus: northern Amazonia (northeastern Peru and northern Brazil) and eastern Brazil (Bahia and Espírito Santo)
Nyctibius maculosus: locally in Andes of eastern Colombia to western Venezuela and western Bolivia
Nycticorax caledonicus: widespread from Philippines and Ogasawara (Bonin) Islands (southeastern Japan), Indonesian Archipelago through New Guinea, Australia, Bismarck Archipelago, Solomon Archipelago, New Caledonia, and Caroline Islands
Nycticorax duboisi: formerly Réunion; extinct, last reported in 1674
Nycticorax mauritianus: formerly Mauritius; extinct, last reported in 1693
Nycticorax nycticorax: Eurasia from central Europe eastward to eastern China and Japan (Hokkaido to Ryukyu Islands), southward to Indonesia, and Africa and Madagascar; southern Canada to Tierra del Fuego and Falkland Islands
Nycticorax olsoni: formerly Ascension Island; known from subfossil bones
Nycticryphes semicollaris: locally in lowlands of Paraguay and southeastern Brazil to south-central Argentina and central Chile
Nyctidromus albicollis: lower Rio Grande Valley (southern Texas) to northern Bolivia, southern Brazil, and northeastern Argentina
Nyctidromus anthonyi: lowlands of southwestern Ecuador and northwestern Peru
Nyctiphrynus mcleodii: montane oak or pine forest on Pacific slope from southwestern Chihuahua and southeastern Sonora (northwestern Mexico) southward to south-central Oaxaca
Nyctiphrynus ocellatus: humid forest from eastern Honduras, southern Nicaragua, and adjacent Costa Rica, in the Amazon basin from southeastern Colombia southward to northern Bolivia (southward to western Santa Cruz), and eastward across the Amazon of Brazil, south of the Amazon River, to eastern Pará, northern Tocantins, and western Maranhão; also in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil from Pernambuco southward to northern Paraná, eastern Paraguay, and far northeastern Argentina
Nyctiphrynus rosenbergi: western Colombia (Chocó) and far northwestern Ecuador
Nyctiphrynus yucatanicus: southern Mexico (Yucatan Peninsula) to northern Belize and Petén of northern Guatemala
Nyctipolus hirundinaceus: arid scrub and deciduous forest with rocky outcrops in eastern Brazil from northern Ceará and Piauí southward to northern and eastern Minas Gerais and southern Espirito Santo
Nyctipolus nigrescens: eastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, the Guianas, Bolivia, and Brazil
Nyctiprogne leucopyga: edges of black-water rivers, igapo forest, and oxbow lakes in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from northern Venezuela and eastern Guyana southward across the Amazon of Colombia, northeastern Ecuador, far eastern Peru, and Amazonian Brazil to northern and eastern Bolivia and adjacent Paraguay; in northeastern Brazil northward to coastal French Guiana
Nyctiprogne vielliardi: eastern Brazil (xeric Caatinga of northern Bahia and northern Minas Gerais)
Nyctyornis athertoni: lowland to submontane forest, wooded ravines, and mossy forest, from southern Himalayas, Western and Eastern ghats of Peninsular India, eastward to south-central China (including Hainan), northern Vietnam, and southward to southeastern Thailand and southern Vietnam
Nymphicus hollandicus: Australia (except Cape York Peninsula, coastal southeastern and southwestern Australia, and Tasmania)
Nystalus chacuru: deciduous and gallery forest from northeastern Brazil (Maranhão), southward across interior Brazil (Mato Grosso do Sul and Paraná), and in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil (Bahia southward to Rio Grande do Sul), eastern Paraguay, and northeastern Argentina (Misiones and northern Corrientes), and westward to eastern and northern Bolivia; also locally in dry valleys and savannas of eastern Peru (San Martin, Cusco, Ayacucho, Huacavelica, Apurimac, and Madre de Dios)
Nystalus maculatus: deciduous woodland and savannas from northeastern Brazil (Pará and Maranhão southward across interior Brazil to Mato Grosso do Sul and western São Paulo), the Chaco of central and western Paraguay and eastern Bolivia, southward to northern Argentina (San Luis and northeastern Mendoza), and along the Atlantic Forest southward to Bahia
Nystalus obamai: western Amazonia: Ecuador southward to Bolivia and east, south of the Amazon River, to Brazil west of the Rio Madeira
Nystalus radiatus: humid forest of western Panama to western Ecuador
Nystalus striolatus: humid forest in Amazonia south of the Amazon River from eastern Brazil in Maranhão southwestward to Mato Grosso and Rondônia, and to northeastern Bolivia

Oceanites oceanicus: breeds islets in southern Chilean fjords and Cape Horn Archipelago; many islands, coasts, and inland sites in Antarctica; Falkland, South Georgia, Crozet, Heard, Kerguelen (southwestern to southeastern Indian Ocean), and Macquarie islands (far southeast of Australia); non-breeders throughout world oceans except tropical and North Pacific
Oceanites pincoyae: known only from waters near Chiloé Island (Reloncavi Sound and the Chacao Channel), Chile
Ochetorhynchus andaecola: Andes of western Bolivia to northwestern Argentina and adjacent northern Chile
Ochetorhynchus melanurus: arid montane scrub, cliffs and slopes with scattered vegetation in central-north Chile from Atacama southward to central Chile (Maule)
Ochetorhynchus phoenicurus: southern Argentina (Neuquén to southern Santa Cruz) and far southern Chile
Ochetorhynchus ruficaudus: arid montane scrub, bunch-grass, and rocky slopes in the Andes of southern Peru, from Arequipa southward across Bolivia and northeastern Chile, to the Andes of central Chile and further southward to Patagonia and Andes of southern Argentina, to northwestern Santa Cruz
Ochthoeca cinnamomeiventris: Andes of Colombia, Ecuador (entire east slope, southward on the west slope to Chimborazo), and far northern Peru (east slope, north and west of the Marañón Valley)

Ochthoeca leucophrys: dry to semi-humid scrub and woodland in the Andes of southern Ecuador, and from northern Peru in the upper Marañón Valley, southward to northernmost Chile and northwestern Argentina (to northern Mendoza)
Ochthoeca nigrita: Andes of western Venezuela (Mérida, western Barinas, and Táchira)
Ochthoeca oenanthoides: arid montane forest, woodland, and cacti in the Andes from northern Peru (southern Cajamarca) southward to far northern Chile and northwestern Argentina (to Mendoza)
Ochthoeca piurae: locally in Andes of northwestern Peru (Piura to Ancash)
Ochthoeca rufipectoralis: humid to semi-humid montane forest, woodland, and treeline in the Santa Marta and Perijá mountains, and the Andes of northeastern Colombia southward along the western and central Andes of Colombia to northwestern Peru (Ancash and adjacent Lima), and in the eastern Andes from northern Peru southward to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz)
Ochthoeca salvini: arid northwestern Peru (Tumbes to La Libertad)
Ochthoeca superciliosa: Andes of western Venezuela (Trujillo, Mérida, and eastern Táchira)
Ochthoeca thoracica: montane cloudforest in the eastern Andes of northern Peru (from Amazonas, south and east of the Marañón Valley) southward to central Bolivia (far western Santa Cruz)
Ochthornis littoralis: southern Guyana to southern Venezuela, northern Bolivia, and Amazonian Brazil
Ocreatus underwoodii: montane cloud forest and foothill forest in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela, from Falcón eastward to Miranda, and in the Andes from western Venezuela and the Sierra de Perijá, southward thorugh the Andes from Colombia to Bolivia (northern Chuquisaca)
Ocyceros birostris: northeastern Pakistan, India, and northwestern Bangladesh
Ocyceros gingalensis: moist deciduous forest of Sri Lanka
Ocyceros griseus: moist deciduous forest of southwestern India
Odontophorus atrifrons: northeastern Colombia to far northwestern Venezuela
Odontophorus balliviani: Andes of southeastern Peru and northern Bolivia
Odontophorus capueira: eastern Brazil to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
Odontophorus columbianus: western Venezuela (southwestern Táchira) and coastal cordillera eastward to Miranda
Odontophorus dialeucos: far eastern Panama and adjacent northwestern Colombia (Chocó)
Odontophorus gujanensis: tropical rainforest from the Pacific lowlands of Costa Rica eastward to northern Colombia, from Córdoba, northern Chocó, and northern Antioquia to Caldas and Boyacá, and western Venezuela; east of the Andes in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from southern and eastern Venezuela and the Guianas, southward across most of Amazonian Brazil to southeastern Peru, northern and central Bolivia, but absent from savannas and llanos
Odontophorus guttatus: forest of southeastern Mexico to far western Panama
Odontophorus hyperythrus: western and central Andes of Colombia
Odontophorus leucolaemus: tropical and subtropical forest of Costa Rica and western Panama
Odontophorus melanonotus: montane forest of northwestern Ecuador and adjacent southwestern Colombia
Odontophorus melanotis: humid forest of lowlands to hills on Caribbean slope of northern Honduras to far eastern Panama
Odontophorus speciosus: far southern Colombia to central Bolivia
Odontophorus stellatus: tropical forest of western Amazon basin
Odontophorus strophium: temperate eastern Andes of Colombia (Santander and Cundinamarca)
Odontorchilus branickii: humid montane forest of Andes from central Colombia to northwestern Bolivia
Odontorchilus cinereus: lowlands of Amazonian Brazil south of the Amazon River, and eastern Bolivia
Oedistoma iliolophus: New Guinea (except Trans-Fly, south-central New Guinea)
Oedistoma pygmaeum: New Guinea including some satellite islands

Oenanthe bottae: highlands of southwestern Arabia (Mecca to Yemen)
Oenanthe chrysopygia: breeds from northeastern Türkiye, southern Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Iran eastward to southern Turkmenistan, southern Tajikistan (Pamir range), Afghanistan, and far northwestern Pakistan; winters from the southern Arabian Peninsula and southern Iraq eastward to Pakistan and northwestern India

Oenanthe frenata: foothill to montane grassy savanna, tussock-grass, and giant-heath moorland, in Ethiopia and Eritrea; some downslope dispersal post-breeding
Oenanthe fusca: rocky hills and cliffs of northeastern Pakistan and northern India
Oenanthe halophila: northern Sahara (eastern Morocco to northern Libya and northwestern Egypt)

Oenanthe hispanica: breeds southwestern Europe (Spain and Portugal eastward to Italy and northern Croatia) and northwestern Africa (eastward to northwestern Libya); winters in the western Sahel (eastward to Niger and northern Nigeria)
Oenanthe isabellina: foothill to montane arid grassland, rocky steppe, semi-desert, and desert margin, from eastern Ukraine, southern Bulgaria, and adjacent Greece eastward to Mongolia and northern China, and southward to Levant, Iran, and northern Pakistan; migrates to African Saheel, northeastern Africa, Arabian Peninsula, and western India

Oenanthe lugens: Egypt (east of the Nile) to Israel, Syria, Jordan, northern Iraq, and southern Iran
Oenanthe lugentoides: rocky desert and hillsides with sparse vegetation from southwestern Saudi Arabia southward to western Yemen and in Oman and adjacent eastern Yemen

Oenanthe melanoleuca: breeds southeastern Europe (eastward from southern Italy and Croatia), Türkiye, and the Levant eastward to southwestern Kazakhstan and western Iran; winters in the central and eastern Sahel, eastward to the southern Red Sea
