Oenanthe moesta: far northwestern Mauritania through Morocco and coastal northwestern Egypt, southern Syria to Jordan, northwestern Saudi Arabia, and southwestern Iraq
Oenanthe monacha: patchy in lowland to foothill barren rocky desert, wadis and ravines, and open stony or sandy steppe, from eastern Egypt and Levant eastward through Arabia to eastern Iran and southern Pakistan; some post-breeding dispersal
Oenanthe oenanthe: breeds northeastern Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Faroe Islands, and British Isles southward to Mediterranean and eastward to Siberia, Alaska, and northwestern Canada (Yukon), southern Spain and Balearic Islands to Iran, Kazakhstan, and Mongolia; winters to western and central Africa
Oenanthe phillipsi: lowland to foothill open stony ground, semi-desert, arid grassland, and burnt-over grassland, in southeastern Ethiopia and northern and central Somalia
Oenanthe picata: breeds eastern Iran eastward to western Tian Shan, Pamirs, northern and western Pakistan, and Kashmir; winters to southeastern Arabian Peninsula and southwestern Asia

Oenanthe pleschanka: breeds stony south-central Eurasia; winters to Arabian Peninsula, Iran, and northeastern Africa

Oenanthe xanthoprymna: breeds in southeastern Türkiye, far northeastern Iraq, and western Iran; winters in eastern Egypt (in the Nile Valley and near the Red Sea), northeastern Sudan, and on the western Arabian Peninsula, locally also in southern Israel
Ognorhynchus icterotis: Andes of Colombia and northern Ecuador
Oncostoma cinereigulare: lowlands of southern Mexico (Veracruz) to western Panama
Oncostoma olivaceum: tropical eastern Panama and northern Colombia (eastward to Santa Marta region)
Oneillornis lunulatus: locally in eastern Ecuador and eastern Peru (west of Río Napo and Río Ucayali)
Oneillornis salvini: eastern Peru to southwestern Amazonian Brazil and central Bolivia
Onychognathus albirostris: submontane to montane rocky steppe with cliffs and gorges and cliffs, and locally in towns, from southern Eritrea southward to central Ethiopia highland

Onychognathus frater: rocky hills of Socotra (off northeastern Somalia)
Onychognathus fulgidus: forest and edge of lowlands and hills from Sierra Leone eastward to western South Sudan and eastern Uganda, in south to northern Angola and east-central Democratic Republic of the Congo; Bioko and São Tomé (Gulf of Guinea)
Onychognathus morio: rocky areas in mountains and in urban areas, Eritrea southward through eastern Africa southward to southern Cape of South Africa
Onychognathus nabouroup: lowland to submontane semi-desert, arid savanna, Karoo, and dry open woodland with escarpments or rocky outcrops, from southwestern Angola southward to southwestern South Africa
Onychognathus neumanni: rocky outcrops of Sahel zone in hills and mountains of southern Mauritania eastward to western Sudan and southward to Central African Republic

Onychognathus tristramii: Dead Sea Valley and western Arabia to Yemen and southern Oman
Onychognathus walleri: montane forest and forest patches of highlands of eastern Nigeria and western Cameroon, Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), Albertine Rift from western Uganda through northern Burundi, highlands of southern South Sudan, Uganda, Kenya, northeastern Tanzania, and Eastern Arc mountains from central to southwestern Tanzania, through northern Malawi

Onychoprion anaethetus: widespread tropical and subtropical islands, mostly near continents but also remote islands of eastern Polynesia and Hawaiian Islands
Onychoprion fuscatus: widespread in all tropical and subtropical oceans
Onychoprion lunatus: breeds islets of tropical Pacific from Marianas and Samoa eastward to main Hawaiian Islands; ranges to northeastern Melanesia and far eastern Polynesia
Onychorhynchus coronatus: humid, semi-humid and dry forest, gallery forest from southeastern Mexico (including Yucatan Peninsula), and Pacific slope from western Costa Rica, southward to eastern Panama, northern Colombia and western Venezuela, southward in interior Colombia to the middle Cauca and Magdalena valleys, and from northwestern Ecuador southward to northwestern Peru; east of the Andes from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward across the Amazon basin to south-central Brazil and northern Bolivia
Onychorhynchus swainsoni: southeastern Brazil (Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, and Paraná)
Onychostruthus taczanowskii: Tibet to western China (Kokonor and Nan Shan Mountains to Sichuan)
Ophrysia superciliosa: formerly west-central Himalayas; probably extinct, last reported 1876
Opisthocomus hoazin: Amazon and Orinoco basin lowlands and the Guianas
Opisthoprora euryptera: central Andes of Colombia to northern Peru (Amazonas to La Libertad)
Oporornis agilis: breeds locally from northeastern British Columbia and southwestern Northwest Territories, eastward to west-central Quebec and south to the northern Great Lakes region of the United States; wintering range poorly known but evidently mainly southern edge of Amazon Basin
Orchesticus abeillei: foothills of southeastern Brazil (southern Bahia and Minas Gerais to Paraná)

Petroica boodang: southwestern and southeastern Australia including Tasmania
Petroica goodenovii: Australia (except far north, wetter southern and eastern fringes, and Tasmania)

Petroica macrocephala: North, South, Stewart, Chatham, Snares, and Auckland islands (New Zealand)

Phaethornis yaruqui: tropical Pacific Colombia and western Ecuador

Platysteira blissetti: patchy in lowland and foothill dense understory of primary and secondary forest, coastal thickets, and plantations, from southern Guinea and Sierra Leone eastward to western Cameroon
Platysteira chalybea: disjunctly in lowland and foothill dense undergrowth of primary and secondary forest, regenerated flooded forest, and plantations, from Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) eastward to southwestern Central African Republic, and southward to Gabon and northwestern Republic of Congo, and in northwestern Angola
Platysteira concreta: lowland to montane forest understory from Sierra Leone and southeastern Guinea eastward to western Kenya, and southward to western Angola and far western Tanzania
Platysteira cyanea: lowland to montane open woodland, secondary forest, farmbush, gardens, and mangroves, from Senegambia eastward through southern Chad and South Sudan to western Ethiopia, and southward to northwestern Angola, northern Tanzania, and western Kenya
Platysteira jamesoni: patchy in foothill to submontane dense understory of primary and secondary forest, and patches of degraded forest, from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward through Uganda to southern South Sudan and western Kenya, and southward to far northern Tanzania and Burundi
Platysteira laticincta: foothill to submontane forest, forest edge, and bamboo thicket in Bamenda Highlands of western Cameroon
Platysteira peltata: lowland to montane forest, gallery forest, gardens, and mangroves, from southwestern and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, western Kenya, and southern Somalia, thence southward through Tanzania, including Mafia Island, and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, to western Angola and southeastern South Africa
Plectorhyncha lanceolata: eastern Australia (northeastern Queensland to northwestern Victoria and eastern Mount Lofty Ranges, southeastern South Australia)
Plectrophenax hyperboreus: breeds Bering Sea islands; winters to coastal Alaska and Aleutians
Plectrophenax nivalis: breeds Holarctic, from Greenland and Arctic islands and coasts eastward to Chukchi Peninsula and Kamchatka, and Aleutians, Alaska, and northern Canada to Ellesmere Island; winters to central Eurasia and central North America
Plegadis chihi: Great Basin of western USA to southwestern Brazil and central Argentina
Plegadis falcinellus: locally in eastern North and southern South America, Africa, Eurasia, and southern Asia to Australasia
Plegadis ridgwayi: high Andes of central Peru to northwestern Argentina and northern Chile
Plocealauda affinis: eastern and southern India and Sri Lanka
Plocealauda assamica: northern India to southern Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, and far western Myanmar
Plocealauda erythrocephala: southern Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, and southern Vietnam
Plocepasser donaldsoni: foothill thornscrub, acacia savanna, and rocky or lava grassland, in southern Ethiopia, northern Kenya, and locally in southern Somalia
Plocepasser mahali: widespread in lowland and foothill acacia and mopane savanna from southern South Sudan, Ethiopia, and western and southern Somali southward to central Tanzania, and from southwestern Angola, northeastern Zambia, and northern Mozambique southward to southern Namibia and northern and central South Africa
Plocepasser rufoscapulatus: lowland to foothill miombo woodland from southwestern and central Angola eastward through southern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia to northern Malawi, and locally in western Tanzania
Plocepasser superciliosus: lowland to foothill open dry woodland, and brushy savanna, from Senegambia eastward through Sahel to Eritrea and Ethiopia, and southward to Central African Republic, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and western Kenya
Ploceus albinucha: patchily distributed in lowland and foothill evergreen forest and farmbush from southern Sierra Leone to southwestern Ghana, and from southern Nigeria, Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to northwestern Republic of Congo and southwestern Central African Republic, and from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to western Uganda
Ploceus alienus: submontane to montane evergreen forest understory, secondary growth, and bamboo, from eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to southwestern Uganda, Rwanda, and Burundi
Ploceus angolensis: disjunctly in lowland to foothill miombo woodland in west-central Angola, and in central and northern Zambia and adjacent Democratic Republic of the Congo
Ploceus aurantius: lowland and foothill riverine corridors, mangroves, coastal lagoons, and papyrus swamps from Sierra Leone eastward to western Central African Republic, and southward through Gabon to northwestern Angola, and from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to Lake Victoria in southern Uganda, western Kenya, and northwestern Tanzania
Ploceus aureonucha: local in lowland forest and secondary forest with tall emergent trees in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and adjacent western Uganda
Ploceus badius: lowland tall grassland and riverine brush with tall trees on the Nile River floodplain in central and southeastern Sudan and South Sudan; nomadic wandering post-breeding
Ploceus baglafecht: patchy in lowland to montane shrubby or lightly wooded areas, marsh, forest edge, and gardens, from eastern Nigeria and Cameroon eastward to Eritrea and Ethiopia, and southward through eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and central Kenya to southwestern Tanzania, northeastern Zambia, and northern Malawi
Ploceus bannermani: foothill to montane forest edge, degraded forest, and open scrub, in southeastern Nigeria and southwestern Cameroon
Ploceus batesi: local and declining in lowland forest of southwestern and southern Cameroon
Ploceus benghalensis: lowlands of Pakistan to Peninsular India, Nepal, and Bangladesh
Ploceus bertrandi: foothill and submontane open woodland, riparian thickets, miombo woodland, and forest edge from northeastern Zambia and east-central Tanzania southward to Malawi and adjacent northwestern Mozambique
Ploceus bicolor: patchy in lowland to montane forest, riverine and gallery forest, and dry subtropical thicket from southeastern Nigeria, southeastern Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) eastward, avoiding Congolian rainforest, to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, southern Somalia, and coastal Kenya, southward to northwestern Angola, Zambia, and Mozambique, thence southward to coastal southeastern South Africa
Ploceus bojeri: lowland to foothill coastal palm savanna, and riverine vegetation, in southern Somalia and central and eastern Kenya, and historically southeastern Ethiopia
Ploceus brachypterus: lowland to foothill savanna woodland, gallery forest, coastal thickets, palm plantations, and mangroves from Senegambia eastward to southwestern Niger, Nigeria, southwestern Cameron, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea)
Ploceus burnieri: lowland reedbeds in seasonally flooded grassland of Kilombero River floodplain (south-central Tanzania)
Ploceus capensis: lowland to submontane savanna, grassland, Fynbos, coastal thickets, farmbush, gardens, and urban parks, in South Africa, Lesotho, and western Eswatini; occasional dispersal to adjacent southern Namibia
Ploceus castaneiceps: lowland to foothill swampy grassland, reeds, and brush in southeastern Kenya and northeastern Tanzania
Ploceus castaneofuscus: patchy in lowland to foothill forest edge and clearing, tall grass savanna, swampy woodland, and villages, from Guinea eastward to central Nigeria, historically also Gambia
Ploceus castanops: lowland to submontane lakeside and riverine vegetation, and papyrus swamps, from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to Uganda and southwestern Kenya, and southward to Rwanda, Burundi, and northwestern Tanzania
Ploceus cucullatus: widespread in sub-Saharan Africa (except southwestern), in lowland and foothill brushy savanna, riverine woodland, cultivated areas, and villages, from southern Mauritania eastward to Somalia, southward to Angola, northern Botswana, and Mozambique, then southward to eastern South Africa; introduced to São Tomé, Mauritius, Réunion, northern Venezuela, Hispaniola, and Martinique
Ploceus dichrocephalus: patchy in lowland to foothill savanna, riverine bush, acacia thornscrub, and semi-desert in southern Ethiopia, far northeastern Kenya, and southwestern Somalia
Ploceus dorsomaculatus: disjunctly in submontane to montane forest and secondary forest in southern Cameroon and northern Gabon eastward to southwestern Central African Republic and northwestern Republic of Congo, and in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Ploceus flavipes: local in lowland forest canopy in Ituri Forest (northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo)
Ploceus galbula: lowland to submontane savanna, arid coastal plain, cultivation, and gardens, from eastern Sudan and Eritrea eastward to southwestern and southern Arabian Peninsula, and southward to southern Ethiopia and northern Somalia; introduced to western Red Sea coast and central Saudi Arabia
Ploceus golandi: local in lowland miombo woodland and coastal forest in southeastern Kenya
Ploceus heuglini: patchy in lowland to foothill wooded dry savanna, coastal thickets, secondary scrub, farmbush, and villages, from Senegambia eastward to southern Chad and Central African Republic, and disjunctly from southern South Sudan and northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to western Kenya; some seasonal dispersal
Ploceus holoxanthus: local in lowland reedbeds, riverine vegetation, and bamboo in eastern Tanzania (the lower Wami River, the Ruvu River, Lake Tagalala, and the Rufiji River)
Ploceus hypoxanthus: marshes, flooded grasslands, and rice paddies from southern Myanmar southwards to central Thailand, thence southwards to southern Vietnam, and disjunctly Sumatra and western Java; introduced Singapore and Bali (at least formerly)
Ploceus insignis: disjunctly in foothill to montane primary and secondary forest, bamboo, gallery forest, and coffee plantations, in southeastern Nigeria, southwestern Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea, and from southeastern South Sudan southward to eastern Uganda, western Kenya, and northeastern Tanzania, and from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to adjacent Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, and western Tanzania, and in west-central Angola; also recorded in northeastern Gabon and southwestern Republic of the Congo
Ploceus intermedius: lowland and foothill wooded savanna, cultivated areas near water, and villages, from southeastern South Sudan, Ethiopia, Djibouti, and Somalia southward to Rwanda, southern Tanzania, and Zambia, and from southern Republic of Congo, Angola, and northern Namibia eastward to Zimbabwe and Mozambique, thence southward to eastern South Africa
Ploceus jacksoni: lowland to foothill reedy or papyrus swamps, riparian thickets, thornscrub, and grassy wetland, from southern South Sudan, Uganda, and western and southern Kenya southward to Burundi and south-central Tanzania; introduced in Kuwait southward to Oman
Ploceus katangae: patchy in lowland wetlands with reedbeds and papyrus from southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to northwestern Zambia
Ploceus luteolus: lowland to foothill acacia savanna, cultivation fringe, and gardens, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to Sudan, Eritrea, and Ethiopia, and southward to northern Cameroon, northern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, and northeastern Tanzania
Ploceus manyar: lowland wetlands, reedbeds, rice paddies, and bulrushes associated with elephant grass, from eastern Pakistan and Indian subcontinent eastward to southeastern Asia, and southward to Sri Lanka and, disjunctly, Java, Bali, and satellite islands; introduced in Nile Valley (Egypt), central and eastern Arabian Peninsula, southeastern Borneo, and north-central and southern Sulawesi
Ploceus megarhynchus: disjunctly in lowland to foothill lightly wooded grassland, seasonally flooded plain, and cultivation, in norhern India (southern Uttarakhand and northern Uttar Pradesh) and adjacent far southwestern Nepal, and northeastern India (West Bengal and Assam; old records from salt lakes in southern West Bengal)
Ploceus melanocephalus: lowland and foothill grassland near rivers, reedbeds, and papyrus, from southern Mauritania eastward across the Sahel to Eritrea and western Ethiopia, southward to eastern Republic of Congo, northern Zambia, and northwestern Tanzania
Ploceus melanogaster: disjunctly in foothill and montane forest of southeastern Nigeria, southwestern Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), and from southern South Sudan, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Burundi, eastward to Uganda and west-central Kenya
Ploceus nelicourvi: lowland to foothill rainforest, secondary forest, and coastal littoral forest in northern and eastern Madagascar
Ploceus nicolli: montane cloudforest in the Usambara, Uluguru (rare or extirpated?), and Udzungwa Mountains, Tanzania
Ploceus nigerrimus: lowland to submontane forest edge and clearings, tall grass savanna, secondary woodland, and villages, from southeastern Nigeria eastward to southeastern South Sudan, Uganda, and western Kenya, and southward to northern Angola, south-central Democratic Republic of the Congo, and western Tanzania
Ploceus nigricollis: lowland to montane wooded savanna, gallery forest, farmbush, and plantations, from Cameroon eastward to southwestern Ethiopia, Kenya, and southern Somalia, southward to northwestern Angola and southern Tanzania
Ploceus nigrimentus: disjunctly in foothill open bushy savanna from southeastern Gabon, south-central Republic of the Congo, and adjacent southwestern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and in northeastern and west-central Angola
Ploceus ocularis: patchy in lowland to montane woodland, bushy savanna, and gardens, from southwestern Nigeria and Cameroon eastward (avoiding Congolian rainforest) to southeastern Ethiopia and Kenya, and southward to southern Angola, northeastern Namibia, and northern Botswana, and through southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia to southern Mozambique, Eswatini, and south-eastern South Africa
Ploceus olivaceiceps: patchy in lowland to submontane open miombo woodland from southwestern Tanzania southward to northern Mozambique, Malawi, and adjacent southeastern Zambia, and disjunctly in southern Mozambique
Ploceus pelzelni: patchy in lowland to montane marshland, papyrus swamps, and mangroves, from Sierra Leone to southern Cameroon, southward to northwestern Angola, and from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, southward to Burundi and northwestern Tanzania, and in southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and adjacent Zambia
Ploceus philippinus: lowland to foothill grassland, marsh, lightly wooded scrub, mangroves, and cultivation, from eastern Pakistan and Indian subcontinent, and Sri Lanka, eastward to south-central China and southeastern Asia, and southward to Sumatra and satellite islands, Java, and Bali; introduced to eastern Arabian Peninsula, Sabah (northern Borneo), locally in Sulawesi, and eastern Nusa Tenggara
Ploceus preussi: disjunctly in lowland to foothill primary and secondary forest from southern Guinea eastward patchily eastward to eastern Nigeria, and from southern Cameroon and southwestern Central African Republic southward to northern Gabon, Republic of the Congo, and southwestern, and disjunctly, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Ploceus reichardi: local and patchy in lowland to foothill papyrus swamp and lakeshore reedbeds in western Tanzania and far northeastern Zambia
Ploceus rubiginosus: disjunct populations in lowland and foothill thornscrub from Eritrea, Ethiopia, and Somalia to northeastern Uganda to northern and central Tanzania, and southwestern Angola to central Namibia; some migratory or nomadic
Ploceus ruweti: local in foothill riverine acacia and flooded savanna at Lake Tshangalele and Kiubo Falls on Lufira River (southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo)
Ploceus sakalava: dry lowland forest and subdesert in northern, western, and southern Madagascar
Ploceus sanctithomae: highlands of São Tomé (Gulf of Guinea)
Ploceus spekei: foothill to montane savanna, open woodland, brushy scrub, and urban gardens, from Ethiopia and Somalia southward to southwestern Kenya and northeastern Tanzania
Ploceus spekeoides: foothill wooded and swampy and papyrus swamp in east-central Uganda; some seasonal dispersal
Ploceus subaureus: lowland and foothill coastal plain, riverine marsh, and floodplain from eastern Kenya southward through Malawi and Mozambique to Eswatini and coastal southeastern South Africa
Ploceus subpersonatus: lowland coastal swamp-forest, palm savanna, beach scrub, and mangroves from Gabon southward to Cabinda (northwestern Angola) and adjacent Democratic Republic of the Congo
Ploceus taeniopterus: patchy in lowland and foothill tall grassland, acacia savanna, papyrus swamps, and shoreline vegetation on large rivers and lakes, from southern Sudan and north-central Ethiopia southward to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and west-central Kenya
Ploceus temporalis: patchy and local in lowland to foothill rank grassland and riverine vegetation from central and northeastern Angola eastward to southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northwestern Zambia
Ploceus tricolor: patchy in lowland and foothill forest and swamp from Sierra Leone eastward to far southwestern South Sudan, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to southern Uganda, and southward to northwestern Angola
Ploceus velatus: southern Angola eastward to Mozambique, southward to southern South Africa; introduced São Tomé (Gulf of Guinea)
Ploceus vitellinus: lowland and foothill dry savanna and arid scrub from southern Mauritania eastward through the Sahel to central Sudan, Ethiopia, and Somalia, southward to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and northern and central Tanzania
Ploceus weynsi: lowland to foothill forest edge, lakeshore woodland; and secondary growth, from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and southern Uganda southward to northwestern Tanzania; in erratic wandering has reached western Kenya and northern Republic of the Congo
Ploceus xanthops: lowland to montane tall grass, brushy grassland, forest margins, and riverine vegetation, from southern Gabon eastward through southern and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to Uganda and southwestern Kenya, and southward to far northern Namibia, northern Botswana, and eastern South Africa
Ploceus xanthopterus: lowland and foothill wetlands with reedbeds or papyrus from southern Tanzania to Malawi, and from southeastern Angola, northeastern Namibia, and northern Botswana eastward to Mozambique, thence southward to coastal eastern South Africa
Pluvialis apricaria: breeds inland low Arctic (mainly) to temperate zone from Greenland eastward to Taymyr Peninsula (north-central Russia); winters to inland and coastal southern Europe, northern Africa, and Middle East
Pluvialis dominica: breeds high Arctic to subarctic from northern Alaska eastward to northeastern Canada, and southward to north-central British Colombia; winters coastal southeastern Brazil and Argentina, and inland grassland, Paraguay to east-central Argentina
Pluvialis fulva: breeds Arctic and subarctic Russia from Yamal Peninsula eastward to Chukotskiy Peninsula and northern Kamchatka and Bering Sea coasts of western Alaska; winters to coastal Horn of Africa and Indian subcontinent eastward through southern Japan (Ryukyu and Ogasawara islands), Taiwan, and Indonesian Archipelago throughout Australasia and Micronesia to eastern Polynesia; widely vagrant elsewhere
Pluvialis squatarola: breeds high (locally low) Arctic coasts and islands (except Ellesmere Island, Greenland, Scandinavia and islands from Svalbard to Severnaya Zemlya); winters almost worldwide on temperate to tropical coasts (except most remote islands)
Pluvianellus socialis: breeds lagoons and ponds of inland western Santa Cruz Province (southwestern Argentina), southeastern Magallanes Province (far southeastern Chile), and northern and central Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego; non-breeders reach coastal east-central and southeastern Argentina northward to southeastern Buenos Aires Province
Pluvianus aegyptius: Senegal and Gambia eastward to Ethiopia, southward to far northern Angola, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Sudan; formerly also Nile River, Egypt
Pnoepyga albiventer: Himalayas, from northwest India eastward through Nepal and Bhutan to northeastern India and northern Myanmar, southward to the Chin Hills (western Myanmar), and eastward through southern China to northern Vietnam (western Tonkin); also central China, in Sichuan (northern Pingwu County, Guanxian, central Emei Shan, and Wa Shan) and western Yunnan (northwestern Gongshan and the western part of the Longchuan River)
Pnoepyga immaculata: Himalayas of Nepal; winters to terai lowlands
Pnoepyga pusilla: foothill to montane thick forest understory, mossy ravines, and dense fern growth, from Nepal and adjacent northern India eastward through Himalayas to southeastern China (including Hainan), and southward through Indochina to Sumatra, Java, Flores, and Timor
Podargus ocellatus: New Guinea and satellite islands, and eastern and northeastern Australia
Podargus papuensis: New Guinea, including Raja Ampat and Aru Islands, and Australia from northeastern Queensland southward to the Wet Tropics region
Podica senegalensis: lowland to submontane silt-free, well-vegetated rivers and lakes in forest and woodland, and mangroves, from Senegambia eastward to western Ethiopia and southeastern Kenya, and southward to southern Angola, northeastern Namibia, and southern South Africa
Podiceps andinus: formerly montane wetlands of Bogotá area (eastern Andes, central Colombia); extinct, last reported 1977
Podiceps auritus: breeds Iceland, northern British Isles, and Scandinavia to eastern Russia; southern and central Alaska through western and central Canada, and northern tier of contiguous western and central USA states; winters to coasts of North Sea, northern Mediterranean, and western Asian seas; Korean Peninsula, and Japan (Hokkaido to southern Honshu); Aleutians to northern Baja California (northwestern Mexico); western North Atlantic and Gulf of Mexico coasts to central Florida
Podiceps cristatus: breeds temperate Eurasia, locally northwestern India, to northeastern Russia, northeastern China, and north-central Japan (Hokkaido to central Honshu); northeastern, eastern, and southern Africa; Australia and South Island (New Zealand); winter withdrawal from northern latitudes
Podiceps gallardoi: breeds submontane lakes of western Santa Cruz Province, southwestern Argentina; winters to Río Santa Cruz estuary and adjacent coast, southeastern Argentina
Podiceps grisegena: central and eastern Europe and Türkiye to temperate west-central Russia and Kazakhstan; subarctic central and eastern Siberia to Kamchatka and northern Japan (Hokkaido), Alaska, and Canada to southwestern Quebec; winters mostly coasts to mid-temperate latitudes
Podiceps major: coastal western Peru; Paraguay and southeastern Brazil to southern Chile and Argentina
Podiceps nigricollis: breeds temperate Eurasia to Russian Far East and northeastern China; eastern and southern Africa; southwestern Canada and western and west-central USA to central Mexico; winters to coasts of northern Africa, Arabian Peninsula, Black and Caspian seas, northwestern Indian subcontinent, southeastern China, Korean Peninsula, and Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu); southern Mexico and east-central USA
Podiceps occipitalis: montane lakes of central Andes of Colombia to northern Chile and northwestern Argentina; central and southern Chile and Argentina to Tierra del Fuego; Falkland Islands
Podilymbus gigas: formerly Lake Atitlan, southwestern Guatemala; extinct, last reported 1986
Podilymbus podiceps: breeds northwestern Canada through USA, Caribbean, Mexico, Central and South America to central Chile and northern and west-central Argentina; winters to western and south-central USA
Podoces hendersoni: desert of central Asia (Kazakhstan to Outer and Inner Mongolia)
Podoces panderi: northern and central Uzbekistan, southern Kazakhstan, and northern and central Turkmenistan; also isolated population in eastern Kazakhstan (south of Lake Balkhash)
Podoces pleskei: desert steppes of central and eastern Iran
Poecile atricapillus: deciduous and mixed forest and woodland, including gardens and towns, from northwestern Alaska (but not the north slope) eastward to Newfoundland (eastern Canada), southward to far northern California, central New Mexico, southern Kansas, and New Jersey, and in Appalachians to far western North Carolina and adjacent Tennessee; some short-range wandering in winter
Poecile carolinensis: swamps, pine, and hardwood forest, riparian woodland, and scrub from southern Kansas eastward to northern Ohio, northern Indiana, southern Pennsylvania, and northern New Jersey (east-central USA) southward to south-central Texas, Gulf coast, and northern Florida (southeastern USA)
Poecile cinctus: lowland to submontane open old-growth coniferous forest, and riverine forest with birch and willow thickets, from northern Scandinavia eastward to eastern Siberia, and southward to northern Mongolia and Kamchatka; former North American population (northern Alaska, northwestern Canada) unrecorded since 2018 and may be extinct
Poecile davidi: mountains of western China (Hubei to Shaanxi, Gansu, and Sichuan)
Poecile gambeli: montane coniferous forest and mixed forest from southern Yukon and southwestern Alberta (western Canada) southward to far northern Baja California (northwestern Mexico) and eastward to western Montana and eastern New Mexico, with an isolated population in western Texas; some winter wandering to adjacent lowland states
Poecile hudsonicus: boreal coniferous forest from northwestern Alaska (except north slope) eastward across northern Canada (south of the Arctic islands) to northern Labrador, southward to southern Canada, northeastern Washington, and northwestern Idaho,and local and declining in northeastern tier of US states from northern Minnesota eastward to northern New Hampshire and Maine
Poecile hypermelaenus: central and eastern China to southeastern Tibet and western Myanmar
Poecile hyrcanus: northern Iran (Elburz Mountains) and adjacent Azerbaijan
Poecile lugubris: dry Mediterranean scrub, bushes and open woodland, orchards, and hedgerows from northwestern Slovenia, northern Serbia, and northern Romania southward to southern Greece (including Crete), and eastward across Türkiye to southernmost Georgia, southern Armenia, adjacent Azerbaijan, northwestern Iran, adjacent Iraq, and southward to south-central Iran
Poecile montanus: lowland to montane coniferous forest, and broadleaf and mixed woodland, from British Isles and Scandinavia eastward to eastern Siberia and Kamchatka (Russia), and southward to France, Greece, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, northeastern China, and Japan
Poecile palustris: disjunctly in lowland to montane mature deciduous woodland, in Europe from British Isles and Scandinavia eastward to southern Ural Mountains (Russia), and southward to northern Spain, Greece, and Caucasus, in eastern Asia from southern Siberia and Mongolia eastward to Sakhalin and northern Japan (Hokkaido), and southward to Korean Peninsula and northeastern China
Poecile rufescens: dense coniferous forest and deciduous woodland from southeastern Alaska southward along the Pacific coast to southern California, and the northern Rocky Mountains from east-central British Columbia (northwestern Canada) southward to northern Idaho and western Montana
Poecile sclateri: coniferous forest of mountains of southeastern Arizona and New Mexico though south-central Oaxaca
Poecile superciliosus: mountains of western China (Qinghai to southeastern Tibet, Gansu, and Sichuan)
Poecile weigoldicus: southwestern China (Sichuan to eastern Tibet, southeastern Qinghai, and northwestern Yunnan)
Poecilodryas cerviniventris: northwestern Australia (Kimberley region, northern Western Australia, eastward to northwestern Queensland)
Poecilodryas hypoleuca: New Guinea, including Raja Ampat Islands (off western New Guinea)
Poecilodryas superciliosa: northeastern Australia (Cape York Peninsula to Wet Tropics region; Bowen southward to Sarina, northern Queensland)
Poecilostreptus cabanisi: cloudforest of southern Mexico (Chiapas) and adjacent Guatemala
Poecilostreptus palmeri: humid foothills of eastern Panama to northwestern Ecuador (Pichincha)
Poecilotriccus albifacies: southeastern Peru (Madre de Dios and Cusco), western Brazil (Acre), and northern Bolivia (Pando)
Poecilotriccus calopterus: southeastern Colombia (Putumayo) to eastern Ecuador and northeastern Peru (Loreto)
Poecilotriccus capitalis: southeastern Colombia to eastern Ecuador, northeastern Peru, and southwestern Brazil (Rondônia)
Poecilotriccus fumifrons: dense humid to semi-humid scrub, bushes, and thickets in Suriname and French Guiana southward across the easternmost Amazon basin in Brazil to northern Mato Grosso, and in the Cerrado of Brazil from northern Maranhão, Piauí, and Ceará southward to southern Tocantins, and in far southern Venezuela; also in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil from Rio Grande do Norte southward to southern Bahia
Poecilotriccus latirostris: dense thickets in shrub in forest edges, riparian, and gallery forest in the Amazon basin from southeastern Colombia southeastward to northern and eastern Bolivia, far northern Paraguay, and in Brazil mainly south of the Amazon River eastward to the Rio Tapajós in central Pará, western and southern Tocantins, Goiás, western Minas Gerais, and southeastward to western São Paulo, Mato Grosso do Sul, and adjacent Paraná
Poecilotriccus luluae: northern Peru (Cordillera de Colán) and adjacent eastern Andes
Poecilotriccus plumbeiceps: humid forest borders and scrub, bamboo stands, and bracken thickets in the Andes of southeastern Peru southward across Bolivia to northwestern Argentina, to Salta and Tucuman, in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil from Pernambuco southward to Rio Grande do Sul and adjacent Uruguay, and inland to western Paraná, northeastern Argentina, and western Paraguay
Poecilotriccus pulchellus: humid foothills of southeastern Peru (Cusco and Puno)
Poecilotriccus ruficeps: montane cloudforest and scrub dominated by bamboo in the Sierra de Perijá and the Andes from western Venezuela southward along the Andes of Colombia to northern Peru north of the Río Marañón, in Piura and Cajamarca
Poecilotriccus russatus: tepuis of southeastern Venezuela and northern Brazil (Cerro Uei-tepui in Roraima)
Poecilotriccus senex: central Amazonian Brazil (Madeira drainage in Amazonas and Rondônia)
Poecilotriccus sylvia: Gulf slope of southern Mexico (Veracruz) southward to Panama (Canal Zone), tropical northern Colombia (Cauca and Magdalena valleys) to northwestern Venezuela (eastward to northern Bolívar), and the Guianas and northern Brazil (Rio Branco to northern Piauí)
Poeoptera kenricki: montane forest and forest patches of central Kenya, northeastern Tanzania, and Eastern Arc mountains from central to southwestern Tanzania
Poeoptera lugubris: patchy in lowland and foothill primary forest, remnant forest patches, plantations and abandoned cultivation, from Sierra Leone eastward through southern Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), to western Uganda, and southward to northwestern Angola and south-central Democratic Republic of the Congo
Poeoptera stuhlmanni: patchy in lowland and foothill primary forest, remnant forest patches, plantations and abandoned cultivation, from Sierra Leone eastward through southern Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), to western Uganda, and southward to northwestern Angola and south-central Democratic Republic of the Congo

Pterocles alchata: disjunctly on treeless plains, semi-desert, open steppe, and dry cultivation, in Iberia southward to northwestern Africa (Morocco to northern Libya), and from southeastern Türkiye and Middle East eastward to western Iran, and from southern Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan southward to western Pakistan; northern populations in central Asia migratory and nomadic, southward to central Arabian Peninsula, northeastern Iran, southern Pakistan, and northwestern India

Pterocles burchelli: southeastern Angola to Namibia, Botswana, and northern Cape Province
Pterocles coronatus: desert to semi-desert and rocky areas across the Sahara from southern Morocco and Western Sahara eastward to northeastern Libya and northern Sudan, in eastern Egypt, the Sinai Peninsula, southern Jordan, and Israel, patchily across the Arabian Peninsula southward to Yemen and Oman; and in eastern Iran, southern Afghanistan, and southwestern Pakistan
Pterocles decoratus: lowland and foothill dry savanna, bushveld, thornscrub, and semi-desert scrub, from southern Ethiopia and western Somalia southward through eastern Kenya to central Tanzania
Pterocles exustus: disjunct populations in Africa and Asia, in lowland and foothill bare semi-desert, grassland, and open thornscrub, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to central Egypt and Somalia, and southward to northern Tanzania, and in southern Arabian Peninsula, and from southeastern Iran to India; nomadic seasonal wandering; introduced to Hawaiian Islands (Hawaii)
Pterocles gutturalis: patchy in foothill to submontane short grassland, grassy plains near swamps, and recently burned areas, of central Ethiopia, and from south-central Kenya southward to northeastern Zambia, and from western Zambia and northeastern Namibia southward to north-central South Africa
Pterocles indicus: arid rocky lowlands of eastern Pakistan and Peninsular India

Pterocles orientalis: steppe and semi-desert plains from the Iberian Peninsula, eastern Canary Islands, and northwestern Africa, eastward across Cyprus, Türkiye, the Middle East, the Caucasus, and Iran to eastern India, southern Kazakhstan, and far western China
Pterocles quadricinctus: savanna and thornscrub of sub-Saharan Africa
Pterocles senegallus: desert of sub-Saharan Africa and Arabian Peninsula to western India

Pterodroma atrata: breeds Henderson Island and Moto Nui (southeastern Pacific); wintering range unknown
Pterodroma axillaris: breeds Rangatira Island (Chatham Islands); non-breeders range to Nazca Ridge west of Peru and Chile; rare
Pterodroma baraui: breeds montane Réunion; ranges tropical Indian Ocean mostly south of the Equator, off Madagascar, and to Arabian Sea and northwestern Australian waters
Pterodroma brevipes: Fiji, Banks Islands (northern Vanuatu), and Cook Islands
Pterodroma cahow: breeds Nonsuch Island (Bermuda); disperses to Gulf Stream
Pterodroma caribbaea: formerly bred montane eastern Jamaica; probably extinct ca. 1936
Pterodroma cervicalis: breeds mostly Macauley Island of Kermadec Islands (northeast of New Zealand), Phillip Island of Norfolk group (east of Australia), and presumed to breed on Banks Islands (northern Vanuatu); ranges to southeastern Australia, southeastern Japan, and eastwards to east-central Pacific

Pterodroma pycrofti: breeds small islands off northern North Island (New Zealand), and formerly Norfolk Island (east of Australia); ranges to North Pacific
Pterodroma rupinarum: formerly bred on St. Helena Island; extinct
Pterodroma sandwichensis: breeds montane Hawaiian Islands, on Kauai, Molokai (formerly), Lana'i, Maui and Hawaii; ranges to Gulf of Alaska and offshore waters from Oregon to California
Pterodroma solandri: breeds mostly Lord Howe Island and (few) Philip Island of Norfolk group (east of Australia); ranges to eastern Australia and northwestern Pacific off Kamchatka and Japan, eastward to Bering Sea
Pterodroma ultima: breeds eastern Polynesian islands of Tuamotu, Gambier, Austral, Pitcairn, Easter, and Salas y Gomez; ranges to south of Aleutians, Gulf of Alaska, and northeastern Pacific coast
Pteroglossus aracari: varied forest and edge types of lowlands and hills of eastern Amazonia and the Guianas from northeastern Venezuela eastward to Piauí and southward to northern Mato Grosso; also eastern Brazil from Alagoas southward to Paraná
Pteroglossus azara: western and central Amazonia, from eastern Ecuador through southern Venezuela to Roraima (northwestern Brazil), and southward through central Bolivia and eastern Amazonas
Pteroglossus bailloni: humid forest of southeastern Brazil to northeastern Argentina and eastern Paraguay
Pteroglossus beauharnaisii: eastern Peru to northern Bolivia and western Amazonian Brazil south of the Amazon
Pteroglossus bitorquatus: northeast Brazil, south of the Amazon River and east of the Rio Madeira to the mouth of the Amazon River, south as far as northeastern Bolivia

Pteroglossus erythropygius: humid to semi-humid forest from far eastern Panama and northwestern Colombia southward along the Pacific slope and lowlands across Ecuador to far northwestern Peru (Tumbes)
Pteroglossus frantzii: Pacific slope of Costa Rica and western Panama (western Chiriquí)
Pteroglossus inscriptus: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin from eastern Colombia southward to eastern Peru and northern and central Bolivia, and eastward across the Brazilian Amazon (to Maranhão and Piauí, but not north of the Amazon River from the Rio Negro eastward); also in the Atlantic Forest of northeastern Brazil (Alagoas and Pernambuco)
Pteroglossus pluricinctus: northeastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, northeastern Peru, and northwestern Amazonian Brazil
Pteroglossus torquatus: humid and semi-humid forest on the Gulf of Mexico slope from Veracruz eastward to the northern lowlands of Panama, including most Yucatan Peninsula, and on the Pacific slope from Oaxaca eastward to eastern Costa Rica; in South America in the lowlands of northern Colombia and northwestern Venezuela
Pteroglossus viridis: eastern Venezuela to the Guianas and northern Brazil
Pteronetta hartlaubii: local in forest streams of equatorial western and central Africa
Pterophanes cyanopterus: elfin forest and shrubby paramo in the eastern and central Andes of Colombia southward across Ecuador to northern Peru, and south of the Río Marañón in the eastern Andes of Peru southward to central Bolivia (Cochabamba)
Pteroptochos castaneus: central Chile (Colchagua to Río Biobío) and adjacent northwestern Neuquén (west-central Argentina)
Pteroptochos megapodius: slopes with scattered bushes and scrub, semiarid rocky outcrops, and boulders from north-central to south-central Chile (Atacama to Bío Bío)

Pterorhinus berthemyi: mountains of southeastern China (northwestern Yunnan, Gansu, and southern Sichuan eastward to Anhui, Zhejiang and northwestern Fujian)

Pterorhinus gularis: eastern Bhutan to northeastern India, northern Myanmar, and northern Laos
Pterorhinus koslowi: montane scrub in juniper forest, and scrub bordering agricultural land, in eastern Tibet

Pterorhinus ruficollis: mixed forest of eastern Nepal to southwestern China, northeastern India, and Myanmar

Pterorhinus woodi: southeastern Assam (Mizo Hills) to western Myanmar (Chin Hills)

Pteruthius intermedius: patchy in foothill to montane broadleaf evergreen forest from northeastern India eastward to southeastern China (including Hainan), and southward to northern Thailand and southern Vietnam
Pteruthius melanotis: foothill to montane broadleaf evergreen forest from central Nepal eastward through Himalayas to northern Vietnam, and patchy southward to peninsular Malaysia
Pteruthius rufiventer: Nepal to Bhutan, Assam, northern Myanmar, Sichuan, northwestern Yunnan, and northwestern Vietnam (Fansipan Mountain)
Pteruthius xanthochlorus: foothill to montane forest from northeastern Pakistan eastward through Himalayas to Tibet, and patchy to southeastern China, southward to northern Myanmar

Ptilinopus arcanus: Negros (known only from a 1953 specimen from Mount Canlaon; west-central Philippines)

Ptilinopus melanospilus: Java region, western and central Lesser Sundas, Sulawesi region, and southern Philippines

Ptilinopus pelewensis: Palau (Babelthuap to Angaur; western Caroline Islands, western Micronesia)
Ptilinopus perlatus: New Guinea and many satellite islands
Ptilinopus perousii: Fiji, Tonga, and Samoa (southwestern to central Polynesia)
Ptilinopus porphyraceus: islets of southern Fiji, Wallis and Futuna, Tonga, Samoa, and Niue (western to central Polynesia)
Ptilinopus porphyreus: montane forest of southern Sumatra, Java, and Bali
Ptilinopus pulchellus: New Guinea, including Raja Ampat Islands (off western New Guinea)
Ptilinopus rarotongensis: Rarotonga and Atiu (southern Cook Islands, eastern Polynesia)

Ptilinopus rivoli: central to southern Moluccas, New Guinea and satellite islands, and Bismarck Archipelago
Ptilinopus roseicapilla: Mariana Islands (Saipan, Tinian, Agiguan, Rota, and Guam)
Ptilinopus speciosus: Numfor, Biak, and Yapen (Cenderawasih Bay, off northwestern New Guinea)
Ptilinopus superbus: Sulawesi to eastern Australia, Bismarck Archipelago, and east-central Solomon Islands
Ptilinopus viridis: central Moluccas, Bird's Head Peninsula and Bird's Neck (northwestern New Guinea), northern coastal New Guinea and satellite islands, and Solomon Archipelago
Ptilinopus wallacii: southern Moluccas including Kai Islands, and lowlands of southwestern New Guinea, including Aru islands (off southwestern New Guinea)

Ptiliogonys cinereus: drier montane forest from southern Sonora and central Nuevo León (northern Mexico) southward to southwestern Guatemala; winters to lower elevations
Ptilocichla mindanensis: East Visayas and Mindanao group (east-central and southern Philippines)
Ptilopachus nahani: northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Uganda
Ptilopachus petrosus: rocky slopes in scrub or patchy woodland from southern Mauritania and Senegal eastward through Chad and southwestern Sudan to Eritrea and Ethiopia, southward to Central African Republic and eastward to central Kenya
Ptiloprora erythropleura: montane Bird's Head Peninsula and Bird's Neck (northwestern New Guinea), and west-central New Guinea
Ptiloprora guisei: montane eastern New Guinea, from the eastern ranges to the Huon and southeastern peninsulas
Ptiloprora meekiana: montane west-central to southeastern New Guinea
Ptiloprora plumbea: patchily in montane west-central, central, and southeastern New Guinea

Ptilopsis leucotis: Senegambia to Somalia, northern Democratic Republic of the Congo, northern Uganda, and central Kenya
Ptiloris intercedens: lowlands of central and southeastern Papua New Guinea
Ptiloris magnificus: western and central New Guinea and northern Cape York Peninsula, northeastern Queensland (northeastern Australia)
Ptiloris paradiseus: eastern Australia (Kroombit Tops, Gympie, southeastern Queensland to Barrington Tops, northeastern New South Wales)
Ptiloris victoriae: northeastern Australia (Wet Tropics region, northern Queensland)
Ptilorrhoa caerulescens: Raja Ampat Islands (northwest of New Guinea) and western and northern New Guinea
Ptilorrhoa geislerorum: eastern New Guinea (Huon Gulf to Collingwood Bay)
Ptilorrhoa nigricrissus: southern New Guinea (Etna Bay to Milne Bay)
Ptilorrhoa urrissia: forested karst of Iagifu Ridge, Agogo Range, Southern Highlands Province, Papua New Guinea
Ptilostomus afer: lowland to foothill lightly-wooded savanna, grazed grassland, and pastures near villages, from southwestern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to southern Sudan, and southward to Uganda, far northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and far western Ethiopia; post-breeding dispersal southward and eastward to northern Tanzania and western Kenya
Ptilotula flavescens: southern coast of southeastern New Guinea and northern Australia
Ptilotula keartlandi: semiarid northern Australia (Pilbara region, central Western Australia, eastward to northwestern and central Queensland)
Ptilotula ornata: southern Australia (southwestern Australia to central New South Wales)
Ptilotula plumula: Australia (except northwestern, coastal eastern, and Tasmania)
Ptiloxena atroviolacea: Cuba including Isla de la Juventud
Ptychoramphus aleuticus: breeds Aleutians and islands off Pacific coast from Alaska through central Baja California; winters nearshore to off-shelf waters southward to southern Baja California
Ptyonoprogne concolor: disjunctly in lowland to submontane cliffs, gorges, and towns and cities, in the Indian subcontinent, and from eastern Myanmar and northern Vietnam southward to Malayan Peninsula and southeastern Vietnam
Ptyonoprogne fuligula: lowland to montane crags, cliffs, coasts, deserts, towns and cities, from western Angola eastward to Zimbabwe, thence southward to southern Mozambique and South Africa

Ptyonoprogne rupestris: breeds southern Palearctic to central Asia; winters to Arabia and India

Pycnonotus bimaculatus: montane central and southern Sumatra and Java
Pycnonotus cafer: northeastern Afghanistan and central Pakistan through India and Nepal southward to Sri Lanka and eastward to central Myanmar and western Yunnan; introduced widely, especially to Arabian Peninsula and islands of the tropical Pacific eastward to Society Islands
Pycnonotus capensis: lowland acacia woodland, coastal scrub, shrubby fynbos, riverine bush, and gardens, in southern and southwestern South Africa, and adjacent southwestern Namibia
Pycnonotus conradi: Thailand, southern Indochina, and the northern and central Thai-Malay Peninsula
Pycnonotus finlaysoni: humid and mixed deciduous forest and scrub from eastern Myanmar, southernmost China (far southern Yunnan; rare), and northern Vietnam (including Côn Đảo) southward to southern Cambodia, southern Vietnam, and the Malayan Peninsula to southern Malayan peninsula
Pycnonotus flavescens: hills of southern Assam (south of the Brahmaputra) through southeastern Asia southward to northern Thai-Malay Peninsula
Pycnonotus goiavier: lowland to foothill second growth, coastal scrub, mangroves, plantations, and suburban parks and gardens, from Indochina eastward to Philippines, and southward to Greater Sundas, and Lesser Sundas eastward to Sumbawa; introduced to southern Sulawesi

Pycnonotus leucogenys: northeastern Afghanistan and Himalayas from northern Pakistan eastward at least to Arunachal (northeastern India)
Pycnonotus leucops: northern Borneo (Mount Kinabalu to mounts Mulu and Murud)
Pycnonotus leucotis: lowland to foothill dry woodland, semi-desert scrub. palm groves, and gardens from Iraq and eastern Arabian Peninsula eastward to Pakistan and western India
Pycnonotus luteolus: open arid scrub, dense thorny thickets, and woodland in the Indian subcontinent from Gujarat eastward to southwestern West Bengal, and southward through Peninsular India to Sri Lanka
Pycnonotus nigricans: lowland to foothill acacia savanna, dry open woodland, and riverine bush, from southwestern Angola, Namibia, and Botswana southward to northern and central South Africa and Lesotho; wanders northward and eastward in dry non-breeding season
Pycnonotus plumosus: Malayan Peninsula, Riau, and Anambas islands, central and eastern Sumatra (east of the Barisan Range), Belitung Island, Borneo, and adjacent islands, including Cagayan Sulu (far southwestern Philippines), Java, and Bawean Island (Java Sea)
Pycnonotus porphyreus: far western Sumatra (west of the Barisan Range) and islands to the west (Nias, Batu, Banyak, and Mentawai islands)
Pycnonotus pseudosimplex: Borneo (confirmed from Sarawak, Sabah, and northeastern Kalimantan, but probably more widespread)
Pycnonotus simplex: Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Borneo, and Java
Pycnonotus sinensis: lowland to foothill open woodland, scrub, cultivation, gardens, from central and northeastern China, coastal Korean Peninsula, and Ryukyu Archipelago (southern Japan) southward to northern Vietnam, southeastern China (including Hainan), and Taiwan; northeastern populations migratory to central Vietnam
Pycnonotus taivanus: coastal lowland forest of eastern and southern Taiwan south of Taroko Gorge (including Hengchun Peninsula)
Pycnonotus xanthopygos: coastal southern Türkiye to Near East, Sinai Peninsula, and Arabia
Pycnonotus xanthorrhous: foothill to montane scrub, tall grass, and bramble thickets, from western Myanmar and southeastern China southward to northern Thailand and northern Laos
Pycnonotus zeylanicus: Myanmar to Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra including Nias, Java, and Borneo
Pycnopygius stictocephalus: lowlands of New Guinea, including Salawati (Raja Ampat Islands, off western New Guinea), and Aru Islands (off southwestern New Guinea)
Pygarrhichas albogularis: central Chile and adjacent Argentina southward to Tierra del Fuego
Pygiptila stellaris: higher strata and edge of Amazonian forest from southeastern Colombia and eastern Ecuador eastward to Suriname, and in the south to northernmost Bolivia and eastward to Mato Grosso and northeastern Pará (Brazil)

Pygochelidon melanoleuca: rapids on rivers of the Guianas, southern Venezuela, and Amazonian Brazil
Pygoscelis adeliae: breeds circumpolarly along coastline of Antarctica and associated islands; winters near edge of ice pack
Pygoscelis antarcticus: breeds on Antarctic Peninsula and associated islands, including Balleny Island (eastern Antarctica); winters mostly south of Antarctic Convergence, to southern South America and subantarctic islands
Pygoscelis papua: mainly subantarctic islands, locally Antarctic islands
Pyrenestes minor: foothill to submontane forest edge, secondary growth, rank streamside grass, reedbeds, and bracken briar, from southern Tanzania and Malawi southward to central Mozambique and adjacent eastern Zimbabwe

Pyrenestes sanguineus: lowland swamp-forest, tidal creek, brushy riparian along streams, and wet sedge in open forest, from Senegambia eastward to central Ivory Coast
Pyrgilauda blanfordi: sandy, stony, and grassy plains from southeastern Xinjiang (southwestern China) and northern Ladakh, northwestern India eastward through northern Nepal and Sikkim and eastern Tibet to northern Sichuan (central China)
Pyrgilauda davidiana: semi-desert and rocky steppe with short dry grass in the Altai mountains of south-central Russia, most of Mongolia eastward to Inner Mongolia (northeastern China), and in northeastern Qinghai (north-central China)
Pyrgilauda ruficollis: stony and dry grass steppe and plateaus from southwestern Xinjiang eastward to Qinghai and western Gansu, in south from eastern Ladakh, northern Nepal, and northern Sikkim eastward to western Sichuan
Pyriglena atra: lowlands of coastal eastern Brazil (southern Sergipe and coastal northeastern Bahia)
Pyriglena leuconota: humid forest in the eastern Amazon basin from the Rio Xingu eastward to the Cerrado of eastern Maranhão and western Piaui; and in the Atlantic Forest of northeastern Brazil, in Paraiba, Pernambuco, and Alagoas
Pyriglena leucoptera: eastern Brazil (eastern Bahia) to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina (Misiones)
Pyriglena maura: semi-humid to humid tropical and montane forest and woodland on the slopes of the central and eastern Andes from southern Colombia southward along the eastern Andes to central Bolivia, and eastward to the Pantanal in eastern Bolivia. south-central Brazil, and far northern Paraguay; also in the Pacific lowlands of western Ecuador and adjacent northwestern Peru
Pyriglena similis: south-central Amazonian Brazil (Rio Tapajós to Rio Xingú)
Pyrilia aurantiocephala: Amazonian Brazil (middle Rio Tapajós and possibly lower Rio Madeira)
Pyrilia barrabandi: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin from southern Venezuela and eastern Colombia southward to northern Bolivia; in Brazil eastward to central Mato Grosso and westernmost Pará, mostly west of the Rio Tapajós
Pyrilia caica: southeastern Venezuela to the Guianas and Brazil north of the Amazon
Pyrilia haematotis: forest from lowlands to mountains on Caribbean slope from southern Veracruz and northern Oaxaca east through southeastern Yucatan Peninsula to southern Nicaragua, thence both slopes Costa Rica and Panama to adjacent west-central Colombia
Pyrilia pulchra: humid forest of western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador
Pyrilia pyrilia: far eastern Panama to northern Colombia and northwestern Venezuela
Pyrilia vulturina: humid forest of eastern Amazonian Brazil south of the Amazon
Pyrocephalus nanus: dry to humid woodland from lowlands to hills of Galapagos (extinct or possibly so on Santa Cruz, Floreana, and San Cristóbal)
Pyrocephalus rubinus: disjunctly, southwestern USA from central California to northeastern Nicaragua, northern South America from Colombia to Guyana, and west of the Andes to southeastern Peru, and breeds northern Argentina and Uruguay to southern Brazil, Paraguay, and southeastern Bolivia; southern breeders winter from southeastern Colombia and eastern Ecuador to eastern Bolivia and central and eastern Brazil
Pyroderus scutatus: mostly humid montane and foothill forest in the Sierra de Perijá, the coastal mountains of northwestern Venezuela, and the Andes of western Venezuela southward along the Andes of Colombia to northwestern Ecuador; again in the eastern Andes from far southeastern Ecuador southward to central Peru, in Pasco; in the tepuis of eastern Venezuela and western Guyana, and in the Atlantic Forest and Cerrado from northern Bahia, in eastern Brazil, southward to eastern Paraguay, northeastern Argentina and southern Rio Grande do Sul and adjacent Uruguay

Pyrrholaemus brunneus: semiarid southern Australia (central western coast to southwestern Queensland and northwestern Victoria)
Pyrrholaemus sagittatus: southeastern Australia (central and eastern Queensland southward to central Victoria)
Pyrrhomyias cinnamomeus: montane cloudforest in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela, from Yaracuy eastward to the Paría Peninsula, and in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Sierra de Perijá and the Andes from western Venezuela southward along the Andes of Colombia to northern Peru, and in the eastern Andes from northern Peru southeastward to northwestern Argentina, southward to Tucuman
Pyrrhoplectes epauletta: montane forest from west-central Nepal eastward to southwestern China (southern and southeastern Tibet, and far western Yunnan), and northern Myanmar
Pyrrhula aurantiaca: montane forest of northern Pakistan to northwestern India (Himachal Pradesh)
Pyrrhula erythaca: patchy in submontane to montane coniferous forest, mixed and deciduous forest, and rhododendron and willow thickets, from northeastern China southward to south-central China, northeastern India, Bhutan, and northern Myanmar; downslope dispersal in winter
Pyrrhula erythrocephala: montane forest from western Kashmir eastward through Himalayas to western Arunachal Pradesh and southern and southeastern Tibet
Pyrrhula leucogenis: montane northern Luzon, Panay (form uncertain), and Mindanao (northern, west-central, and southern Philippines)
Pyrrhula murina: mountains of eastern São Miguel, in eastern Azores
Pyrrhula nipalensis: Himalayas from Himachal Pradesh to west-central and southeastern China (including Hainan), mountains of northern southeastern Asia, southern Vietnam, and Malayan Peninsula

Pyrrhura caeruleiceps: west slope of eastern Andes of northern Colombia and Sierra de Perijá
Pyrrhura calliptera: eastern Andes of Colombia (Boyacá and Cundinamarca)
Pyrrhura cruentata: lowlands of southeastern Brazil (Bahia to Rio de Janeiro)
Pyrrhura devillei: forest of northern Paraguay and southwestern Brazil (southwestern Mato Grosso)
Pyrrhura egregia: humid forest in the tepuis of southeastern Venezuela, far north Brazil in Roraima, and western Guyana
Pyrrhura frontalis: humid montane forest, gallery, and araucaria forest from east-central Brazil (Bahia and southern Mato Grosso do Sul), southward to northern Uruguay, northern Argentina (southward to Santa Fe and Corrientes), and eastern Paraguay
Pyrrhura hoematotis: humid montane forest in the coastal cordillera of north-central Venezuela, from Aragua eastward to Miranda, and in the northern part of the Andes of Venezuela, in Lara
Pyrrhura hoffmanni: montane forest and edge from west-central Costa Rica through west-central Panama
Pyrrhura lepida: humid forest in northeastern Brazil south of the Amazon River in Pará, Maranhão, and northern Tocantins southward to northern Mato Grosso
Pyrrhura lucianii: Brazil (west-central Amazonia along Amazon River at Tefe and Rio Purus)

Pyrrhura orcesi: Andean foothills of southwestern Ecuador (El Oro and Azuay)
Pyrrhura perlata: Brazil (western Pará, eastern Amazonas, and Mato Grosso) to northern Bolivia
Pyrrhura picta: southeastern Venezuela to the Guianas and northern Amazonian Brazil (Amapá)
Pyrrhura rhodocephala: Andes of western Venezuela (Mérida, Táchira, and Trujillo)
Pyrrhura roseifrons: humid forest in the foothills of the cordilleras de Cutucu and del Condor in southeastern Ecuador and northeastern Peru and patchily along the eastern Andes of Peru; and in the Amazonian lowlands south of the Amazon River from eastern Peru and western Brazil in westernmost Amazonas and Acre, southward to northwestern Bolivia

Pyrrhura viridicata: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)

Pytilia phoenicoptera: lowland dry woodland, thickets, and villages from Senegambia eastward through southern Mali, northern Cameroon, and Central Africa Republic, to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northern Uganda
Quechuavis decussata: arid littoral of western Peru and far northern Chile
Quelea cardinalis: patchy in foothill to montane dry wooded grassland and rank vegetation from South Sudan and western Ethiopia southward to eastern Zambia and Malawi; seasonal dispersal after rains
Quelea erythrops: lowland to foothill savanna, grassland, and cultivation, from Senegambia and Mali eastward though Cameroon and São Tomé (Gulf of Guinea) to western Ethiopia, and southward to Angola, Zambia, Mozambique, and southeastern South Africa; some populations intra-African migrants; extirpated in Príncipe (Gulf of Guinea) but recently reintroduced there

Querula purpurata: tropical Costa Rica to northern Bolivia, the Guianas, and Amazonian Brazil

Quiscalus mexicanus: varied open habitats, including forest edge, prairies, deserts, mangroves, and cities, from southeastern Oregon eastward to central Iowa (and expanding northward), and southward across central and western USA through Mexico (but rare Baja California) and Central America to northern Colombia and western Venezuela, and from western Colombia southward to northwestern Peru (spreading southward in interior Colombia and to southwestern Ecuador, and also spreading in Greater Antilles)
Quiscalus nicaraguensis: Lake Nicaragua, Lake Managua, and northern Costa Rica
Quiscalus niger: varied open habitats of lowlands of Greater Antilles and satellite islands from Cuba and Cayman Islands eastward through Puerto Rico; also reported Virgin Islands (status?)
Quiscalus palustris: formerly marshes and headwaters of Valley of Mexico (Río Lerma Santiago and Xochimilco); extinct, last reported 1910
Quiscalus quiscula: varied open habitats from forest borders and open woodland to marshes and fields from Northwest Territories eastward to Newfoundland (north-central to northeastern Canada), southward from central New Mexico to southern Florida; resident in southern two-thirds of range, with northern birds moving southward
Radinopsyche sellowi: Caatinga of north-central and eastern Brazil
Radjah radjah: Moluccas, New Guinea and satellite islands, and northern and eastern Australia
Rallicula forbesi: montane west-central to northeastern (Adelbert Range and Huon Peninsula) and southeastern New Guinea
Rallicula leucospila: montane forest of western New Guinea (Bird's Head Peninsula)
Rallicula rubra: montane Bird's Head Peninsula (northwestern New Guinea) and western to east-central New Guinea
Rallina eurizonoides: lowland to foothill forest, dense scrub, and long grass with dense bush, from northwestern India eastward through Himalayan foothills to southern China (including Hainan), Taiwan, and Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), and southward to west-central India, central Vietnam, Sulawesi, Philippines, and Palau; some populations winter to Sri Lanka and Greater Sundas
Rallina fasciata: south-central Myanmar eastward to northern Thailand, southern Vietnam, and Philippines (very local), and southward through Indonesian Archipelago eastward to eastern Wallacea
Rallina tricolor: far eastern Indonesia, in Nanusa Islands (northern Talaud Islands), Halmahera, Obi, Ambon, Tanimbar, and Kai islands, New Guinea including satellite islands, Lavongai and New Ireland (Bismarck Archipelago), and northeastern Australia (northeastern Cape York Peninsula, Wet Tropics region, Queensland)
Rallus aequatorialis: reedbeds in freshwater marshes and damp grasslands with rushes, sedges and tall grass in the Andes from far southern Colombia (Nariño and adjacent Putumayo) southward to southern Ecuador (southern Azuay), and in coastal marshes from central Peru, in La Libertad, southward to southeastern Arequipa
Rallus antarcticus: marshes of central Chile and Argentina to Tierra del Fuego

Rallus caerulescens: swamps and reedbeds of eastern and southern Africa
Rallus crepitans: brackish marshes and mangroves of the Atlantic coast from northeastern US, in southernmost Maine, southward to southern Florida, and westward along the Gulf of Mexico coast to northeastern Mexico, in northern Tamaulipas; also in the northern coast of Yucatan Peninsula southward to Belize and adjacent Guatemala; and in the Bahamas and the Greater and Lesser Antilles southward to Guadeloupe, except the Cayman Islands
Rallus elegans: tidal, brackish and non-tidal marshes, swamps and rice fields in the Gulf of Mexico coast of the US southward seasonally and locally along the coast of Mexico to southern Veracruz; in the Atlantic coast from northeastern US southward to southern Florida and Cuba; also breeds locally northward to north-central US and southernmost Canada

Rallus obsoletus: coastal and tidal marshes, and freshwater marshes with emergent plants from the west-central coast of California southward to southern Baja California, and the Colorado River from westernmost Arizona and adjacent Nevada southward along the Pacific coast of Mexico to southern Jalisco, Colima, and western Guerrero

Rallus wetmorei: very local in mangroves and coastal swamps of northwestern Venezuela

Ramosomyia viridifrons: drier woodland and edge in lowlands to hills on Pacific slope from Guerrero (south-central Mexico) to far southwestern Guatemala

Ramphastos brevis: Pacific slope of western Colombia to southwestern Ecuador
Ramphastos dicolorus: humid forest of southeastern Brazil to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
Ramphastos sulfuratus: humid to semi-humid forest in the Gulf of Mexico slope in central Mexico, from Veracruz and adjacent Puebla eastward across most Central America, including the Yucatan Peninsula, to the lowlands of northern South America in northern Colombia and westernmost Venezuela
Ramphastos toco: varied drier, open woodland types of lowlands from the Guianas eastward to Piauí and southward through southeastern Peru (Pampas del Heath) and northern Argentina to Rio Grande do Sul (southeastern Brazil)
Ramphastos tucanus: forest and edge of lowlands to hills of Amazonia and the Guianas from eastern Ecuador and Venezuela east through Maranhão (northeastern Brazil) and southward through central Bolivia and southern Mato Grosso do Sul
Ramphastos vitellinus: tropical rainforest in the lowlands of northern Colombia, including the Magdalena Valley southward to Boyacá, eastward to the lowlands of western Venezuela, and to the eastern slope of the Andes of Venezuela southward across Amazonian Colombia, Ecuador and Peru to central Bolivia; in northern South America from Trinidad south and eastward across eastern and southern Venezuela and the Guianas, to the entire Amazon basin of Brazil, southward to Mato Grosso do Sul; also in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil from Pernambuco southward to Santa Catarina

Ramphiculus leclancheri: Philippines and Taiwan including Lan-yü Island (just off southeastern Taiwan)
Ramphiculus occipitalis: Philippines (except Palawan group and Sulu Archipelago)
Ramphiculus subgularis: Peleng and Banggai, in Banggai Islands (off eastern Sulawesi)

Ramphocelus nigrogularis: humid southeastern Colombia to northern Bolivia and western Amazonian Brazil

Ramphodon naevius: lowlands of southeastern Brazil (southern Minas Gerais to Santa Catarina)
Ramphomicron dorsale: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
