Saltatricula multicolor: southeastern Bolivia (central Santa Cruz southward) to western Paraguay, northwestern Uruguay, and northern Argentina
Sapayoa aenigma: tropical central Panama to Colombia and far northwestern Ecuador
Sappho sparganurus: arid montane scrub in the Andes of Bolivia (from La Paz), southward in western Argentina (to central Mendoza), and in isolated mountain ridges in west-central Argentina (Catamarca, Santiago del Estero, San Luis, and Córdoba)
Sarcoramphus papa: southern Mexico to northern Argentina and Brazil
Sarkidiornis melanotos: tropical Africa and Madagascar; disjunctly India to southern China
Sarkidiornis sylvicola: tropical South America (east of the Andes) to northern Argentina
Saroglossa spilopterus: foothills of northern India and Nepal; winters to Myanmar and Thailand
Sarothrura affinis: disjunctly in lowland to montane dry upland grassland, bracken bramble, and lowland Fynbos, from southern South Sudan and southwestern Kenya southward to Malawi, eastern Zimbabwe, and adjacent Mozambique, and Eswatini and eastern and southern South Africa
Sarothrura ayresi: highlands of Ethiopia and eastern South Africa
Sarothrura boehmi: locally in wet grassland of central Africa
Sarothrura elegans: patchy in lowland to montane thickets, scrub, and forest, including juniper and bamboo, from Guinea and Sierra Leone eastward through Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to southwestern Ethiopia and southwestern Kenya, and southward to southern Angola and southern South Africa
Sarothrura insularis: humid forest of eastern and northwestern Madagascar
Sarothrura lugens: very patchy in lowland and foothill grassy marsh in savanna or forest, lakeside marsh, and dambos, from Cameroon and Gabon eastward to Rwanda (and long ago, Tanzania), and southward to central Angola and central Malawi
Sarothrura pulchra: lowland to foothill rainforest, forest swamps and pools, and dense thicket in gallery forest, from Senegambia eastward to southern South Sudan and western Kenya, and southward to northern Angola and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Sarothrura rufa: very patchy in sub-Saharan Africa in lowland to montane wetland habitat, including wet grassland, sedge meadow, and papyrus swamps, from Sierra Leone eastward to western Ethiopia, and southward through Angola and Tanzania, including Pemba and Unguja (in Zanzibar), to southern South Africa
Sasia abnormis: humid and swamp forest and bamboo stands in the Malayan Peninsula from southern Myanmar (Tenasserim) and Peninsular Thailand southward to southern Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatra (including Nias), Belitung, Java, and Borneo
Sasia ochracea: foothill to submontane forest, bamboo, and dense scrub, from central Nepal eastward through the Himalayas to southern China, and southward to peninsular Thailand and southern Vietnam
Satrapa icterophrys: far southeastern Peru to northern Argentina, eastern and southern Brazil; Venezuela
Saucerottia beryllina: drier forest and woodland of lowlands and hills from southeastern Arizona (southwestern USA) through Pacific slope of Mexico and inland to central Veracruz southward through southern Honduras
Saucerottia castaneiventris: west slope of eastern Andes of north-central Colombia
Saucerottia cupreicauda: tepuis of southern Venezuela, southwestern Guyana, and far northern Brazil (Roraima)
Saucerottia cyanifrons: lowlands and foothills of northern and central Colombia
Saucerottia cyanocephala: drier forest and edge of lowlands to mountains on Caribbean slope from southern Tamaulipas (northeastern Mexico) through southern Belize and inland to northern Nicaragua
Saucerottia cyanura: open woodland and edge of lowlands to hills mostly on Pacific slope from eastern Chiapas to southern Nicaragua
Saucerottia edward: forest to semi-open areas in lowlands and hills mostly on the Pacific slope of southwestern Costa Rica and northwestern Panama east through Panama (including satellite islands) to adjacent far northwestern Colombia
Saucerottia hoffmanni: semiarid western Nicaragua to central Costa Rica
Saucerottia saucerottei: arid scrub and forest borders, savanna, and open habitats from northern Colombia and western Venezuela southward in the Magdalena Valley to its headwaters (Huila), and southward in the Cauca Valley to southwestern Colombia (Río Patía Valley)
Saucerottia tobaci: humid to dry forest and scrub, savanna and clearings in northern Venezuela, including Isla Margarita and Trinidad and Tobago, southward to the Orinoco basin and the tepuis of south-central Venezuela in southern Bolívar and northern Amazonas, and westward to the Andes of western Venezuela
Saucerottia viridigaster: humid forest border and scrub in the Andes of far western Venezuela southward in the eastern slope of the eastern Andes of Colombia to Meta, including the Serrania La Macarena
Saundersilarus saundersi: breeds Yellow Sea coasts from Liaoning to Jiangsu (eastern China) and Songdo (northwestern South Korea); winters coasts of East China Sea from Japan (central Honshu and Ryukyu Islands) and Korean Peninsula to northern Vietnam
Saxicola caprata: lowland to montane bare stony ground, scrubby open grassland, steppe, thickets near reedbeds, tamarisk scrub, and abandoned pasture, from southern Kazakhstan and eastern Iran eastward through Indian subcontinent, and Sri Lanka, to southeastern Asia, and southward Philippines, Sulawesi, Java, Lesser Sundas, New Guinea, and satellite islands
Saxicola ferreus: foothill to montane open scrub, forest edge, terraced agriculture, weedy fields, and gardens, from northern Pakistan eastward through Himalayas to central and southeastern China, and southward to western Myanmar and northern Thailand, and disjunctly in northern Laos and central Vietnam; downslope dispersal in winter
Saxicola gutturalis: eastern Lesser Sundas (Timor, Rote, and Semau)
Saxicola insignis: rocky alpine meadows of central Asia; winters to northern India
Saxicola jerdoni: eastern India and Bangladesh eastward to south-central China (western Yunnan), northeastern Laos, and northern Vietnam
Saxicola leucurus: eastern Pakistan to Nepal, northern India, and Myanmar
Saxicola macrorhynchus: arid plains of southern Afghanistan, eastern Pakistan, and northwestern India
Saxicola maurus: breeds eastern Europe and Russia southward through Himalayas and eastern to eastern Siberia, Korean Peninsula, and Japan (Hokkaido to central Honshu); winters eastern Africa to southern China and southeastern Asia
Saxicola rubetra: breeds Western Palearctic; winters to tropical and southern Africa
Saxicola rubicola: lowland to foothill open scrub, grassy hillside, dry plain, field margins, and woodland edge, from British Isles and Denmark eastward to central Ukraine, and southward to northwestern Africa, Mediterranean Europe, and Türkiye; northern populations migrate to northern and western Africa, Middle East, and Arabian Peninsula
Saxicola torquatus: patchy in lowland to montane scrub, wooded grassland, floodplain, coastal dunes, and clearings in forest, from Senegal and Sierra Leone eastward through Cameroon, and Bioko, to Ethiopia and southwestern Arabian Peninsula, and southward (avoiding rainforest) to South Africa, Grand Comoro, and Madagascar; some highland populations move downslope post-breeding
Sayornis nigricans: southwestern Oregon and southwestern USA south through mountains of South America to northwestern Argentina
Sayornis phoebe: breeds eastern Canada and USA; winters to southeastern Mexico
Sayornis saya: breeds in dry open country from lowlands to mountains of western North America from northern Alaska and northwestern Canada southward through central Baja California and central plateau of Mexico; non-breeders withdraw mainly to southwestern USA and south-central Mexico
Scelorchilus albicollis: xeric scrub from north-central to south-central Chile (southwestern Antofagasta southward to Maule)
Scelorchilus rubecula: humid coniferous and Nothofagus forests with dense shrubby patches; also deciduous forest and woodland from south-central Chile (including Mocha Island) to southern Chile (from Bío Bío southward to Aisén) and adjacent southwestern Argentina and immediately adjacent parts of Argentina (Neuquén southward to western Chubut)
Scenopoeetes dentirostris: northeastern Australia (Wet Tropics region, northern Queensland)
Scepomycter winifredae: montane dense understory of forest and forest clearings of central Tanzania (Uluguru, Ukaguru, and Rubeho mountains)
Schiffornis aenea: eastern Andes of Ecuador and adjacent northern Peru (Piura and Cajamarca)
Schiffornis major: varzea forest in the Amazon basin from southern Venezuela southward to northwestern Bolivia and Amazonian Brazil (eastward to the western side of Rio Tapajos in eastern Amazonas, adjacent Pará, and northwestern Mato Grosso)
Schiffornis olivacea: eastern Venezuela, the Guianas, and northeastern Brazil north of the Amazon River
Schiffornis stenorhyncha: humid forest from eastern Panama, northern Colombia, and western Venezuela southward to the middle Magdalena Valley in interior Colombia and along the base of the eastern Andes to northeastern Colombia
Schiffornis turdina: tropical rainforest in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from southern Venezuela southward to central Bolivia and south-central Brazil (southwestern Mato Grosso, eastward to northeastern Pará and western Maranhão); also in the Atlantic Forest region of northeastern Brazil (Paraiba southward to Rio de Janeiro)
Schiffornis veraepacis: humid forest from the Gulf of Mexico slope in southeastern Mexico southward along the Caribbean slope of Central America, including the Yucatan Peninsula, to eastern Panama and in the Pacific slope of Costa Rica and western Panama; in the Pacific lowlands from northwestern Colombia southward to southwestern Ecuador and adjacent northwestern Peru (Tumbes)
Schiffornis virescens: southeastern Brazil (southern Bahia) to eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina
Schistes albogularis: both slopes of western Andes and west slope of central Andes of Colombia and west slope of Andes of western Ecuador
Schistes geoffroyi: foothill and montane cloudforest in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Yaracuy eastward to western Miranda), in Sierra de Perijá, the Andes of western Venezuela southward in the eastern Andes of Colombia (including the headwaters of the Río Magdalena), the central Andes, the eastern Andes of Ecuador and far northern Peru north of the Río Marañón, and in the eastern Andes of Peru from Amazonas south and east of the Marañón, southeastward to central Bolivia (to Cochabamba and western Santa Cruz)
Schistochlamys melanopis: northeastern Colombia to Venezuela, western Guyana, Amazonian and southeastern Brazil (Brazil south of the Amazon River eastward to northern Ceará, then southward to Mato Grosso, São Paulo, and Rio de Janeiro, and up eastern coast to Pernambuco), and Paraguay
Schistochlamys ruficapillus: eastern Brazil (southern Pará, central Maranhão, and Pernambuco southward to Santa Catarina)
Schistolais leontica: disjunctly in foothill to submontane forest edge, riparian scrub, and thickets along highland streams, in Guinea, northern and eastern Sierra Leone, northern Liberia, and western Ivory Coast
Schistolais leucopogon: lowland to montane riparian woodland, gallery forest, and bracken thickets, from southeastern Nigeria and southern Cameroon eastward to southern South Sudan and western Kenya, and southward to northern Angola and western Tanzania

Schoeniclus chrysophrys: breeds taiga of Siberia from Irkutsk, Nizhnyaya Tunguska River and Bratsk eastward to Vilyuy River and Yakutsk, southward to Chamar Daban range (south of Lake Baikal), and Stanovoy Mountains; winters in central and southeastern China, western Korean Peninsula, and Taiwan

Schoeniclus personatus: breeds woodland edge, Sakhalin and southern Kuril Islands to Honshu and Shikoku; winters Honshu to Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), some reaching South Korea, east-central Chinese coast, and Taiwan
Schoeniclus pusillus: breeds tundra and taiga of northern Eurasia from Scandinavia eastward to Chukotka, and southward to northeastern China; winters from east-central India to eastern China and Korean Peninsula and Taiwan
Schoeniclus rusticus: breeds swamp forest of northern Palearctic from Scandinavia eastward to Kamchatka and Sakhalin; winters to eastern China, southern Japan, Korean Peninsula, and Taiwan

Schoeniclus siemsseni: mountains of central China (southern Shaanxi, southeastern Gansu, and northeastern Sichuan)
Schoeniclus spodocephalus: temperate north-central, northeastern, and central Palearctic, in shrubby areas in woodland, from south-central Russia and northern Mongolia eastward to Sea of Okhotsk and northern Sakhalin (southeastern Russia) and southward to northeastern Inner Mongolia, northern Heilongjiang (northeastern China) and northern and central Korean Peninsula; disjunctly Qinghai and Shaanxi southward to Yunnan and Guizhou (central China); winters in subtropical eastern Asian disturbed areas and wetlands from central Nepal through northeastern Himalayas, northern southeastern Asia, southern and eastern China, Taiwan, and Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan)
Schoeniclus sulphuratus: breeds in montane forest edge of northern and central Honshu (central Japan); winters to southeastern China, Taiwan and (mainly) northern Philippines
Schoeniclus tristrami: breeds northeastern China (from Lesser Khingan Mountains and Zeja River, in Heilongjiang) eastward to southeastern Russian Far East (Amurland and Ussuri regions, including Sikhote Alin Mountains), and North Korea; winters in southeastern China (southeastern Yunnan eastward to Fujian, also Hunan and eastern Sichuan); rare winter visitor also far northeastern India, northern Myanmar, northwestern Thailand, northern Laos, and northern Vietnam (Tonkin)

Schoeniclus yessoensis: far east-central Palearctic marshes, patchily in far eastern Mongolia, Heilongjiang (northeastern China), far southeastern Ussuriland (southeastern Russia), and Honshu to Kyushu (central to southern Japan); winters central Honshu to Kyushu (central and southern Japan), Korean Peninsula, and coastal east-central China
Schoenicola platyurus: grassland of southwestern India (Western Ghats from Karnataka to Kerala)
Schoeniophylax phryganophilus: gallery and riparian scrub and thickets in the Cerrado, Caatinga, and Chaco of interior Brazil, from Piauí southward to Minas Gerais, and inland to western São Paulo, Mato Grosso do Sul, and southern Mato Grosso, and Paraguay, westward to eastern and northern Bolivia, and southward to northern Argentina to northern Buenos Aires, and Uruguay
Schoeniparus brunneus: foothill to submontane understory in broadleaf evergreen forest, and grassy scrub, in southeastern China (including Hainan) and Taiwan
Schoeniparus castaneceps: foothill to montane understory in broadleaf evergreen forest, secondary growth, forest edge, and bamboo, from central Nepal eastward to south-central China, and southward to western and southern Myanmar, adjacent Thailand, central Vietnam, and disjunctly on Malayan Peninsula
Schoeniparus cinereus: Nepal to northeastern Myanmar, southern China (Yunnan), and northern Laos
Schoeniparus dubius: foothill to montane understory in broadleaf and pine forest, bracken bramble, bamboo scrub, and secondary growth, from Bhutan and northeastern India eastward to southeastern China, and southward to western Myanmar, western Thailand, and southern Laos and adjacent Vietnam
Schoeniparus rufogularis: patchy in lowland to foothill understory in broadleaf forest, second growth, scrub, and bamboo, from southern Bhutan and northeastern India eastward to northern Vietnam, southward to northeastern Cambodia, and disjunctly in southeastern Thailand and adjacent Cambodia
Schoeniparus variegaticeps: montane forest of southern China (eastern Sichuan and Guangxi)
Schoutedenapus myoptilus: patchy in foothill and montane gorges and waterfalls in forest from western Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) eastward to Ethiopia and Kenya, and southward to Angola, eastern Zimbabwe, and adjacent Mozambique; post-breeding dispersal likely but poorly understood
Sciaphylax castanea: tropical rainforest in the western Amazon basin from far southeastern Colombia and northeastern Ecuador southward to northeastern Peru
Sciaphylax hemimelaena: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin from northeastern Peru south of the Río Marañón, southward to northern and central Bolivia, and southwestern Brazil (eastward to the Rio Xingu, in central Pará, south of the Amazon River)
Scissirostrum dubium: Sulawesi region, including Bangka, Lembeh, Togian, and Banggai islands (off eastern Sulawesi) and Buton (to southeast)
Sclateria naevia: tropical rainforest, swampy, and flooded forest from northeastern Venezuela, Trinidad, and the Guianas southward across the Orinoco and Amazon basins to south-central Brazil, northern Bolivia, and southeastern Peru
Scleroptila afra: grassland of Lesotho and west-central South Africa
Scleroptila elgonensis: montane moorlands of eastern Uganda to central Kenya
Scleroptila finschi: patchily distributed in Congo, southwestern Democratic Republic of the Congo and central Angola

Scleroptila psilolaema: montane moorlands of central and southern Ethiopia
Scleroptila shelleyi: southern Uganda and southwestern Kenya to northeastern South Africa
Scleroptila streptophora: southwestern Cameroon; western Uganda to western Kenya and northwestern Tanzania
Scleroptila whytei: southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to northern Zambia and northern Malawi
Sclerurus albigularis: humid forest in montane areas from northwestern Costa Rica to western Panama; in South America from Trinidad and Tobago westward to the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela from Monagas west to western Lara, and in the Andes from western Venezuela, Sierra de Perijá, and Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta southward along the eastern slope of the eastern Andes of Colombia to southeastern Peru; in southeastern Amazonia of Peru extends eastward to the lowlands to Acre, Rondônia and Mato Grosso, in Brazil, and southward to northwestern Bolivia

Sclerurus mexicanus: humid forest of foothills and mountains on Caribbean slope from Hidalgo (east-central Mexico) through northern Oaxaca to southern Belize and through eastern Panama
Sclerurus obscurior: tropical rainforest to montane cloudforest in the lowlands and Andean foothills from eastern Panama and western Venezuela southward along the western Andes of Colombia to Valle del Cauca, central Andes to Tolima and eastern Andes to Putumayo; west of the Andes in the Pacific lowlands of western Colombia southward to southwestern Ecuador; east of the Andes locally in eastern and southern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to the eastern Amazon of Brazil southward to Tocantins and eastward to northern Maranhão, and westward to the western Amazon in southeastern Colombia, eastern Ecuador and Peru to northern Bolivia; also in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil from central Bahia (possible further north from Alagoas) southward to Paraná

Sclerurus scansor: humid forest from northeastern Brazil in Ceará southward across interior Brazil to Goiás, Minas Gerais, and central Bahia, and in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil from southern Bahia southward to Rio Grande do Sul and westward to eastern Paraguay and northern Argentina in Misiones

Scolopax minor: breeds temperate forest and edge from southwestern Alberta eastward to Maritime Provinces (south-central to southeastern Canada) and southward to southeastern Texas and northern Florida (southeastern USA); winters in southeastern USA
Scolopax mira: Amami-Oshima, Tokunoshima, Okinawa, Tokashiki-Shima (Ryukyu Islands, southern Japan)
Scolopax rusticola: breeds locally in moist woodland and bogs from British Isles and Scandinavia southward to northern Iberian Peninsula and Azores to Canary Islands, eastward to southeastern Russia southward to central Japan (Honshu and Izu Islands), and disjunctly in the Caucasus and Himalayas; winters southward to northern Africa and eastward to central and southern Japan (to Ryukyu Islands) and Taiwan
Scolopax saturata: mountains of Sumatra and western Java
Scopus umbretta: southwestern Arabian Peninsula, tropical Africa, and Madagascar
Scotocerca inquieta: patchy in lowland to submontane arid scrub, day grassland, including rocky steppe, and vegetated sandy plain, from Mauritania and Morocco eastward to coastal Libya, and in northeastern Egypt and Arabian Peninsula, and in southern Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan southward to southern Iran and southern Pakistan; some post-breeding dispersal in northern populations
Scotopelia bouvieri: southern Cameroon to Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Gabon, and northern Angola
Scotopelia peli: locally in riverine forest of sub-Saharan Africa
Scotopelia ussheri: rainforest of Sierra Leone, Liberia, Ivory Coast, and Ghana
Scytalopus acutirostris: central Andes of Peru (eastern La Libertad to Junín)
Scytalopus affinis: western Andes of Peru (southern Cajamarca to Ancash)

Scytalopus alvarezlopezi: Pacific slope of Colombian Andes (western Antioquia southward to southwestern Valle del Cauca)
Scytalopus androstictus: Andes of southeastern Ecuador and far northern Peru
Scytalopus argentifrons: montane forest from northwestern Costa Rica to central Panama
Scytalopus atratus: undergrowth of humid foothill and montane forest in the Sierra de Perijá and the Andes from western Venezuela southward along the Andes of Colombia and eastern Andes of Ecuador to far northern Peru north of the Río Marañón; also in the eastern Andes of Peru south and east of the Río Marañón, southward to southeastern Peru, in Puno, including Cerros del Sira
Scytalopus bolivianus: Andes of southeastern Peru (Ayacucho and Puno) to southern Bolivia (Chuquisaca)
Scytalopus caracae: coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Aragua to Miranda)
Scytalopus chocoensis: Pacific slope of eastern Panama (Cerro Pirre) to northwestern Ecuador
Scytalopus diamantinensis: Chapada Diamantina region of northeastern Brazil (Bahia)
Scytalopus femoralis: east slope of Andes of eastern Peru (Amazonas to Junín)
Scytalopus frankeae: Andes of central Peru (Pasco and Junín)
Scytalopus fuscus: Andes of central Chile (Atacama to Biobío)
Scytalopus griseicollis: undergrowth of humid montane forest, bamboo stands, and elfin forest in the Andes of western Venezuela and northeastern Colombia, including Serrania de los Yariguies, southward to southern Cundinamarca
Scytalopus intermedius: central Andes of northern Peru (southern Amazonas)
Scytalopus iraiensis: southwestern Brazil (river basins in Iguaçu and Tibagi, eastern Paraná)
Scytalopus krabbei: east slope of the Andes of northern Peru (Amazonas, south of the Río Marañón, to Huánuco, north of the Río Huallaga)
Scytalopus latebricola: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
Scytalopus latrans: undergrowth of humid montane forest and humid to semi-humid montane scrub in the Andes from western Venezuela (Táchira and Mérida) southward to northern Peru (in Piura, Cajamarca, and Lambayeque), north and south of the Río Marañón
Scytalopus macropus: east slope of central Andes of Peru (southern Amazonas to Junín)
Scytalopus magellanicus: Andes of central Chile and Argentina to Tierra del Fuego
Scytalopus meridanus: montane humid forest and edge of Andes of western to north-central Venezuela
Scytalopus micropterus: Andes of Colombia to Ecuador and far northern Peru
Scytalopus novacapitalis: southern Brazil (southern Goiás, Distrito Federal, and western Minas Gerais)
Scytalopus opacus: central Andes of Colombia to east-central Ecuador
Scytalopus pachecoi: northeastern Argentina (Misiones) and far southern Brazil (southwestern Paraná to southern Rio Grande do Sul)
Scytalopus panamensis: eastern Panama and adjacent northern Colombia (Cerro Tacarcuna massif)
Scytalopus parkeri: Andes of southern Ecuador to far northern Peru (eastern Piura and northern Cajamarca)
Scytalopus parvirostris: Andes of northwestern Peru to east-central Bolivia (Santa Cruz)
Scytalopus petrophilus: central and southern Minas Gerais, Brazil
Scytalopus robbinsi: Pacific slope of southwestern Ecuador (Azuay and El Oro)
Scytalopus rodriguezi: undergrowth of humid montane forest in Serrania de los Yariguies and in the eastern slope and the headwaters of the Magdalena Valley in the central Andes of Colombia
Scytalopus sanctaemartae: Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
Scytalopus schulenbergi: Andes of southeastern Peru (Vilcanota Mountains) to central Bolivia (Cochabamba)
Scytalopus simonsi: Andes of southeastern Peru (Vilcanota Mountains) to central Bolivia (Cochabamba)
Scytalopus speluncae: southeastern Brazil (southwestern Espírito Santo to northern Rio Grande do Sul)
Scytalopus spillmanni: central Andes of Colombia to central Ecuador
Scytalopus superciliaris: undergrowth of Polylepis and alder woodland in the Andes of northwestern Argentina from Jujuy southward to La Rioja
Scytalopus unicolor: Andes of northern Peru (southern Cajamarca and La Libertad) and adjacent Ecuador
Scytalopus urubambae: Andes of east-central Peru (southern Cordillera Vilcabamba)
Scytalopus vicinior: Pacific slope of southwestern Colombia (Risaralda) to Ecuador (Cotopaxi)
Scytalopus whitneyi: Andes of south-central Peru (Ayacucho and Apurímac)
Scytalopus zimmeri: Andes of southern Bolivia (Chuquisaca and Tarija) and northwestern Argentina (Jujuy and Salta)

Selasphorus ardens: mountains of western Panama (Chiriquí and Veraguas)

Spermestes griseicapilla: lowland to foothill semiarid acacia thornscrub, grassland, and open woodland, from southern Ethiopia and southeastern South Sudan southward to northeastern and central Tanzania; dispersive wandering post-breeding
Spermophaga haematina: lowland undergrowth in Upper Guinea rainforest, coastal palm forest, and thickets, from Senegambia eastward through southern Nigeria to western Central African Republic, and southward to Republic of the Congo, Cabinda (northeastern Angola), and to western, northeastern, and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Spermophaga poliogenys: lowland to foothill primary forest, old secondary forest, dense understory, and swamp-forest, from southeastern Cameroon and northern Republic of the Congo eastward to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and adjacent western Uganda
Spermophaga ruficapilla: patchy in lowland to montane forest undergrowth, streams and thickets, from eastern Central African Republic and southern South Sudan southward through northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, to Burundi, and eastward to central Kenya and to the Usambara Mountains (northwestern Tanzania), and to southern Democratic Republic of the Congo and northern Angola
Sphecotheres vieilloti: Kai Islands (southeastern Moluccas), southeastern New Guinea, and northern and eastern Australia
Sphecotheres viridis: eastern Lesser Sundas (Rote, Semau, and Timor)
Spheniscus demersus: breeds coastal southern Namibia and southern South Africa; ranges to central Namibia and southeastern Africa
Spheniscus humboldti: Humboldt Current region of coastal northern Peru to central Chile
Spheniscus magellanicus: breeds coastal central Chile and central Argentina to Cape Horn and Falkland Islands; winters to southeastern Brazil
Sphenoeacus afer: disjunctly in lowland to montane coast Fynbos scrub, and grassland with proteas or bushes, of eastern Zimbabwe highlands and adjacent Mozambique, and from northeastern South Africa southward to coastal southern South Africa
Sphenopsis frontalis: humid montane forest and bamboo stands locally in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela, Sierra de Perijá, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward along the Andes of Colombia to northwestern Ecuador and in the eastern Andes southward to southeastern Peru
Sphenopsis melanotis: Andes from western Venezuela to western Ecuador
Sphenopsis ochracea: west slope of Andes of southwestern Colombia (Nariño) and western Ecuador
Sphenopsis piurae: locally in Andes of far southwestern Ecuador and northwestern Peru (Piura and La Libertad)
Sphyrapicus nuchalis: breeds southwestern Canada to southwestern USA; winters to northern Mexico and southern Baja California
Sphyrapicus ruber: mostly coniferous forest in western Canada and adjacent far southern Alaska southward along western US to southern California; winters at lower elevations from western Canada southward to northern Baja California, Mexico
Sphyrapicus thyroideus: montane coniferous and mixed coniferous-deciduous forest from far southwestern Canada southward along western US to southern California and locally in northern Baja California, Mexico, and along the Rocky Mountains to central Arizona and central New Mexico; winters in western Texas, and in Mexico southward along the Sierra Madre Occidental to northern Michoacan; in the Sierra Madre Oriental only in Chihuahua, Coahuila and Nuevo León
Sphyrapicus varius: breeds southeastern Alaska and Yukon across Canada to Newfoundland and south in USA in northern tier of states from North Dakota east, and farther south in the Appalachian Mountains; winters southeastern USA to Panama
Spilopelia chinensis: lowland to montane forest, open woodland, mangroves, cultivation, and towns, from northern Pakistan, Nepal, India, and Sri Lanka eastward to southern China (including Hainan) and Taiwan, and southward through Malayan Peninsula and Philippines to Indonesia; Himalayan populations move downslope in winter; introduced to Mauritius and Rodrigues (Mascarenes), eastern Indonesia, Australia, New Zealand, New Caledonia, Fiji, Hawaii (all main islands), and southern California
Spilopelia senegalensis: desert oases from Morocco to Egypt, Nile Valley from delta southward to Sudan; widespread in sub-Saharan Africa, from Senegal eastward to Somalia and southward to South Africa (absent from wetter forest such as the Congo basin); Arabian Peninsula eastward to India (where widespread) and Nepal and north to Transcaspia, Kazakhstan, and western China; introduced São Tomé and Príncipe, Israel, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Türkiye, Malta, and Australia
Spiloptila clamans: lowland to foothill acacia thornscrub, and arid and semiarid savanna, from Western Sahara and Mauritania eastward across Sahel to Sudan and Eritrea, and southward to northern Senegal, northern Nigeria, and northern Cameroon
Spilornis cheela: lowland to submontane forest, savanna, mangroves, and plantations, from sub-Himalayan Indian subcontinent and associated islands eastward to southern China (including Hainan), and Taiwan, and southern Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), and southward to Palawan (Philippines) and Greater Sundas, including many related islands
Spindalis zena: varied woodland types from lowlands to hills; Bahamas from Grand Bahama southward to Mayaguana, Turks and Caicos Islands, Cuba and satellite islands, Cozumel (off Yucatan Peninsula), and Grand Cayman (Cayman Islands)
Spinus atratus: Andes of central Peru to northern Chile and Argentina
Spinus atriceps: coniferous forest of southern Mexico (Chiapas) and western Guatemala
Spinus barbatus: central Chile and southern Argentina to Tierra del Fuego and Falkland Islands
Spinus crassirostris: montane shrubby steppe, scattered woodland (including Polylepis), and shrubland from the western Andes of north-central Peru (Ancash) southward to western Bolivia and adjacent Chile, and from the Andes of central Bolivia (Cochabamba) southward to northwestern Argentina (to Mendoza) and adjacent central Chile
Spinus cucullatus: northeastern Colombia, northern Venezuela, and southwestern Guyana; local and threatened
Spinus lawrencei: breeds southern California and northwestern Baja; winters to Texas and northern Sonora
Spinus magellanicus: disjunctly in dry to humid montane woodland and scrub, and open areas with trees, in tepuis of southern Venezuela, far northern Brazil (Roraima), and adjacent Guyana, in the central Andes of Colombia and locally in the western Andes southward through Peru, where also reaches the Pacific coast, to far northern Chile, across Bolivia and in the Cerrado, Caatinga, and Atlantic Forest of central and eastern Brazil, from Tocantins southward to central Argentina (to Río Negro)
Spinus notatus: forest and edge of hills and mountains in Mexico southward from southern Sonora in the west and southern Tamaulipas in the east, southward through southern Mexico (except northern Yucatan Peninsula), Guatemala, west-central Belize, and Honduras to northern Nicaragua
Spinus olivaceus: east slope of Andes of southeastern Ecuador to Peru and western Bolivia (La Paz and Cochabamba)
Spinus pinus: breeds open coniferous forest, mixed coniferous-deciduous forest, and woodland from southern Alaska eastward to Newfoundland and Labrador (northeastern Canada), southward in western USA to mountains in northern Baja California (northwestern Mexico), throughout mountains of western and central USA and Mexico southward to western Guatemala, and northeastern USA (Minnesota to Maine); winters irregularly across the Great Plains and eastern USA southward to central Mexico
Spinus psaltria: varied woodland, scrub, and forest-edge habitats and agricultural fields from western USA, from central Washington to southern Wyoming and southward to southern Texas, Baja California, and through mountains of Mexico to northern Nicaragua, also in Yucatan Peninsula, southwestern Costa Rica and Panama, Sierra de Perijá, Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, central Venezuela, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward along the Andes of Colombia to northern Ecuador and from southern Ecuador to north-central Peru (to Ancash)
Spinus siemiradzkii: southwestern Ecuador including Isla Puná, and far northwestern Peru (Tumbes)
Spinus spinescens: Andean grassland in paramos from northwestern Venezuela southward to the high Andes of northeastern Colombia, including the Sierra de Perijá and Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, and in the western and central Andes of Colombia southward to far northern Ecuador (Carchi)
Spinus spinus: breeds northern Palearctic; winters southward to Mediterranean region, China, and Ryukyu Islands
Spinus thibetanus: breeds montane coniferous forest of southeastern Tibet, Sichuan, northern Myanmar, and northwestern Yunnan (southwestern China); winters to lower elevations, from western Nepal to Arunachal Pradesh (northeastern India)
Spinus tristis: breeds in weedy and grassy fields, orchards, bushy areas, and gardens from southern British Columbia eastward to southwestern Newfoundland (southwestern to southeastern Canada) southward through southern California and to northern Louisiana and Georgia; winters southward to northern Baja California and northern (northwestern Mexico), Veracruz (eastern Mexico), and southern Florida
Spinus uropygialis: Andes of central Peru to northwestern Argentina and northern Chile
Spinus xanthogastrus: highly disjunct in humid to semi-humid woodland, forest borders, and scrub in the mountains of Costa Rica and western Panama, in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela, and in the Andes of western Venezuela southward along all Andes of Colombia to the western Andes of Ecuador and far northern Peru, and in the Andes of far southeastern Peru and Bolivia (to western Santa Cruz)
Spinus yarrellii: northern Venezuela; interior northeastern Brazil (Ceará to Bahia)
Spiza americana: breeds eastern North America; winters to southern Mexico to northern South America
Spizaetus isidori: coastal mountains of Venezuela to Andes of northwestern Argentina
Spizaetus melanoleucus: forest of southern Mexico to northern Argentina and Brazil
Spizaetus ornatus: deciduous to humid lowland to foothill forest on the Gulf of Mexico slope from northeastern Mexico and isolated on the Pacific slope in Nayarit and Jalisco, southeastward across Central America to northwestern Colombia and southward in Pacific Colombia to southwestern Ecuador; also in northern Colombia and western Venezuela and southward in the foothills of the central and western Andes of Colombia to Tolima and Valle del Cauca; east of the Andes in northern, western, and eastern Venezuela, Trinidad, and the Guianas southward across the Río Orinoco and Amazon basins to central Bolivia and southward in the Yungas to far northwestern Argentina; also in the Cerrado of interior Brazil from southern Maranhão, and Atlantic Forest from southern Bahia, southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul, northeastern Argentina, and eastern Paraguay
Spizaetus tyrannus: humid forest from the Gulf of Mexico slope in southeastern Mexico southeastward across Central America to eastern Panama, including the Pacific slope of Costa Rica and Panama; also in the Pacific lowlands in Nayarit and Jalisco, northern Colombia and western Venezuela, southward in interior Colombia to the mid- to upper Cauca and Magdalena valleys, west of the Andes from southwestern Colombia southward to southwestern Ecuador and adjacent Peru, northern and eastern Venezuela, Trinidad, and the Guianas southward across the Orinoco and Amazon basins to northern Bolivia and southern Mato Grosso, Brazil; in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil from Rio Grande do Norte and Paraíba southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul, eastern Paraguay, and far northeastern Argentina
Spizella atrogularis: central California through New Mexico and disjunctly southward to central Baja California through northern Oaxaca; withdraws from north in winter
Spizella breweri: breeds mainly in sagebrush, except in the northern mountains, where breeds in dwarf willow and birch, from southeastern Alaska and northwestern Canada southward to southern California and eastward to western North Dakota and northern New Mexico; winters in southwestern USA southward to southern Baja California and Guanajuato and Queretaro (central Mexico)
Spizella pallida: breeds western Canada and USA; winters to Guatemala
Spizella passerina: breeds open coniferous forest, woodland and groves with grassy and shrubby undergrowth, including human-modified habitats and towns, from eastern Alaska eastward to southern Newfoundland (eastern Canada) and southward to northern Baja California, through mountains of Mexico to northeastern Nicaragua, the Gulf coast, and northern Florida; Central American populations resident; northern populations winter in southern USA and northern Mexico
Spizella pusilla: breeds southeastern Canada to central and eastern USA; winters to northeastern Mexico
Spizella wortheni: northeastern Mexico (Coahuila to Nuevo León, Zacatecas, and Veracruz)
Spizelloides arborea: breeds in open scrub and tundra with scattered shrubs from northern Alaska eastward to northern Labrador (northeastern Canada), southward to northern British Columbia and central Quebec (southern Canada); winters across southern Canada to west-central and eastern USA southward to eastern New Mexico and northern Georgia
Spiziapteryx circumcincta: Chaco of northern Argentina, western Paraguay, and eastern Bolivia
Spizixos canifrons: foothill and montane open and stunted forest, montane scrub, bamboo, and brambles, from northeastern India eastward to south-central China, and southward to western and eastern Myanmar, northern Thailand, and northern Laos
Spizixos semitorques: foothill to submontane open woodland, second growth, montane scrub, and brushy ravines, in southeastern China and Taiwan
Spizocorys conirostris: lowland to submontane grassland, semiarid Karoo, and Kalahari grassy dunes and savanna, from far southern Angola, northern Namibia, and western Zambia, and southward through central Botswana to eastern South Africa; nomadic after rains
Spizocorys fremantlii: lowland to montane arid grassland, short grazed grassland, and semiarid scrub, from Ethiopia and northern Somalia southward to southern Kenya and adjacent northern Tanzania
Spizocorys fringillaris: foothill short grassland, and grazed areas with bare patches, in east-central South Africa
Spizocorys obbiensis: lowland vegetated coastal dunes, open grazed grassland on coastal plains, and open scrubby grassland away from coast, in coastal central Somalia
Spizocorys personata: patchy in foothill and montane sparse dry grassland on black or red lava of southern and eastern Ethiopia, and of northern and central Kenya
Spizocorys sclateri: lowland stony plains with ephemeral grassland, and scattered open scrub in bare stony Karoo, in southern Namibia and interior western South Africa
Spizocorys starki: lowland arid and semiarid grassland on gravel and hard limestone, and lightly-shrubbed grassy plains, from western Angola coastal plain southward through Namibia to southwestern Botswana and northwestern South Africa; nomadic dispersal after rains
Spodiopsar cineraceus: northeastern Asia; winters in southern China and Philippines
Spodiopsar sericeus: lowlands of south-central China; winters to southeastern Asia and Philippines
Sporathraupis cyanocephala: montane cloudforest and foothill forest in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (eastward to Paria Peninsula) and Trinidad, and in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Sierra de Perijá, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward to central Bolivia
Sporophila albogularis: northeastern Brazil (Piauí and Pernambuco to northern Bahia)
Sporophila americana: southeastern Colombia to the Guianas, and Amazonian Ecuador, Peru, and Brazil
Sporophila angolensis: shrubby and grassy fields from interior Colombia (Magdalena Valley), Trinidad, the Guianas, and northern Venezuela southward across the Orinoco and Amazon basins to central Bolivia, in the Cerrado of interior Brazil, and the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil (southward to Rio Grande do Sul), eastern Paraguay, and northeastern Argentina
Sporophila ardesiaca: eastern Brazil (southern Minas Gerais, Espírito Santo, and Rio de Janeiro)
Sporophila atrirostris: damp grasslands in the western Amazon basin from southeastern Colombia southward through eastern Ecuador to southeastern Peru, and very locally in the foothills of the Andes of Bolivia (Beni)
Sporophila beltoni: breeds southern Brazil (Paraná southward to Río Grande do Sul); migrates northward to Goiás, Minas Gerais, and southwestern Bahia
Sporophila bouvreuil: eastern and central South America, from Suriname and French Guiana southward to southern Brazil
Sporophila bouvronides: breeds northern Colombia, Venezuela, Trinidad and Tobago, and the Guianas; winters to northern Amazonia
Sporophila caerulescens: northern Bolivia to Paraguay, eastern Brazil, Uruguay, and Argentina
Sporophila castaneiventris: the Guianas and southern Venezuela to northern and central Bolivia (Pando to eastern Cochabamba) and Amazonian Brazil
Sporophila cinnamomea: Paraguay to south-central Brazil, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
Sporophila collaris: flooded grassland and marshland with shrubs and tall grasses from central Brazil, in Tocantins and adjacent Pará, southward through Paraguay to northeastern Argentina and Uruguay, and westward to south-central Brazil (southern Mato Grosso and Rondônia), to northeastern Bolivia
Sporophila corvina: weedy fields, dry to damp grassland, thickets, and scrub from southern Mexico southward along the Caribbean slope of Central America and the Pacific slope from southeastern Nicaragua to northwestern Colombia, and along the Pacific lowlands of Colombia southward to northwestern Peru
Sporophila crassirostris: shrubby and grassy fields and riparian thickets from northern Colombia and northern Venezuela eastward locally through the Guianas and southward to northernmost Brazil; from southwestern Venezuela southward to eastern Ecuador and northeastern Peru, and in interior Colombia southward along the Rio Cauca and Rio Magdalena; also west of the Andes from northwestern Colombia southward to southwestern Ecuador
Sporophila falcirostris: lowlands of southeastern Brazil, Paraguay, and northeastern Argentina (Misiones)
Sporophila fringilloides: savanna of eastern Colombia to southern Venezuela and northwestern Amazonian Brazil
Sporophila frontalis: eastern Paraguay to southeastern Brazil and northeastern Argentina
Sporophila funerea: southern Mexico (Veracruz) southward (including Coiba and Pearl islands, western Panama) to western Colombia and western Ecuador
Sporophila hypochroma: locally in eastern Bolivia, Paraguay, southwestern Brazil, and northeastern Argentina
Sporophila hypoxantha: Bolivia to Paraguay, southern Brazil and northern Argentina
Sporophila iberaensis: breeds in northern Argentina (Iberá wetlands of Corrientes), also reported Paraguay and southern Brazil
Sporophila intermedia: Colombia (western Andes, Cauca, and Magdalena Valleys) to northern Venezuela, Trinidad, western Guyana, and northeastern Brazil
Sporophila leucoptera: southeastern Peru (Madre de Dios) to northwestern Bolivia (Beni and Santa Cruz), southern Suriname and Mexiana Island (off northeastern Brazil in Pará), eastern Brazil, eastern Paraguay, and northern Argentina
Sporophila lineola: breeds in northeastern Brazil, migrating to Venezuela, the Guianas, and northeastern Amazonian Brazil; also breeds from southern Bolivia to southern Brazil, southward to Paraguay and northern Argentina; migrating to Amazonia; seasonal status (migrant or resident) in some regions not clear
Sporophila luctuosa: Andes of Colombia to western Venezuela, northern Bolivia, and southwestern Brazil
Sporophila maximiliani: grassy marshes, riparian thickets and damp grassland very locally from eastern Venezuela (now rare), and at least formerly western Guyana, eastern French Guiana, and northern Brazil (no recent records), and disjunctly central and eastern Brazil (now rare)
Sporophila melanogaster: southeastern Brazil (southern Goiás and Minas Gerais to Rio Grande do Sul)
Sporophila minuta: open savanna and grassy fields, roadside, agricultural land, and shrubby fields on the Pacific slope from west-central Mexico southward to eastern Panama; northern Colombia, northern Venezuela, Trinidad, and northern Guianas eastward to northeastern Brazil in the mouth of the Amazon River and southward along eastern Venezuela to northernmost Brazil (Roraima), the llanos of southwestern Venezuela southward to eastern Colombia, in interior Colombia southward to the headwaters of the Rio Cauca and Rio Magdalena, and in northwestern Ecuador and adjacent southern Colombia
Sporophila morelleti: grassland often near water, in lowlands and hills from lower Rio Grande Valley (Texas) southward through Caribbean slope of Mexico (including Yucatan Peninsula and Cozumel); at Isthmus of Tehuantepec reaches Pacific slope and southward thence on both slopes through central Panama
Sporophila nigricollis: southern Costa Rica through South America including Trinidad and Tobago, and Grenada, to Brazil and northeastern Argentina
Sporophila nigrorufa: far eastern Bolivia and southwestern Brazil (Mato Grosso)
Sporophila nuttingi: Caribbean lowlands of Nicaragua, Costa Rica, and western Panama
Sporophila palustris: locally in Paraguay, southern Brazil, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
Sporophila peruviana: arid scrub and grassy fields from western Ecuador (Manabí) southward to southwestern Peru (Ica)
Sporophila pileata: eastern Paraguay to southern Brazil (southern Mato Grosso) and northeastern Argentina
Sporophila plumbea: northern Colombia (Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta and lower Magdalena Valley), llanos of eastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, the Guianas, and northern Brazil, and southeastern Peru to northern Bolivia, eastern Paraguay, southern Brazil, and northeastern Argentina
Sporophila ruficollis: southeastern Bolivia (southeastern Tarija), southwestern Brazil (western Mato Grosso do Sul, southern Rio Grande do Sul), Paraguay, northern Argentina (Salta eastward to Corrientes, southward to Tucumán, northern Córdoba and northern Buenos Aires), and western Uruguay; non-breeding to northern and eastern Bolivia and central and southern Brazil (eastward to Minas Gerais, and southward to Rio Grande do Sul)
Sporophila schistacea: Belize and Guatemala to northern Brazil and northwestern Bolivia
Sporophila simplex: arid southern Ecuador; upper Marañón Valley of northern Peru southward to Ica
Sporophila telasco: coastal lowlands of southwestern Colombia to far northern Chile (Tarapacá)
Sporophila torqueola: Pacific slope of Mexico from southern Sonora southward to Nayarit, thence also the transvolcanic belt to San Luis Potosí, and southward to southern Oaxaca
Sporopipes frontalis: lowland to montane thornscrub, acacia thickets, and villages, from southern Mauritania eastward across the Sahel to Eritrea and Ethiopia, and southward to western Uganda and south-central Tanzania; some dispersal in non-breeding season
Sporopipes squamifrons: lowland to foothill dry savanna, thornscrub, open mopane woodland, arid Karoo, and gardens, from western and southern Angola eastward to southern Zambia and Zimbabwe, and southward to northern and central South Africa
Stachyris grammiceps: locally in forest of western Java
Stachyris humei: Himalayas from Sikkim to northern Assam (north of the Brahmaputra)
Stachyris maculata: Malay Peninsula, Sumatra and satellite islands, and Borneo
Stachyris nigriceps: foothill to submontane understory in broadleaf evergreen forest, secondary growth, and bamboo scrub, from Nepal eastward through Himalayas to south-central China and northern Vietnam, and southward to Borneo, Sumatra, and satellite islands
Stachyris nigricollis: forest of Thai-Malay Peninsula, eastern Sumatra, and Borneo
Stachyris nonggangensis: limestone hills of southwestern Guangxi (southeastern China), and in adjacent far northeastern Vietnam (eastern Tonkin)
Stachyris oglei: mountains of northeastern India (northeastern Assam and southeastern Arunachal Pradesh)
Stachyris poliocephala: peninsular Thailand, Malayan Peninsula, Sumatra, Lingga Archipelago, and Borneo
Stachyris roberti: hill forest of southern Assam (south of the Brahmaputra) to northeastern Myanmar
Stachyris strialata: lowland to submontane understory in broadleaf evergreen forest, secondary growth, and bamboo, from eastern Myanmar eastward to south-central China (including Hainan), and southward to peninsular Thailand and Sumatra
Stactolaema anchietae: foothill and submontane miombo woodland, riverine woods, and forest edge, from Angola eastward to southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northern Zambia
Stactolaema leucotis: foothill and submontane forest, miombo woodland, and plantations with fruiting trees, from central and southeastern Kenya southward through eastern Tanzania, Malawi, and eastern Zimbabwe to Eswatini and southeastern South Africa
Stactolaema whytii: patchy in foothill miombo woodland from southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, eastern Zambia, and southwestern Tanzania, and southward to Malawi, northern Zimbabwe, and adjacent Mozambique
Stagonopleura guttata: southeastern Australia (central Queensland coast to Eyre Peninsula)
Stagonopleura oculata: southwestern Australia (Avon Valley to Cape Arid, Western Australia)
Staphida castaniceps: foothill understory of broadleaf evergreen forest, and scrub in secondary growth, from northeastern India and Bhutan eastward through Himalayas to northern Myanmar and adjacent China, and southward to southeastern Myanmar and western Thailand
Staphida torqueola: northern plateau of Thailand to southern China and northern Indochina
Starnoenas cyanocephala: lowlands of Cuba (in danger of extinction)
Steatornis caripensis: locally from Panama and northern South America including Trinidad to western Bolivia
Stelgidillas gracilirostris: lowland to montane forest, farmbush, and wooded savanna, from southwestern Senegal eastward through southern Nigeria and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to southern South Sudan and central Kenya, thence southward to northwestern Angola and western Tanzania
Stelgidopteryx ruficollis: open areas often near water in lowlands and hills of southeastern Honduras through northern Argentina and Uruguay
Stelgidopteryx serripennis: breeds in open areas, often near water and rocky outcrops, gorges, and embankments, from southeastern Alaska and western British Columbia eastward to southern New Brunswick (southwestern to southeastern Canada) and southward to northern Baja California, Pacific and Atlantic slopes of Mexico, southern Mexico (including Yucatan Peninsula) to central Costa Rica, Gulf coast, and southern Florida; populations from Canada and USA winter in the Greater Antilles more widely and Mexico to central Panama
Stenostira scita: breeds scrub and fynbos of hills and mountains of southern South Africa; non-breeders reach southern Namibia to Zimbabwe
Stephanophorus diadematus: Paraguay to southeastern Brazil, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
Stephanoxis lalandi: eastern Brazil (southern Minas Gerais to Espírito Santo and northeastern São Paulo)
Stephanoxis loddigesii: eastern Paraguay and northeastern Argentina (Misiones) to southern Brazil
Stercorarius antarcticus: southern oceans and coasts from coastal southern Argentina, Falkland Islands, Tristan da Cunha group (south-central South Atlantic), subantarctic and Antarctic islands from Cape Horn to New Zealand region
Stercorarius chilensis: breeds coasts of southern Chile and southern Argentina; ranges north to coasts of southern Peru and central Brazil
Stercorarius longicaudus: breeds Holarctic high and low Arctic tundra, locally in subarctic, from northwestern and southeastern Greenland, Arctic northern Scandinavia to northeastern Siberia and Kamchatka (eastern Russia); Arctic, western, and southern Alaska through Arctic Canada to Ellesmere and Baffin islands; in winter highly pelagic and mostly occurs southerly, to offshore subantarctic and subtropical waters off Africa, Madagascar, southern Australia, Peru, Chile, and east-central Argentina
Stercorarius maccormicki: breeds coastal Antarctica, especially Ross Sea; also South Shetland and South Orkney islands (off Antarctic Peninsula); winters to northern offshore waters and North Indian Ocean: mostly clockwise to Japanese and Korean waters and Gulf Stream of eastern USA, then southwestern Canada to northern Baja California and northwestern Africa
