Stercorarius pomarinus: breeds high Arctic tundra, mainly northwestern to northeastern Russia (including many high Arctic islands), northern and southwestern Alaska, eastward through Arctic Canada to Baffin Island (northeastern Canada); winters to temperate to tropical coasts and offshore waters worldwide
Stercorarius skua: breeds Iceland, Faroe Islands, Ireland, Scotland, Norway including Svalbard, and northwestern Russia to Novaya Zemlya; winters North Atlantic Ocean offshore waters to central Gulf Stream of New England to North Carolina, northeastern Brazil, North Sea to Iberian Peninsula, western Mediterranean, Atlantic islands, and western Africa
Sterna acuticauda: inland Indus Valley (Pakistan), sub-Himalayan India and Ayeyarwady River (central Myanmar); formerly to southern China and Vietnam
Sterna aurantia: rivers of Indus Valley (Pakistan), sub-Himalayan India, northwestern and central Myanmar, southwestern China, and southeastern Cambodia (formerly also southern Vietnam)
Sterna dougallii: patchily temperate to tropical Atlantic, tropical Indian, and subtropical to tropical western Pacific to Vanuatu
Sterna forsteri: breeds inland central Alberta eastward to central Manitoba (south-central Canada) patchily southward to northern Baja California (northwestern Mexico), Colorado, and the Great Lakes, also North Atlantic coast from New Jersey to North Carolina, and Gulf coast southward to northern Tamaulipas (northeastern Mexico); winters to Gulf coast, Bahamas, Cuba, and southern Mexico
Sterna hirundinacea: coasts and islands of southern South America and Falkland Islands
Sterna hirundo: widespread, subarctic, temperate, and locally tropical Northern Hemisphere; winters coastally to southern Africa, western Madagascar, southern Australia, and southeastern South America
Sterna paradisaea: breeds circumpolarly, Arctic coasts and inland, from Greenland, Iceland, and British Isles eastward to Kamchatka (eastern Russia), through Aleutians, Alaska mainland through Arctic and subarctic Canada to southeastern Canada; winters subantarctic and Antarctic Ocean to edge of pack-ice
Sterna repressa: coastal Kenya to Persian Gulf, Red Sea, and coastal Pakistan
Sterna striata: breeds coastal New Zealand, including Chatham and Auckland islands, also Furneaux group in Bass Strait; winters to southeastern Australia including Tasmania
Sterna sumatrana: islands off tropical Indian and Pacific oceans from Seychelles to Cook Islands (eastern Polynesia)
Sterna trudeaui: coastal lagoons and marshes of coastal Aconcagua to Llanquihue (central Chile) and southeastern Brazil and Uruguay to inland east-central Argentina
Sterna virgata: subantarctic islands of western and central South Indian Ocean: Crozet, Prince Edward, and Kerguelen islands
Sterna vittata: widespread in subantarctic and Antarctic islands of South Atlantic, South Indian, western South Pacific, and Antarctic Peninsula; winters north to southern Brazil and southern South Africa
Sternoclyta cyanopectus: Andes of western Venezuela and coastal cordillera eastward to Miranda
Sternula albifrons: breeds southwestern Europe and southwestern Russia, central Asia, Mongolia to southeastern Russia, Japan (Honshu to Ryukyu Islands), eastern China, Taiwan, and Vietnam; northern and western Africa; Persian Gulf and Iraq to Indus Valley (Pakistan) and Gangetic Plain (north-central India); Sri Lanka; Gulf of Thailand, Malayan Peninsula, Singapore, and islands off Greater Sundas; off New Britain (southeastern Bismarck Archipelago), Bougainville (northern Solomon Archipelago); coastal Australia including Tasmania; and Saipan (southern Northern Mariana Islands, northwestern Micronesia); winters in southern portions of range
Sternula antillarum: Great Plains to Texas and northern Louisiana; central California and Gulf of California coasts to Oaxaca (western Mexico), El Salvador, and Nicaragua; western North Atlantic coast from Maine to Florida, Gulf of Mexico, and Caribbean Sea from Bahamas to Lesser Antilles, islands off Yucatan Peninsula, Belize, and northern Honduras, and islands north of Venezuela; winters to coasts of northern South America
Sternula balaenarum: breeds coastal Namibia to Cape Province; winters to northern Angola
Sternula lorata: breeds patchily on arid Humboldt Current coasts of central Ecuador southward to northern Chile; winters coastally in same region
Sternula nereis: western to southeastern Australia, northern North Island (New Zealand), and New Caledonia
Sternula saundersi: breeds Red Sea and Persian Gulf to islands between India and Sri Lanka; apparently winters mainly Seychelles to Maldives and Cocos (Keeling) Islands
Sternula superciliaris: breeds large rivers from northern Colombia eastward to Guianas and southward to northeastern Peru and east-central Argentina; non-breeders concentrate mainly on coast and estuaries
Sterrhoptilus affinis: Philippines (southern Sierra Madre Mountains of southern Luzon)
Sterrhoptilus capitalis: East Visayas and Mindanao group (east-central and southern Philippines)
Sterrhoptilus dennistouni: northern Philippines (Sierra Madre Mountains of northern Luzon)
Stigmatura bahiae: northeastern Brazil (Ceará and Rio Grande do Norte southward to southern Bahia)
Stigmatura budytoides: arid scrub and woodland, Chaco woodland, monte desert, and gallery forest in Caatinga of northeastern Brazil (southern Ceará and Piauí southward to northern Minas Gerais), central and southeastern Bolivia, and western Paraguay southward to central Argentina (Río Negro and eastern Chubut)
Stigmatura napensis: along larger rivers of western and central Amazonia from eastern Ecuador (Napo River) and eastern Peru (Río Napo, Río Ucayali, and Amazon River) eastward to central Brazil (to the lower Río Tapajós); also a population (possibly an undescribed taxon) in Río Orinoco drainages in far eastern Colombia (Vichada) and southwestern Venezuela (western Amazonas)
Stilpnia argyrofenges: humid montane forest in the eastern Andes from southeastern Ecuador southward to northeastern Peru and in southeastern Peru southward to south-central Bolivia
Stilpnia cayana: open and semi-open areas near semi-humid to dry forest, gallery forest, woodland savanna, white-sand forest, campo grasslands, and gardens and parks from northeastern Colombia eastward to northern and eastern Venezuela, northern Guianas, and northeastern Brazil westward to the llanos of northeastern Colombia; and in the Cerrado, Caatinga, and Atlantic Forest regions from northeastern Brazil southward to northern Paraná, southern Mato Grosso, northern Bolivia, southeasternmost Peru, eastern Paraguay, and northeasternmost Argentina; also isolated in the Rio Mayo valley of northern Peru
Stilpnia cucullata: scrub to forest at all elevations, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, and Grenada (southern Lesser Antilles)
Stilpnia cyanicollis: humid lowland and montane forest, gallery forest, and woodland in the coastal mountains of northwestern Venezuela, Sierra de Perijá, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward to northern Peru north of the Río Marañón; in western Ecuador and adjacent southwestern Colombia down to the lowlands, the eastern Andes of Peru south of the Río Marañón, southward to central Bolivia, the Cerrado and southern Amazon basin of Brazil (southeastern Pará and northern Tocantins southward to southern Mato Grosso), and adjacent northeastern Bolivia
Stilpnia cyanoptera: mountains of northern Colombia including Santa Marta region to northeastern Venezuela
Stilpnia heinei: mountains of northern Colombia to northern Venezuela and northern Ecuador
Stilpnia larvata: humid forest from southeastern Mexico southward along the Caribbean slope of Central America and the Pacific slope of Costa Rica and Panama to northwestern Colombia; in interior Colombia eastward to the upper Magdalena Valley in Tolima, and west of the Andes southward to northwestern Ecuador
Stilpnia meyerdeschauenseei: east slope of Andes of far southeastern Peru (Puno)
Stilpnia nigrocincta: southeastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, Guyana, northern Bolivia, and western Brazil
Stilpnia peruviana: lowlands of southeastern Brazil (Rio de Janeiro to Santa Catarina)
Stilpnia phillipsi: Andes of eastern Peru (Cerros del Sira in eastern Huánuco)
Stilpnia preciosa: eastern Paraguay to southeastern Brazil, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
Stilpnia viridicollis: humid to dry montane forest and scrub in the Andes from southern Ecuador southward to northern Peru and along the eastern Andes from northeastern Peru southward to western Bolivia
Stilpnia vitriolina: arid scrub of western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador
Stilpnia whitelyi: tepuis of southern Venezuela (in Amazonas and Bolívar), adjacent northern Brazil, and southwestern Guyana (Mount Twek-quay)
Stiphrornis erythrothorax: lowland to foothill understory of Upper Guinea rainforest, gallery forest, and forest patches in savanna, from Guinea and Sierra Leone eastward to central Nigeria, Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), and southern Cameroon, and southward to central and eastern Gabon
Stiphrornis mabirae: lowland to montane understory of Congolian rainforest, and forest patches in savanna, from northern Republic of Congo, possibly southwestern Central African Republic, and eastward to southern South Sudan and western Uganda, southward to central Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northwestern Tanzania; reported western Kenya
Stiphrornis pyrrholaemus: lowland primary forest understory in Gabon and southwestern Republic of the Congo
Stipiturus mallee: southeastern Australia (west-central Victoria, formerly southeastern South Australia)
Stipiturus ruficeps: arid central Australia (Pilbara region through southern Northern Territory to southwestern Queensland)
Stizorhina finschi: lowland to foothill dense understory of primary and secondary forest, and swamp forest, from Sierra Leone and southeastern Guinea eastward to southwestern Nigeria
Stizorhina fraseri: lowland and foothill primary and old secondary forest from southeastern Nigeria and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) eastward to southern South Sudan and Uganda, and southward to northwestern Angola and northwestern Zambia
Stomiopera unicolor: northern Australia (Kimberley region to Sarina, northern Queensland)
Strepera fuliginosa: Tasmania and Bass Strait islands (southeastern Australia)
Strepera graculina: eastern Australia and Lord Howe Island (east of Australia)
Strepera versicolor: southern Australia, including Kangaroo Island and Tasmania (southeastern Australia)
Streptopelia bitorquata: Java, Bali, and Lombok to Sumbawa, Flores, Solor, and Timor
Streptopelia capicola: widespread in open country and savanna from Gabon eastward (except rainforest) through central Sudan and Ethiopia to Eritrea, Djibouti, and Sudan, and southward to South Africa; introduced in Comoro Islands including Mayotte
Streptopelia decaocto: naturally occurring or recently expanded range is Europe to Middle East, India, Sri Lanka, western China, and Korean Peninsula; introduced in Japan (central Hokkaido), eastern China (including Hong Kong), Taiwan, southern Canada, most of USA including southern Alaska, the West Indies, and northern Mexico to Panama
Streptopelia decipiens: arid habitats near water in the Sahel from southern Mauritania through Sudan to Eritrea, southward in thornscrub and riparian woods through Ethiopia and western Somalia to East Africa, and from northwest Angola and northwestern Namibia to northeastern South Africa (Limpopo River basin)
Streptopelia dusumieri: Philippines (including Sulu Archipelago); introduced to northern Marianas (Saipan southward to Guam)
Streptopelia hypopyrrha: highlands of eastern Nigeria, northern Cameroon, and far southwestern Chad
Streptopelia lugens: montane forest of eastern Africa and southwestern Arabia
Streptopelia orientalis: lowland to subalpine montane forest, scrub, wooded farmland, and oak or bamboo woodland, from Ural Mountains (southern Russia) eastward to central Siberia and Sakhalin (Russia), southward to central India, northern Vietnam, southern China (including Hainan), Taiwan, and Japan (Hokkaido to Ryukyu and Izu islands); northern populations migrate southward to tropics
Streptopelia reichenowi: borassus palm regions of southeastern Ethiopia and southwestern Somalia
Streptopelia roseogrisea: arid habitats near water in the Sahel from Mauritania and Guinea-Bissau through southern Algeria and northern Cameroon to Sudan, Ethiopia, and Somalia, and southwestern Arabian Peninsula, with recent northward expansion along Red Sea coasts of Egypt and Saudi Arabia; widely introduced to New Zealand, Puerto Rico, New Providence (Bahamas), Mexico (Guerrero), Spain, and the Canary Islands as "Ringed Turtle Dove," escapees often noted in the southern USA and southern Europe
Streptopelia tranquebarica: lowland to foothill open country with trees, scrub, and dry woodland, from Pakistan eastward to southern Japan (southern Ryukyu Islands), southern China (including Hainan), and Taiwan, and southward to south-central India, Sri Lanka, Andaman Islands, southeastern Asia, and northern Philippines; some northern populations migratory to southern Asia; introduced to Malayan Peninsula, Sulawesi, and Palawan (southwestern Philippines)
Streptopelia turtur: lowland to foothill open woodland, steppe, heath, semi-desert, and date-palm oases, from British Isles and Poland eastward to western Siberia (Russia) and northwestern China, southward to northwestern Africa, the Canary Islands, the Nile Valley (Egypt), Arabian Peninsula, and Iran; most populations migratory, wintering from Senegambia eastward across the Sahel to Eritrea and Ethiopia
Streptoprocne biscutata: dry to humid tropical forest near waterfalls and caves from northeastern Brazil (Ceará), southward along the Atlantic Forest, Caatinga, and Cerrado (to northern Rio Grande do Sul, western Santa Catarina, and western Paraná), northeasternmost Argentina, and adjacent Paraguay
Streptoprocne phelpsi: tepuis of southern Venezuela, adjacent northwestern Guyana, and northern Brazil (Roraima)
Streptoprocne rutila: western Mexico (Durango, Sinaloa, and Zacatecas southward to Panama, Venezuela (Andes and coastal ranges), Trinidad, and Andes from Colombia to Bolivia
Streptoprocne semicollaris: mountains of western Mexico (Chihuahua to Nayarit, Hidalgo, and Morelos)
Streptoprocne zonaris: southern Mexico and Caribbean to Bolivia, southern Brazil, Paraguay, and northern Argentina
Strigops habroptilus: now mostly Codfish Island (=Whenua Hou, west of Stewart Island); formerly North, South, and Stewart islands (New Zealand); extremely rare and intensively managed
Strix albitarsis: Andes of Colombia to Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, and Bolivia
Strix aluco: Europe from Britain and Scotland through southern Fennoscandia to western Siberia, southward to the southernmost Iberian Peninsula, through the Levant, western Iran, and the western Himalayas eastward to Kashmir
Strix butleri: distribution poorly known; documented from northeastern United Arab Emirates, northern Oman, northeastern Iran, and southwestern Pakistan
Strix chacoensis: Chaco of southern Bolivia, western Paraguay, and northern Argentina
Strix fulvescens: mountains of southern Mexico (eastern Oaxaca and Chiapas) to El Salvador
Strix hadorami: desert of northern Egypt, Sinai Peninsula, Syria, Jordan, and Arabian Peninsula
Strix huhula: humid forest in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward across the Amazon basin to eastern Peru and central Bolivia, and southward in the Yungas to northwestern Argentina (Salta and Jujuy), in Brazil eastward to the Cerrado from easternmost Piauí southward to central Brazil, and in the Atlantic Forest region from central Bahia southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul, northeastern Argentina, and eastern Paraguay
Strix hylophila: Paraguay to southeastern Brazil (Minas Gerais) and far northeastern Argentina
Strix leptogrammica: patchy in lowland to submontane forest, especially primary forest, and densely wooded gardens, from northwestern India eastward through Himalayan foothills to southern China (including Hainan) and Taiwan, and southward to southwestern India, Sri Lanka, Sumatra, Java, and Borneo, and some associated islands
Strix nebulosa: Holarctic mainly in taiga from Fennoscandia eastward to central Chukotka, southward to Poland, Belarus, and northern Ukraine, northern Mongolia, northeastern China, and Sakhalin, and boreal forest of northern North America
Strix nigrolineata: lowlands of southern Mexico to western Ecuador and far northwestern Peru
Strix nivicolum: foothill to montane coniferous forest, oak forest, and rocky forested ravines, from northeastern India eastward through the Himalayas to northeastern China and Korean Peninsula, and southward to northern Myanmar, northern Vietnam, and Taiwan; some downslope dispersal in winter
Strix occidentalis: various mature and old-growth forest types from far southwestern Canada southward across western US to southern California and (formerly) northern Baja California, Mexico, in southern US eastward to central Colorado, eastern New Mexico and adjacent Texas, and in Mexico southward to southern Jalisco and northern Michoacan
Strix ocellata: lowland to foothill open woodland, and wooded plains of northern and Peninsular India
Strix rufipes: humid Patagonian and Nothofagus forest in the Andes and coast of north-central Chile and west-central Argentina southward to Tierra del Fuego, including Chiloé Island
Strix sartorii: mountains of northern Mexico (Durango) to Veracruz and Oaxaca
Strix seloputo: patchy in lowland open forest, including second-growth and forest edge, and plantations, from southern Myanmar, eastward through Cambodia and southern Vietnam to Palawan and adjacent islands (Philippines), and southward to Sumatra, Java (extirpated?), and some associated islands
Strix uralensis: foothill to montane mature forest from Scandinavia eastward to Siberia and Sakhalin (Russia), and patchy southward to montane eastern and southern Europe, central China, Korean Peninsula, and Japan (Hokkaido to Kyushu)
Strix varia: various forest and woodland habitats in western to eastern Canada and far southern Alaska southward in western US to central California and in the Rocky Mountains southward to northeastern Oregon and south-central Idaho; in central and eastern US southward to southern Texas, the Gulf of Mexico coast, and southern Florida
Strix virgata: varied forest to wooded habitats, including towns, of lowlands to mountains from central Sonora and northern Tamaulipas through South America, in the west to southwestern Ecuador, and east of the Andes eastward to the Guianas and northeastern Brazil, and southward through eastern Peru to eastern Paraguay, northeastern Argentina, and southeastern Brazil
Strix woodfordii: lowland to montane forest, rainforest, and riparian and coastal woodland, from Senegambia eastward through Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to Ethiopia and western Somalia, and southward to southern Angola and southern South Africa
Struthio camelus: desert to savanna plains of sub-Saharan Africa (except northeast), in Sahel zone (rare in west), east through Eritrea, southward to Tanzania, and in southern Africa from southern Angola eastward to northern Zimbabwe and through the Cape region
Struthio molybdophanes: desert to savanna plains of northeastern Africa, from northern Ethiopia, Djibouti, and Somalia southward through far southeastern South Sudan, and southeastern Kenya
Sturnella lilianae: southwestern USA from northern Arizona, southern Colorado, and western Texas southward through Chihuahua (north-central Mexico) and western and central Mexico from Sinaloa and southern Durango southward to Estado de Mexico
Sturnella magna: varied grassland and savanna habitats from southeastern Canada and north-central and northeastern USA southward to the Gulf coast and southern Florida, Cuba, from southern Texas southward in eastern Mexico locally to northern and central Colombia and Venezuela, the tepuis of southern Venezuela, northern Brazil (Roraima), and adjacent Guyana, and in northern Guianas eastward to northeastern Brazil (Amapá and northern Pará); withdraws from northern tier of range in winter
Sturnella neglecta: breeds in varied native and exotic grasslands and prairies from southern Canada (central British Columbia to Saskatchewan) southward across western and central USA to northern Baja California, and in central Mexico southward to northern Jalisco and Guanajuato; largely resident but northern birds winter in the USA southward to the Gulf coast and southward to southern Baja California and central Mexico
Sturnia malabarica: southwestern, northern, central, and northeastern India (southern Assam), Nepal, southern China (Yunnan), Myanmar, northwestern and western Thailand, Laos, and Vietnam; winters to south
Sturnia pagodarum: eastern Afghanistan to Bangladesh, southern Nepal, India, and Sri Lanka
Sturnia sinensis: breeds southern China to Indochina; winters to southeastern Asia and northern Philippines
Sturnornis albofrontatus: forest of wet zone of southwestern Sri Lanka
Sturnus unicolor: Iberian Peninsula to Corsica, Sardinia, Sicily, and northwestern Africa
Sturnus vulgaris: breeds Britain and Scandinavia to central Europe, southern Siberia, northern Mongolia, Pakistan, and western Himalayas; northern populations winter to south
Sublegatus arenarum: open arid scrub, woodland, secondary scrub, and mangroves from the Pacific lowlands of northwestern Costa Rica and western to eastern Panama (including islands off Pacific coast and the canal zone), in the lowlands of northern Colombia and western Venezuela southward to the middle Magdalena Valley, the llanos of southwestern Venezuela and northeastern Colombia, and east of the Andes in northern Venezuela, Aruba, Curaçao, Bonaire, Isla Margarita, and Trinidad, eastward to coastal Guianas
Sublegatus modestus: breeds in open and deciduous woodland and scrub from northern and eastern Bolivia and southern Brazil southward through Paraguay and Uruguay to south-central Argentina (to Río Negro); winters from far northern Argentina northward to southeastern Peru, northern Bolivia, and northeastern Brazil, and more locally in the Amazon basin to southern Guyana and Suriname
Sublegatus obscurior: eastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, the Guianas, northern Bolivia, and Amazonian Brazil
Sugomel nigrum: western and central Australia (central Western Australia eastward to southwestern Queensland and northwestern Victoria)
Suiriri suiriri: open woodland and shrubs in the Sipaliwini savanna in southern Suriname and in the Cerrado and Caatinga from northeastern Brazil (Maranhão to Ceará) southwestward to eastern and central Bolivia and Paraguay, Uruguay, and northern Argentina, southward to northern Buenos Aires and Mendoza, and only as breeder southward to northern Rio Negro; locally in the southern Amazon of Brazil
Sula brewsteri: breeds rocky islands and sandy atolls off southern California (Channel Islands) and western Mexico from central Baja California and Gulf of California (northwestern Mexico) to Revillagigedo and Clipperton islands, and Pacific islands off Central America and Colombia, from islands in Gulf of Fonseca (Honduras) to Gorgona Island (off Colombia); breeding range has expanded to include the northern Mariana Islands, the northern Line Islands, and the Hawaiian Islands (Northwestern eastward to Oahu, in small numbers)
Sula dactylatra: breeds islands in Red Sea and northwestern Arabian Sea, Malagasy region through Indian Ocean to Cocos (Keeling) Islands, northern Australia, Lord Howe, Norfolk, and Kermadec islands, northward to southern Ryukyu, Ogasawara (Bonin), and Iwo (Volcano) islands (southern Japan), and eastward in Pacific to Hawaiian Islands (Northwestern and islets off main islands), Easter Islands, islands off western Mexico, Cocos Island (off Costa Rica), Isla Malpelo (off Colombia), and Islas Desventuradas (off northern Chile), islands (including peripheral ones) in Caribbean, Fernando de Noronha, Abrolhos, and Trindade (off Brazil), and Ascension and St. Helena (South Atlantic)
Sula granti: breeds islands off western Mexico (Revillagigedo and Clipperton islands), Cocos Island (off Costa Rica), Isla Malpelo (off Colombia), Galapagos, Isla de la Plata (off Ecuador), and Lobos de Afuera (off northwestern Peru); ranges mainly to coastal Baja California (northwestern Mexico) and Pacific coast of Central America
Sula leucogaster: widespread tropical and subtropical ocean islands; Cabo Verde, Boatswain Bird Island (just off Ascension, south-central South Atlantic Ocean), Alcatraz Island (west of northwestern Guinea), and Gulf of Guinea islands, Caribbean islands off Yucatan Peninsula and Honduras to Panama and northern Colombia, Bahamas and Cayman Islands to Lesser Antilles, islands north of Venezuela and Tobago and off Brazil, islands off Somalia and Socotra, Aldabra, and Madagascar, and Chagos Archipelago, Cocos (Keeling), and Christmas islands (tropical Indian Ocean), islands off northern Australia, Tench (St. Matthias group, north-central Bismarck Archipelago), remote islands in Melanesia, southern Japan (Ryukyu, Izu, Ogasawara, and Iwo islands), Taiwan, offshore islands of Philippines, Vietnam, and Malaysia, in Flores and Banda seas, from Marianas and Palau through Hawaiian Islands (Northwestern and islets off main islands) and Gambier Islands (eastern Tuamotu Archipelago; eastern Polynesia)
Sula nebouxii: breeds east-central subtropical and tropical Pacific coast islands patchily from Gulf of California to northwestern Peru; non-breeders range to California and central Peru
Sula sula: breeds islands east of Brazil, Boatswain Bird Island (just off Ascension Island, south-central South Atlantic Ocean); islands off Belize and eastern Honduras; Cayman Islands through Lesser Antilles and islands north of Venezuela; small islands of Malagasy region, Chagos Archipelago, Cocos (Keeling) and Christmas islands (tropical Indian Ocean); Flores and Banda seas islands, islands northwest and east of Australia, Tench (St. Matthias Group, north-central Bismarck Archipelago), many other islands in outer Melanesia including New Caledonia, Tubbataha Reefs (west-central Philippines), Spratly Islands (South China Sea), southern Ryukyu and Iwo (Volcano) Islands (southern Japan), Taiwan, Micronesia through Hawaiian Islands (Northwestern eastward to Oahu), and Pitcairn group (eastern Polynesia); islands west of Mexico, Costa Rica, and Colombia, and Galapagos
Sula variegata: breeds islands off northern Peru (Piura) southward to central Chile (Isla Mocha); ranges along coast northward to Colombia
Surnia ulula: forested tundra, taiga, dense coniferous and mixed coniferous-deciduous forest, and woodland and forest edges from Scandinavia eastward across Russia, northern Kazakhstan, and Mongolia to southeastern Russia and northernmost China, and southward in the Altai and Tian Shan mountains of westernmost China and adjacent Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, and Alaska and northwestern Canada eastward to southeastern Canada and far northeastern US; seasonal irruptions in northern US and northern Europe
Surniculus dicruroides: Himalayan foothills, central and southern India, and Sri Lanka
Surniculus lugubris: northwestern Himalayas to southeastern China, southward to Malayan Peninsula, Greater Sundas, and Palawan group (western Philippines)
Surniculus musschenbroeki: Sulawesi region including Banggai and Sula islands (off eastern Sulawesi) and Buton (to southeast), and Halmahera, Bacan, and Obi (northern Moluccas)
Suthora alphonsiana: foothill to submontane scrub, tall grass, thickets, forest edge, and tea plantations, from west-central China southward to northern Vietnam
Suthora atrosuperciliaris: patchy in lowland to submontane bamboo in broadleaf evergreen forest, forest edge, and tall grass, from northeastern India and Bhutan eastward through Himalayas to northern Myanmar and adjacent southern China, and southward to northwestern Thailand, central Laos, and adjacent Vietnam
Suthora brunnea: eastern and east-central Myanmar eastward to southern China (western and northwestern Yunnan)
Suthora conspicillata: foothill to montane broadleaf scrub, willow thickets, bamboo, and reedbeds near forest, in central and east-central China
Suthora davidiana: disjunctly from eastern Myanmar and southern China to northern Thailand and northern Vietnam
Suthora fulvifrons: patchy in foothill to montane dense bamboo within or near forest, from central Nepal eastward through Himalayas to central China
Suthora nipalensis: patchy in foothill to montane bamboo and understory in broadleaf evergreen forest from northern India eastward through Himalayas to northern Myanmar and adjacent China, and southward to southern Myanmar, nearby Thailand, and central Vietnam
Suthora przewalskii: mountains of south-central China (southeastern Qinghai to southeastern Gansu and adjacent Sichuan)
Suthora ricketti: southern China (southern Sichuan and northern Yunnan)
Suthora verreauxi: patchy in foothill to montane bamboo in broadleaf evergreen forest, and bamboo in hemlock forest, from central and southeastern China southward to eastern Myanmar, northern Laos, and northern Vietnam, and on Taiwan
Suthora webbiana: lowland to montane scrub, marsh, bamboo thickets, and secondary growth, from northeastern China and Ussuriland (Russia) southward through Korean Peninsula and eastern China to northern Vietnam, and Taiwan
Suthora zappeyi: mountains of southern China (Washan and Omei Shan in eastern Sichuan)
Swynnertonia swynnertoni: disjunctly in lowland to montane forest understory from northeastern central Tanzania southward to eastern Zimbabwe and northern and central Mozambique
Sylvia abyssinica: patchy in montane forest understory in western Cameroon and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), and northern and western Angola, and from central Ethiopia and southern South Sudan southward through eastern Uganda and western Kenya, to southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, southern Tanzania and northern Mozambique
Sylvia atricapilla: lowland to montane deciduous or mixed forest, laurel forest, parks, and gardens, from British Isles and Scandinavia eastward to southwestern Siberia, and southward to Atlantic islands (Azores, Madeira, Canary Islands, Cabo Verde), northwestern Africa, Caucasus, and patchy in Middle East; northern populations migrate to sub-Saharan western and easterb Africa
Sylvia atriceps: disjunctly in foothill to montane forest, bamboo thickets, dense secondary growth, and plantations, in southeastern Nigeria and western and central Cameroon, and in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to southwestern Uganda, Rwanda, and Burundi
Sylvia borin: lowland to submontane understory in woodland and riparian forest, scrub, and willow thickets, from British Isles and Scandinavia eastward to central Siberia, and southward to Iberia, Caucasus, and northern Kazakhstan; migrates to sub-Saharan Africa
Sylvia galinieri: montane dense thickets in juniper woodland, giant heather, highland bamboo, and well-wooded gardens in highlands of western and central Ethiopia
Sylvia nigricapillus: foothill to submontane broadleaf evergreen forest on slopes and ravines, forest edge, and adjacent scrub, in eastern and southern South Africa and adjacent Eswatini and Lesotho; some downslope dispersal in winter
Sylvietta brachyura: lowland to montane arid thornscrub, wooded savanna, and acacia woodland, from southern Mauritania and northern Sierra Leone eastward through the Sahel to northeastern Sudan, Eritrea, Ethiopia, and Somalia, thence southward to southern Cameroon, northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and northeastern Tanzania
Sylvietta denti: lowland and hill forest edge of western Guinea through southwestern Nigeria and disjunctly from southeastern Nigeria to western Uganda and southward to northwestern Angola
Sylvietta isabellina: lowland to foothill thornscrub, and acacia thickets along watercourses, from eastern Ethiopia and northern Somalia southward through northern and eastern Kenya to far northeastern Tanzania
Sylvietta leucophrys: montane forest undergrowth and edges, and bamboo, from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, western Uganda, and western Kenya, southward to Rwanda, Burundi, and far northwestern Tanzania
Sylvietta philippae: lowland to foothill acacia thickets, and arid scrub on rocky ground or red sandy soil, in eastern and southeastern Ethiopia and adjacent Somalia
Sylvietta rufescens: lowland and foothill dry savanna, and open woodland with understory, from western Angola, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and southwestern Tanzania southward through Namibia to South Africa
Sylvietta ruficapilla: foothill wooded savanna, miombo woodland, and brushy thickets, from southeastern Gabon and central Republic of the Congo eastward through southern Democratic Republic of the Congo to far southwestern Tanzania, thence southward to central Angola and western Mozambique
Sylvietta virens: lowland to montane forest understory, mangrove edge, and savanna thickets from Senegambia eastward to southern South Sudan and western Kenya, thence southward to western Angola and far northwestern Tanzania
Sylvietta whytii: foothill to montane thornscrub, and acacia and miombo woodland, from southwestern Ethiopia, southeastern South Sudan, to central Kenya, and southward to northeastern Namibia and southern Mozambique
Sylviorthorhynchus desmurii: central and southern Chile and adjacent Argentina
Sylviorthorhynchus yanacensis: locally in Andes of central and southeastern Peru, Bolivia, and northwestern Argentina (Jujuy, Salta)
Sylviparus modestus: patchy in submontane to montane oak and rhododendron forest, conifer forest, and alpine moss scrub, from Kashmir eastward to southeastern China, and southward to western Myanmar, northwestern Thailand, and southern Vietnam; downslope movement in winter
Syma megarhyncha: montane west-central to northeastern (Huon Peninsula) and southeastern New Guinea
Syma torotoro: New Guinea and satellite islands, and northeastern Australia
Symposiachrus barbatus: Bougainville, Guadalcanal, Choiseul, and Santa Isabel (northern Solomon Islands)
Symposiachrus brehmii: Biak (Cenderawasih Bay, off northwestern New Guinea)
Symposiachrus browni: west-central Solomon Islands (except Ranongga and Vella Lavella)
Symposiachrus guttula: New Guinea, including Raja Ampat Islands (off western New Guinea), and Louisiade Archipelago (off southeastern New Guinea)
Symposiachrus julianae: Kofiau (Raja Ampat Islands, off western New Guinea)
Symposiachrus leucurus: Kai Islands (Kai Kecil, Kai Besar, and Baer)
Symposiachrus manadensis: patchily distributed lowland forest of New Guinea
Symposiachrus melanopterus: D'Entrecasteaux and Louisiade archipelagoes and some Milne Bay islands (off southeastern New Guinea)
Symposiachrus menckei: Mussau, in St. Matthias group (north-central Bismarck Archipelago)
Symposiachrus mundus: eastern Lesser Sundas (Babar, Damar, Larat, Yamdena, and Selaru)
Symposiachrus nigrotectus: Ranongga and Vella Lavella (west-central Solomon Islands)
Symposiachrus rubiensis: lowlands of western New Guinea (absent from Bird's Head Peninsula)
Symposiachrus trivirgatus: Lesser Sundas and eastern Australia; some winter to southern New Guinea

Tringa stagnatilis: breeds freshwater marshes from eastern Poland and Baltic states eastward through southern Russia and northern Kazakhstan to Amurland and northeastern China; winters wetlands from Africa eastward through southern Asia to southern Japan (Ryukyu Islands) and Mariana Islands, and southward to Australia
Tringa totanus: breeds subarctic to temperate coastal and inland marshes and meadows from Iceland to northern Scandinavia and southward to Iberian Peninsula and coastal Tunisia, in north from Baltics, southwestern Russia, Kazakhstan, and northern Mongolia eastward to Amurland (southeastern Russia), southward through northern Middle East, most of central Asia, Himalayas, Tibetan Plateau, and eastward to northeastern China and far northern Japan (eastern Hokkaido); winters temperate to tropical inland and coastal wetlands from southern British Isles, Africa (except southern), Middle East, southern Asia to eastern China, Philippines, Taiwan, and Ryukyu Islands (southern Japan), and Indonesian Archipelago
Trochalopteron affine: montane understory in broadleaf evergreen and mixed forest, scrub oak and bamboo, and dwarf rhododendron scrub above timberline, from Nepal eastward through Himalayas to central China, and southward to northern Vietnam and adjacent Laos; downslope dispersal post-breeding
Trochalopteron austeni: foothill to montane understory of broadleaf evergreen forest, rhododendron thickets, secondary growth, and bamboo, from northeastern India southward to western Myanmar
Trochalopteron chrysopterum: patchy in foothill to montane understory in forest, bamboo thickets, and dwarf rhododendron scrub, from northeastern India eastward to south-central China, and southward to western Myanmar
Trochalopteron erythrocephalum: foothill to montane understory of broadleaf and coniferous forest, dwarf rhododendron scrub, and bramble, from northern India eastward through Himalayas to southeastern Tibet; some downslope dispersal post-breeding
Trochalopteron formosum: disjunctly in foothill to montane understory of broadleaf evergreen forest, secondary growth, and bamboo scrub, in south-central China, and in northern Vietnam and adjacent southern China
Trochalopteron henrici: semiarid montane scrub of western China (southwestern Xinjiang and southeastern Tibet)
Trochalopteron lineatum: foothill to montane scrub in open forest, scrubby juniper and pine forest, and gardens, from Tajikistan and eastern Afghanistan eastward through Himalayas to northeastern India, and southward to western Pakistan
Trochalopteron melanostigma: southeastern Asia from eastern Myanmar through northern Vietnam, and southern Yunnan
Trochalopteron milnei: foothill to submontane understory of broadleaf evergreen forest, dense secondary growth, and bamboo scrub, from eastern Myanmar eastward to southeastern China, and southward to central Vietnam and southeastern Laos
Trochalopteron ngoclinhense: western highlands of Vietnam (Mount Ngoc Linh)
Trochalopteron peninsulae: high mountains of peninsular Thailand and Malayan Peninsula
Trochalopteron squamatum: montane forest of Nepal to southwestern China, Myanmar, and northwestern Tonkin
Trochalopteron subunicolor: montane understory in broadleaf evergreen forest, bramble and rhododendron thickets, and bamboo, from central Nepal eastward through Himalayas to southern China and adjacent northern Vietnam
Trochalopteron variegatum: submontane to montane open forest, dense rhododendron and bamboo scrub, and dwarf rhododendron at or above tree-line, from northeastern Afghanistan and adjacent Pakistan eastward through Himalayas to Nepal
Trochalopteron virgatum: mountains of northeastern India (Assam) and southwestern Myanmar (Chin Hills)
Trochilus scitulus: far eastern Jamaica (east of the Río Grande Valley and the Morant River Valley, and the easternmost Blue Mountains)
Trochocercus cyanomelas: lowland to montane forest understory, coastal thickets, and sand forest, from Uganda and southern Somalia southward through southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, eastern Tanzania, and Unguja (in Zanzibar), to eastern and coastal southern South Africa
Trochocercus nitens: lowland to lower montane primary and secondary forest understory from Guinea and Sierra Leone eastward to southern South Sudan, and southward to northern Angola and southeastern Uganda; recorded in far northwestern Tanzania
Troglodytes aedon: deciduous forest and edges, shrubby areas near water, woodland, gardens, and parks from southwestern and southeastern Canada southward across most US to southern Arizona, New Mexico, northern Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina and northern Baja California in Mexico; also along the Sierra Madre Occidental and Oriental southward to southern Mexico; northern populations winter in southern US and Mexico to the Isthmus of Tehuantepec
Troglodytes browni: upper tree zone and páramo of high mountains of central Costa Rica to western Panama
Troglodytes martinicensis: Dominica; at least formerly Guadeloupe and Martinique (Lesser Antilles)
Troglodytes monticola: high grassland of Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (northeastern Colombia)
Troglodytes musculus: various habitats from southeastern Mexico, including the Yucatan Peninsula, southward across most Central America and South America to Tierra del Fuego, but excluding high elevations and tops of tepuis
Troglodytes ochraceus: montane forest from northwestern Costa Rica through far northwestern Colombia, on Cerro Tacarcuna
Troglodytes rufociliatus: humid montane forest from northwestern Chiapas (southeastern Mexico) through El Salvador and northern Nicaragua
Troglodytes sissonii: Socorro Island (Revillagigedo Islands off western Mexico)
Troglodytes solstitialis: humid forest of high Andes from Sierra de Perijá (northern Colombia-Venezuela border) and Andes of Venezuela southward through Andes to Catamarca in northwestern Argentina
Troglodytes tanneri: Clarion Island (Revillagigedo Islands off western Mexico)
Trogon ambiguus: oak-pine woodland of southeastern Arizona and southwestern New Mexico to northwestern Mexico (Sinaloa), Tres Marías Islands (off western Mexico), and northern Nuevo León and central Tamaulipas westward to Nayarit and southward to Oaxaca (eastern to southern Mexico)
Trogon bairdii: Pacific slope of southwestern Costa Rica and western Panama
Trogon caligatus: humid to semi-humid forest of the Gulf of Mexico slope from southern Tamaulipas and eastern San Luis Potosí and the Pacific slope from eastern Oaxaca southeastward across Central America, including the Yucatan Peninsula, to eastern Panama; in South America in the lowlands of northern Colombia and western Venezuela, including the foothills of the Venezuelan Andes, southward in the Magdalena Valley (to Cundinamarca); west of the Andes in the lowland of western Colombia southward across Ecuador to northwesternmost Peru
Trogon chionurus: lowlands of eastern Panama to western Colombia and western Ecuador
Trogon chrysochloros: humid forest in the Atlantic Forest region of eastern Brazil in Alagoas, and from central Bahia southward to northern Rio Grande do Sul, northeastern Argentina and eastern Paraguay
Trogon citreolus: semiarid woodland of lowlands of Pacific slope of western Mexico from central Sinaloa to western Chiapas
Trogon clathratus: Caribbean coast of Costa Rica and western Panama
Trogon collaris: humid to semi-humid forest in the Gulf of Mexico and Pacific slopes of Mexico from eastern San Luis Potosí and central Guerrero southeastward across Central America, including the Yucatan Peninsula, to northern Nicaragua, and in foothill areas of Costa Rica and adjacent southern Nicaragua southeastward to eastern Panama and adjacent Colombia; in South America in foothills of the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela eastward to the Paría Peninsula, in Sierra de Perijá, and the Andes of western Venezuela southwestward along the Andes of Colombia to the humid lowlands of western Ecuador; east of the Andes in the Amazon basin and the Guiana Shield from southern Venezuela, Trinidad and Tobago and the Guianas southwestward to eastern Colombia, Ecuador and Peru to northern Bolivia, southward to western Santa Cruz, and in the entire Amazon of Brazil northeastward to Amapá, southward to southern Mato Grosso, and eastward to eastern Para; also in the Atlantic Forest of central-eastern Brazil in Bahia and Espirito Santo
Trogon comptus: humid forest of western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador
Trogon cupreicauda: tropical western Colombia and western Ecuador
Trogon curucui: forest and edge in lowlands and hills of South America east of the Andes from central Colombia eastward, thence mostly south of the Amazon River to northeastern Brazil and southward to northwestern Argentina, eastward through Paraguay and Mato Grosso do Sul (south-central Brazil)
Trogon elegans: dry forest, woodland, and scrub from southeastern Guatemala eastward to northern Honduras and southward across El Salvador and western Nicaragua to northwestern Costa Rica
Trogon massena: humid forest in the Caribbean slope from southern Veracruz and northern Oaxaca east and southward in Central America to eastern Panama; also in the Pacific lowlands of southeastern Nicaragua southeastward across Costa Rica to Panama in the Azuero Peninsula; in South America only west of the Andes in the Pacific lowlands of Colombia southward to northernmost Ecuador
Trogon melanocephalus: southeastern Mexico to northern Costa Rica
Trogon melanurus: forest and edge of lowlands and hills from central Panama through far northern to southwestern Colombia, and east of the Andes from eastern Colombia through the Guianas and Amazonia to Maranhão, in the south to central Bolivia and Mato Grosso (central Brazil)
Trogon mexicanus: montane forest of eastern Sonora and western Chihuahua on Pacific slope, and central Nuevo León on Caribbean slope, thence southward through transvolcanic belt of Mexico (except Yucatan Peninsula) through Honduras
Trogon personatus: montane cloudforest in the Andes from western Venezuela, Sierra del Perijá and Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta southward along the western, central and eastern Andes of Colombia through Ecuador to northern Peru, and along the eastern Andes of Peru southeastward to southern Bolivia, southward to Chuquisaca; also in the tepuis of southern and eastern Venezuela, adjacent Guyana and northernmost Brazil
Trogon ramonianus: tropical rainforest in the upper Orinoco and Amazon basins from southern Venezuela and northwestern Brazil, west of the Rio Negro, southward across Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru to central Bolivia (southward to central Santa Cruz), and eastward in Brazil south of the Amazon River (to northeastern Pará, adjacent Maranhão, and northern Tocantins)
Trogon rufus: forest of lowlands to hills of Amazonia and the Guianas, from eastern Ecuador eastward to French Guiana and Maranhão, southward to northern Bolivia and northern Mato Grosso (south-central Brazil)
Trogon surrucura: humid to semi-deciduous and gallery forest in interior and eastern Brazil (from northern Bahia, eastward to easternmost Tocantins and western Goais, and southward to southern Rio Grande do Sul), far northern Uruguay, eastern Paraguay, and northeastern Argentina (southward to Corrientes and northeastern Santa Fe, and eastward to eastern Chaco)
Trogon tenellus: northern Honduras to far northwestern Colombia
Trogon violaceus: Venezuela, Trinidad, the Guianas, and adjacent northern Brazil
Trogon viridis: east of the Andes from Colombia southward to Peru and Bolivia, and eastward to Trinidad, the Guianas, and eastern Brazil (to Maranhão and Mato Grosso; also Alagoas, and from Bahia southward to São Paulo
Tropicoperdix charltonii: disjunctly in the northern Malayan Peninsula, northern Sumatra, and southern Sumatra, from where there is just one old record; on the Malayan Peninsula, it occurs southward to northern Pahang, and north to southernmost Thailand (where the species is now very rare); on Sumatra, known only from the far north, around Aceh, Lampung, and Telukbetung
Tropicoperdix chloropus: widespread across Indochina, across most of Thailand, except the Peninsula, Laos, Cambodia, and Vietnam, as well as in northern, central, and southern Myanmar, and locally to southwest China, in Yunnan
Trugon terrestris: New Guinea, including Salawati (Raja Ampat Islands, off western New Guinea)
Tunchiornis ferrugineifrons: tropical rainforest in the western Amazon and Orinoco basins from eastern Venezuela southward to northwestern Bolivia, and in Brazil eastward to eastern Amazonas, west of the Rio Madeira
Tunchiornis luteifrons: far eastern Venezuela (eastern Bolívar), the Guianas, and northern Amazonian Brazil (east of the Rio Negro)
Tunchiornis ochraceiceps: humid to semi-humid forest from the Gulf of Mexico slope in southeastern Mexico, including the Yucatan Peninsula, southward to eastern Panama, and in the Pacific slope of Costa Rica and Panama, and from northwestern Colombia, including the northern end of the central and western Andes, southward along the Pacific lowlands to northwestern Ecuador
Tunchiornis rubrifrons: tropical rainforest in the Amazon basin south of the Amazon River from northeastern Brazil, in Maranhão, southwestward to southwestern Brazil, in Rondônia, east of the Rio Madeira
Turacoena sulaensis: Banggai and Sula islands (off eastern Sulawesi)
Turdinus macrodactylus: Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Java, and central Kalimantan (south-central Borneo)
Turdoides atripennis: lowland and foothill dense rainforest understory, including rainforest, and thickets in secondary forest, from Senegambia eastward to Central African Republic, and southward to northern Republic of the Congo and western Uganda
Turdoides bicolor: lowland to foothill arid savanna, acacia thornscrub in sparse grassland, dry woodland, and riparian scrub, from northern Namibia and far southern Angola eastward to western and southern Zimbabwe, and southward through Botswana to northern and northeastern South Africa, and possibly southwestern Mozambique; some nomadic wandering
Turdoides chapini: foothill and montane transitional broadleaf forest in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Turdoides gilberti: patchy in foothill to submontane primary forest and secondary growth, especially with thick epiphytic moss, in highlands of southeastern Nigeria and southwestern Cameroon
Turdoides gymnogenys: arid bush of southwestern Angola and northwestern Namibia
Turdoides hartlaubii: lowland to montane dense scrub, acacia woodland, and marsh, from eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda southward to Zambia and southwestern Tanzania, and from central Angola and northern Namibia eastward to northern Botswana and far western Zimbabwe
Turdoides hindei: patchy in foothill riparian thicket and Lantana scrub in river valleys, and brushy riverine gulleys in drier open woodland, in south-central Kenya
Turdoides hypoleuca: foothill brushland, thickets and scrub, and gardens, from central and southern Kenya southward to northern and northeastern Tanzania
Turdoides jardineii: lowland to montane thickets in lightly-wooded savanna, riverine scrub, and brushy termitaria, from southern Gabon and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to western Uganda and southwestern Kenya, and southward to northeastern Namibia, northern and eastern Botswana, northeastern South Africa, Eswatini, and southern Mozambique
Turdoides leucocephala: lowland to foothill dense riverine scrub, and dry acacia woodland, in southeastern Sudan, Eritrea, and northwestern Ethiopia
Turdoides leucopygia: foothill and montane scrub in juniper woodland, open stony hills, and farmbush, from coastal Eritrea and northern Ethiopia southward to southern South Sudan, and eastward to northwestern Somalia
Turdoides melanops: lowland to foothill riverine thickets, acacia savanna, and camelthorn woodland, from southwestern Angola and northern Namibia eastward to northwestern Botswana and northeastern Namibia (Caprivi Strip)
Turdoides nipalensis: Himalayas of western and central Nepal
Turdoides plebejus: lowland to montane wooded grassland, brushy savanna, and riparian thickets, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to western Ethiopia, and southward to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and western Kenya
Turdoides reinwardtii: lowland to foothill riparian scrub, wooded savanna, and swampy thickets, from Senegambia eastward to southern Chad, Central African Republic, and adjacent northern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Turdoides rufocinctus: patchy in foothill to montane primary forest with mossy epiphytes, and dense bamboo thickets, from eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward to southwestern Uganda, Rwanda, and northern Burundi
Turdoides sharpei: foothill and montane wooded savanna, thickets and scrub, and elephant grass, in highlands around Lake Victoria, in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda, Burundi, southern Uganda, southwestern Kenya, and northern and western Tanzania
Turdoides squamulata: patchy in lowland riparian thickets, and dense coastal bush, from southern Ethiopia and southern Somalia southward to southeastern Kenya
Turdoides tenebrosa: patchy in lowland to foothill understory of hilly woodland, and dense riparian scrub, South Sudan and southwestern Ethiopia, and southward to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and northwestern Uganda
Turdus abyssinicus: montane forest from Eritrea, Ethiopia, and southern South Sudan southward through eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Tanzania to Malawi and northeastern Zambia
Turdus albicollis: Yungas of Bolivia (La Paz, Santa Cruz, and Tarija) and far northwestern Argentina, and disjunctly in eastern Brazil from Bahia, Espírito Santo, and Alagoas southward to Mato Grosso, eastern Paraguay, Rio Grande do Sul, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
Turdus albocinctus: Himalayas of northern India to southeastern Tibet, southwestern China, and northwestern Myanmar
Turdus amaurochalinus: eastern Peru to central Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay, and Brazil
Turdus ardosiaceus: Hispaniola, including Gonâve and Tortue islands, Puerto Rico, and Dominica (Lesser Antilles)
Turdus arthuri: eastern Colombia eastward to southern Venezuela and Guyana, southward locally to central Amazonian Brazil, from the east bank of the Río Madeira to the east bank of the Río Tapajós
Turdus assimilis: deciduous, humid and coniferous forest and woodland in the Pacific and Gulf of Mexico slopes from northern Mexico (Sonora and Tamaulipas) southward along montane regions to central Panama
Turdus atrogularis: breeds eastern Russia to western Siberia; winters to northern India and China
Turdus aurantius: wooded hills and mountains of Jamaica
Turdus boulboul: Himalayas of western Pakistan to northern Myanmar, southern China, and northern southeastern Asia
Turdus cardis: breeds central China and Japan; winters to southern China and Indochina
Turdus celaenops: Izu Islands and Yakushima (Ryukyu Islands, southern Japan)
Turdus chiguanco: dry to semi-humid montane woodland and scrub, bushy gorges, and fields in the Andes from central Ecuador southward to east-central Chile and west-central Argentina (Rio Negro), sierras of Cordoba and San Luis, and east-central Argentina (La Pampa southward to coastal Chubut); in southern Peru reaches the coastal lowlands
Turdus chrysolaus: Sakhalin and Kuril islands (southeastern Russia) to Honshu (central Japan); winters mainly to northern and western Philippines
Turdus daguae: eastern Panama (Darién) to western Colombia and northwestern Ecuador, also locally in southwestern Ecuador
Turdus deningeri: montane Taliabu (Sula Islands, east of Sulawesi) and Mount Binaia on Seram (southern Moluccas)
Turdus dissimilis: mountains of Assam to southwestern China, northern Myanmar, and northern southeastern Asia
Turdus eremita: Tristan da Cunha, Inaccessible, and Nightingale islands (Tristan da Cunha group, South Atlantic Ocean)
Turdus eunomus: breeds northern Siberia to Kamchatka; winters to Japan, southern China, and Myanmar
Turdus falcklandii: northern Chile from Region IV south and from Mendoza eastward to southern Buenos Aires province (central Argentina), thence southward through Tierra del Fuego; Falkland Islands; introduced (?) to Juan Fernandez Islands, far west of central Chile
Turdus feae: breeds mountains of northeastern China (Liaoning); winters to India and Myanmar
Turdus flavipes: disjunctly in humid to semi-humid forest and woodland of foothills of the Andes of northeastern Colombia and western Venezuela, Santa Marta and Perijá mountains, coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Falcón eastward to the Paría Peninsula), Isla Margarita, Trinidad and Tobago, tepuis of southern Venezuela, western Guyana, and far northern Brazil (Roraima), and in the Atlantic Forest of eastern Brazil from Rio Grande do Norte southward to far eastern Paraguay, far northeastern Argentina, and Uruguay
Turdus fulviventris: eastern Andes of Colombia to northwestern Venezuela and far northern Peru
Turdus fumigatus: humid forest and woodland, gallery forest, savanna, and mangroves in the lowlands of northeastern Colombia and western Venezuela eastward to Trinidad and to St. Vincent and Grenada (southern Lesser Antilles), westward to southwestern Colombia (Cauca), eastern Venezuela and the Guianas southward to central and eastern Amazon basin in Brazil (to Tocantins), and the Atlantic Forest region of eastern Brazil from northern Bahia southward to Espírito Santo
Turdus fuscater: humid to dry montane woodland and scrub, shrubby paramo, and fields, in the Santa Marta and Perijá mountains, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward to central Bolivia (western Santa Cruz)
Turdus grayi: open forest to gardens from lowlands to hills of southern Texas on Caribbean slope southward through central Veracruz, thence both slopes (perhaps introduced in southern Oaxaca but now widespread there) southward through Mexico including Yucatan Peninsula and Cozumel, through Panama to northwestern Colombia eastward to the Venezuelan border, and southward in Cauca Valley of west-central Colombia
Turdus haplochrous: northern Bolivia (Beni and Santa Cruz); rare and local
Turdus hauxwelli: southeastern Colombia to northern Bolivia, southern Venezuela, and western Amazonian Brazil
Turdus heinrothi: Mussau, in St. Matthias Group (north-central Bismarck Archipelago), mountains of New Ireland, and Tolokiwa Island (eastern Bismarck Archipelago)
Turdus helleri: local in foothill and submontane understory of forest in Taita Hills (southeastern Kenya)
Turdus hortulorum: breeds eastern Siberia, northeastern China, and North Korea; winters to southeastern Asia
Turdus ignobilis: humid forest, woodland and borders, and gallery forest in the Sierra de Perijá and foothills of the Andes of western Venezuela and west of the Andes southward to far southern Colombia (Pasto), the Amazon basin from southern Venezuela southward to central Bolivia, and Brazil mostly in the western Amazon eastward along the Amazon River to northeastern Pará and southward to western Mato Grosso
Turdus iliacus: lowland to submontane open coniferous forest, edges of open deciduous and mixed forest, shoreline thickets, tundra scrub, and gardens, from Iceland, Scotland, and Scandinavia eastward to eastern Siberia, and southward to northeastern Europe, northern Kazakhstan, and northern Mongolia; migrates to western Europe, northwestern Africa, and Middle East
Turdus infuscatus: humid montane forest of eastern, southeastern and southern Mexico to northwestern Nicaragua
Turdus jamaicensis: montane forest and wooded hills of Jamaica
Turdus javanicus: mountains of Sumatra, Java, and northern Borneo
Turdus kessleri: breeds Himalayas of western China (Gansu to Sichuan); winters to northern India
Turdus kulambangrae: mountains of Kolombangara and Guadalcanal (central and southeastern Solomon Islands)
Turdus lawrencii: southeastern Colombia to northern Bolivia, southern Venezuela, and western Amazonian Brazil
Turdus leucomelas: disjunctly in humid forest borders, dry woodland, wooded savanna, gallery forest, and fields from northern and central Colombia and western Venezuela, the tepuis of southern Venezuela and adjacent Brazil eastward to the Guianas and northeastern Brazil and westward along the Amazon River (to eastern Amazonas), in interior and northeastern Brazil southward to eastern Bolivia, northeastern Argentina, and northern Uruguay, with isolated populations in western Bolivia and adjacent Peru and in the Rio Mayo of eastern Peru (San Martín)
Turdus leucops: Andes of Colombia to western Bolivia; tepuis and mountains of western Venezuela
Turdus lherminieri: hill and montane forest and edge of Lesser Antilles from Montserrat to St. Lucia
Turdus libonyana: lowland to montane miombo woodland, acacia woodland, and gardens, from Angola and southeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo eastward (excluding Congolian rainforest) to southeastern Burundi and northern Tanzania, and southward to northeastern Namibia, northern and southeastern Botswana, southern Mozambique, eastern South Africa, and Eswatini
Turdus litsitsirupa: lowland to montane open woodland, sandveld, and moorland, from Angola, southern and eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, Zambia, and southwestern Tanzania, southward to central Namibia, Botswana, north-central and eastern South Africa, and southern Mozambique
Turdus ludoviciae: foothill to submontane open juniper woodland in northern Somalia
Turdus maculirostris: coastal western Ecuador (Esmeraldas) to far northwestern Peru (Tumbes)
Turdus mandarinus: lowland to montane open woodland, parkland, grassland with shrubs, orchards, and gardens, in central and eastern China, and has recently expanded to southern South Korea; some northern populations migrate southward to northern Indochina and Hainan (China)
Turdus maranonicus: northern Peru (upper Marañón Valley) and adjacent Ecuador
Turdus maximus: western Pakistan and India to Sikkim, Bhutan, and southeastern Tibet
Turdus merula: lowland to submontane open forest, woodland with shrubby understory, parkland, and gardens, from southern Iceland (scarce), Faroe Islands, British Isles, and Scandinavia eastward to northwestern China, and southward to Azores, Madeira, and Canary Islands, northwestern Africa, southern Greece, Levant, Iran, and northern Afghanistan; northern and highland populations move downslope in winter, and some migrate to north-coastal Africa and Persian Gulf; introduced to southeastern Australia and New Zealand
Turdus migratorius: breeds in varied woodland, forest, and garden types from northern Alaska eastward to northern Labrador (eastern Canada) and southward to far northern and (disjunctly) far southern Baja California, mountains of Mexico (to Oaxaca), and southern Texas eastward to northern Florida; winters from southern Alaska and southern Canada southward to San Luis Potosí and Veracruz (central Mexico) and southern Florida
Turdus mupinensis: western China (southern Gansu to Shaanxi, Hubei, Sichuan, and northwestern Yunnan)
Turdus murinus: southeastern Venezuela (Amazonas and Bolívar) and Guyana
Turdus naumanni: breeds central Siberia to northeastern China, Amurland, and Sakhalin; winters to Korean Peninsula
Turdus nigrescens: mountains of Costa Rica and western Panama (far western Chiriquí)
Turdus nigriceps: breeds in the Andes of southern Bolivia (north to Santa Cruz) and northwestern Argentina (southward to Córdoba), also locally in southwestern Ecuador and northwestern Peru; nonbreeding migrant to the east slope of the Andes from southeastern Ecuador to Bolivia
Turdus nigrorum: mountains of Negros, Panay, Sibuyan, and Mindanao (west-central and southern Philippines)
Turdus nudigenis: varied woodland from lowlands to hills from Guadeloupe to Grenada (central and southern Lesser Antilles), Trinidad and Tobago; northern and central Colombia to the Guianas, and northern Brazil southeastward to Maranhão and southward to northern Tocantins
Turdus obscurus: breeds Siberia, Mongolia, and Japan; winters to Indonesia and Philippines
Turdus obsoletus: humid forest edge of hills and mountains of Caribbean slope of Costa Rica through western Panama, thence both slopes to north-central Colombia and southward west of Andes to southwestern Ecuador
Turdus olivaceus: foothill and montane forest, unburnt Fynbos, thornscrub, and gardens, from southern Malawi, eastern Zimbabwe, and western Mozambique, southward to eastern and southern South Africa; local downslope movement in southern winter
Turdus olivater: highly disjunct in humid montane and cloudforest in coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Falcón eastward to Miranda), the Santa Marta and Perijá mountains, the Andes of western Venezuela and far northeastern Colombia, tepuis and mountains of southern Venezuela, western Guyana, southern Suriname, and far northern Brazil (Roraima and northern Amazonas), and southwestern Colombia (Huila and Cauca)
Turdus pallidus: breeds northeastern Siberia to Kuril Islands and Japan; winters to southeastern Asia and Sumatra
Turdus papuensis: mountains of New Guinea, including Goodenough Island (off southeastern New Guinea)
Turdus pelios: lowland to montane deciduous and evergreen woodland, wooded savanna, farmland, and parks, from Senegambia eastward through Nigeria and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea) to Eritrea and Ethiopia, and southward to western Angola, northern Zambia, and western Tanzania; northern populations partially migratory
Turdus phaeopygus: eastern Colombia to northern Venezuela, Trinidad and Tobago, the Guianas, and through the Amazonian basin from eastern Ecuador, northern Bolivia, and western Brazil
Turdus philomelos: lowland to submontane open woodland, parkland, small woodlots, orchards, and suburban gardens, from British Isles eastward to central Siberia, and southward to Iberian Peninsula, Balkans, Caucasus, and northern Iran; northern populations migrate southward as far as northern Africa, Arabian Peninsula, and Persian Gulf
Turdus pilaris: breeds northern Palearctic; winters to northern Africa, Mediterranean, and Near East
Turdus plebejus: montane forest and edge from southeastern Oaxaca (southern Mexico) through south-central Panama
Turdus plumbeus: Greater Antilles from Grand Bahama and Abaco southward to Cat Island, Cuba including Isla de la Juventud and other satellite islands, Cayman Brac (eastern Cayman Islands), and formerly also Swan Island (north of Honduras)
Turdus poliocephalus: formerly Lord Howe and Norfolk islands; extinct
Turdus pritzbueri: southern Vanuatu and Lifou (Loyalty Islands, New Caledonia, probably extirpated)
Turdus ravidus: formerly Grand Cayman Island; extinct, last reported 1938
Turdus reevei: arid scrub of southwestern Ecuador and northwestern Peru
Turdus roehli: local in foothill and submontane understory of forest in Taita Hills (southeastern Kenya)
Turdus rubrocanus: disjunctly in foothill to montane coniferous and mixed broadleaf evergreen forest, from northeastern Afghanistan eastward to northern India and Bhutan, and from eastern Tibetan Plateau to central China; downslope dispersal in winter, and short-distance migrant to Himalayan foothills and northern Thailand
Turdus ruficollis: breeds eastern Siberia to northeastern China; winters to western China, Myanmar, and northeastern India
Turdus rufitorques: highlands of southern Mexico (Chiapas) to central Honduras
Turdus rufiventris: open woods to city lawns of lowlands to mountains from eastern Maranhão eastward through northeastern Brazil, southwestward through central Bolivia, and southeastward to southern Buenos Aires province and Rio Grande do Sul

Turdus sanchezorum: northern and central Amazonian Peru, southwestern Amazonian Brazil
Turdus schlegelii: mountains of Sulawesi and Timor (eastern Lesser Sundas)
Turdus serranus: montane cloudforest in the coastal mountains of northern Venezuela (Yaracuy eastward to Monagas), the Sierra de Perijá, and the Andes of Venezuela southward through all Andes of Colombia to northern Peru, and in the eastern Andes of northern Peru east and south of the Río Marañón, southward to northwestern Argentina (Salta)

Turdus smithi: lowland to foothill riparian woodland, semi-desert, Karoo, plantations, and towns, from southern Namibia and northwestern South Africa eastward to southeastern Botswana, northeastern South Africa, and western Lesotho

Turdus swalesi: humid montane forest of southeastern Haiti and southwestern Dominican Republic (south-central Hispaniola)
Turdus tephronotus: lowland to foothill thornscrub, open brushy woodland, and arid rocky thickets, from southern Ethiopia and southern Somalia southward to northeastern and central Tanzania

Turdus unicolor: breeds Himalayas of Kashmir to Nepal; winters to southern Peninsular India
Turdus vanikorensis: Rennell and Temotu (southeastern Solomon Islands) and northern to central Vanuatu, and formerly Maré (Loyalty Islands), where extinct
Turdus viscivorus: lowland to foothill lightly-wooded open land, riverine forest, grassland with scrub, mountain steppe, and park-like farmland, from British Isles eastward to central Siberia, and southward to northwestern Africa, Mediterranean Europe, Caucasus, northern India, and western Nepal; northern populations migrate southward as far as northwestern Africa, Middle East, and south-central Asia
Turdus xanthopus: New Caledonia and satellites (possibly extinct except for Yandé, northwest of Grande Terre)

Turnagra tanagra: formerly New Zealand (North Island); extinct, last confirmed report in 1902
Turnix castanotus: northwestern Australia (Kimberley region, northern Northern Territory) and offshore islands
Turnix hottentottus: mountains of South Africa (southwestern Cape Province to Port Elizabeth)

Turnix nanus: Ghana to Kenya, Uganda, and southeastern Cape Province
Turnix nigricollis: Madagascar; introduced (?) Mauritius, Réunion, and Glorieuses
Turnix novaecaledoniae: formerly New Caledonia; probably extinct, not certainly reported since 1889
Turnix ocellatus: grassland, brush, and crops of lowlands and mountains of Luzon (northern Philippines)
Turnix olivii: northeastern Australia (Cape York Peninsula, northern Queensland); possibly extinct, last verified record 1924
Turnix pyrrhothorax: savanna and scrub of northern, central and eastern Australia (Kimberley region, northern Western Australia, eastward to eastern South Australia)

Turnix velox: grassland and woodland in Australia (except Tasmania)
Turtur abyssinicus: arid scrub and woodland of sub-Saharan Africa
Turtur brehmeri: Upper Guinea and Congolian rainforest from Sierra Leone and southern Guinea eastward through Central African Republic to Rift Valley of Democratic Republic of the Congo, and southward to far northwestern Angola
Turtur chalcospilos: woodland and thornscrub of east and southern Africa

Tychaedon coryphoeus: lowland strandveld, Karoo scrub, and hillside bush, from central Namibia southward to western and central South Africa, and Lesotho

Tympanuchus cupido: prairies with interspersed woodland in central US from North Dakota and adjacent Minnesota southward to northeastern Colorado, northern Kansas, southern Oklahoma and eastward to Missouri and southern Illinois; also isolated in the coastal plains of southeastern Texas; formerly to south-central Canada

Tyranneutes stolzmanni: eastern Colombia to southern Venezuela, northern Bolivia, and Amazonian Brazil
Tyranneutes virescens: southeastern Venezuela to the Guianas and northeastern Amazonian Brazil
Tyranniscus cinereiceps: Andes of Colombia to Ecuador and southern Peru (Puno)
Tyranniscus nigrocapillus: montane cloudforest in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, the Andes from western Venezuela southward to northern Peru north of the Río Marañón (Cajamarca), and the eastern Andes of Peru (Amazonas to northwestern Cusco)
Tyranniscus uropygialis: Andes of Colombia and western Venezuela to western Bolivia (southward to Tarija)
Tyrannopsis sulphurea: southern Venezuela, Trinidad, and the Guianas to northern Bolivia and Amazonian Brazil
Tyrannulus elatus: southwestern Costa Rica to northern Bolivia, the Guianas, and Amazonian Brazil
Tyrannus albogularis: southern Venezuela and the Guianas to northern Bolivia and Amazonian Brazil

Tyrannus savana: southern Mexico (Veracruz) to Colombia, the Guianas, and northern Brazil disjunctly to central Argentina; southern populations migratory
Tyrannus tyrannus: breeds eastern North America; winters mainly western Amazon basin

Tyto inexspectata: hill forest of northern and north-central Sulawesi

Tyto prigoginei: poorly known; reported only from the Itombwe Mountains and Itombwe Forest, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Tyto soumagnei: very locally northern and eastern Madagascar; most recent records from far north
Tyto tenebricosa: rainforest from lowlands to mountains of New Guinea (except Trans-Fly) including Yapen (Cenderawasih Bay, off northwestern New Guinea), and eastern Australia southward to southeastern Victoria
Upucerthia albigula: west slope of Andes of southwestern Peru and far northern Chile (Arica)

Urocissa whiteheadi: local in lowland and hill woodland from southeastern Sichuan through central Vietnam and Hainan

Uromyias agraphia: humid montane forest and treeline in the eastern Andes of Peru from the northern Amazonas southward to Cusco
Uropelia campestris: west-central Brazil (Mato Grosso) and adjacent Bolivia

Urosphena whiteheadi: mountains of northern Borneo (Kinabalu to Liang Kubung)
Urosticte benjamini: Pacific slope of western Colombia to southwestern Ecuador and northwestern Peru
Urosticte ruficrissa: east slope of Andes in southern Colombia and eastern Ecuador
Urothraupis stolzmanni: Andes of southeastern Colombia and eastern Ecuador
Urotriorchis macrourus: Liberia to western Uganda and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo
Vanellus armatus: inland west-central Angola to south-central Kenya and southward to South Africa
Vanellus chilensis: inland from northern Honduras (and expanding northward) to southern Chile and southern Argentina
Vanellus cinereus: breeds inland northeastern China (Heilongjiang and Inner Mongolia), and central and southern Japan (Honshu to Kyushu); winters to southern and northeastern India, through southeastern Asia, Malayan Peninsula, Vietnam, southeastern China, and central and southern Japan
Vanellus coronatus: inland northeastern to southern Africa, from northern Somalia in the northeast and Angola in the south, southward through South Africa
Vanellus crassirostris: inland sub-Saharan Africa, mostly from South Sudan and Kenya southward through northern Botswana and central Mozambique
Vanellus duvaucelii: rivers of India and Nepal to southwestern China and Indochina

Vanellus malabaricus: southern Indus Valley of Pakistan, inland India eastward to central Assam, and Sri Lanka
Vanellus melanocephalus: montane grassland of north-central to south-central Ethiopia
Vanellus melanopterus: inland northeastern to southeastern Africa from Eritrea to northern Tanzania and disjunctly eastern South Africa

Vanellus resplendens: Andes of south-central Colombia to northern Chile and northwestern Argentina
Vanellus senegallus: inland sub-Saharan Africa (except Congolian forest and northwestern and southwestern arid regions) from southern Mauritania east through Eritrea and southward through northeastern South Africa
Vanellus spinosus: Senegambia to Red Sea, northeastern Tanzania, and eastern Mediterranean
Vanellus superciliosus: range poorly known; breeds from Nigeria east (probably) to northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo; disperses west to Ghana, southward to Cameroon and southern Democratic Republic of the Congo, and eastward to western Tanzania
Vanellus tectus: inland Sahel zone from southern Mauritania eastward to Eritrea and in south from northern Guinea eastward to far northern Tanzania
Vanellus tricolor: inland and southern Australia including Tasmania

Vauriella gularis: mountains of northern Borneo (Mount Kinabalu and adjacent mountains)

Veniliornis sanguineus: humid coastal lowlands of the Guianas
Veniliornis spilogaster: southeastern Brazil to southeastern Paraguay, Uruguay, and northeastern Argentina
Vermivora bachmanii: formerly bred southeastern USA; wintered to Cuba and Bahamas (probably extinct)
Vermivora chrysoptera: breeds eastern North America; winters Guatemala to northwestern South America and Greater Antilles
