Zentrygon frenata: montane cloudforest in the Andes from northwestern, central, and east-central Colombia southward to northern Peru north of the Río Marañón, and in the eastern Andes from northern Peru east and south of the Marañón, southward across Peru and Bolivia to northwestern Argentina (to Jujuy and adjacent northern Salta)
Zentrygon goldmani: humid forest of foothills and mountains of east-central Panama through Darién and adjacent far northwestern Colombia
Zentrygon linearis: northern, central, and eastern Colombia to northeastern Venezuela, and Trinidad and Tobago
Zimmerius acer: eastern Venezuela, the Guianas, and northeastern Brazil north of the Amazon River and east of the Rio Branco and Rio Negro; populations south of the Amazon River (west to the lower Rio Madeira, eastward to Ceará and Alagoas) included here, but may represent an undescribed taxon
Zimmerius albigularis: southwestern Colombia (Nariño) and western Ecuador (southward to southwestern Guayas)
Zimmerius bolivianus: Andes of southeastern Peru (Huánuco to Puno) to western Bolivia
Zimmerius chicomendesi: south-central Amazonian Brazil (between the Rio Madeira and Rio Aripuanã)
Zimmerius chrysops: humid lowland to montane forest in the coastal mountains of northeastern Venezuela (Falcón, and Anzoátegui eastward to the Paría Peninsula), the Santa Marta and Perijá mountains, and the Andes of western Venezuela southward in all Andes of Colombia to far northwestern and eastern Ecuador, and northern Peru (Amazonas and San Martín), in eastern Ecuador reaching the Amazon lowlands
Zimmerius cinereicapilla: foothills of eastern Ecuador and eastern Peru (southward to Madre de Dios)
Zimmerius gracilipes: tropical rainforest in the Orinoco and Amazon basins from central and southern Venezuela southward to northeastern Ecuador, eastern Peru, and northern to central Bolivia, and eastward in Brazil to eastern Amazonas west of the Rio Negro, and to central Mato Grosso (central Brazil)
Zimmerius improbus: foothill and montane cloudforest in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Sierra de Perija, and the Andes of western Venezuela and northeastern Colombia
Zimmerius parvus: lowlands from eastern Guatemala, Belize, and Honduras southward to Panama and far northwestern Colombia (Chocó)
Zimmerius petersi: coastal cordillera of northern Venezuela (southern Lara eastward to Miranda)
Zimmerius vilissimus: highlands of southern Mexico (Chiapas), Guatemala and western El Salvador
Zimmerius villarejoi: two disjunct regions in northern Peru: in the Río Mayo Valley and along the adjacent Río Huallaga (San Martín); and in the Río Nanay drainage (Loreto)
Zimmerius viridiflavus: montane cloudforest and humid scrub in the Andes of southern Ecuador (from Chimborazo), southward to northern Peru north of the Río Marañón, and in the eastern Andes from northern Peru, south and east of the Río Marañón, to south-central Peru (Junín)
Zonerodius heliosylus: New Guinea, including Salawati (Raja Ampat Islands, northwest of New Guinea), and Aru Islands (off southwestern New Guinea)
Zonibyx modestus: breeds inland south-central Chile, southern Argentina, and Falkland Islands; winters to coastal southern Peru and southeastern Brazil
Zonotrichia albicollis: breeds northern North America; winters to southern USA and northern Mexico
Zonotrichia atricapilla: breeds Alaska and western Canada; winters to Sonora and Baja California
Zonotrichia capensis: varied grassland, savanna, scrub, cultivated fields, and urban areas from Chiapas (southeastern Mexico) southward through montane areas of Central America to central Panama, mountains of Hispaniola, and Aruba and Curaçao, coastal mountains of northern Venezuela, Perijá and Santa Marta ranges, and the Andes from western Venezuela southward to the southern Andes of Chile and Argentina, from eastern Colombia eastward to the Guianas, and southward through eastern and interior Brazil to Tierra del Fuego; southernmost populations winter to northward
Zonotrichia leucophrys: breeds in boreal forest, tundra, alpine meadows, dense shrubbery and thickets from northern Alaska eastward (south of Arctic islands) to Newfoundland (northeastern Canada), southward through northern and western USA to southwestern California and northern New Mexico; winters along the Pacific coast from southernmost Alaska southward to southern Baja California, and in western to eastern USA southward to Michoacan and Mexico DF (central Mexico), and in eastern USA southward to southern Florida
Zonotrichia querula: breeds north-central Canada; winters to southern USA
Zoonavena sylvatica: India south of the Himalayas to western Myanmar
Zoonavena thomensis: mountains of São Tomé and Príncipe (Gulf of Guinea)
Zoothera andromedae: patchily distributed Philippines to Sumatra, Java, and Lesser Sundas
Zoothera aurea: foothill to submontane coniferous and mixed forest, deciduous forest with dense understory, and wooded steppe, from western Siberia eastward to Sakhalin, and southward to northeastern China, Korean Peninsula, and Japan southward to Ogasawara (Bonin) Islands; migrates to southeastern China, Taiwan, northern Indochina, and northern Philippines
Zoothera dauma: breeds northern Pakistan eastward to northeastern India, southern China, and northern Indochina, also mountains of Sumatra, Java, Bali, Lombok, and Sumbawa, and Iriomotejima (southern Ryukyu Islands, southern Japan); northern populations winter to northern South Asia and continental southeastern Asia
Zoothera dixoni: breeds Himalayas to southwestern China and southeastern Tibet; winters to southeastern Asia
Zoothera everetti: high mountains of northern Borneo (Sarawak and Sabah)
Zoothera griseiceps: breeds south-central China (central Sichuan); winter range poorly known, but reported from northern Vietnam (Tonkin)
Zoothera heinei: New Guinea to St. Matthias (north-central Bismarck Archipelago), east-central Australia, and Choiseul (north-central Solomon Islands)
Zoothera lunulata: north-eastern, southeastern, and southern Australia including Tasmania
Zoothera major: Amami Ōshima (northern Ryukyu Islands, southern Japan)
Zoothera marginata: Nepal to northern India, southwestern China, Myanmar, Thailand, and northern Indochina
Zoothera mollissima: breeds in the Himalayas from northern Pakistan to southeastern Tibet and south-central China (Sichuan); winters at lower elevations, southward to Yunnan (China)
Zoothera monticola: Himalayas of northern India to northeastern Myanmar, and northern Vietnam (northwestern Tonkin)
Zoothera neilgherriensis: southern Peninsular India (Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu)
Zoothera salimalii: breeds in the eastern Himalayas from eastern Nepal to south-central China (Sichuan and Yunnan); winter range poorly known, but reported from northeastern India to northern Vietnam (Tonkin)
Zoothera talaseae: New Britain and Umboi (southeastern Bismarck Archipelago)
Zoothera terrestris: formerly Ogasawara (Bonin) Islands; extinct, last reported 1889
Zosterops abyssinicus: lowland to foothill open woodland in southern Arabian Peninsula, and from northeastern Sudan and Eritrea southward to Ethiopia, and eastward to Djibouti and western Somalia
Zosterops albogularis: formerly Norfolk Island (east of Australia); extinct, last recorded ca. 2000-2009
Zosterops anderssoni: lowland to montane woodland, wooded savanna, and plantations, from far western Democratic Republic of the Congo to eastern Tanzania, and southward to northern Namibia to eastern South Africa
Zosterops atrifrons: Sulawesi region, including Banggai and Sula islands (east of Sulawesi)
Zosterops auriventer: patchy in foothill to submontane broadleaf evergreen forest, secondary growth, scrub, and plantations, from southern Myanmar eastward to Cambodia, and southward through Malayan Peninsula to Sumatra and Borneo
Zosterops buruensis: mainly montane forest of Buru (southern Moluccas)
Zosterops chloris: islets north of Java and west of Borneo, Sulawesi, Lesser Sundas, central and southern Moluccas,and islands off western New Guinea
Zosterops citrinella: central Lesser Sundas, southern Moluccas, and far northeastern Australian islands
Zosterops erythropleurus: breeds southeastern Siberia and southwestern to northeastern China; winters to southeastern Asia
Zosterops eurycricotus: foothill to montane forest, forest edge, and wooded towns, in Mt. Kilimanjaro, Mt. Meru, and adjacent highlands (northern Tanzania)
Zosterops everetti: Talaud Islands (northeast of Sulawesi), Visayas (except westernmost), Mindanao group, and Sulu Archipelago (east-central and southern Philippines)
Zosterops explorator: Fiji (Viti Levu, Ovalau, Kadavu, Gau, Vanua Levu, and Taveuni)
Zosterops finschii: woodland of Palau Archipelago (western Caroline Islands)
Zosterops flavilateralis: lowland and foothill dry woodland, forest edge, and thornscrub, from southern Ethiopia and southern Somalia southward through lowlands of Kenya to northeastern Tanzania
Zosterops flavus: mangroves and bamboo belt of coastal northwestern Java and southeastern Borneo
Zosterops fuscicapilla: mountains of coastal northern New Guinea, including Goodenough, in D'Entrecasteaux Archipelago (off southeastern New Guinea)
Zosterops griseotinctus: widely disjunct islets in Louisiade (off southeastern New Guinea) and Bismarck archipelagos
Zosterops hypolais: forest and scrub of Yap (northwestern Caroline Islands)
Zosterops hypoxanthus: Bismarck Archipelago, including Manus, Admiralty Islands
Zosterops japonicus: disjunctly from lowland to montane forest, woodland, secondary growth, parks and gardens, from southern Sakhalin (Russia) southward to coastal South Korea, Japan and satellite islands, Philippines, and in Indonesia from Sumatra eastward to Java, Bali, and Lesser Sundas eastward to Timor, and on Sulawesi and Wallacea; introduced to Singapore, Ogasawara (Bonin) Islands (Japan), and Hawaiian Islands (all main islands)
Zosterops kaffensis: foothill to montane forest edges and cultivation, in southwestern Ethiopia and northern Kenya (Mount Kulal)
Zosterops kasaicus: lowland to foothill open woodland and savanna, acacia thickets, and plantations, from western and central Democratic Republic of the Congo southward to northern and western Angola
Zosterops kikuyuensis: foothill to montane forest, forest edge, bamboo thickets, and wooded gardens, in highlands of central Kenya
Zosterops kulambangrae: Solomon Islands (Kolombangara, Vonavona, Kohinggo, New Georgia, Vangunu, and Nggatokae)
Zosterops lacertosus: woodland and scrub of Nendö (northern Temotu, southeastern Solomon Islands)
Zosterops lateralis: Australia, New Zealand and outlying islands, New Caledonia, and western Pacific islands to Fiji (southwestern Polynesia)
Zosterops maderaspatanus: Madagascar, Europa Island, Cosmoledo Atoll, and Isles Glorieuses, Mohéli and Anjouan islands (Comoros), and Aldabra and Astove islands (Indian Ocean)
Zosterops mbuluensis: foothill to submontane forest, and forest edge, in southern Kenya (Namanga and Chyulu hills) and northern Tanzania highlands (from Mt. Hanang, Mbulu and Crater Highlands, Mt. Ketumbeine and Longido eastward to northern Pare Mountains)
Zosterops meeki: uplands of Tagula (Louisiade Archipelago, off southeastern New Guinea); status unknown
Zosterops melanocephalus: submontane to montane forest clearings and edge, bushy thickets, and scrub in highland grassland on Mt. Cameroon (southwestern Cameroon)
Zosterops meratusensis: Meratus Mountains, South Kalimantan, southeastern Borneo
Zosterops metcalfii: Buka to Florida (northern and central Solomon Islands)
Zosterops meyeni: islands southeast of Taiwan, and northern and central Philippines
Zosterops minor: New Guinea, including Yapen (Cenderawasih Bay, off northwestern New Guinea)
Zosterops minutus: forest and scrub of Lifou (central Loyalty Islands, New Caledonia)
Zosterops modestus: forest of Mahé and Conception Island (Seychelles); reintroduced to Frégate, Cousin, and North islands
Zosterops mouroniensis: Grand Comoro Island (montane heath of Mount Karthala)
Zosterops mysorensis: mountains of Supiori and Biak (Cenderawasih Bay, off northwestern New Guinea)
Zosterops natalis: Christmas Island; introduced Cocos (Keeling) Island (east-central Indian Ocean)
Zosterops nigrorum: Philippines (except Palawan group, East Visayas, Mindanao, and Sulu Archipelago)
Zosterops novaeguineae: northwestern and eastern New Guinea, including Aru Islands (off southwestern New Guinea)
Zosterops pallidus: patchy in lowland to montane open hilly country with scattered trees, wooded savanna, acacia thickets, riverine and coastal dune scrub, and wooded gardens, from far southern Angola southward through Namibia to northwestern South Africa, and eastward to north-central South Africa; some post-breeding dispersal
Zosterops palpebrosus: lowland to montane forest, secondary growth, and mangroves, from northeastern Afghanistan eastward through Himalayas to southeastern China, and southward to Indian subcontinent, Sri Lanka, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Indochina, and disjunctly in coastal southern Iran and Mahawt Island (Oman); montane populations move downslope in winter
Zosterops paruhbesar: Wangi-wangi, Wakatobi (Tukangbesi) Islands, off southeastern Sulawesi
Zosterops poliogastrus: foothill to montane woodland, forest edges, patches of trees in steppe, cultivation, and gardens, from Eritrea southward through Ethiopia highlands, and disjunctly in highlands of southeastern South Sudan
Zosterops rotensis: Sabena Plateau on Rota (southernmost Northern Mariana Islands)
Zosterops semperi: Palau, Chuuk, and Pohnpei (Caroline Islands, western and central Micronesia)
Zosterops senegalensis: lowland to montane open woodland, wooded savanna, and thornscrub, from southern Mauritania and Senegambia eastward to northern Ethiopia and Eritrea, and southward to northern Republic of the Congo, and highlands of Kenya and northern Tanzania
Zosterops silvanus: foothill to submontane forest edge, forest remnants and adjacent scrub, and wooded gardens on Mt. Kasigau and Taita Hills (southeastern Kenya)
Zosterops simplex: disjunctly in lowland to foothill deciduous or mixed forest, thickets, secondary growth, scrub, mangroves, and gardens, from eastern Myanmar eastward to eastern China (including Hainan) and Taiwan, and southward to northern Vietnam, and from coastal Thailand and southern Vietnam southward to Malayan Peninsula, coastal Borneo, and Sumatra and satellite islands; some northern populations migrate to Indochina; introduced to urban southern California
Zosterops socotranus: lowland to foothill semi-evergreen woodland, thornscrub, and gardens on Socotra; apparently endemic to Socotra, as populations in Somalia may be a yet-unnamed species
Zosterops stenocricotus: lowland to montane open woodland, forest clearings and edge, riverine thickets, and wooded swamps, from southeastern Nigeria and southern Cameroon, and Bioko (Gulf of Guinea), eastward to northern Republic of the Congo, and southward to Gabon
Zosterops strenuus: formerly Lord Howe Island (east of Australia); extinct, last recorded 1910s
Zosterops stuhlmanni: foothill to montane forest edge, open woodland, and plantations, from northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda southward to Burundi and northwestern Tanzania
Zosterops superciliosus: open woodland of Rennell (southeastern Solomon Islands)
Zosterops vaughani: lowland mangrove forest, coral rag thickets, plantations, and gardens, on Pemba and adjacent coral islets (off northeastern Tanzania)
Zosterops vellalavella: Vella Lavella and Bagga (west-central Solomon Islands)
Zosterops virens: lowland to montane open woodland and savanna, acacia thickets, and dune scrub, from southwestern Botswana, northeastern South Africa, and far southwestern Mozambique southward through southern and southwestern South Africa, and Eswatini and Lesotho
Zosterops winifredae: submontane to montane tree-heath at forest edge, forest clearings, and low heath, in South Pare Mountains (northeastern Tanzania)
Zosterops xanthochroa: New Caledonia, including Grande Terre and Île des Pins, and Maré (eastern Loyalty Islands, New Caledonia)
